chapters.title: Chapter 551
paragraphs: On the night six young men and women slipped secretly out of Henan, two men clinked wine cups in a moonlit pavilion.
Clink.
The cups tilted with a clear ring. Fire King Jeok Cheongang drained his wine in one gulp and muttered, “The wine doesn’t taste right tonight.”
Mae Jonghak smiled from across the table. “Perhaps Yeoahong isn’t to your taste.”
“I don’t know. My throat’s been scratchy and my tongue bitter for a while now. You haven’t poisoned it, have you?”
No one else could have said that, even as a joke. Only Jeok Cheongang could—and only Mae Jonghak, sitting opposite him, could laugh it off.
“Me, poison Great Hero Jeok? Never. Though I may try it someday.”
“Do your research first. I’m confident I could withstand even Formless Ultimate Poison now.”
“Oh. Then I’ll look into it, even if I have to put the full strength of the Murim Alliance behind the effort.”
Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly. “How frightening. Anyone listening might think you were serious.”
“Oh, that was a joke? And here I thought...”
Surely not.
Mae Jonghak nodded as though he had only just realized it was a joke, sending a chill down Jeok Cheongang’s spine.
What a lunatic old man.
His looks had grown younger, but he was just as insane as he’d been forty years ago. Then again, Jeok Cheongang didn’t have to look that far back for proof. Cheongpung alone made it obvious.
Like master, like disciple. Those two...
His hand jerked as he filled his cup.
Disciple.
Wine splashed over the brim. Reflected in it was the bitter expression of a middle-aged man.
Jeok Cheongang gazed at his own face, familiar yet still strange, then spoke without warning.
“Nothing will happen to him, will it?”
Mae Jonghak filled his own cup. “Are you worried?”
“Worried? Why would I be? Once a man’s past twenty, he ought to go his own way. He’s old enough to start a family.”
Jeok Cheongang tried to sound confident, but his mouth still tasted bitter. He was thinking of someone who must be heading south by now.
Mae Jonghak caught the emotion that briefly crossed his face.
“He can’t have gone far.”
“Even though we already said our goodbyes, what would be the point of seeing him again? It would only make it harder to leave.”
“Now that you mention it, I suppose you’re right.”
“So? What’s your answer?”
“Hm? To what?”
“You become Alliance Leader and suddenly go deaf? You know... what I asked you earlier.”
Jeok Cheongang toyed with his cup before continuing more cautiously.
“Nothing will happen to him. Right?”
Mae Jonghak thought for a moment. “Maybe. Maybe not.”
“...You call that an answer?”
“Well, it was something I said. It just came out of my mouth.”
“Damn it. You’re driving me insane. Anyone could give me an answer like that!”
“Oh. I suppose that’s true.”
“Then give me a proper answer as Alliance Leader. A proper answer!”
Mae Jonghak smiled at Jeok Cheongang’s outburst.
“He’ll do fine. Just as he always has.”
“You mean that?”
“Of course. If I didn’t believe in him, why would I have entrusted the Fire Dragon Pavilion with such an important mission?”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice softened. “Have you made preparations in case things go wrong?”
“The Hidden Shadow Pavilion has eyes and ears throughout the realm. Nanman is no exception.”
“Sending the Fire Dragon Pavilion to Nanman is the fastest and most reliable option. We don’t have enough time to raise an army right now.”

The Murim Alliance was by no means smaller than it had been during the Great Faction War. If anything, it was larger. Shaolin Temple, the Sichuan Sect, and several other sects had suffered heavy losses, but not a single province in the Nine Provinces, still the territory of the orthodox faction, had fallen.

The problem was the time and supplies it would take to gather troops and send them to Nanman. The Fire Dragon Pavilion, led by Jin Taekyung, was one of the few cards the Murim Alliance could play with confidence.
“Hmm.”
None of this eased Jeok Cheongang’s worry. As he silently glared at his cup, Mae Jonghak muttered almost too softly to hear.
“There is one especially reliable source of support.”
“Hm? What was that?”
“Nothing. Just talking to myself.”
“Don’t try to fool me! I heard you say something with these ears!”
“Calm down and finish your drink. Then I’ll think about it.”
Jeok Cheongang stared at him. “Why do you keep trying to make me drink this tasteless wine?”
“Great Hero Jeok.”
“What?”
Mae Jonghak held his gaze. “You’ve already drunk five jars of that tasteless wine.”
“You’re on your sixth.”
“Let’s drink.”
Jeok Cheongang fell silent and raised his cup. The fragrant wine slid down his throat, nowhere near as bitter as he’d claimed. Moonlight touched his face as he tipped his head back.
I wonder where he is down there.
Heartless brat. You could’ve at least shown your face once before leaving.
The words in his heart scattered on a breeze that came from somewhere.
Clip-clop. Clip-clop.
The old horse walked slowly, and the straw packed around my entire body was cold and prickly. Outside the carriage, the voices of hawkers and passersby gradually faded.
Did we make it out?
The thought had barely crossed my mind when someone whispered in my ear.
“Captain. I need to take a shit.”
Hyuk Mujin, you insane bastard. You’re really doing this here?
We needed to move as little as possible, which meant I could not even subdue him by force. I lowered my voice as much as I could and barked, “You lunatic. I told you to go before we left.”
“I’m nervous. That’s why. I’m nervous.”
“Then hold it, you son of a bitch.”
“Why are you swearing at me? I can’t say a thing around you.”
“How am I supposed to not swear? What are we going to do about the smell if you shit in here?”
Even a fart under the same blanket would make me swear. I refused to suffer anything worse while we were buried together in straw.
“I’ve been thinking about that. If I just went, wouldn’t the smell make it easier to get through inspection?”
“Die. Please, just die.”
“I’m sorry. I’ve held it as long as I can, but I don’t think I can hold it anymore. This might be the end for me.”
“Hey, Mujin. Wait. Just wait a second.”
“I’ll accept my punishment later.”
No! You bastard!
I was so terrified I was about to spring up, disguise be damned, when—
“We’ve passed through the center of Luoyang. We’re on an empty mountain road now, so you can come out for a moment.”
“Gasp!”
“Phew!”
Rustle!
Hyuk Mujin burst through the straw and sprinted toward the bushes. Saved at the edge of a cliff, I bowed repeatedly to my savior.
“Thank you. I’ll be a good person. Thank you so much.”
“The inspection must have taken a while for Hyuk Mujin to be that desperate. I’m glad we weren’t too late.”
The voice was familiar. The smiling woman’s face was not.
In the moonlight spilling between the high branches, the freckles across her cheeks and her dry, rough skin stood out.
No matter how many times I look, it’s amazing.
Her features and a few small details had changed, yet the whole impression she gave was different.
Ju Hwaran noticed me staring and touched her face. “Ah, I have changed a little, haven’t I?”
“Yes. But your eyes are still the same.”
A smile flickered in her beautiful dark-blue eyes.
“That isn’t something a disguise mask can alter. If Captain Song hadn’t helped, it would have been difficult to obtain a mask this good on such short notice.”
Song Ilseom, sitting on the driver’s bench, added flatly, “It was nothing. Just a little trick I learned to survive.”
“That’s impressive for a little trick.”
“I assume that’s empty praise, but I’ll thank you for it.”
That bastard has to take everything the wrong way. I meant it.

Song Ilseom had made the mask that turned Ju Hwaran into someone else entirely. I knew he’d started at the bottom and been through all kinds of hardship, but I hadn’t expected him to know how to make disguise masks.
He’s more useful than I thought.
The things he’d learned as a wandering martial artist would surely help us on the road ahead. I was admiring him in spite of myself when a thought made my eyes widen.
“Wait. Why don’t I have one?”
If I had a disguise mask, I wouldn’t have needed to ride like a piece of luggage beside a shit bomb that might go off at any moment.

Song Ilseom clicked his tongue at my protest. “Everyone’s features are different. Just making the mold for a disguise mask takes days. How was I supposed to make yours in the time we had? A poorly fitted mask would only draw more attention. If you’re so upset, you should have learned a disguise technique.”
Hyuk Mujin emerged from the bushes looking thoroughly relieved and joined in.
“Then what about Young Lady Ju? You said it takes days.”
“The Young Bureau Head’s mask...”
Song Ilseom trailed off, then frowned. “What a pointless question. Shut up and get back under the straw. And keep that shit smell out of my face.”
“You shit too. What are you getting on my case for...?”
Song Ilseom glared as Hyuk Mujin grumbled his way back into the straw, then turned to me.
“Can I cut him?”
“No.”
I turned to Ju Hwaran. “The others must be out by now, right?”
She knew whom I meant and gave a small nod. “Probably. They went through the West Gate, where inspections are the weakest. They should have left Luoyang ahead of us.”
Taishan’s size worried me, but Ju Hwaran had planned too carefully to overlook it. Besides, we had the Alliance Leader’s Hall and the Hidden Shadow Pavilion behind us. I could afford to relax.
Rustle.
Hyuk Mujin poked his head out of the straw. “Are we going straight to Mount Daebyeol, then?”
“Of course. We’ll change horses once along the way, but nothing will happen before then.”
Ju Hwaran continued without pause. “If we keep moving, two shichen. With thorough inspections, it could take three shichen. Once we meet the other two at Mount Daebyeol...”
“We leave Henan immediately. Correct?”
She smiled and nodded. “Just as you said, Pavilion Master.”
“...Pavilion Master?”
“Why? Isn’t that the right title?”
Technically, it was. It just felt like a set of clothes that didn’t fit. I smacked my lips and nodded.
“Well, never mind that. We shouldn’t have any problems before Mount Daebyeol, then?”
“Not at all. You could have a good long sleep and wake up before we arrive.”
Henan was the Murim Alliance’s base. An enemy attack here was all but impossible. Still, I let out a quiet laugh, neither agreeing nor disagreeing.
“What is it?”
“Nothing.”
How could I put it? I thought for a moment before going on.
“It just feels strange to think I’ll be dreaming again after so long.”
“Dreaming?”
“Yes. I dream sometimes. I sleep so deeply I wouldn’t notice if someone carried me away.”
Ju Hwaran looked puzzled. Song Ilseom frowned as if I were talking nonsense. Leaving them to it, I burrowed deep into the straw piled in the carriage.
Two shichen to Mount Daebyeol if we’re quick. That’s plenty of time.
It was time to have the dream I’d put off for so long.
Logout.
Ding.
With the clear chime of a bell, my alert consciousness slowly began to sink.

chapters.title: Chapter 552
paragraphs: System Synchronization begins. 10, 9, 8, 7... 1, 0. Synchronization completed successfully. Increased stats have been applied to the body, and use is restricted for certain Titles. Logout complete.
Ding.
Before my blackened vision had even cleared, a cool breeze swept over my entire body, as it always did.
No—it washed through me, cleansing me.
Synchronization.
It was a process I had gone through every time I traveled between Murim and reality.

Changes to my stats took effect immediately, while scars and injuries didn’t carry over. There was even a considerate feature that made changes to my physique and appearance happen gradually and naturally—probably because a sudden transformation would make people suspicious.
Fwoosh.
This time was no different.

Strength flowed into my body, which had already surpassed human limits, and I felt my muscles grow more supple. The internal energy refined through my battle with the Water God Dragon and Mungyeong’s teachings changed with it.
“Phew.”
The first thing I saw was a ceiling without a speck of dust on it. Several meters above me, it was covered by an old-fashioned painting.
Is it because I haven’t seen it in a while? Or am I still not used to it?
I’d last been here before traveling along a tributary of the Yangtze toward Hubei Province. Roughly two months had passed before I returned.
Maybe that was why everything around me felt unfamiliar.
I lay under the soft blankets, staring at the ceiling for a long while. Then I asked, “What was the title of that painting again?”
A quiet answer came from nearby.

“The official title is the Sistine Chapel ceiling frescoes, but in Korea, it’s better known as The Creation—The Genesis. It’s a masterpiece created by Michelangelo Buonarroti, a sculptor and painter of the Renaissance.”
“Ah, Michelangelo. Right.”
“You’ve heard of him?”
“He’s famous. Are you looking down on me because my school grades were Level 7?”
“What do your school grades have to do with it? You’re much more famous than that painting now, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
Tap.
Soft leather slippers met the marble floor.
I turned my head on the pillow and saw a man crossing the vast—no, practically boundless—room.
How does he get more handsome every time I see him?

If he were merely good-looking, I might have been jealous. But once someone passed a certain point, all I could do was admire him. Especially when he had the presence to make those looks seem perfectly natural.
I grinned at the man I was seeing for the first time in two months.
“It’s been a while, Team Leader Choi.”
Team Leader Choi, handsome as ever in a silk robe, stopped in his tracks.
“You say that as though you’ve come back from somewhere far away.”
“I dreamed about a pretty distant place. It was a long dream, too.”
I’d spent more than two months in Murim, so it wasn’t a lie. Considering everything that had happened, two months almost felt too short.
“It must not have been a bad dream.”
“Not really. I had to fight a dragon right at the start.”
“A Dragon?”
“Something a little different, but close.”
“A nightmare, then. Better to wake up quickly from one of those.”
Clink.
Team Leader Choi set the cup he was holding on the bedside table.
“Have some coffee.”
“Is this made from some incredibly expensive beans?”
If it was coffee made from cat shit—or Hyuk Mujin’s shit—like last time, I was going to refuse.
I glared suspiciously at the cup, but then my eyes widened as a familiar scent reached deep into my nose.
“Huh?”
When I looked at him with an expression that said surely not, Team Leader Choi gave a quiet laugh.
“It’s instant. Gold. Made strong.”
“Damn, Team Leader Choi. You know what’s good.”
“At least I know you and coffee brewed from beans aren’t a good match.”
“Good. Ten points to Gryffindor.”
I gave him a thumbs-up and downed the coffee in one gulp.
Mm. That’s the stuff.
Cheap and sweet. Getting a taste of modern civilization again made me feel alive.
“Ah, that’s good. I’m starting to wake up.”
“Are you? You did sleep longer than usual today.”
Like other Awakened and Murim martial artists, I had a body that had surpassed human limits. I needed even less sleep than most.
I rarely slept more than two hours a day, and even that was more to satisfy the desire to sleep than out of any real need.
Unless I’ve pushed my body too hard or worn myself out mentally, I’m fine.
So when someone like me slept like the dead for hours, people were bound to wonder why.
I yawned and stretched.
“Are you all right?” he asked.
“I get days like this sometimes. Maybe all the fatigue caught up with me at once.”
I sat up groggily and reached out. The smartphone on the bedside table flew toward me through Seizing an Object Through Empty Space and snapped into my hand like a magnet.
Maybe it’s because I haven’t seen this in a while, but it feels really strange.
It was part of the disorientation I felt every time I returned to reality.
I tapped the screen awkwardly. The time appeared.
Seven in the morning. I’d gone to bed not long after midnight, so I’d slept about seven hours...
“Hm?”
What was this? The date looked strange.
I stared at the smartphone screen. Then a thought flashed through my mind, and my eyes widened.
“Ah.”
So much had happened that I’d forgotten what day it was—and why I’d waited until after midnight to return to my room.
Just as I remembered, Team Leader Choi spoke.
“I said this last night, but I suppose I should say it again.”
Swish.
He held out his hand, his quiet voice following close behind.
“I look forward to working with you this year as well, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
January 1, 2047.
Right. It was the first day of a new year in the modern world. And...
“Happy birthday.”
It was also my twenty-eighth birthday.
Damn it. Already?
The number thirty loomed so close that my vision went dark. Then two people burst in from across the room, making a racket.
“Hey, Twenty-Eight! Mom says to come eat seaweed soup!”
“I hereby congratulate you on the day of your birth!”
I take it back. They weren’t people. They were two monsters.
Jin Hayeon, my old enemy on the family register, whom I was seeing for the first time in a while—and the blond foreigner beside her, the Skeleton King.
I sighed at the sight of them.
The time difference between Murim and the modern world was enormous.
From what I’d learned, whenever I crossed into one world, time in the other slowed to a crawl. Ten days in Murim amounted to about an hour in the modern world. No wonder I sometimes felt out of step.
Especially this time. So much happened.
Both worlds had changed rapidly. One of the changes was the enormous mansion where I now lived.
Step. Step.
White marble gleamed beneath our feet, and old-fashioned paintings and statues filled the halls.
More than anything, though...
“Wow. This place is ridiculously huge.”
Huge enough to leave me speechless. Even if I put together every place I’d stayed while traveling between the two worlds, the total would be nothing next to this mansion.
Its owner didn’t seem to agree.
“As you said, Mr. Jin Taekyung, it is somewhat large. It also takes a lot of work to maintain.”
“For a place that takes so much work, I don’t see anyone else around. Right, old man?”
Hayeon, who’d been trailing behind us, had suddenly joined the conversation.
She wasn’t talking to Team Leader Choi.
The foreigner with hair like molten gold and strangely gleaming golden eyes frowned. At a glance, he looked like the sort of man who’d be caught up in Hollywood dating scandals.
“Surely you don’t mean me.”
“I do.”
“Hah.”
The Skeleton King—given a human appearance by Magic Johnson’s illusion magic—let out a short laugh.
“You seem to misunderstand. As I understand it, the term you used refers to a male relative of an older generation, or a middle-aged man.”
“Yes.”
The Skeleton King was silent for a moment before squeezing out his voice.
“What I mean is...”
“You said you’re over thirty. That makes you an old man to me.”
“I am over thirty, but...”
“Oh, I get it. You are an old man. You just don’t want to be called one, right?”
His golden eyes trembled. He stopped walking and glared at Hayeon.
“They say blood relatives resemble each other. You two really are siblings.”
Hayeon and I answered together.
“I’m an only child.”
“I’m an only child, old man.”
Good heavens. Now there were two wicked humans.
That was written all over his face as he looked from one of us to the other. Finally, he shook his head in defeat.
“All right. All right, so stop it, both of you. And you, insolent human girl. If you ever call me an old man again...”
Step.
He never finished.
Hayeon had stopped walking. She was staring at him blankly.
“What did you say?”
“No. That isn’t what I meant. I misspoke.”
The Skeleton King scrambled to take it back, glancing at me. Team Leader Choi sighed as though he’d been expecting this to happen sooner or later.
“You’ve done it now. I’ll take him away, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Please calm your sister down, and be careful she doesn’t misunderstand.”
What was he talking about?
I blinked at him.
“Why?”
“Pardon?”
“No, why? Why do I have to calm her down?”
“Why? Miss Hayeon was just insulted—”
Before he could finish, Hayeon spoke.
“‘Insolent human girl’? Is that something you say to a person, you long-nosed bastard?”
“...What?”
Here we go. I smiled warmly.
She hasn’t changed a bit.
Yes. This was Jin Hayeon.
As my capillaries swelled magnificently, I finally felt that I had truly returned to the modern world.
Hayeon whipped around to face me.
“Did you hear what that Yankee bastard just said?”
I nodded silently.
“I heard.”
“Does he have dirt on you? Did someone catch you doing a private webcam show? Why else would you hang around with a bastard like that? Someone who isn’t even human...”
That’s surprisingly accurate.
“Oh, right,” I said, impressed. “He really isn’t human.”
“He called me an insolent human girl. Does that psycho think that even counts as words?”
“Well, they are words. Just bad ones.”
“If he’d called me a crazy bitch or something normal, I wouldn’t even complain. But human girl? It feels so gross. Seriously.”
I took out my smartphone and whispered, “Siri, tell me today’s weather.”
“Today’s weather is clear.”
“You asshole. You think I’m in the mood for wordplay? Your one and only little sister just got called that by someone else!”
I hurriedly straightened my clothes and bowed politely.
“Hello. My name is Jin Taekyung, and I’m an only child.”
“You really are a lunatic.”
“That’s rather harsh for a first meeting. I’ll sue you for defamation by stating facts.”
Hayeon’s eyes turned cold.
“I’m telling Mom everything.”
“What?”
“I’m telling Mom. Every last thing.”
“Are you threatening me?”
“Yep.”
“You little...”
Wham!
Eyes bulging, I grabbed someone by the collar with all my strength.
Not Hayeon’s, of course. The Skeleton King’s.
“Apologize to my sister right now! You less-than-human bastard! You monster!”
“I-I’m sorry! I was wrong! I’ll apologize a hundred times, just please...!”
“Of course she’s insolent! And human! And a girl! But you can’t put all three together like that!”
“Ugh! Grrrgh!”
“Say it properly! Put the right words together!”
“I-Insolent! Person! Girl!”
Boom.
At least, I thought I heard something like that.
It was Hayeon’s anger gauge bursting. She picked up the nearest plaster statue.
“Die. Just die, both of you!”
Whoosh! Clang!
The hallway descended into chaos, beginning with the daily clang.
Hayeon charged at us like a brave Viking warrior, while Team Leader Choi stared at the scene unfolding before him in stunned disbelief.
That was when—
“I told you to come eat. What’s all this noise...!”
The elevator at the far end of the hallway opened. A familiar face emerged and froze.
Dear Lady Kim Jeonghee.
My mother.
“...What are you doing, all of you?”
From her tiny body—not even 160 centimeters tall—I felt an aura to rival at least one of the Ten Kings.

Before my blackened vision had even cleared, a cool breeze swept over my entire body, as it always did.

The internal energy refined through my battle with the Water God Dragon and Mungyeong’s teachings changed with it.

Then I asked, “What was the title of that painting again?”

Tap.

I turned my head on the pillow and saw a man crossing the vast—no, practically boundless—room.
How does he get more handsome every time I see him?
If he were merely good-looking, I might have been jealous.
But once someone passed a certain point, all I could do was admire him.
Especially when he had the presence to make those looks seem perfectly natural.
I grinned at the man I was seeing for the first time in two months.

“I dreamed about a pretty distant place.

I’d spent more than two months in Murim, so it wasn’t a lie.
Considering everything that had happened, two months almost felt too short.
“It must not have been a bad dream.”
“Not really.
I had to fight a dragon right at the start.”
“A Dragon?”
“Something a little different, but close.”
“A nightmare, then.
Better to wake up quickly from one of those.”
Clink.
Team Leader Choi set the cup he was holding on the bedside table.
“Have some coffee.”
“Is this made from some incredibly expensive beans?”
If it was coffee made from cat shit—or Hyuk Mujin’s shit—like last time, I was going to refuse.
I glared suspiciously at the cup, but then my eyes widened as a familiar scent reached deep into my nose.
“Huh?”
When I looked at him with an expression that said surely not, Team Leader Choi gave a quiet laugh.
“It’s instant.
Gold.
Made strong.”
“Damn, Team Leader Choi.
You know what’s good.”
“At least I know you and coffee brewed from beans aren’t a good match.”
“Good.
Ten points to Gryffindor.”
I gave him a thumbs-up and downed the coffee in one gulp.
Mm.
That’s the stuff.
Cheap and sweet.
Getting a taste of modern civilization again made me feel alive.
“Ah, that’s good.
I’m starting to wake up.”
“Are you?
You did sleep longer than usual today.”
Like other Awakened and Murim martial artists, I had a body that had surpassed human limits.
I needed even less sleep than most.
I rarely slept more than two hours a day, and even that was more to satisfy the desire to sleep than out of any real need.
Unless I’ve pushed my body too hard or worn myself out mentally, I’m fine.
So when someone like me slept like the dead for hours, people were bound to wonder why.
I yawned and stretched.
“Are you all right?” he asked.
“I get days like this sometimes.
Maybe all the fatigue caught up with me at once.”
I sat up groggily and reached out.
The smartphone on the bedside table flew toward me through Seizing an Object Through Empty Space and snapped into my hand like a magnet.
Maybe it’s because I haven’t seen this in a while, but it feels really strange.
It was part of the disorientation I felt every time I returned to reality.
I tapped the screen awkwardly.
The time appeared.
Seven in the morning.
I’d gone to bed not long after midnight, so I’d slept about seven hours...
“Hm?”
What was this?
The date looked strange.
I stared at the smartphone screen.

So much had happened that I’d forgotten what day it was—and why I’d waited until after midnight to return to my room.

Swish.

Jin Taekyung.”
January 1, 2047.
Right.
It was the first day of a new year in the modern world.
And...

It was also my twenty-eighth birthday.
Damn it.
Already?

chapters.title: Chapter 553
paragraphs: No matter how many levels I gained or how high I raised my stats, one fact would never change: to one person, I was still her immature little boy.
And... my mother, dear Lady Kim Jeonghee, had attack power that ignored every defense.
“What are you two doing?”
One hand was clenched into a fist. The other held a ladle. Sensing that things were getting serious, I spoke quickly.
“Lady Kim. You may have forgotten, but it’s your son’s birthday today.”
“So?”
“I’m almost thirty. Wouldn’t hitting me in front of other people be a little embarrassing?”
“I’ll be sixty before you know it.”
“Ah. Right...”
Wrong approach. I acknowledged my mistake deep in my heart and changed tack.
“Two months—no, not that long ago, I was fighting monsters for my life.”
“Thank goodness you came back safely, son.”
“Thank you, Mother.”
“Then why do you keep fighting with your little sister, who’s eight years younger than you, instead of a monster?”
“Mother. I don’t fight people. Therefore, that thing isn’t my little sister. It’s a monster.”
“Then you’re saying I gave birth to a monster.”
“My palm or my ladle—which would you prefer?”
Checkmate. Realizing there was no escape, I closed my eyes and answered quietly.
“Your palm.”
“Forearm? Back?”
“I’ll take the back.”
I considered my answer carefully. The punishment came immediately.
“Mom told you—”
Smack!
“Not to fight!”
Smack!
“Didn’t I?”
Smack!
“Eek!”
“Ugh!”
Good heavens. Was that the Flame Divine Palm?
Pain bored into my back, and Hayeon and I screamed.
Even the perfect body known in Murim as the Heavenly Martial Physique was useless now. This fear—and this pain—were engraved on my soul.
I can’t dodge, either.
If I did, she would apply the crime of insolence and trigger a tenfold event.

In the end, Hayeon and I weren’t released until Mom had stamped her handprints on our backs. Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King stared at Lady Kim as she turned away, breathing hard. Their eyes were practically shaking.
“Y-Your mother. I was trying to stop them.”
“I am American. Citizen of the United States. Do not touch me. Please.”
Their desperate attempts to survive were almost pitiful.
Of course, Lady Kim gave them a warm smile as though nothing had happened.
“Oh, my children were making trouble, weren’t they? I’m sorry. Neither of them has grown up yet. I’m making breakfast, so come eat with us.”
“Th-Thank you.”
“Thank you. Thank you, Jeonghee.”
What the hell, you son of a bitch?
I could let the rest go, but the Skeleton King was dead for that “Thank you, Jeonghee.”
I promised him murder with a look, then headed toward the dining room.
The mansion was enormous, so the distance to the dining room was considerable. But the elevator installed inside the house and the short-range Teleport magic circles made the journey quick.
Wait. Now that I thought about it, this was ridiculous. Why was there a Teleport magic circle inside a mansion?
I stared at Team Leader Choi in disbelief. He answered calmly.
“The mansion is quite large. As I understand it, they were installed to reduce travel time.”
“...Right. That’s what Teleport magic circles are for. Obviously.”
He might as well have said, People eat to fill their stomachs.
Then again, perhaps all of this really was normal to Team Leader Choi.
He certainly didn’t grow up in an ordinary family.

Even a third-generation Korean chaebol heir or the youngest son of a famed swordsmanship family would have to defer to him. His maternal grandfather was the immortal hero who had defeated the Demon King Asmodeus in the final battle and saved humanity.
Cheon Taemin.
If the birth of a prophet had divided an era into before and after, Cheon Taemin had decided the fate of humanity.
Tens of millions had seen him. Hundreds of millions remembered him. The vast records of his existence would remain through countless ages, until the day humanity itself came to an end.
And that very Cheon Taemin once lived in this mansion.
Even Team Leader Choi, his maternal grandson, did not know where he was or whether he was alive. But putting that aside, the thought was moving in its own way.
I was only staying here temporarily because the press wouldn’t leave me alone, but it felt as though I was sharing a space with the immortal hero Cheon Taemin.
This is incredible.
I looked around the mansion, where immensely valuable A-rank Magic Gems had been slotted in like batteries to provide a constant supply of energy, and drew in a deep breath.
“Hoooh.”
Team Leader Choi gave me an uneasy look.
“...What are you doing?”
“Should I say I’m absorbing the energy? Or that I’m sensing the scent of a hero?”
Hayeon rubbed her sore back and muttered, “He’s just a pervert. He has a smell fetish.”
“Would you be quiet, insolent human girl?”
“Oh, really? Mom—mmph!”
“If you don’t want to get murdered tonight, keep your mouth shut.”
I was almost thirty. I didn’t want to get hit in front of other people again.
Fortunately, someone appeared just before Lady Kim, sensing that something was amiss, turned around.
“Good morning.”
A smooth, low voice that sounded like a coffee commercial had started playing. Even at this early hour, his pompadour was immaculate, and his tailored suit was neat and dignified.
Butler Kim approached at an unhurried pace and bowed first to Team Leader Choi.
“Did you sleep well, Young Master?”
Team Leader Choi nodded as though this were perfectly ordinary.
“Yes. I went to bed a little late because I had a few things to take care of, but I’m feeling fine.”
“The proposal from Mr. Johnson, I presume.”
“A few terms in our agreement with the Wizard Guild need adjusting. I’ve put the details together, so...”
Hayeon, listening to them, muttered, “Is this a scene from a TV drama or what?”
“Not a drama. If anything, it’s a web novel.”
A webtoon, maybe. Turning this kind of fantasy into a TV drama would cost a fortune.
“Just let it go. You’ll get used to it if you watch long enough.”
“To that?”
“...At least try.”
Honestly, it still threw me every time.

Barely six months ago in modern-world time, I’d been an F-rank Hunter getting by on blood sausage gukbap and cup noodles. Now the media hailed me as the new hero following in Cheon Taemin’s footsteps, and an S-rank Hunter license made from specially processed top-grade Magic Gems sat in the old leather wallet I still hadn’t replaced.
I should be getting used to this by now, but somehow it isn’t happening.

Maybe I still had too much to do. Keeping up with one crisis after another while rushing between the modern world and Murim was hard enough. Perhaps it would be stranger if I could settle in and enjoy the wealth and fame I’d been given.
“We can discuss the details after breakfast, Young Master.”
“Ah, yes. Let’s do that.”
Their brief conversation ended, and I followed Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim into the dining room.
No, dining room didn’t do it justice. Banquet hall was closer.
It was enormous, spotless, and elegant. Robots equipped with advanced AI waited at their assigned positions.
Yet in this room, where every detail had been prepared with meticulous care, one thing wasn’t ready.
“Hmm.”
“Just as I thought.”
Everyone except Hayeon and me blinked. The Skeleton King sounded genuinely confused when he whispered to me.
“Wicked human. May I ask you something?”
“Go ahead.”
“We were told to eat. Why, then, is there nothing on the table?”
The enormous table in the center of the banquet hall was completely empty. No dishes, no food—nothing but a perfect blank slate.
I had already guessed the reason, so I quietly nodded.
“That’s how it works.”
“What?”
“An absolute rule. Or a species-wide habit. Something like that.”

When Mom called us to eat, it meant she was still making the food. Whether she called once or ten times, yelling that everything was ready and we needed to come out right now, the result was the same when we got there.
Hayeon knew it too. She was already looking for the utensils.
“Sorry, where do you keep the spoons and chopsticks?”
“Pardon?”
“Spoons and chopsticks.”
Team Leader Choi blinked, then turned slowly toward Butler Kim.
“Butler Kim?”
At that moment, a single stray hair stuck out from Butler Kim’s perfectly arranged pompadour.
“Those functions are all integrated into the robots’ circuits, so they should bring everything automatically... But why aren’t the robots moving?”
Just then, Lady Kim peeked her head out from the kitchen. She had rushed there earlier with a ladle in hand, saying that the soup was boiling.
“Oh, I turned them all off.”
“What?”
“Pardon?”
“I already feel bad imposing on you. It seemed a waste of electricity. The kids can set things out in no time, so please, have a seat.”
There was no way Lady Kim would hear that every robot in the mansion ran on embedded Magic Gems rather than electricity, or that there was no need to save money on the electric bill.
She was a veteran homemaker who had spent her life scrimping and scraping to raise two children.
As everyone stared at me, speechless, I merely smacked my lips.
“Just accept it. I’ve tried explaining it more than once or twice, but it never gets through.”
She’d even saved every bit of the money I sent home, saying she couldn’t possibly spend it.
Remembering her old days working in a restaurant kitchen, I smiled bitterly, then smacked the Skeleton King on the back of the head.
Whack!
“Why me...?”
“What are you doing, asshole? Go help.”
“Wicked human. This is unfair. And un-American!”
“Then go to America. The moment you arrive, they’ll find out you’re a monster and drag you off to the Octagon.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me in bewilderment.
“It’s the Pentagon, Mr. Jin Taekyung...”
“Octagon, Pentagon—whatever. You and Butler Kim go help too.”
“Pardon?”
“We’re eating together. We should all help get it ready.”
Team Leader Choi’s gaze wavered.
“Eating... together?”
“You heard me. Go set out the utensils. I’ll be watching to make sure you do it properly.”
His gaze steadied again.
“Watching?”
“Yes.”
“And what about you, Mr. Jin Taekyung? Aren’t you doing anything?”
“It’s my birthday. Even at the Hunter training camp, they gave people free time on their birthdays.”
“What are you waiting for? We need to be ready before the seaweed soup comes out.”
His parents had died, his grandfather Cheon Taemin had disappeared, and Lee Jungryong had shut him out afterward. But Team Leader Choi was still the Young Master of a wealthy household.
This must have been something he had never experienced in his life.
I let out a quiet laugh as he walked away with Butler Kim, wearing a dazed expression I’d never seen on him before. Then I sat down and pulled out my smartphone.
Nothing beats the news when you need to figure out what’s going on.
Tap. Tap-tap.
A few touches took me to a large online community open only to Hunters. I found an article posted just ten minutes earlier, and my hand stopped.

Former Ares Guild Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong, 68: National funeral scheduled for tomorrow. Where is the immortal hero Cheon Taemin? Amid global attention, Ares Guild members remaining in Sichuan Province depart the country. Interest from around the world turns to Hunter Go Jun, the late Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security...
“Go Jun.”

sentences.text: No matter how many levels I gained or how high I raised my stats, one fact would never change: to one person, I was still her immature little boy.
And... my mother, dear Lady Kim Jeonghee, had attack power that ignored every defense.
“What are you two doing?”
One hand was clenched into a fist.
The other held a ladle.
Sensing that things were getting serious, I spoke quickly.
“Lady Kim.
You may have forgotten, but it’s your son’s birthday today.”
“So?”
“I’m almost thirty.
Wouldn’t hitting me in front of other people be a little embarrassing?”
“I’ll be sixty before you know it.”
“Ah.
Right...”
Wrong approach.
I acknowledged my mistake deep in my heart and changed tack.
“Two months—no, not that long ago, I was fighting monsters for my life.”
“Thank goodness you came back safely, son.”
“Thank you, Mother.”
“Then why do you keep fighting with your little sister, who’s eight years younger than you, instead of a monster?”
“Mother.
I don’t fight people.
Therefore, that thing isn’t my little sister.
It’s a monster.”
“Then you’re saying I gave birth to a monster.”
“My palm or my ladle—which would you prefer?”
Checkmate.
Realizing there was no escape, I closed my eyes and answered quietly.
“Your palm.”
“Forearm?
Back?”
“I’ll take the back.”
I considered my answer carefully.
The punishment came immediately.
“Mom told you—”
Smack!
“Not to fight!”
Smack!
“Didn’t I?”
Smack!
“Eek!”
“Ugh!”
Good heavens.
Was that the Flame Divine Palm?
Pain bored into my back, and Hayeon and I screamed.
Even the perfect body known in Murim as the Heavenly Martial Physique was useless now.
This fear—and this pain—were engraved on my soul.
I can’t dodge, either.
If I did, she would apply the crime of insolence and trigger a tenfold event.
In the end, Hayeon and I weren’t released until Mom had stamped her handprints on our backs.
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King stared at Lady Kim as she turned away, breathing hard.
Their eyes were practically shaking.
“Y-Your mother.
I was trying to stop them.”
“I am American.
Citizen of the United States.
Do not touch me.
Please.”
Their desperate attempts to survive were almost pitiful.
Of course, Lady Kim gave them a warm smile as though nothing had happened.
“Oh, my children were making trouble, weren’t they?
I’m sorry.
Neither of them has grown up yet.
I’m making breakfast, so come eat with us.”
“Th-Thank you.”
“Thank you.
Thank you, Jeonghee.”
What the hell, you son of a bitch?
I could let the rest go, but the Skeleton King was dead for that “Thank you, Jeonghee.”
I promised him murder with a look, then headed toward the dining room.
The mansion was enormous, so the distance to the dining room was considerable.
But the elevator installed inside the house and the short-range Teleport magic circles made the journey quick.
Wait.
Now that I thought about it, this was ridiculous.
Why was there a Teleport magic circle inside a mansion?
I stared at Team Leader Choi in disbelief.
He answered calmly.
“The mansion is quite large.
As I understand it, they were installed to reduce travel time.”
“...Right.
That’s what Teleport magic circles are for.
Obviously.”
He might as well have said, People eat to fill their stomachs.
Then again, perhaps all of this really was normal to Team Leader Choi.
He certainly didn’t grow up in an ordinary family.
Even a third-generation Korean chaebol heir or the youngest son of a famed swordsmanship family would have to defer to him.
His maternal grandfather was the immortal hero who had defeated the Demon King Asmodeus in the final battle and saved humanity.
Cheon Taemin.
If the birth of a prophet had divided an era into before and after, Cheon Taemin had decided the fate of humanity.
Tens of millions had seen him.
Hundreds of millions remembered him.
The vast records of his existence would remain through countless ages, until the day humanity itself came to an end.
And that very Cheon Taemin once lived in this mansion.
Even Team Leader Choi, his maternal grandson, did not know where he was or whether he was alive.
But putting that aside, the thought was moving in its own way.
I was only staying here temporarily because the press wouldn’t leave me alone, but it felt as though I was sharing a space with the immortal hero Cheon Taemin.
This is incredible.
I looked around the mansion, where immensely valuable A-rank Magic Gems had been slotted in like batteries to provide a constant supply of energy, and drew in a deep breath.
“Hoooh.”
Team Leader Choi gave me an uneasy look.
“...What are you doing?”
“Should I say I’m absorbing the energy?
Or that I’m sensing the scent of a hero?”
Hayeon rubbed her sore back and muttered, “He’s just a pervert.
He has a smell fetish.”
“Would you be quiet, insolent human girl?”
“Oh, really?
Mom—mmph!”
“If you don’t want to get murdered tonight, keep your mouth shut.”
I was almost thirty.
I didn’t want to get hit in front of other people again.
Fortunately, someone appeared just before Lady Kim, sensing that something was amiss, turned around.
“Good morning.”
A smooth, low voice that sounded like a coffee commercial had started playing.
Even at this early hour, his pompadour was immaculate, and his tailored suit was neat and dignified.
Butler Kim approached at an unhurried pace and bowed first to Team Leader Choi.
“Did you sleep well, Young Master?”
Team Leader Choi nodded as though this were perfectly ordinary.
“Yes.
I went to bed a little late because I had a few things to take care of, but I’m feeling fine.”
“The proposal from Mr.
Johnson, I presume.”
“A few terms in our agreement with the Wizard Guild need adjusting.
I’ve put the details together, so...”
Hayeon, listening to them, muttered, “Is this a scene from a TV drama or what?”
“Not a drama.
If anything, it’s a web novel.”
A webtoon, maybe.
Turning this kind of fantasy into a TV drama would cost a fortune.
“Just let it go.
You’ll get used to it if you watch long enough.”
“To that?”
“...At least try.”
Honestly, it still threw me every time.
Barely six months ago in modern-world time, I’d been an F-rank Hunter getting by on blood sausage gukbap and cup noodles.

Now the media hailed me as the new hero following in Cheon Taemin’s footsteps, and an S-rank Hunter license made from specially processed top-grade Magic Gems sat in the old leather wallet I still hadn’t replaced.
I should be getting used to this by now, but somehow it isn’t happening.
Maybe I still had too much to do.
Keeping up with one crisis after another while rushing between the modern world and Murim was hard enough.
Perhaps it would be stranger if I could settle in and enjoy the wealth and fame I’d been given.
“We can discuss the details after breakfast, Young Master.”
“Ah, yes.
Let’s do that.”
Their brief conversation ended, and I followed Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim into the dining room.
No, dining room didn’t do it justice.
Banquet hall was closer.
It was enormous, spotless, and elegant.
Robots equipped with advanced AI waited at their assigned positions.
Yet in this room, where every detail had been prepared with meticulous care, one thing wasn’t ready.
“Hmm.”
“Just as I thought.”
Everyone except Hayeon and me blinked.
The Skeleton King sounded genuinely confused when he whispered to me.
“Wicked human.
May I ask you something?”
“Go ahead.”
“We were told to eat.
Why, then, is there nothing on the table?”
The enormous table in the center of the banquet hall was completely empty.
No dishes, no food—nothing but a perfect blank slate.
I had already guessed the reason, so I quietly nodded.
“That’s how it works.”
“What?”
“An absolute rule.
Or a species-wide habit.
Something like that.”
When Mom called us to eat, it meant she was still making the food.
Whether she called once or ten times, yelling that everything was ready and we needed to come out right now, the result was the same when we got there.
Hayeon knew it too.
She was already looking for the utensils.
“Sorry, where do you keep the spoons and chopsticks?”
“Pardon?”
“Spoons and chopsticks.”
Team Leader Choi blinked, then turned slowly toward Butler Kim.
“Butler Kim?”
At that moment, a single stray hair stuck out from Butler Kim’s perfectly arranged pompadour.
“Those functions are all integrated into the robots’ circuits, so they should bring everything automatically...
But why aren’t the robots moving?”
Just then, Lady Kim peeked her head out from the kitchen.
She had rushed there earlier with a ladle in hand, saying that the soup was boiling.
“Oh, I turned them all off.”
“What?”
“Pardon?”
“I already feel bad imposing on you.
It seemed a waste of electricity.
The kids can set things out in no time, so please, have a seat.”
There was no way Lady Kim would hear that every robot in the mansion ran on embedded Magic Gems rather than electricity, or that there was no need to save money on the electric bill.
She was a veteran homemaker who had spent her life scrimping and scraping to raise two children.
As everyone stared at me, speechless, I merely smacked my lips.
“Just accept it.
I’ve tried explaining it more than once or twice, but it never gets through.”
She’d even saved every bit of the money I sent home, saying she couldn’t possibly spend it.
Remembering her old days working in a restaurant kitchen, I smiled bitterly, then smacked the Skeleton King on the back of the head.
Whack!
“Why me...?”
“What are you doing, asshole?
Go help.”
“Wicked human.
This is unfair.
And un-American!”
“Then go to America.
The moment you arrive, they’ll find out you’re a monster and drag you off to the Octagon.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me in bewilderment.
“It’s the Pentagon, Mr.
Jin Taekyung...”
“Octagon, Pentagon—whatever.
You and Butler Kim go help too.”
“Pardon?”
“We’re eating together.
We should all help get it ready.”
Team Leader Choi’s gaze wavered.
“Eating... together?”
“You heard me.
Go set out the utensils.
I’ll be watching to make sure you do it properly.”
His gaze steadied again.
“Watching?”
“Yes.”
“And what about you, Mr.
Jin Taekyung?
Aren’t you doing anything?”
“It’s my birthday.
Even at the Hunter training camp, they gave people free time on their birthdays.”
“What are you waiting for?
We need to be ready before the seaweed soup comes out.”
His parents had died, his grandfather Cheon Taemin had disappeared, and Lee Jungryong had shut him out afterward.
But Team Leader Choi was still the Young Master of a wealthy household.
This must have been something he had never experienced in his life.
I let out a quiet laugh as he walked away with Butler Kim, wearing a dazed expression I’d never seen on him before.
Then I sat down and pulled out my smartphone.
Nothing beats the news when you need to figure out what’s going on.
Tap.
Tap-tap.
A few touches took me to a large online community open only to Hunters.
I found an article posted just ten minutes earlier, and my hand stopped.
Former Ares Guild Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong, 68: National funeral scheduled for tomorrow.
Where is the immortal hero Cheon Taemin?
Amid global attention, Ares Guild members remaining in Sichuan Province depart the country.
Interest from around the world turns to Hunter Go Jun, the late Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security...
“Go Jun.”
Right.
That guy was still around.

chapters.title: Chapter 554
paragraphs: The monster wave in Sichuan Province, dubbed the Small Cataclysm, had devoured so much.
Buildings, people, hope... More than four million people were dead or injured, and property damage ran into the hundreds of trillions of won.
But as someone once said, people leave their names behind when they die. Among the countless dead, a few names stood out.
[Search Efforts Exhausted, but the Hero’s Remains Were Never Found]
[Who Was the Late Lee Jungryong?]
[The Immortal Hero Cheon Taemin Always Had One Person at His Side]
[Wu Heixing and Lee Jungryong: Their Deaths Were the Same, but Their Nobility Was Not]
[Late Lee Jungryong to Receive National Funeral... Waves of Mourning Pour In from Around the World]
Every article occupying the top of the major forum sites contained the same person’s name.
Lee Jungryong. Another hero of the Great Cataclysm, who had wielded full authority over the Ares Guild in place of the vanished Cheon Taemin.
No. A hero of the past now, I suppose.
Lee Jungryong was dead.
The world had been told that the Lich killed him, but I was the one who had ended his life.
Yes. That day.
I had broken Wu Heixing’s neck while he begged me to spare him, then driven the blade of my spear into Lee Jungryong’s chest and reduced him to ash.
There had been no other choice. I’d gone with them all the way to the Lich’s stronghold despite suspecting they might stab me in the back. That was the last chance I’d given them.
Last meant there wouldn’t be another.
Even if it hadn’t happened then, I would have killed him eventually.
If Wu Heixing had been like a fish bone stuck in my throat, Lee Jungryong had been a blade digging into it.

He was as strong as a beast of prey and as cunning as a fox. When I first met him, he had seemed like a wall I could never overcome. I’d brought him down only because I’d grown far faster than he thought possible.
If Lee Jungryong had been a little bolder, things might have turned out differently...
But he had misjudged me, and here was the result: me, reading about his death on my smartphone on the first day of the new year.
His final words flashed through my mind.
“I... have no regrets. None.”
Lee Jungryong had been smiling when he said them.
His entire body was drenched in blood and battered beyond recognition, yet as he smiled brightly, his eyes burned with the obsession and fury he had refused to let go of until the very end.
As if this wasn’t over. As if he’d become a vengeful spirit and haunt me even after death.
Well, he couldn’t haunt me now that he was dead. But on one point, I agreed with him: it wasn’t over.
There was still someone in this world who was practically another Lee Jungryong.
Go Jun.
Lee Jungryong’s blindly devoted Head of Security. No—his Disciple.
I stared down at my smartphone and tapped an article.
Tap.
An image filled the screen at once. It showed Ares Guild members departing Sichuan Province, with Go Jun among them, his face set and rigid.
[Ares Guild Heads Home for the Funeral of the Late Lee Jungryong]
[Who Is Go Jun, Head of Security for the Late Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong?]
I read the bold headlines and scrolled down to the long stream of comments.

└ May the deceased rest in peace. └ Lee Jungryong is dead... Another great star has fallen. └ I don’t know whether Jun Dragon was a good person. I heard some pretty suspicious stories about him, too. └ I agree, but those stories are still unverified rumors. And you think a dinosaur of a Guild like Ares could operate without getting a little dirty? Just shut up, press X, and pay your respects. Considering what Lee Jungryong did during the Great Cataclysm, it’s the least you can do. └ But who’s Go Jun? They say he was Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security, but I’ve never seen him before. └ People who know, know. You’re either not a Hunter or you’re still new. └ How did you know? I spent all my time stuck in a study room, then awakened by accident. Now I don’t know anything. If you know something, tell me. └ Actually, I don’t know either. This is my older brother’s account. └ You fucking bastard. └ Waaah. I’m a baby fucking bastard. └ What a shitshow up there. Hunters with some standing or experience probably know him, though. Go Jun is famous as Jun Dragon’s right-hand man. He appeared out of nowhere about ten years ago and caused quite a stir. After that, Jun Dragon always brought him to official events. └ Seriously. I just searched iTube, and he was standing behind Lee Jungryong at last year’s UN General Assembly. That was from a quick search. If someone really dug, they’d probably find tons more. └ Think Lee Jungryong raised him as a Disciple? └ King-sized possibility. Other communities are already digging into Go Jun’s background. Apparently, he came from a children’s home—orphanage?—that Lee Jungryong sponsored. He’s never taken the ranker test, but they say he’s stronger than the highest-ranked rankers. └ So is he Ares Guild’s next Vice Guild Master? └ No one knows, but he’s probably the front-runner. Unless Cheon Taemin shows up, Go Jun will likely take over without much trouble. Strength plus legitimacy. That’s a pure enough bloodline to make Voldemort shed a tear. └ Agreed. He looks like a Death Eater, too. Probably a Slytherin. └ Keep attacking his looks and Ares Guild might attack you. └ Speaking of pure bloodlines, I heard something weird recently. └ ? └ ?? └ What? └ I’m too scared to say exactly who, but you know. Someone in the P— Guild is Cheon Taemin’s—no, not Cheon Taemin. I’m deleting this myself. Please don’t bring it up. └ Ah, fuck. └ There are two ways to make someone angry. The first is to start saying something and then stop. └ Ha... Some bastard just cost me a night’s sleep.
Clink.
The sudden noise drew my eyes from the phone.
Team Leader Choi had set the tableware down beside me. He looked faintly displeased.
“What are you reading so intently?”
“Something about you in the article comments, Team Leader Choi.”
“Pardon?”
“It’d be quicker to show you. Just a moment.”
I looked back at my phone and smacked my lips. The comment had been deleted in the brief time I’d looked away.
He said he was scared and would delete it. He really did delete it and run.
“What comment?”
“It’s gone now. But it was definitely about you.”
“If it was about me... was it related to my maternal grandfather?”
I gave a small nod.

I wasn’t the only one who’d drawn attention during the Small Cataclysm in Sichuan Province. While the world was in an uproar over the monster wave caused by the Lich, the media and the public had barely stopped talking about me. But at some point, word of Team Leader Choi had begun to spread as well.
A needle in a bag.

That was Team Leader Choi. He’d learned martial arts from me and taken his skills to another level, then distinguished himself on the battlefield. He was also handsome enough to put a celebrity to shame. The attention from people who cared about looks alone was nothing to sneeze at.
And he was Cheon Taemin’s only living blood relative.
But Lee Jungryong had kept Team Leader Choi’s existence under wraps while he was alive. Team Leader Choi had done the same.
Until then, the two of them had been a dinosaur and an ant. Even if revealing his identity turned him into a golden ant, he would still be an ant.
Now Lee Jungryong was dead, and the truth they’d hidden—whether by choice or circumstance—was slowly coming to light.
What bothered me was how natural it all seemed. How perfectly timed.
I gazed steadily at Team Leader Choi.
“This was what you intended, wasn’t it, Team Leader Choi?”
“To be honest, yes. I judged that now was the right time.”
“Wow. I didn’t expect you to admit it. Have you always been this honest?”
“What else do I have to hide from you, Mr. Jin Taekyung? Of course, even if I’m honest with you, you still have plenty of secrets.”
“...You didn’t have to put it like that.”
A twinge of guilt caught me off guard.

I already knew Team Leader Choi suspected there was more to me than he’d been told. Since getting the System, I’d spent more time with him than with anyone else in the modern world, and I’d heard him say as much himself.
Still, when he came right out with it, I had no answer.
I scratched my chin awkwardly.
“Putting that aside, can I ask you a few things?”
“Go ahead. The seaweed soup will be out soon, so you’ll have to be quick.”
“If this was your plan, wouldn’t it have been better for me to tell everyone what Lee Jungryong was really like?”
Lee Jungryong’s and Wu Heixing’s deaths had been blamed on the Lich. The truth had been buried, which was why people were mourning them with some goodwill.

Wu Heixing had always been a rotten bastard, and the atrocities involving his family had come to light, so people were still cursing him after his death. Lee Jungryong, on the other hand, was being mourned as a fallen great star.
They were giving him a national funeral. That said it all.
If the truth had come out, things would have been different. I might not have had hard evidence, but I’d earned enough Fame as a new hero that people couldn’t simply dismiss my testimony as nonsense.
Lee Jungryong’s reputation would have been ruined, and Team Leader Choi’s plan would have gone smoothly.
“But you told me not to tell the media what Lee Jungryong had done.”
Team Leader Choi nodded calmly.
“Yes, I did.”
“Why?”
His answer came without a moment’s hesitation.
“Because I didn’t want to dirty what’s mine.”
“What?”

“Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong was certainly a man with an ugly side. He helped my maternal grandfather and made major contributions during the Great Cataclysm, but he gradually became corrupted. He took full control of the Ares Guild and committed all kinds of crimes. The important thing is...”
Team Leader Choi went on in a dry voice.
“The blame wouldn’t fall on Lee Jungryong alone. It would fall on the entire Ares Guild.”
“The Ares Guild’s influence is immense. My maternal grandfather has been out of sight for years, and Lee Jungryong is dead, but people still have absolute faith in its power.”
Clink.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi ran his fingers over the perfectly clean tableware, his eyes sinking into deep stillness.

“I don’t want food splashed with filth. Even if there’s hair in it and it’s crawling with maggots, it must look better than anything else on the outside. I want it in my hands with all its influence intact.”
I’d overlooked the power of the Ares name. Its influence.
And Team Leader Choi wanted the Ares Guild whole, without a blemish on its surface. He wanted all that power and influence for himself.
Removing the hair Lee Jungryong had planted and picking out the vermin would come afterward.
“I’ve waited a long time for this.”
Team Leader Choi murmured the words, his eyes glinting coldly.

And he was Cheon Taemin’s only living blood relative.
But Lee Jungryong had kept Team Leader Choi’s existence under wraps while he was alive.
Team Leader Choi had done the same.
Until then, the two of them had been a dinosaur and an ant.
Even if revealing his identity turned him into a golden ant, he would still be an ant.
Now Lee Jungryong was dead, and the truth they’d hidden—whether by choice or circumstance—was slowly coming to light.
What bothered me was how natural it all seemed.
How perfectly timed.
I gazed steadily at Team Leader Choi.
“This was what you intended, wasn’t it, Team Leader Choi?”
“To be honest, yes.
I judged that now was the right time.”
“Wow.
I didn’t expect you to admit it.
Have you always been this honest?”
“What else do I have to hide from you, Mr.
Jin Taekyung?
Of course, even if I’m honest with you, you still have plenty of secrets.”
“...You didn’t have to put it like that.”
A twinge of guilt caught me off guard.
I already knew Team Leader Choi suspected there was more to me than he’d been told.
Since getting the System, I’d spent more time with him than with anyone else in the modern world, and I’d heard him say as much himself.
Still, when he came right out with it, I had no answer.
I scratched my chin awkwardly.
“Putting that aside, can I ask you a few things?”
“Go ahead.
The seaweed soup will be out soon, so you’ll have to be quick.”
“If this was your plan, wouldn’t it have been better for me to tell everyone what Lee Jungryong was really like?”
Lee Jungryong’s and Wu Heixing’s deaths had been blamed on the Lich.
The truth had been buried, which was why people were mourning them with some goodwill.
Wu Heixing had always been a rotten bastard, and the atrocities involving his family had come to light, so people were still cursing him after his death.
Lee Jungryong, on the other hand, was being mourned as a fallen great star.
They were giving him a national funeral.
That said it all.
If the truth had come out, things would have been different.
I might not have had hard evidence, but I’d earned enough Fame as a new hero that people couldn’t simply dismiss my testimony as nonsense.
Lee Jungryong’s reputation would have been ruined, and Team Leader Choi’s plan would have gone smoothly.
“But you told me not to tell the media what Lee Jungryong had done.”
Team Leader Choi nodded calmly.
“Yes, I did.”
“Why?”
His answer came without a moment’s hesitation.
“Because I didn’t want to dirty what’s mine.”
“What?”
“Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong was certainly a man with an ugly side.
He helped my maternal grandfather and made major contributions during the Great Cataclysm, but he gradually became corrupted.
He took full control of the Ares Guild and committed all kinds of crimes.
The important thing is...”
Team Leader Choi went on in a dry voice.
“The blame wouldn’t fall on Lee Jungryong alone.
It would fall on the entire Ares Guild.”
“The Ares Guild’s influence is immense.
My maternal grandfather has been out of sight for years, and Lee Jungryong is dead, but people still have absolute faith in its power.”
Clink.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi ran his fingers over the perfectly clean tableware, his eyes sinking into deep stillness.
“I don’t want food splashed with filth.
Even if there’s hair in it and it’s crawling with maggots, it must look better than anything else on the outside.
I want it in my hands with all its influence intact.”
I’d overlooked the power of the Ares name.
Its influence.
And Team Leader Choi wanted the Ares Guild whole, without a blemish on its surface.
He wanted all that power and influence for himself.
Removing the hair Lee Jungryong had planted and picking out the vermin would come afterward.
“I’ve waited a long time for this.”
Team Leader Choi murmured the words, his eyes glinting coldly.

chapters.title: Chapter 555
paragraphs: He was built like an iron tower. His expression was as hard and unchanging as stone, his lips pressed tightly together.
And then... there were his eyes.
Bloodshot eyes filled with rage, grief, and emotions too tangled to name. Meeting his gaze alone was enough to send a chill down anyone’s spine.
Even the Prime Minister of Korea—a permanent member of the UN Security Council and one of the world’s great powers—was no exception.
What the hell is with that look...?
The gaze struck him like a blade the moment he entered the room. The Prime Minister flinched, then forced his pounding heart to settle.

The man before him might be one of Korea’s most formidable Hunters, but he himself had spent sixty years of life in the mud of politics. There was no reason to be intimidated before they had even begun to talk.
Especially not now.
Having recovered some of his composure, the Prime Minister held out his hand.
“Oh, there you are, Mr. Go Jun.”
Go Jun stared at the offered hand. Instead of shaking it, he answered in a dry voice.
“It’s been a while, Prime Minister Jang.”
That was no way to treat either a man considerably older than himself or the prime minister of his country. Wrinkles bunched across Prime Minister Jang’s forehead.
“...Ha. You must be grieving more deeply than I realized. I understand how you feel.”
“Understand?”
Go Jun’s eyes grew redder. No one could understand what he was feeling.
Yet this sly old raccoon had the nerve to smile and say that.
Crack.
The bones in his clenched fist shifted with an audible snap.

Go Jun had once been so quiet and sparing with his emotions that he seemed carved from stone. The death of Lee Jungryong, the man he had respected and followed more than anyone, had changed him unmistakably.
“Ahem.”
Prime Minister Jang was not too oblivious to notice. He glanced uneasily at Go Jun’s fist and lowered himself awkwardly into a chair.
“I seem to have misspoken. If I offended you, I apologize.”
“...It’s fine. I let my emotions get the better of me as well.”
Go Jun forced down his boiling anger.
He was no longer the orphan of thirty-odd years ago, with nothing left to lose. He had what his Master had passed down to protect, and a mountain of work to do if he meant to protect it.
“But did you really come alone, Prime Minister?”
There it was. Prime Minister Jang answered the abrupt question as calmly as he could.
“I did.”
“Then where is the President?”
“I imagine you already know where he is.”
Prime Minister Jang glanced toward the covered window. Specially treated blackout curtains hid the view, but drawing them back would reveal the Blue House directly beyond.
“The President has pressing matters to attend to. He’ll come when the national funeral officially begins in three hours. I believe his office already informed you...?”
As Prime Minister Jang’s words trailed off, Go Jun’s gaze darkened.
“That’s why I asked again. I couldn’t believe what I’d been told.”
“What?”
“Prime Minister Jang. No...”
Go Jun leaned forward from the sofa. The old politician’s reflection appeared in his red eyes, and a chilling voice passed his lips.
“Mr. Jang Taekhwan.”

“Stop screwing around and let’s speak frankly. Go back and arrange a private meeting with the President right now. There are still three hours before the national funeral proceedings begin, so I’ll give you one hour.”
“H-Hey! How dare you—”
“How dare I?”
Crsh.
Prime Minister Jang’s eyes widened. The sturdy crystal glass in Go Jun’s hand was crumbling into fine powder, spilling between his fingers.
At the same time, the change in Go Jun’s tone cut into the Prime Minister’s ears.
“That’s right. How dare you act like this. Have you forgotten who paved the easy road you’ve walked all these years?”
“Y-You...”
The old politician’s voice shook.
Go Jun was telling the truth. The name Ares Guild was an indelible stain on Prime Minister Jang’s decades in politics.
They were the ones who had cleaned up the filth he left behind, wiped his ass, and loaded heavy boxes into his car trunk.
But...
“That—that was Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong! Not you!”
“That’s right. It was all the Vice Guild Master’s doing. No—my Master’s.”
A dry smile touched Go Jun’s lips.
“And now it’s my job.”
“Don’t get the wrong idea. He may be dead, but the Ares Guild still stands.”
The Ares Guild was an impregnable fortress.
Cheon Taemin, the immortal hero and savior of humanity, had laid its cornerstone. Lee Jungryong had built walls no one dared challenge.
“There isn’t a place in Yeouido—or anywhere in this country—beyond our reach.”
This was a world ruled by the laws of capitalism.

None of the world’s ten largest Guilds appeared in Forbes’s annual rankings of major corporations. Everyone knew how much power and wealth those Guilds held anyway, and how much influence the Ares Guild held even among them.
Now that power would pass from the dead to the living.
“Do you think all he left me was his dying wish?”
“W-What?”
Prime Minister Jang’s eyes widened. According to the NIS, Lee Jungryong had left no will.
No—there was not supposed to be a will.
The ignorant public had been talking about it endlessly, but the Prime Minister had firmly believed the information he had received.
“Then you...”
Go Jun’s eyes flashed red.
“You should call me Vice Guild Master, not ‘you.’”
A faint tremor ran through the old politician’s body. After a suffocating silence, he spoke weakly.
“Mr. Go Jun. No, Vice Guild Master Go. The situation isn’t as simple as you think.”
The red light in Go Jun’s eyes gradually faded. His voice remained dry, but his tone softened somewhat.
“I know. That’s why you’ll have to work harder, Prime Minister Jang. You and the others.”
“Whew. That’s... not easy. There are rumors, too.”
“Rumors?”
“Hunter Jin Taekyung. No—I’m not trying to talk about him. Of course, he is connected to this to a considerable degree.”
Prime Minister Jang had hurried to explain himself when Go Jun reacted to the name. He continued.
“You already know about the young Team Leader from the Peace Guild, don’t you? His name is Choi Minwoo, I believe.”
“...Go on.”
“Since Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong passed away, people around us have had plenty to say. Even with someone to succeed him... it’s true that the Ares Guild isn’t what it used to be.”
Lee Jungryong had been a symbol in his own right.
He was a hero who had suppressed the Great Cataclysm at Cheon Taemin’s side, as well as an S-rank Hunter counted among the very best in the entire world.
His death would not bring the Ares Guild down overnight. But its strength and influence were bound to diminish sharply.
Damn it.
Go Jun knew that. Better than anyone.
The grumbling and resistance already rising throughout the Guild were proof. So was Prime Minister Jang’s attitude—something he would never have dared while Lee Jungryong was alive.
If Master were here. If he were still alive...
The words lingered on Go Jun’s tongue, but he did not let them out.
He could not afford to show any more uncertainty. His face hardened as he spoke.
“You seem to have plenty of worries, Prime Minister Jang. And plenty of time.”
“What does that—”
“The Ares Guild will handle its own affairs. You should handle yours.”
“No, that’s not what I—”
Go Jun watched him try to explain, then leaned back against the sofa.
“Fifty minutes.”
“F-Fifty minutes? What do you mean?”
“Ten minutes have passed since I gave you an hour. That leaves fifty. I don’t think you have time to sit here any longer. Am I wrong?”
It was a clear dismissal: arrange the private meeting with the President, whatever it took, before the national funeral began.
Prime Minister Jang rose on unsteady legs and turned toward the door. Go Jun’s quiet voice reached him from behind.
“One more thing. That person... the Guild Master won’t be coming. Keep everyone in line so there’s no gossip.”
What more could he say?
Prime Minister Jang nodded weakly and left the private room.
Click.
The door sounded unusually loud as it shut. Go Jun stared at the empty place where the Prime Minister had been, then glanced down at his left arm.
Two black stripes marked his mourning armband. With no suitable blood relative to take the role for Lee Jungryong, Go Jun had become the chief mourner.
Master. Are you at peace there?
He could not remember his parents’ faces, yet he missed the face of Lee Jungryong—a man who shared none of his blood—with a pain that cut deep.
He would probably never forget his Master. Nor would he forget the two names that followed him like tags.
“...Jin Taekyung. Choi Minwoo.”
The man who had killed his Master. And the man who meant to take everything his Master had built.
His voice came hot through clenched teeth, and his eyes burned redder than ever.
Still trembling with rage, Go Jun suddenly felt at his neck.
Clink.
Cold metal met his fingertips. He unclasped the necklace and stared down at it. Its plating had worn away in patches, leaving it ugly and battered.
Master.
He knew this necklace was not Lee Jungryong. It was not even something Lee Jungryong had left behind.
But one thing was certain.
It was the only thing that had kept its shape in the ruins of what had once been the Arch Lich’s stronghold.
It was a mere trinket. To Go Jun, it had been worth paying the head of the investigation team a fortune in bribes to smuggle it out.
“...Whew.”
Go Jun let out a deep sigh and rose from his seat.

He was the chief mourner at this grand funeral. He had to greet the countless people waiting outside and show his face to media from around the world, making clear who now wielded power in the Ares Guild.
Click.
When he opened the door, dozens of men and women lined up along the corridor bowed their heads.
Their eyes were fierce, and even their smallest movements carried force. Each one looked every bit the A-rank Hunter they were.
They were Go Jun’s new hands and feet.
“Let’s go.”
At his quiet command, dozens of footsteps crossed the corridor.
The national funeral for Lee Jungryong, former Vice Guild Master of the Ares Guild, lasted five days and was held on a grand scale.
Media and powerful figures from around the world came to Korea. Hundreds of thousands of citizens took to the streets to mourn while the funeral was under way.
But not everyone did. To people hungry today, someone else’s death could feel very far away.
Slash!
Stab-stab-stab!
“Kill it! Stab it now!”
“Keep your distance! Hey, you bastard! Don’t rush out!”
—Kieeeek!
Shrill cries rang through a damp, dark cave.
Weapons deliberately smeared with mud to dull their shine moved without pause, seeking to end their enemies’ lives.
Whoosh—thud!
“Seongha!”
“You monster bastards!”
—Kik. Kiririik!
The battle between Hunters and monsters was fierce, and desperate besides.
Then, as the two species’ differently colored blood sprayed in every direction—
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The ground shook. Stalactites fell from the cave ceiling.
At the same moment, a surge of powerful magical power swept through the Gate from somewhere. The humans screamed.
“A Mutated Gate!”
“Fuck...”
That much magical power could not come from a low-level Gate. Mid-level at the very least. No, high-level.
Perhaps higher still.
Th-This is...
It’s over.
Death. Just as despair settled over every face at the thought of it, someone’s sighing voice echoed through the dark cave.
“Fuck. Brings back old memories.”
