chapters.title: Chapter 556
paragraphs: Whew.
I looked around with a sigh.
A damp, chilly cave. Narrow passages tangled together like a maze. Sharp stalactites hanging from the ceiling. Exhausted faces, frightened out of their minds.
Just like back then.
Three years ago. No—if I counted the time I’d spent in Murim, it had been four.
The accident that day remained seared into my heart like an indelible brand, and even now, after taking my revenge, I still couldn’t completely forget it.
“Fuck. Brings back old memories.”
Unlike me, muttering gruffly, the Skeleton King smiled fondly.
“I feel the same. It is as though I have returned to what you humans call home.”
That’s not what I meant, man.
We seemed to be remembering entirely different things. For all I knew, this guy might have been Skeleton One, some skeleton I’d run into back when I was going from one low-level Gate to the next.
Anyway...
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
That wave of magical power is much stronger than I expected.
It was lucky we had been nearby. Otherwise, twenty hardworking living people would almost have been wiped out.
I beckoned to the Hunters staring blankly at us.
“It’s dangerous. Come over here.”
A man in his late twenties who looked like the Team Leader blinked.
“W-What?”
“I said come over here. Hurry.”
“W-Who are you?”
The cave was dark, and they were standing a considerable distance away. Their level was far too low for them to make out my face from that far.
I scratched my chin awkwardly. “I’m... Uh, look behind you.”
“What?”
Their reaction was slow. Instead of answering, I snapped my fingers.
Whoosh—boom!
A faint whistle cut through the air, and green blood splattered everywhere. Behind one of the Hunters, a rusty ax slipped from the hand of a goblin that had been creeping up on him.
Then its headless body collapsed like a rotten log.
Thud!
“Gah!”
“Behind you! Watch your backs!”
“What the hell is this?”
What else? Finger Qi.
I muttered inwardly as I watched the Hunters hurriedly reform their ranks, then realized something.
It’ll be faster if I go to them than if they come to me.
They were struggling against goblins before they’d even made it halfway through the Gate. Being low-level Hunters was one thing, but they couldn’t have much experience, either.
The Skeleton King swept back his blond hair and put on a solemn expression.
“Hmph. It seems the time has come for this body to take the field.”
“Stay put. Don’t get cocky.”
I knew what needed doing, so there was no reason to hesitate. I headed toward them, neither hurrying nor taking my time.
Step.
One step. At the same time, ten streams of Finger Qi shot from my outstretched hands and tore through the air.
Whoosh—thud-thud-thud-thud!
Once more.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
And again.
Boom!
It took only a moment for nearly thirty goblins to end up sprawled across the ground as headless corpses. The last to fall was a hobgoblin that looked like their leader.
And then...
Step.
With my third and final step, a sphere of light summoned by an unknown mage’s Light magic shone on my face.
Flash.
An invisible shock wave and wave of agitation swept through the cave.
For a moment, everyone stared at my face in a daze. Then cries burst out from all around, like water breaking through a dam.
“L-Lord Fuck!”
“Lord Sibu-leol!”
“J-J-Jin Taekyung!”
The last one was better, at least.
The stutter had stretched my name to six syllables, but compared to those nicknames, it was practically respectable. Vice-minister respectable.
Come to think of it, the name fit the situation. The vibrations had grown steadily stronger, and now the whole cave was sh-sh-sh-shaking like a fucking earthquake.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The Skeleton King sauntered over, dodged a falling stalactite, and muttered, “This much commotion does not bode well.”
“Tell me about it.”
The magical power I was feeling was as far beyond what belonged in this E-rank Gate—or F-rank, even—as the Nanman Beast Palace was from Henan.
I clicked my tongue and beckoned to the still-stunned Hunters.
“Like I said, it’s dangerous, so come over—”
Patter-patter-patter-patter!
“Whoa. You startled me.”
“Undead, have mercy.”
What was that, a Blink spell?
Being famous did have its advantages. Some old lady named Kim in the middle of nowhere had probably heard of me. Of course Hunters in the same line of work would know who I was.
Before I could finish speaking, all twenty of them came running at the speed of light. They looked at me with fear and trust in their eyes.
“Hyung. I’m a fan. A real fan.”
“Eek! What do I do? What do I dooo?”
“...Thanks, but are you all out of your minds?”
How were they thinking about that at a time like this? I shook my head in disbelief and looked for the Team Leader.
At least he seemed to understand how serious things were. His face was stiff as he rummaged through his pocket and held something out to me.
“Could I get your autograph? Please write, ‘Go, Hunter Lee Seungyeop!’”
“Please. I’ll make it a family heirloom and pass it down for generations.”
Ah, fuck. I had no words.
Feeling miserable, I scrawled my signature across the briefing board. The Team Leader cautiously added, “And if it wouldn’t be too much trouble, could you swear once?”
“What?”
“Swear at me. It’s my wish.”
“...You fucking bastard.”
“Thank you! Thank you!”
“I meant it.”
“Gasp.”
One person—or rather, one monster—watched the exchange with obvious envy.
“You are rather popular, wretched human. They say that if one defecates, one becomes famous and people applaud.”
He had that backward somehow. Taking a shit in public might make you famous, but wouldn’t people slap you instead of applauding?
I didn’t have time to correct the Skeleton King’s distorted understanding. Just as I opened my mouth, the cave, already shaking like an earthquake had struck, lurched violently.
Rumble-rumble—crack!
The ground split, and cracks spread across the ceiling like a spiderweb. One of the Hunters groaned, “Is it collapsing...?”
Half right. Half wrong.
While everyone stared at the ceiling, which looked ready to come crashing down at any moment, I was the only one who knew what was happening below as well.
Crack. Crack-crack.
A sprout pushed its way through the solid rock covering the ground.
Dark red. Even as I watched, it grew at a frightening pace.
It produced thorns. A flower bud burst open, scattering seeds that soon began spreading in every direction.
Crack-crack-crack-crack!
“W-What is that?”
“Eeeeeek!”
“Ugh!”
“Cut it! Chop it down!”
The Hunters finally noticed and sprang into action. But screaming and hacking at the undergrowth did nothing to stop it from spreading.
Because this wasn’t happening only here.
Even if the Skeleton King and I stepped in, we couldn’t make it through the entire Gate and deal with all of it in so little time.
This is...
Not a simple collapse. A change.
The entire Gate was taking on a new form.
Mutation. Literally.
Before everyone’s horrified eyes, the Mutated Gate neared the end of its transformation.
Rumble-rumble-rumble. Boom!
The hairline cracks spreading across the ceiling darkened, and the gaps opened wide. It looked as though a giant egg—the cave itself—was breaking open.
And then...
Crack!
Beyond the ceiling, where nothing should have existed, something appeared, wreathed in red light and dim mist.
A vast space that dwarfed the cave. Dense vegetation. Heat as muggy as a wet sauna.
“What is that?”
“A-A jungle?”
Everyone was struck speechless. The Skeleton King whispered so that only I could hear.
“Wretched human. This body’s power is growing stronger.”
Illusion magic hid his true appearance, but the Skeleton King was a monster. If his power was growing stronger, it meant one thing.
The amount and density of the magical power.
I couldn’t see it. But I could feel it.
Whoosh...
Immense magical power filled the air. It had swelled almost to bursting, pressing down on the jungle.
It was a level of magical power that would be difficult to sense even in an A-rank Gate. There was no chance ordinary low-level Hunters could withstand it.
“Hhk. Hhk.”
“I-I can’t... breathe...”
Their pupils gradually lost focus, and they staggered. Not one of the twenty Hunters was spared. As they began passing out one by one, the Skeleton King frowned at me for standing by and watching.
“Wretched human. You...”
“This is better.”
“What?”
“Nothing good would come of them staying awake.”
I had to conceal the Skeleton King’s existence as much as possible. If so, it was better to remove these people from the situation from the beginning, as long as doing so didn’t endanger their lives.
The fewer witnesses, the better.
Thud.
Once the last Hunter had lost consciousness, the Skeleton King nodded at my signal and snapped his fingers.
Crack-crack-crack!
Countless bones rose from somewhere and closed around the Hunters without leaving a gap. The Skeleton King looked smug.
“Done. Since this body has personally demonstrated its abilities, the safety of those humans is guaranteed.”
I studied the small dome. “I don’t know. I think you should reinforce it.”
“Tsk, tsk. Wretched human, you are distrustful indeed. This would hold firm even against a horde of ogres.”
Ogres were monsters whose terrifying strength was always considered among the highest, regardless of their Grade.
“It’d probably be fine against ogres. But those things look a little different.”
“Huh?”
The Skeleton King turned to look. In the vast jungle, something was slowly rising to its feet.
Twenty meters tall. Arms and legs longer and thicker than the countless giant trees around it.
And...
One enormous eye gazing down at the earth.
A Cyclops.
Mist shrouded the mythical giant from head to toe. Its single eye turned toward us, and an eerie voice boomed like thunder.
—Intruders. Humans. Kill.
And the next moment—
System You have been forcibly moved to the Mutated Gate! An Unexpected Quest, Forest of Giants, has been created.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Along with the System notification drilling into my ears, the jungle shook.
No. It came alive.
Flap-flap!
Nameless birds shot into the sky. Beneath their beating wings, hundreds of trees rose with monstrous cries.
Ancient tree spirits from countless tales. Ents awoke from their slumber and roared.
—Gwoooooar!
—Grrrrrrrr!
One person—or rather, one monster—had watched it all in silence. He promptly changed his mind.
“...I shall reinforce the humans’ barrier.”
“Uh, yeah.”
Crack-crack.
Far more bones than before surged upward, piling on in layer after layer.
The Skeleton King took care to finish the reinforcement, then fixed a grave stare on the advancing jungle.
“Ready, Jin?”
“Of course, King... Wait, where the hell did you learn this kind of thing?”
“The internet. It is entertaining.”
“You bastard. Once we get out of here, I’m confiscating your phone.”
I muttered a threat at him, then spoke under my breath.
“Inventory open. Summon.”
At my command, the shaft of White Flame appeared in my empty hand. Its familiar feel was one I hadn’t known in a long time.
I looked around at what had become a battlefield, and a smile touched my lips.
Let’s go.
Whoosh.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi surged up from my lower dantian, became a fire dragon, and spread through every limb and bone in my body.

chapters.title: Chapter 557
paragraphs: Whew.
My breath mingled with the muggy air of the forest. Watching the enemies closing in from every direction, I quietly muttered to myself.
Keep my center low. Keep my lower body firm. When launching an attack...
Be fierce. Don’t hesitate.
Flash.
The instant I half-opened my eyes, I kicked off the ground.
Bam—!
Compressed air burst from my toes, and tremendous wind pressure slammed into me. My superhuman body pushed through it. Leaning into the wind, I shot forward like a cannonball.
Whoooosh!
My hair whipped wildly. The forest blurred past.
Behind me, the Skeleton King yelled at me to take him along, but the rush of air swallowed his voice.
The hundreds of monsters advancing through the deep, sticky swamp and trampling the dense undergrowth were suddenly right in front of me.
—Gwoooooar!
Hundreds of them. Or hundreds of trees.
I didn’t know which word to use for monsters called Ents, but I knew one thing.
I’ll win.
That wasn’t a guess. I was certain. Even the Cyclops watching from behind the Ents as though it were their king was no exception.

The three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi coursing through me were my proof. I’d defeated countless powerful enemies to get here; I was my own witness. And the blue-white Force rising around White Flame’s spearhead was the judge.
The verdict came swiftly, and it was destructive.
Now.
Hiss.
Blue flames evaporated the moisture around me. In less than an instant, White Flame’s transparent spearhead had swept diagonally across the Ents at the front.
Shwaak!
There was no explosive sound. No scream.
Only a gust of wind, and a faint line drawn through the air by the Extreme Yang energy on my spearhead.
The line looked like part of something that belonged in a legend.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear. First form.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Before I could even finish thinking the four syllables of the form’s name, the faint line suspended in the air rippled.
The dormant blue-white flames awoke from their brief slumber.
Fwoosh.
Tiny embers flared. Feeding on the Ents’ trunks, branches, and lush leaves, the flames became hellfire and devoured everything the line had touched.
Kraaaaaash—!
Blue-white light burst outward, illuminating the forest.
In its wake, the ground lay blackened and melted. Hundreds of Ents stood frozen in place. Then a clear bell rang from somewhere.
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System Critical Strike! - You defeated Level 95 Corrupted Ent Great Warrior! - You defeated Level 90 Corrupted Ent Vanguard! - You defeated Level 89 Corrupted Ent Vanguard! - ... - ... - ... - Since the level difference between you and the defeated targets is 20 or more, the EXP gained is reduced. - Since you defeated 20 or more Corrupted Ents with a single strike, bonus EXP has been awarded! - You obtained a large amount of EXP and Fame!
But the System notifications didn’t end there.
Ding.

System You have been surrounded by a great many enemies. But do not be afraid. It is not you who must retreat, but the enemy. - The effect of the Title One Against a Thousand has activated! - Number of identified enemies: 281 - Since you are facing a large number of enemies, all your attributes will temporarily increase according to the number of enemies. - When fighting a large number of enemies, your Stamina consumption during battle is greatly reduced, and you will not easily feel fatigue!
One Against a Thousand.
Two months ago, I’d earned the Title by single-handedly sweeping away the undead army serving the Arch Lich. At last, it was showing its worth.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
The bells rang in quick succession, and all my attributes—including Strength and Stamina—rose slightly.
But that wasn’t all. One of the greatest effects of One Against a Thousand was its ability to maximize a single attribute.

System Intimidation has increased dramatically! - Your majesty and aura, rising like a wildfire, are overwhelming your enemies! - Your enemies are greatly intimidated by your Intimidation! - Your allies’ morale is greatly increased by your Intimidation!
Intimidation.

The power to suppress enemies and encourage allies. An ability that could change the flow of an entire battlefield instead of affecting only me. The System’s information hadn’t been wrong in the slightest.
The encirclement closing around me faltered. Thick branches that had been thrashing violently stopped in place.
—Gwooooo...
The Ents—evil spirits dwelling in giant trees—let out frightened cries. Hundreds of pairs of black eyes trembled between their hard bark.
Fear.
I knew the feeling. Once, it had been mine. Now it belonged to the enemies facing me.
Exhilaration rose in my chest as I took a step forward.
Step.
—Gwoooooar...
—Grrk. Gwooooo...
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
The Ents retreated as I advanced.
No—the entire jungle moved.
The magical power they released as they huddled together was crushed beneath the wave of qi and Intimidation radiating from me.
Power. Momentum.
They couldn’t match me in either of the two things that decided a battle. I had no reason not to fight, and no reason I couldn’t win.
There was, of course, one variable.
—Kraaaaaaaar!
The Cyclops.
The mythical giant’s roar shook the jungle. Its single eye was larger than a boulder, and the Ents that had been edging backward on their roots flinched.
Ding.
System Giant’s Roar has activated! - The effect of Intimidation has been slightly neutralized! - Some enemies have escaped the pressure of Intimidation!
A fitting ability for the boss monster of this Gate.
But even the Cyclops couldn’t completely lift the pressure on them, and I had no intention of giving it more time.
No. Correction.
We had no intention of giving it more time.
“Haaap!”
Krkrkrkrk! Pow-pow-pow!
With a powerful shout, a spear of bone shot through the air and pierced the Ents.
The Skeleton King had caught up with me. He was raising hell.
“Come at me, you worthless monsters!”
The bastard had completely lost track of what he was.
Apparently getting the full benefit of One Against a Thousand, he charged ahead without a thought.
“How dare you oppose this exalted body! Die! Die! Dieee!”
Papapapat!
The Skeleton King might have been a little off his rocker, but he was still a Named Monster who had undergone an evolution. There was no denying his power.
Bones erupted from the ground and the air, snapping branches and piercing Ent trunks without pause.
Pow-pow-pow!
“How dare you wave those adorable little leaves before this body!”
Craack!
“No matter how many of you attack, it’s like striking bone with an egg!”
—Gwoooooar!
The Ents’ mournful cries rang through the scene of forest destruction.
The Skeleton King’s arrival had cleared a path. I shot down it like an arrow.
Whoooosh! Slash!
I swept past like the wind, slashing in every direction. Flames crossed the air, and the Ents vanished before they could even scream.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
Hearing the bells ring noisily in my ears, I twisted aside. A tree trunk shot toward me with tremendous force, grazed my side, and pierced the ground.
Boom!
Mud exploded upward. I stepped onto another stem whipping toward me and sprang lightly into the air.
Tap. Swish.
Since Mungyeong’s lessons, my movements had grown smoother and more precise. I glided forward like a feather and arrived before an unusually massive tree.
Level 102 Corrupted Ent Elder
—H-u-man! D-i-e!
Its level wasn’t the only thing that was high. The Ent Elder had enough intelligence to speak.
I brought my spearhead down diagonally without hesitation.
“Welcome, Chikorita.”
Whoosh. Slash!
The hundreds of branches it hastily gathered to defend itself were useless. So were the thorns it fired at me.
Along the path of my spearhead, the tree—several meters around—slowly split apart.
Crash! Fwoosh!
It fell with a thunderous crash and burst into flames.
I kicked off its stump, dense growth rings exposed, and shot upward. At last, I came face-to-face with the gigantic being blocking out the sky.
Level 130 ‘Red Eye’ Cyclops
There it was. The master of this jungle. A savage, one-eyed giant with hundreds of Ents for servants.
Now that I could identify it, I saw that its level was higher than any monster that had served the Arch Lich during the Small Cataclysm. It even had an epithet. A Named Monster.
A Named Monster in a low-grade Gate like this...
The thought weighed on me, but I had to put it aside. A gigantic shadow was plunging down from high above.
Whoom!
A rock over ten meters in diameter—no, something closer to a meteorite—crushed the air beneath it as it fell.
I chose to break through it head-on.
Finish it quickly.
I shot upward. The rock plunged down.
At the moment of impact, I poured the Scorching Yang Qi within White Flame into the tip of its spearhead and thrust at the rock’s center.
And then...
Slash.
Like a hot knife cutting through cheese, the spearhead slid into the rock and turned.
Krkrkrk.
It broke through at a single point. Mighty Force tore through the interior, and cracks spread across the enormous rock’s surface.
Kraaaaaaang!
It shattered with a thunderous roar, scattering hundreds—thousands—of fragments in every direction.
The Cyclops’s single red eye widened. Unable to withstand the force, it staggered.
Rumble. Crack!
—Gwoooooar!
The ground broke beneath the giant’s movements. Small-bodied Ents were trampled underfoot and screamed.
Neither the Cyclops nor I paid them any attention.
All that mattered was bringing down the enemy in front of us.
—Huuuuuu... maaaaan...
The Cyclops’s roar sounded as though it had been slowed to 0.1 speed.
In that slowed world, I stepped onto empty air and shot upward again without a moment’s hesitation.
Bam!
Stepping on Empty Air.
Compressed air exploded beneath my toes, propelling me farther and higher.
Whoooom.
Sensing danger, the Cyclops swung its fist too late. It was slow enough to make me yawn.
Boom!
The punch split the air with a terrifying sound. But by the time its fist struck empty space, I had already passed it and risen above its head.
Gooooong.
Blue flames spread across the spearhead, heavy with Scorching Yang Qi.
A force both sharp and destructive.
The second and final form of the Blazing Flame Divine Spear, which concentrated three hundred years of the Fire Gate Clan’s macho spirit—the time-honored clan with absolutely no concept of retreat.
Heavenly Strike.
Blue flames fell toward the giant’s head.
Shwoooooosh. Slash!

sentences.text: Whew.
My breath mingled with the muggy air of the forest.
Watching the enemies closing in from every direction, I quietly muttered to myself.
Keep my center low.
Keep my lower body firm.
When launching an attack...
Be fierce.
Don’t hesitate.
Flash.
The instant I half-opened my eyes, I kicked off the ground.
Bam—!
Compressed air burst from my toes, and tremendous wind pressure slammed into me.
My superhuman body pushed through it.
Leaning into the wind, I shot forward like a cannonball.
Whoooosh!
My hair whipped wildly.
The forest blurred past.
Behind me, the Skeleton King yelled at me to take him along, but the rush of air swallowed his voice.
The hundreds of monsters advancing through the deep, sticky swamp and trampling the dense undergrowth were suddenly right in front of me.
—Gwoooooar!
Hundreds of them.
Or hundreds of trees.
I didn’t know which word to use for monsters called Ents, but I knew one thing.
I’ll win.
That wasn’t a guess.
I was certain.
Even the Cyclops watching from behind the Ents as though it were their king was no exception.
The three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi coursing through me were my proof.
I’d defeated countless powerful enemies to get here; I was my own witness.
And the blue-white Force rising around White Flame’s spearhead was the judge.
The verdict came swiftly, and it was destructive.
Now.
Hiss.
Blue flames evaporated the moisture around me.
In less than an instant, White Flame’s transparent spearhead had swept diagonally across the Ents at the front.
Shwaak!
There was no explosive sound.
No scream.
Only a gust of wind, and a faint line drawn through the air by the Extreme Yang energy on my spearhead.
The line looked like part of something that belonged in a legend.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear.
First form.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Before I could even finish thinking the four syllables of the form’s name, the faint line suspended in the air rippled.
The dormant blue-white flames awoke from their brief slumber.
Fwoosh.
Tiny embers flared.
Feeding on the Ents’ trunks, branches, and lush leaves, the flames became hellfire and devoured everything the line had touched.
Kraaaaaash—!
Blue-white light burst outward, illuminating the forest.
In its wake, the ground lay blackened and melted.
Hundreds of Ents stood frozen in place.
Then a clear bell rang from somewhere.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.

System Critical Strike! - You defeated Level 95 Corrupted Ent Great Warrior! - You defeated Level 90 Corrupted Ent Vanguard! - You defeated Level 89 Corrupted Ent Vanguard! - ... - ... - ... - Since the level difference between you and the defeated targets is 20 or more, the EXP gained is reduced. - Since you defeated 20 or more Corrupted Ents with a single strike, bonus EXP has been awarded! - You obtained a large amount of EXP and Fame!
But the System notifications didn’t end there.
Ding.
System You have been surrounded by a great many enemies.
But do not be afraid.

It is not you who must retreat, but the enemy. - The effect of the Title One Against a Thousand has activated! - Number of identified enemies: 281 - Since you are facing a large number of enemies, all your attributes will temporarily increase according to the number of enemies. - When fighting a large number of enemies, your Stamina consumption during battle is greatly reduced, and you will not easily feel fatigue!
One Against a Thousand.
Two months ago, I’d earned the Title by single-handedly sweeping away the undead army serving the Arch Lich.
At last, it was showing its worth.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
The bells rang in quick succession, and all my attributes—including Strength and Stamina—rose slightly.
But that wasn’t all.
One of the greatest effects of One Against a Thousand was its ability to maximize a single attribute.

System Intimidation has increased dramatically! - Your majesty and aura, rising like a wildfire, are overwhelming your enemies! - Your enemies are greatly intimidated by your Intimidation! - Your allies’ morale is greatly increased by your Intimidation!
Intimidation.
The power to suppress enemies and encourage allies.
An ability that could change the flow of an entire battlefield instead of affecting only me.
The System’s information hadn’t been wrong in the slightest.
The encirclement closing around me faltered.
Thick branches that had been thrashing violently stopped in place.
—Gwooooo...
The Ents—evil spirits dwelling in giant trees—let out frightened cries.
Hundreds of pairs of black eyes trembled between their hard bark.
Fear.
I knew the feeling.
Once, it had been mine.
Now it belonged to the enemies facing me.
Exhilaration rose in my chest as I took a step forward.
Step.
—Gwoooooar...
—Grrk.
Gwooooo...
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
The Ents retreated as I advanced.
No—the entire jungle moved.
The magical power they released as they huddled together was crushed beneath the wave of qi and Intimidation radiating from me.
Power.
Momentum.
They couldn’t match me in either of the two things that decided a battle.
I had no reason not to fight, and no reason I couldn’t win.
There was, of course, one variable.
—Kraaaaaaaar!
The Cyclops.
The mythical giant’s roar shook the jungle.
Its single eye was larger than a boulder, and the Ents that had been edging backward on their roots flinched.
Ding.
System Giant’s Roar has activated! - The effect of Intimidation has been slightly neutralized! - Some enemies have escaped the pressure of Intimidation!
A fitting ability for the boss monster of this Gate.
But even the Cyclops couldn’t completely lift the pressure on them, and I had no intention of giving it more time.
No.
Correction.
We had no intention of giving it more time.
“Haaap!”
Krkrkrkrk!
Pow-pow-pow!
With a powerful shout, a spear of bone shot through the air and pierced the Ents.
The Skeleton King had caught up with me.
He was raising hell.
“Come at me, you worthless monsters!”
The bastard had completely lost track of what he was.
Apparently getting the full benefit of One Against a Thousand, he charged ahead without a thought.
“How dare you oppose this exalted body!
Die!
Die!
Dieee!”
Papapapat!
The Skeleton King might have been a little off his rocker, but he was still a Named Monster who had undergone an evolution.
There was no denying his power.
Bones erupted from the ground and the air, snapping branches and piercing Ent trunks without pause.
Pow-pow-pow!
“How dare you wave those adorable little leaves before this body!”
Craack!
“No matter how many of you attack, it’s like striking bone with an egg!”
—Gwoooooar!
The Ents’ mournful cries rang through the scene of forest destruction.
The Skeleton King’s arrival had cleared a path.
I shot down it like an arrow.
Whoooosh!
Slash!
I swept past like the wind, slashing in every direction.
Flames crossed the air, and the Ents vanished before they could even scream.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
Hearing the bells ring noisily in my ears, I twisted aside.
A tree trunk shot toward me with tremendous force, grazed my side, and pierced the ground.
Boom!
Mud exploded upward.
I stepped onto another stem whipping toward me and sprang lightly into the air.
Tap.
Swish.
Since Mungyeong’s lessons, my movements had grown smoother and more precise.
I glided forward like a feather and arrived before an unusually massive tree.
Level 102 Corrupted Ent Elder
—H-u-man!
D-i-e!
Its level wasn’t the only thing that was high.
The Ent Elder had enough intelligence to speak.
I brought my spearhead down diagonally without hesitation.
“Welcome, Chikorita.”
Whoosh.
Slash!
The hundreds of branches it hastily gathered to defend itself were useless.
So were the thorns it fired at me.
Along the path of my spearhead, the tree—several meters around—slowly split apart.
Crash!
Fwoosh!
It fell with a thunderous crash and burst into flames.
I kicked off its stump, dense growth rings exposed, and shot upward.
At last, I came face-to-face with the gigantic being blocking out the sky.
Level 130 ‘Red Eye’ Cyclops
There it was.
The master of this jungle.
A savage, one-eyed giant with hundreds of Ents for servants.
Now that I could identify it, I saw that its level was higher than any monster that had served the Arch Lich during the Small Cataclysm.
It even had an epithet.
A Named Monster.
A Named Monster in a low-grade Gate like this...
The thought weighed on me, but I had to put it aside.
A gigantic shadow was plunging down from high above.
Whoom!
A rock over ten meters in diameter—no, something closer to a meteorite—crushed the air beneath it as it fell.
I chose to break through it head-on.
Finish it quickly.
I shot upward.
The rock plunged down.
At the moment of impact, I poured the Scorching Yang Qi within White Flame into the tip of its spearhead and thrust at the rock’s center.
And then...
Slash.
Like a hot knife cutting through cheese, the spearhead slid into the rock and turned.
Krkrkrk.
It broke through at a single point.
Mighty Force tore through the interior, and cracks spread across the enormous rock’s surface.
Kraaaaaaang!
It shattered with a thunderous roar, scattering hundreds—thousands—of fragments in every direction.
The Cyclops’s single red eye widened.
Unable to withstand the force, it staggered.
Rumble.
Crack!
—Gwoooooar!
The ground broke beneath the giant’s movements.
Small-bodied Ents were trampled underfoot and screamed.
Neither the Cyclops nor I paid them any attention.
All that mattered was bringing down the enemy in front of us.

Bam!

chapters.title: Chapter 558
paragraphs: Flash.
The man’s eyes flew open.
For a moment, he stared dazedly into space. Then he began piecing together what had happened.
An F-rank Gate. Goblins. An earthquake. And...
Jin Taekyung.
That last name brought everything back. The man sprang up as if launched by a spring.
“Gaaaaah!”
There was just one problem. He had the large build of a tank, and there wasn’t much room to spring up in.
Thump. Bang!
“Gah! Huh?”
He struck his head on the ceiling. His cry of pain cut off as his eyes widened.
It hurt. It really hurt. But if he could feel pain, that meant...
I-I’m alive!
He’d never expected toprotagonist.
As the tension finally left his body, he realized he was lying inside a vehicle. An ambulance, to be precise.
An ambulance?
He was lucky to have escaped death, but this wasn’t necessarily a good sign. Surviving only to be left disabled would be its own kind of misfortune.
He hurriedly began checking himself from head to toe.
That was when—
Bang. Rattle.
The door flew open, and light poured in. He raised both arms to shield his face.
Or perhaps it was the dazzling beauty of the woman who had opened it that made him do that.
“Oh, you’re awake. I thought I heard something as I was passing by.”
He stammered at the beautiful woman who had appeared out of nowhere. “W-Who are you?”
“You’re Team Leader Lee Seungyeop, right? Thirty-three years old, a freelancer with no Guild affiliation.”
“H-How do you know who I am?”
“Questions in a moment. First, are you feeling all right?”
Her gentle but firm interruption caught him off guard, and he nodded.
“You should be fine. All you had were a few scrapes—hardly enough to call injuries. The others, too...”
The others?
That casual mention made his eyes fly open.
“R-Right! My team! Are they all right? Did anyone die or get hurt?”
“Your team members are all safe. But if you keep shouting, my ears won’t be.”
“Really? You’re sure? Guh, is that really true?”
“I know someone who always stakes something dirty on it at times like this. I don’t have any balls, so I’ll stake my ovaries. Satisfied?”
She delivered the answer without missing a beat, then continued.
“And to answer your earlier question, I checked your belongings. Thanks to that, we were able to complete your identity verification quickly.”
Tap.
She set down a small extradimensional Pocket and a briefing board. A short message had been scrawled across the board’s white surface in atrocious handwriting.
Go, Hunter Lee Seungyeop!
—Jin Taekyung
The woman gave a quiet laugh.
“That had actually fallen on the ground. Someone picked it up and handed it to me himself. Said it was going to be a family heirloom, so we couldn’t let you lose it.”
Team Leader Lee Seungyeop’s eyes widened.
“Then the person who handed it to you was...?”
“If a name just came to mind, you’ve got it.”
Her neat eyebrows lifted. Her voice was as open and bright as her features.
“Oh, I haven’t introduced myself. I’m Song Song.”
“Song? What kind of song?”
“...It’ll be faster if I just give you my business card. Here.”
Swish.
The Team Leader took the card from her long, pale fingers and stared.
“Peace Guild?”
“Officially, I’m the Healer Team Leader. I’m temporarily heading the emergency rescue team, too.”
He caught his breath. Even someone as busy making ends meet as he was knew about the Peace Guild.
You’d have to be a monster not to.
Jin Taekyung himself belonged to it.
Its enormous financial resources and ability to draw public attention had fueled explosive growth in just a few months. The Peace Guild was no longer some unremarkable small or medium-sized Guild.
I hear it’s harder to get into the Peace Guild than Ares Guild these days.

It offered Hunters some of the best treatment in the industry, and its prospects seemed limitless. Of course talented people were flocking to it. After Lee Jungryong’s national funeral a week ago, he’d even heard that Hunters from Ares Guild had transferred there instead of renewing their contracts.
And the woman in front of him was a team leader at that very Guild. She looked barely into her twenties, but she was already a big deal.
Come to think of it, he might have seen her celebrity-like face on television once or twice.
“But... what exactly is the emergency rescue team? I haven’t heard of it before.”
“Exactly what it sounds like. It’s a new team dedicated solely to rescuing people.”
“I know Guilds of a certain size have rescue teams. But neither my team nor I belong to the Peace Guild.”
Freelance Hunters and small Guilds relied on government agencies for help; even mid-sized Guilds commonly ran their own rescue teams. He couldn’t understand why the Peace Guild had shown up for them.
“Would you rather we hadn’t?”
“N-No! How could I think that? I’m grateful, of course. We nearly died in that Mutated Gate, and you saved us.”
Song Song gave a quiet laugh.
“Then that settles it. It’s what we came to do.”
“What?”

“The Peace Guild emergency rescue team is on a trial run, focusing on mid- and low-grade Gates in the capital region. We’re working with government agencies, and we respond to all Hunters. You could call it volunteer work for public safety.”
“Volunteer... work?”
“Oh, I and the others get paid, of course.”
He stared past Song Song’s shoulder. Hunters were hurrying in every direction, each with the Peace Guild emblem on their chest.
Volunteer work? With this many people?

No matter how much of a golden goose a modern Hunter Guild was, most of its income still came from Gates. Guilds paid Hunters enormous salaries because they could make even greater profits from raids.
But the Peace Guild had sent these Hunters out to rescue people instead—and paid them properly to do it.
They all look like at least mid-grade Hunters.
Dozens of them wore equipment that looked expensive even at a glance. As a low-grade Hunter, he couldn’t begin to guess how much the Peace Guild had spent on them today.
“Um. You said you’re Team Leader Song Song?”
“Yes. Go ahead.”
“I was wondering... are there treatment fees? Rescue fees? Anything like that?”
“No. Have you ever seen a firefighter rescue someone and send them a bill?”
“Then...?”
“Transport and treatment are free, obviously. Oh, and if anyone’s been hurt psychologically, we cover counseling too. For trauma and that sort of thing.”
Wait. What treatment? Did I hear that right?
He stared at her, dazed, then asked in all sincerity, “Does the Peace Guild dig its money out of the ground?”
Song Song winked.
“No, but the man funding us has quite a lot of it.”
“The man funding you?”
“You know him. You even got his autograph.”
“Anyway, there’s someone like that. He complains every day that he feels like he’s being bled dry, but he’s smiling the whole time.”
A smile touched Song Song’s lips as she thought of him.
When she’d first met him, she’d wondered what kind of lunatic he was. Watching him since then had taught her what it meant to be a true Hunter. What it meant to care about people.
“You. Let’s do a job together.”
“...That sounds like a line I’ve heard somewhere. First, you should know I’m not overseas Chinese.”
Jin Taekyung had come to her out of nowhere with that proposal a week ago. For a moment, she’d thought he wanted her to join Gold Moon—no, Ares Guild—and act as a spy.
What he’d said next had been nothing like she expected.
“You’re better than I expected, Taurus.”
To be a little more honest, he’d been kind of cool this time.
The same had been true when he’d used the money from selling the Black Wyvern’s carcass to establish a charitable foundation. Every now and then, he showed her an unexpected side of himself.
Song Song let out a quiet laugh and looked up at the sky.
It was January, and the cold hadn’t yet faded. But the sunlight overhead was warm.
Kiiiiing.
—Jin Taekyung. Iris recognition complete.
A red light swept across my pupil, accompanied by a mechanical voice. I stepped through the door as it opened automatically and entered the Guild House.
Everyone going about their work stopped in their tracks, as though they’d arranged it in advance.
“W-Welcome.”
“Welcome!”
“Thank you for your hard work!”
“Ah, yes. Hello, everyone.”
I told them not to do this. What is this, a gangster office?
I gave them an awkward smile. I still couldn’t get used to it.
The Skeleton King whispered beside me, “Wretched human. This does not seem right.”
“You, of all people? You have thoughts like that—”
Before I could finish, he strode forward and pointed at a Hunter who looked like a new recruit.
“You there. You’re bending only eighty degrees at the waist. Make it ninety. Or you could try a grandjeol.”
“Y-Yes! Understood!”
Don’t go adjusting their angles. And what exactly does he understand?
Just watching was enough to leave me speechless. I stopped the Guild member from attempting a grandjeol, kindly advised him not to listen to this idiot, and finally made it to my destination.
Familiar faces were waiting there.
“Taekyung!”
“Welcome.”
Im Kkeokjeong spread both arms to greet me. Beside him, Team Leader Choi was busy dealing with something.
“Take it easy. Take it easy. What if you reopen your wounds?”
“I’m just happy to see you, punk.”
“We see each other every day.”
As soon as I sat Im Kkeokjeong down—he was still undergoing rehabilitation training—Team Leader Choi suddenly spoke.
“I received a report over the hotline. A Named Monster appeared?”
“A Cyclops. Plus three hundred Ents for good measure.”
“A Cyclops in an F-rank Gate... It was fortunate you happened to be nearby, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“They all knelt before this body’s majesty.”
“One more word and you’ll be listening on your knees.”
“...Sorry.”
That shut him up. Team Leader Choi handed me a folder.
“What’s this?”
“The data you requested. I compiled the number of Mutated Gates that have appeared recently in Korea and elsewhere in Asia.”
It didn’t take long to go through. Once I’d found what I was looking for, I let out a groan.
“Five in Korea alone over the past month...”
“The frequency of Mutated Gates is rising explosively. The incident in Sichuan Province is the most notable example.”
Mutated Gates were extremely rare. Even in Korea, with its hundreds of Gates, they normally appeared only once or twice a year—three times at most. Yet last month’s count had already passed five.
And it’s already happened twice this month, counting the one I just dealt with.
It was a bizarre phenomenon I couldn’t explain. But the fact that events in Murim came to mind right now couldn’t be a coincidence.
Something’s happening.
Tap. Tap-tap.
I drummed my fingers on the table in silence, then asked, “What about North America and Europe?”
“I expect the situation is similar. But for something more certain, I’ve requested data from someone I trust.”
“Someone you trust?”
The moment I asked, every one of my senses snapped awake.
Whoooooosh.
A sudden storm of qi.
An immense amount of mana, far beyond what even an A-rank Hunter possessed, was converging somewhere in the Guild House.
This is...
I knew that flow of mana. And I recognized the distinctive presence within it.
“Team Leader Choi, don’t tell me...”
“It’s the person you’re thinking of. Though I didn’t expect him to come in person.”
At Team Leader Choi’s calm answer, the Skeleton King turned to me with a bewildered expression.
“Wretched human. Whom are you talking about?”
“Your dad.”
His confusion lasted only a moment. Someone’s message magic entered all our minds, and a smile spread across his face.
—Have you all been well?
The voice had a hip-hop soul and groove to it. I gave a quiet laugh as a name came to mind.
Magic Johnson.
The American Grand Mage had come to visit the Peace Guild.

“I was wondering... are there treatment fees?
Rescue fees?
Anything like that?”
“No.
Have you ever seen a firefighter rescue someone and send them a bill?”
“Then...?”
“Transport and treatment are free, obviously.
Oh, and if anyone’s been hurt psychologically, we cover counseling too.
For trauma and that sort of thing.”
Wait.
What treatment?
Did I hear that right?
He stared at her, dazed, then asked in all sincerity, “Does the Peace Guild dig its money out of the ground?”
Song Song winked.
“No, but the man funding us has quite a lot of it.”
“The man funding you?”
“You know him.
You even got his autograph.”
“Anyway, there’s someone like that.
He complains every day that he feels like he’s being bled dry, but he’s smiling the whole time.”
A smile touched Song Song’s lips as she thought of him.
When she’d first met him, she’d wondered what kind of lunatic he was.
Watching him since then had taught her what it meant to be a true Hunter.
What it meant to care about people.
“You.
Let’s do a job together.”
“...That sounds like a line I’ve heard somewhere.
First, you should know I’m not overseas Chinese.”
Jin Taekyung had come to her out of nowhere with that proposal a week ago.
For a moment, she’d thought he wanted her to join Gold Moon—no, Ares Guild—and act as a spy.
What he’d said next had been nothing like she expected.
“You’re better than I expected, Taurus.”
To be a little more honest, he’d been kind of cool this time.
The same had been true when he’d used the money from selling the Black Wyvern’s carcass to establish a charitable foundation.
Every now and then, he showed her an unexpected side of himself.
Song Song let out a quiet laugh and looked up at the sky.
It was January, and the cold hadn’t yet faded.
But the sunlight overhead was warm.
Kiiiiing.
—Jin Taekyung.
Iris recognition complete.
A red light swept across my pupil, accompanied by a mechanical voice.
I stepped through the door as it opened automatically and entered the Guild House.
Everyone going about their work stopped in their tracks, as though they’d arranged it in advance.
“W-Welcome.”
“Welcome!”
“Thank you for your hard work!”
“Ah, yes.
Hello, everyone.”
I told them not to do this.
What is this, a gangster office?
I gave them an awkward smile.
I still couldn’t get used to it.
The Skeleton King whispered beside me, “Wretched human.
This does not seem right.”
“You, of all people?
You have thoughts like that—”
Before I could finish, he strode forward and pointed at a Hunter who looked like a new recruit.
“You there.
You’re bending only eighty degrees at the waist.
Make it ninety.
Or you could try a grandjeol.”
“Y-Yes!
Understood!”
Don’t go adjusting their angles.
And what exactly does he understand?
Just watching was enough to leave me speechless.
I stopped the Guild member from attempting a grandjeol, kindly advised him not to listen to this idiot, and finally made it to my destination.
Familiar faces were waiting there.
“Taekyung!”
“Welcome.”
Im Kkeokjeong spread both arms to greet me.
Beside him, Team Leader Choi was busy dealing with something.
“Take it easy.
Take it easy.
What if you reopen your wounds?”
“I’m just happy to see you, punk.”
“We see each other every day.”
As soon as I sat Im Kkeokjeong down—he was still undergoing rehabilitation training—Team Leader Choi suddenly spoke.
“I received a report over the hotline.
A Named Monster appeared?”
“A Cyclops.
Plus three hundred Ents for good measure.”
“A Cyclops in an F-rank Gate...
It was fortunate you happened to be nearby, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“They all knelt before this body’s majesty.”
“One more word and you’ll be listening on your knees.”
“...Sorry.”
That shut him up.
Team Leader Choi handed me a folder.
“What’s this?”
“The data you requested.
I compiled the number of Mutated Gates that have appeared recently in Korea and elsewhere in Asia.”
It didn’t take long to go through.
Once I’d found what I was looking for, I let out a groan.
“Five in Korea alone over the past month...”
“The frequency of Mutated Gates is rising explosively.
The incident in Sichuan Province is the most notable example.”
Mutated Gates were extremely rare.
Even in Korea, with its hundreds of Gates, they normally appeared only once or twice a year—three times at most.
Yet last month’s count had already passed five.
And it’s already happened twice this month, counting the one I just dealt with.
It was a bizarre phenomenon I couldn’t explain.
But the fact that events in Murim came to mind right now couldn’t be a coincidence.
Something’s happening.
Tap.
Tap-tap.
I drummed my fingers on the table in silence, then asked, “What about North America and Europe?”
“I expect the situation is similar.
But for something more certain, I’ve requested data from someone I trust.”
“Someone you trust?”
The moment I asked, every one of my senses snapped awake.
Whoooooosh.
A sudden storm of qi.
An immense amount of mana, far beyond what even an A-rank Hunter possessed, was converging somewhere in the Guild House.
This is...
I knew that flow of mana.
And I recognized the distinctive presence within it.
“Team Leader Choi, don’t tell me...”
“It’s the person you’re thinking of.
Though I didn’t expect him to come in person.”
At Team Leader Choi’s calm answer, the Skeleton King turned to me with a bewildered expression.
“Wretched human.
Whom are you talking about?”
“Your dad.”
His confusion lasted only a moment.
Someone’s message magic entered all our minds, and a smile spread across his face.
—Have you all been well?
The voice had a hip-hop soul and groove to it.
I gave a quiet laugh as a name came to mind.
Magic Johnson.
The American Grand Mage had come to visit the Peace Guild.

chapters.title: Chapter 559
paragraphs: Teleportation.

The spatial-transference magic commonly called Teleport was notoriously difficult, even among mages. Get the coordinates wrong and you could die in an instant. It consumed so much mana that a mage attempting long-distance travel might well clutch the back of their neck and collapse.
The ultimate shitty cost-to-benefit ratio.
But in the end, what mattered was who used it.

In the hands of a Supreme Peak master, even the Three Calamities Sword Technique could rival a divine technique. The same principle applied to a Grand Mage—one of only three among the world’s seven billion people.
“Fucking Korea. I think this every time, but it’s too damn far away. I almost got motion sickness on the way here.”
I gave a quiet laugh at Magic Johnson, the dark-skinned Grand Mage grumbling in front of me.
“Motion sickness is a small price to pay for crossing continents. Any other mage would be seasick on the Sanzu River by now.”
“Sanzu River? What’s that? Is it like Cheonggyecheon in Seoul?”
“...A little different. Anyway, let’s move on.”
Magic Johnson, who had turned Seoul into a city of hell in one sentence, spotted the people inside the room and broke into a wide smile.
“Hey, what’s up, gays! It’s been a while.”
Team Leader Choi answered Time magazine’s pick for the “world’s most influential LGBTQ person” in the firmest voice imaginable.
“It’s guys, Mr. Johnson. Not gays.”
“Choi, now you’re hurting my feelings. I came running the moment you asked.”
“I appreciate you coming in person, but couldn’t you have sent it by secure email?”
“Is that any way to treat someone you haven’t seen in a while?”
“If I remember correctly, it hasn’t even been a week since we last met. Isn’t that right, Mr. Jin Taekyung?”
I nodded.
“That’s true. Johnson was here for the national funeral, too.”
The national funeral held this time had been enormous. Nearly a million citizens had come to pay their respects, and influential figures from countries around the world had traveled to Korea.
That said plenty about the influence Lee Jungryong had wielded in life. Quite a few of the mourners were presidents, prompting one news outlet to call the gathering a “summit meeting.”
Magic Johnson, one of the symbols of the United States, had been among them.
“Hey, Jin. Is this how you’re going to act? I didn’t come to meet you people. I came simply to pay my respects.”
“Your respects?”
“That’s right. I came to see off an old comrade.”
“Then why did you go to a gay bar in Itaewon? You even changed your face with illusion magic.”
“...Who told you that ridiculous nonsense?”
“The guy who went with you. Pretty conclusive testimony.”
There was no trace left of his initial delight at seeing Johnson. The victim of that day, the Skeleton King, spoke with an enraged expression.
“I knew something was wrong when something touched this body’s backside. That damned human tricked me.”
“You ungrateful monster-murder fucker...”
Look at that expression. I’d believe it if Time had named him the “world’s most violent LGBTQ person.”
Magic Johnson muttered in a threatening voice, then noticed everyone’s eyes on him and quickly adopted a serious expression.
“Don’t misunderstand. I only went to experience Korean culture.”
“Did you sell your tribute to an old comrade on eBay?”
“Jin, don’t be like that. I paid my respects at the funeral ceremony. You know better than anyone what Mr. Lee was like.”
I did. Who could know better than me?
And Johnson was one of the very few people who knew what had happened at the Arch Lich’s stronghold.
“Anyway, we’re meeting again, so let’s stop talking about this. You there, you agree, don’t you? Your name was... Robin Hood, right?”
Unfortunately, Korea’s Robin Hood—Im Kkeokjeong—didn’t have a translation Item. He answered with a frozen expression.
“I-I’m fine, thank you. And you...”
“I’m fine, of course. But I’m afraid what I have to tell you isn’t good news.”
Swish.
With a sigh, Johnson held out a memory chip no bigger than a fingernail.
Team Leader Choi took it and examined it, his eyes sharpening.
“Is this the information I asked for?”
“That’s right. I had to pull a few strings for the first time in a while.”
“I’ll thank you after I’ve reviewed it.”
“Take your time.”
Tap. Whoooooosh.
It happened in an instant.
Team Leader Choi tapped somewhere beneath the table. Every window and opening in his private office was covered, and unseen mana spread across them like a curtain.
Magic?
If I’d noticed it, there was no way Johnson hadn’t. He looked around the office with interest.
“Seven overlapping spells. Your security is tighter than I expected. Only a handful of mages in our Guild could manage magic at this level... Whose work is it?”
“Someone who has been my hands and feet since I was young.”
Kim the Butler and Johnson had never met face-to-face. After that brief answer, Team Leader Choi inserted the chip into his smartphone, and a holographic video sprang up above the screen.
—Krrrraaaaaash!
With a thunderous roar, the ground within a radius of several dozen meters heaved over, spraying sand in every direction. It looked like an earthquake.
Around a hundred Hunters of different ethnicities shouted and cursed.
—“Fuck!”
—“Spread out! Spread out now! They’re coming!”
—“Healer! Healeeer!”
Screams and shouts filled the scene. Several buildings were collapsing among the dead trees and sand dunes.
Im Kkeokjeong’s eyes widened as he realized what that meant.
“M-Monster Wave?”
Correct. Modern buildings had no business being inside a Gate.
Every Gate contained at least a minimal amount of mana, and its Grade was determined by the total amount of mana it held.
But if a monster appeared whose power far exceeded the Gate’s Grade, that was a different matter.
That was a Mutated Gate.
A Mutated Gate was already a serious problem. But if the presence of the higher-grade monster caused the Gate’s mana to exceed the total amount it could contain, an even greater disaster awaited.
A Monster Wave.
When a sturdy dam gave way under pressure, the water it had held back came flooding out.
That was what we were seeing in the hologram.
—Sssshhhk!
More than ten enormous scorpions let out strange cries. Buried deep in the sand, they sent their tails shooting up through the surface. Screams erupted, and blood sprayed in every direction.
—“Gaaaaah!”
—“Joseph! Save Joseph!”
—“Commence volley fire!”
Krrrraack!
At the very moment humans and monsters threw themselves at one another in an attempt to kill each other—
Ffft.
The holographic video filling the office vanished as though it had been washed away.
Team Leader Choi had stopped the video. He spoke in a subdued voice.
“When did this happen?”
Johnson’s expression darkened.
“Four days ago. The Mojave Desert. It stretches across several states, but this was closer to Arizona. I don’t know the exact coordinates.”
I frowned as I listened.
“Four days ago?”
“Yes. Four days ago.”
“There should’ve been an official announcement by now.”

Gates were like ticking time bombs with a slim chance of going off. That was why every country kept watch on them, stationed government Hunters—the so-called “bomb disposal squads”—around the country, and required incidents to be announced within a set period.
Then why has everything been so quiet?
Mutated Gates were rare. Monster Waves were dozens of times rarer. An incident like this should have made headlines.
Team Leader Choi and I had both been watching news from around the world lately. It made no sense that neither of us had heard about it.
That left only one answer.
“There was no official announcement.”
Johnson gave a small nod.
“That’s right. The Ministry of National Defense stepped in and covered the whole thing up. As neatly as those monsters turned over the desert.”
“They can do that?”
“Can they? Come on, Jin. This was handled in secret by the United States Ministry of National Defense. You should be asking what they can’t do.”
He let out a dry laugh.
“Twenty-two people died and thirty-five were injured, but that doesn’t change anything. It happened at a military base closed to civilians. Probably made it easier to hide.”
“But that’s... a cover-up.”
“It is. It violates the constitution, too—the one extensively revised after the Great Cataclysm. But sometimes a kind lie is better than a cold truth.”
For a moment, it felt as though someone had struck me in the back of the head.
I knew this was wrong. And yet I’d been thinking the same thing as Johnson.
Dark Heaven.

People unprepared for the truth were bound to be thrown into confusion when it arrived without warning. That was true of Dark Heaven in Murim. I, too, believed it was too soon for their identities to become known.
But that wasn’t the only reason the back of my head felt numb.
The vague fear I’d been carrying had just become real.
“How many times?”
I hadn’t said what I was asking about. Johnson’s face went rigid. He understood.
“Johnson.”
“...Fuck.”
He muttered the curse like a sigh, then turned to Team Leader Choi.
“Choi, how many videos are stored on the chip I gave you?”
Team Leader Choi stared silently at the smartphone screen before answering in a voice that sounded almost like a groan.
“Thirty-two.”
“Right. Two were Monster Waves. The rest were Mutated Gates. And that’s only what I managed to get my hands on.”

No one could doubt Magic Johnson’s standing and influence in the United States. But even he could not compare with the intelligence-gathering capabilities of the Ministry of National Defense of the United States, which still claimed to be the most powerful nation in the world.
Thirty-two incidents in the data Johnson managed to acquire alone.
How many more had there been?
At that moment, Team Leader Choi and I fell silent at the same time, as though we had arranged it in advance.
“Wait. Hold on.”
The Skeleton King had been diligently counting something on his fingers. Now he looked at Magic Johnson with eyes as round as lanterns.
“Human I’m no longer grateful to—doesn’t what you just said mean incidents like this have been happening every single day?”
“You loose-lipped monster. Aren’t you taking this a little too lightly?”
“Huh?”
I would have been happier not hearing what Johnson said next.
“Not over the past month. They all happened in the past week.”
A suffocating silence settled over the room. Then the voice of the only person who hadn’t understood Johnson rang out.
“I-I’m fine, thank you. And you?”
To hell with ‘and you.’ Holy shit. Fuck.

chapters.title: Chapter 560
paragraphs: Holy shit. What the fuck.
Even if I used every English-language curse I knew, I still couldn’t express how fucked things were.
Thirty-two times in a single week.
An outrageous number. And that was only what Magic Johnson had managed to find out.
I didn’t know the exact count, but it was bound to be higher than thirty-two.
Yeah. Maybe this was inevitable.
The United States was ninety-eight times the size of Korea and had nearly twenty times as many Gates.
It had been Demon King Asmodeus’s top-priority target during the Great Cataclysm and suffered tremendous damage throughout the war.
Ironically, what had restored the United States to its position as the world’s greatest power was what the war had left behind: Gates.
Oil fields.
Modern Gates were, quite literally, a new and far more abundant kind of oil field.
More than thirty years had passed since the disaster that swallowed the world. Monster byproducts had long fetched high prices, and Magic Gems had become an environmentally friendly energy source.
The survivors had built a civilization even grander and more dazzling atop the ruins of the war.
But...
“The party seems to be over.”
As Magic Johnson had put it, the winners’ lavish party was over.
The oil fields called Gates had caught fire. Explosions would soon erupt all over the world. No—they were already happening.
For now, an invisible hand was hiding them all.
“Ah, fuck...”
The words came out like a groan. I turned to Team Leader Choi.
“Things aren’t like this in Korea too, are they?”
What I meant was: had other incidents happened without my knowing, like the ones in the United States?
Team Leader Choi thought for a moment before answering.
“I always keep unexpected possibilities in mind, but as far as I know, there aren’t any.”
“Team Leader Choi, we need to be sure.”
“I know. That’s why I’m thinking of arranging another meeting while I have the chance.”
Magic Johnson, who had been listening, asked, “A meeting? With whom?”
“Some people I’ve come to know through circumstance. I doubt they lied to me, but you never know what people are thinking.”
“True. Especially politicians.”
Team Leader Choi nodded quietly at Johnson’s offhand remark.
“So you knew.”
“Choi looked awfully busy at Mr. Lee’s national funeral. A lot of people were looking for you.”

Team Leader Choi and I had attended Lee Jungryong’s national funeral and paid our respects. Our private feelings were another matter, but maintaining our public image wasn’t the only reason we had gone.
“They’re looking for a new shadow to shelter under,” Team Leader Choi said. “That’s what I wanted, too.”
Figures from politics and business, along with key members of mid-sized and large Guilds that Ares Guild had kept under its thumb, had shown enormous interest in us.
More than half of them had approached me first, of course. But I’d known from the start what I would say.
Don’t talk to a nobody Hunter like me. Talk to our Team Leader Choi.
Earning a place at Lee Jungryong’s national funeral, where every kind of heavyweight had gathered, meant they were people who had claimed their own victories in society after fighting tooth and nail.
They understood exactly what I meant and immediately set about arranging meetings with Team Leader Choi.
“The powerless are ignored,” Johnson said. “But people reach out to the powerful from every direction. The world may have changed, but that hasn’t.”
It was the sharp truth.
No one had sought out Team Leader Choi or me before. Now the Peace Guild had risen to become the only force capable of standing against Ares Guild.
The public might not know it, but the people at the top of society knew it better than anyone.
By now, political and business figures were probably calculating what they stood to gain from a fight between the two Guilds—and whose shadow would be cooler to stand in.
The owners of the mid-sized and large Guilds probably wanted to use this opportunity to escape Ares Guild’s excessive monopoly as well.
Team Leader Choi had gained new allies and the power they held.
It was his first step toward digesting the entire feast that was Ares.
Perhaps that was why, when he spoke again, the voice that emerged from between his immaculate lips carried more strength than ever.
“I won’t turn away the hands they’ve offered.”
Magic Johnson studied him for a moment, then spoke up.
“So... it seems the rumor was true.”
“What rumor?”
“That rumor. The one saying that Choi is connected to him.”
“There’s no reason to hide it anymore. It’s true.”
Johnson’s eyes widened.
“I didn’t expect Choi to admit it so easily. Have you told everyone else you’ve met recently?”
“No. But even without saying it, they know, and I know. We know whose blood runs through my veins.”
A quiet laugh escaped the Grand Mage’s thick lips.
“Right. No one can deny that fact. He’s the only pureblood in existence in the twenty-first century.”
No living noble or royal could compare to Team Leader Choi. Not even if the haughty Prince Felix of the United Kingdom became king.
If his ancestor had built a vast empire upon which the sun never set, then Cheon Taemin was the savior who had allowed billions of people to see the sun rise on another day.
“And it was wise not to mention him directly,” Johnson said. “People trust a man who keeps his own counsel and doesn’t reveal himself too easily.”
“Thank you for the compliment.”
“No need. It’s the truth.”
There was no trace of Johnson’s usual playful manner. He went on in a calm voice.

“But Choi, keep this in mind. Your grandfather, wherever he may be now, and I have always known what came first. We risked our lives and fought for a better future. Is that what people in the East call a greater cause?”
He was telling Team Leader Choi, without saying it outright, that the crisis on our doorstep had to come before Ares Guild.
After a brief silence, Team Leader Choi answered, “I’ll remember, Mr. Johnson. But I’m not going after Ares Guild for personal reasons alone.”
“I know what kind of man Choi is. You want to weaken Ares in case the worst happens and build up the Peace Guild’s own strength. Teeth like yours aren’t enough to swallow a tiger.”
Team Leader Choi smiled bitterly.
“A hyena... I can’t deny it.”
Lee Jungryong might be gone, but Ares was still Ares.

The Peace Guild had grown rapidly, its name seared into minds around the world because of me. But we couldn’t bring down the impregnable fortress Ares Guild had spent decades building in a single blow.
“Keep building your strength, so long as you’re not doing it for personal glory,” Johnson said. “The Wizard Guild and I will help. If you need it, I can introduce you to a few friends of mine, too.”
“Yes. That’s what I intend to do. The bad blood from the past hasn’t run its course.”
“You mean that young fellow. Mr. Seok.”
Magic Johnson suddenly drew his brows together.
“I haven’t spent much time with him, but I know he isn’t particularly kind. Isn’t that right, Jin?”
I nodded at once.
“He’s a fucking asshole.”
“I had a feeling from his surname. Even the way it’s pronounced sounds like ‘suck.’ And I didn’t like it when he attacked Jin at the Arch Lich’s stronghold while we were still investigating...”
Johnson’s expression grew serious.
“He gives off an even more dangerous smell now than he did before. Jin, you were right in front of me. Didn’t you notice?”
“Jin?”
I hesitated before answering. “Well, I did fart in front of you.”
“What the fuck...”
“Even so, there’s no need to swear. And Go Jun was already a dangerous bastard to begin with.”
“Whew. True. But please try not to fart when I’m standing behind you from now on.”
I had been uneasy about having Magic Johnson at my back too, but I had been the one to fart in the end, so I had nothing to say.
I looked away as I answered. Johnson’s nose twitched.
“All right. That’s enough for today. Whatever anyone else thinks, I want you two to know I trust you completely.”
He looked warmly at Team Leader Choi and me, then turned to the two standing there blankly—no, the one man and one monster.
“You two as well, of course.”
The Skeleton King and Im Kkeokjeong answered at the same time.
“Just don’t take us to a gay bar.”
“I-I don’t speak English.”
“...Very reassuring.”
Johnson’s face said otherwise. He pulled a small glass bottle from inside his clothes and drained it.
I recognized it as a potion to replenish spent mana.
“Are you leaving?”
“I should get back. I’m going to be busy from now on, too. There are friends I haven’t seen in a while whom I need to contact.”
“Friends?”
“The ones I mentioned earlier. About half have retired, but they can still be a great help. Oh, if Choi wants, I could take you to them right now. What do you say?”
Team Leader Choi hesitated under Magic Johnson’s eager gaze, then quickly shook his head.
“N-No, that’s all right.”
“What a shame. My friend Joseph was interested in Choi.”
“I’m disappointed too, but maybe next time... Wait. Did you say Joseph?”
“Unless your hearing’s gone, you heard right.”
“Then... do you mean former United States President Joseph Biden?”
“That’s right. He retired quite a while ago, but we meet for a drink about once a month. He’s so old he can hardly drink anymore, though.”
Team Leader Choi wasn’t the only one shocked. My mouth fell open, and so did Im Kkeokjeong’s.
“That Joseph Biden?”
“Ah, I know! I know Joseph Biden!”
I didn’t care whether the name of the American president was Chakumba Okumbo or Kim Cheol Soo, but I had heard the name Joseph Biden many times since my days at the Hunter training camp.
The Great Cataclysm had struck during his presidency. He’d had it worse than the mayor of New York in a superhero movie.
Would you look at those connections.
In the United States, he was practically a second Founding Father after George Washington.
I knew Magic Johnson was a big deal, but I hadn’t realized his connections were this impressive.
“Don’t look at me like that. Joseph and I have been ball buddies for nearly fifty years. Most people don’t know we’re close.”
Team Leader Choi froze. Johnson hurriedly added, “Forget the ‘ball’ part. We’re just friends. Best friends.”
“Whew.”
“Shit. Do I really have to explain myself?”
“Mr. Johnson, we have a saying in Korea: you reap what you sow.”
“Damn it. I really got what I deserved. So, what are you going to do, Choi?”
Team Leader Choi answered without hesitation.
“Let’s go. I’ll take you up on your offer.”
“Good idea. You might get a little motion sick traveling between continents, though.”
“What’s a little motion sickness compared to this?”
Team Leader Choi answered calmly and took the hand Magic Johnson held out to him.
With a light nod, an enormous amount of mana wrapped tightly around their entire bodies.
Whoooosh!
At that exact moment, a blinding flash erupted and sent their figures flying somewhere else.
Brrrrrrr.
All three smartphones left behind—Im Kkeokjeong’s, the Skeleton King’s, and mine—began vibrating violently.
