chapters.title: Chapter 561
paragraphs: Brrrrrrr.
A smartphone suddenly began vibrating. I, Im Kkeokjeong, and finally the Skeleton King checked the screen in rapid succession before opening our mouths one after another.
“What’s this?”
“T-Taekyung!”
“Oh. Ohoho. Look at this, you primitive humans. A girl-group member has sent this body a DM.”
That fucking bastard. I told him to stop screwing around on social media.
No wonder his phone was ringing when he isn’t even in the group chat.
I felt like stomping him until his illusion magic shattered, but that wasn’t important right now.
Which girl-group member... No. Another incident like this?
I barely swallowed my thoughts and stared at the smartphone screen.
Song Song had posted an urgent message in the group chat for the Peace Guild’s founding members, including Team Leader Choi and me.

Peace Guild └ Song Song: Hey hey heyyy └ Song Song: C-rank Gate anomaly. └ Song Song: Just heard from the government hotline. └ Song Song: They say the magical power readings are skyrocketing. └ Song Song: Fuck; why aren’t you reading this? └ Song Song: If you’ve read it, answer me, you crazy bastard. └ Butler Kim: Sorry. I’m at the Blue House right now. └ Song Song: S-sorry;; I didn’t know it was you, Butler Kim Please get back to what you were doing... └ Butler Kim: Of course. Have a happy day too, Song-i. ^^ └ Song Song: Huh. Everyone but one person has read it? └ Song Song: Whoever’s seen this, get over there and check it out as fast as you can. └ Song Song: It’s far from me, and I have something to take care of, so I can’t go right away. └ Song Song: [Map attached] └ Song Song: ? └ Song Song: Oh, but now that I’ve checked, that Gate is kind of... └ Song Song: Just go for now. └ Song Song: Especially you, Jin Taekyung. Reply as soon as you read this.
Where is it?
What kind of Gate would make her react like that?
I put my questions aside, left a reply saying I had seen the message, and checked the attached map. The moment I did, I understood why Song Song had reacted that way.
“Ah. Hmm.”
The location was definitely a little... awkward.
Im Kkeokjeong checked the map a beat later, and his face hardened.
“Taekyung. Is this...?”
“Probably exactly where you think it is.”
The C-rank Gate marked on the map sat on prime land near a subway station in Bucheon. It was also one of those Gates blessed with what Hunters called “luck.”
The monsters that appeared there were relatively easy to deal with compared to those in other C-rank Gates, and Magic Gems dropped frequently.
Im Kkeokjeong had worked as a Hunter in Bucheon for over ten years. There was no way either of us wouldn’t know the Gate—or the name of the Guild that controlled it.
“This isn’t exactly welcome news...”
The Skeleton King looked up from the smartphone he had been fiddling with at Kkeokjeong’s low mutter.
“Humans. Where is this place that has you making such a fuss?”
I answered quietly.
“The place isn’t the problem. The owner is.”
“Hm? The owner?”
“That’s right.”
Gates couldn’t be privately owned, but mid-sized Guilds and larger effectively controlled them through long-term leases.
And there wasn’t a person in Korea—or anywhere else in the world—who didn’t know the Guild that controlled the C-rank Gate at this address.
“Then who owns it?”
Kkeokjeong gave the Skeleton King a curt answer.
“Ares Guild.”
My eyes went to both of his arms before I could stop them.
The arms severed on someone’s orders had been reattached so cleanly you would never have known anything had happened. But they were trembling faintly, as though he remembered the pain.
“Uncle Kkeokjeong. No—hyung.”
“...I’m fine.”
The answer rang hollow. His trembling was growing worse, and his expression had darkened.
As if he’d noticed the look on my face, he made an effort to relax his own.
“I’m telling you, I’m fine. Now hurry up and go. If the magical power readings are skyrocketing, we could have another Mutated Gate on our hands.”
“...No. Those bastards can handle it themselves.”
How am I supposed to go? Not in this situation. Especially to help them, of all people.
I stood rooted to the spot. Kkeokjeong gave me a faint smile.
“Taekyung.”
“Yes?”

“I meant it when I said I’m fine. Everyone who cut off my arms, Lee Jungryong included, has paid for it. My rehabilitation’s practically finished, too. These days, I’m happy spending time with my wife and watching the kids grow up.”
“Hyung...”

“I’m really fine, so hurry up and go. There must be plenty of good people in Ares Guild, too. If you let a petty personal reason stop you from helping, you’ll regret it for a long time. At least, the Taekyung I know would.”
“I’d like to help too, but I can’t. My rehabilitation isn’t quite done, and honestly, I’m not strong enough.”
He laughed heartily at his own forced joke. I watched him for a moment, then nodded.
He was right. The people facing danger inside the Gate weren’t enemies of mine or the Peace Guild.
If I sensed danger and possessed the strength to save someone from it, then stepping forward was the right thing to do.
That’s why we created the rescue team.
Maybe what I had to do had been decided the moment I obtained the System.
I gave Im Kkeokjeong a brief look of acknowledgment.
“I’ll be back soon.”
“All right. Don’t get hurt.”
“Deal with it quickly and return, you wicked human. As a reward, I shall show you this girl-group member’s selfie.”
I smiled warmly at the Skeleton King.
“Quit screwing around and follow me. Or I’ll smash your smartphone as punishment.”
“...Understood.”
I should’ve done this from the start. You trying to get yourself killed?
By the time we reached the C-rank Gate Orc Wasteland, marked on Song Song’s map, the area was full of frantic voices and shouting.
“The magical power readings are more than twice their usual level!”
“I know that. What about the request for backup?”
“N-Nothing yet!”
“Fuck, there have to be people left at the Bucheon branch! Tell them it’s urgent and ask again for at least one A-rank Hunter!”
“We already passed that along, but most of the A-rank Hunters stationed in Bucheon are deployed overseas, and some of the others are on vacation, so they’re refusing...”
“What? Vacation? They’re refusing because they’re on vacation? Those fucking—!”
It happened in an instant.
A fist filled with rage slammed into a parked car.
Bam!
With a thunderous crash, the foreign car worth more than a hundred million won crumpled, sending large and small fragments flying in every direction.
That was when the flushed, hard-breathing B-rank Hunter spotted the Skeleton King and me.
“Hell, this is driving me crazy. No matter how urgent things are, they should still be controlling access properly—”
His voice trailed off. His eyes went wide.
“Huh? Uh? Huh? Huhhhhh?”
Question after question spilled from his lips, his gaze fixed on my face. The Skeleton King snorted and opened his mouth with a meaningful expression.
“Heh heh. Yes, this human is that human.”
Why is this bastard stepping in and making a scene when I’m just standing here?
I shot the Skeleton King a wary look and cleared my throat. Everyone who had been rushing around was now standing frozen, staring at us.
“Ahem. In case anyone here doesn’t know who I am—”
“Jin Taekyung!”
“Lord Fuck!”
“Lord Sibu-leol!”
“...though I guess that won’t be necessary.”
I hated to say it myself, but at this point, I’d have to wonder if any Hunter who didn’t recognize my face was actually a monster.
“Is that r-really Jin Taekyung?”
“I don’t think he’s a fake Jin Taekyung.”
“Ah, that’s not what I meant...”
“It’s fine. That isn’t important right now.”
I turned to the B-rank Hunter who had smashed the car.
“From what I’ve seen, you seem to be in charge here. Am I right?”
“Y-Yes. I’m Gwak Hangu, Branch Leader of Ares Guild’s Yeokgok Branch.”
He wasn’t even the Bucheon Branch Leader. He was one of the dozens of lower Branch Leaders beneath him, and he was a B-rank Hunter.
It reminded me just how large Ares Guild was—and how deep its talent pool ran. It also reminded me of something I’d briefly overlooked.
Maybe because of their public image, but the atmosphere here is better than I expected.

Ares Guild, the Peace Guild, and I had plenty of bad blood between us. But that fight had taken place beneath the surface. To people who knew nothing about it, everything above the surface looked calm.
No. If anything, the eyes of the Ares Guild members here held expectation and even goodwill.
Maybe we can build up our strength faster than Team Leader Choi expected.
But something more important needed my attention. I pushed the thought aside and spoke to the Branch Leader.
“Let’s skip the rest and get straight to the point.”
“Y-Yes?”
“Getting backup from the Guild is difficult, isn’t it? Ares Guild has more than one or two Gates to look after, and you’re sending people overseas too.”
“Pardon?”

“Even if someone leaves now, they’ll arrive too late. That A-rank Hunter on vacation probably has his phone and pager turned off while he enjoys himself. And if the people here rush in, there’s a good chance they’ll die without rescuing anyone. Am I right?”
“W-We don’t know that—”
“Come on. What we don’t know is how long the people inside can hold out.”
He gasped.
“It’s been fifteen minutes since the readings first started rising. Your team members could be dying in there right now.”
“W-Wait.”
The B-rank Hunter barely managed to stop me before continuing in a trembling voice.
“I know. I know that too. But... letting an outsider intervene would be a serious violation of Guild policy.”
“So?”
“Everyone here, including me, desperately wants to ask you for help. But we can’t. You already know that. You’ve heard about it.”
Anyone who worked as a Hunter had to know how strict and difficult Ares Guild’s rules were.

Lee Jungryong had selected only the most capable Hunters from each rank and locked them inside a tall, enormous cage. The fact that no Guild would accept a Hunter expelled from Ares Guild wasn’t some vague urban legend.
“Fuck...”
Sighs and curses came from all around me. I looked at the Ares Guild members, then asked abruptly, “One person? Or two?”
“Huh? What are you—”
“I have a feeling two people have died while you’ve been hesitating.”
“M-Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
“Hey, you by the measuring device. What’s the reading now?”
A C-rank Hunter who had kept chewing his nails in front of the device even after I arrived answered with something close to a scream.
“Three times! It’s passed three times the average magical power level!”
Everyone there knew what that meant.
A Mutated Gate.
The third Mutated Gate to erupt in the week since the new year began.

sentences.text: Brrrrrrr.
A smartphone suddenly began vibrating.
I, Im Kkeokjeong, and finally the Skeleton King checked the screen in rapid succession before opening our mouths one after another.
“What’s this?”
“T-Taekyung!”
“Oh.
Ohoho.
Look at this, you primitive humans.
A girl-group member has sent this body a DM.”
That fucking bastard.
I told him to stop screwing around on social media.
No wonder his phone was ringing when he isn’t even in the group chat.
I felt like stomping him until his illusion magic shattered, but that wasn’t important right now.
Which girl-group member...
No.
Another incident like this?
I barely swallowed my thoughts and stared at the smartphone screen.
Song Song had posted an urgent message in the group chat for the Peace Guild’s founding members, including Team Leader Choi and me.

Peace Guild └ Song Song: Hey hey heyyy └ Song Song: C-rank Gate anomaly. └ Song Song: Just heard from the government hotline. └ Song Song: They say the magical power readings are skyrocketing. └ Song Song: Fuck; why aren’t you reading this? └ Song Song: If you’ve read it, answer me, you crazy bastard. └ Butler Kim: Sorry.
I’m at the Blue House right now. └ Song Song: S-sorry;; I didn’t know it was you, Butler Kim Please get back to what you were doing... └ Butler Kim: Of course.
Have a happy day too, Song-i. ^^ └ Song Song: Huh.

Everyone but one person has read it? └ Song Song: Whoever’s seen this, get over there and check it out as fast as you can. └ Song Song: It’s far from me, and I have something to take care of, so I can’t go right away. └ Song Song: [Map attached] └ Song Song: ? └ Song Song: Oh, but now that I’ve checked, that Gate is kind of... └ Song Song: Just go for now. └ Song Song: Especially you, Jin Taekyung.
Reply as soon as you read this.
Where is it?
What kind of Gate would make her react like that?
I put my questions aside, left a reply saying I had seen the message, and checked the attached map.
The moment I did, I understood why Song Song had reacted that way.
“Ah.
Hmm.”
The location was definitely a little... awkward.
Im Kkeokjeong checked the map a beat later, and his face hardened.
“Taekyung.
Is this...?”
“Probably exactly where you think it is.”
The C-rank Gate marked on the map sat on prime land near a subway station in Bucheon.
It was also one of those Gates blessed with what Hunters called “luck.”
The monsters that appeared there were relatively easy to deal with compared to those in other C-rank Gates, and Magic Gems dropped frequently.
Im Kkeokjeong had worked as a Hunter in Bucheon for over ten years.
There was no way either of us wouldn’t know the Gate—or the name of the Guild that controlled it.
“This isn’t exactly welcome news...”
The Skeleton King looked up from the smartphone he had been fiddling with at Kkeokjeong’s low mutter.
“Humans.
Where is this place that has you making such a fuss?”
I answered quietly.
“The place isn’t the problem.
The owner is.”
“Hm?
The owner?”
“That’s right.”
Gates couldn’t be privately owned, but mid-sized Guilds and larger effectively controlled them through long-term leases.
And there wasn’t a person in Korea—or anywhere else in the world—who didn’t know the Guild that controlled the C-rank Gate at this address.
“Then who owns it?”
Kkeokjeong gave the Skeleton King a curt answer.
“Ares Guild.”
My eyes went to both of his arms before I could stop them.
The arms severed on someone’s orders had been reattached so cleanly you would never have known anything had happened.
But they were trembling faintly, as though he remembered the pain.
“Uncle Kkeokjeong.
No—hyung.”
“...I’m fine.”
The answer rang hollow.
His trembling was growing worse, and his expression had darkened.
As if he’d noticed the look on my face, he made an effort to relax his own.
“I’m telling you, I’m fine.
Now hurry up and go.
If the magical power readings are skyrocketing, we could have another Mutated Gate on our hands.”
Those bastards can handle it themselves.”
How am I supposed to go?
Not in this situation.
Especially to help them, of all people.
I stood rooted to the spot.
Kkeokjeong gave me a faint smile.
“Taekyung.”
“Yes?”
“I meant it when I said I’m fine.
Everyone who cut off my arms, Lee Jungryong included, has paid for it.
My rehabilitation’s practically finished, too.
These days, I’m happy spending time with my wife and watching the kids grow up.”
“Hyung...”
“I’m really fine, so hurry up and go.
There must be plenty of good people in Ares Guild, too.
If you let a petty personal reason stop you from helping, you’ll regret it for a long time.
At least, the Taekyung I know would.”
“I’d like to help too, but I can’t.
My rehabilitation isn’t quite done, and honestly, I’m not strong enough.”
He laughed heartily at his own forced joke.
I watched him for a moment, then nodded.
He was right.
The people facing danger inside the Gate weren’t enemies of mine or the Peace Guild.
If I sensed danger and possessed the strength to save someone from it, then stepping forward was the right thing to do.
That’s why we created the rescue team.
Maybe what I had to do had been decided the moment I obtained the System.
I gave Im Kkeokjeong a brief look of acknowledgment.
“I’ll be back soon.”
“All right.
Don’t get hurt.”
“Deal with it quickly and return, you wicked human.
As a reward, I shall show you this girl-group member’s selfie.”
I smiled warmly at the Skeleton King.
“Quit screwing around and follow me.
Or I’ll smash your smartphone as punishment.”
“...Understood.”
I should’ve done this from the start.
You trying to get yourself killed?
By the time we reached the C-rank Gate Orc Wasteland, marked on Song Song’s map, the area was full of frantic voices and shouting.
“The magical power readings are more than twice their usual level!”
“I know that.
What about the request for backup?”
“N-Nothing yet!”
“Fuck, there have to be people left at the Bucheon branch!
Tell them it’s urgent and ask again for at least one A-rank Hunter!”
“We already passed that along, but most of the A-rank Hunters stationed in Bucheon are deployed overseas, and some of the others are on vacation, so they’re refusing...”
“What?
Vacation?
They’re refusing because they’re on vacation?
Those fucking—!”
It happened in an instant.
A fist filled with rage slammed into a parked car.
Bam!
With a thunderous crash, the foreign car worth more than a hundred million won crumpled, sending large and small fragments flying in every direction.
That was when the flushed, hard-breathing B-rank Hunter spotted the Skeleton King and me.
“Hell, this is driving me crazy.
No matter how urgent things are, they should still be controlling access properly—”
His voice trailed off.
His eyes went wide.
“Huh?
Uh?
Huh?
Huhhhhh?”
Question after question spilled from his lips, his gaze fixed on my face.
The Skeleton King snorted and opened his mouth with a meaningful expression.
“Heh heh.
Yes, this human is that human.”
Why is this bastard stepping in and making a scene when I’m just standing here?
I shot the Skeleton King a wary look and cleared my throat.
Everyone who had been rushing around was now standing frozen, staring at us.
“Ahem.
In case anyone here doesn’t know who I am—”
“Jin Taekyung!”
“Lord Fuck!”
“Lord Sibu-leol!”
“...though I guess that won’t be necessary.”
I hated to say it myself, but at this point, I’d have to wonder if any Hunter who didn’t recognize my face was actually a monster.
“Is that r-really Jin Taekyung?”
“I don’t think he’s a fake Jin Taekyung.”
“Ah, that’s not what I meant...”
“It’s fine.
That isn’t important right now.”
I turned to the B-rank Hunter who had smashed the car.
“From what I’ve seen, you seem to be in charge here.
Am I right?”
“Y-Yes.
I’m Gwak Hangu, Branch Leader of Ares Guild’s Yeokgok Branch.”
He wasn’t even the Bucheon Branch Leader.
He was one of the dozens of lower Branch Leaders beneath him, and he was a B-rank Hunter.
It reminded me just how large Ares Guild was—and how deep its talent pool ran.
It also reminded me of something I’d briefly overlooked.
Maybe because of their public image, but the atmosphere here is better than I expected.
Ares Guild, the Peace Guild, and I had plenty of bad blood between us.
But that fight had taken place beneath the surface.
To people who knew nothing about it, everything above the surface looked calm.
No.
If anything, the eyes of the Ares Guild members here held expectation and even goodwill.
Maybe we can build up our strength faster than Team Leader Choi expected.
But something more important needed my attention.
I pushed the thought aside and spoke to the Branch Leader.
“Let’s skip the rest and get straight to the point.”
“Y-Yes?”
“Getting backup from the Guild is difficult, isn’t it?
Ares Guild has more than one or two Gates to look after, and you’re sending people overseas too.”
“Pardon?”
“Even if someone leaves now, they’ll arrive too late.
That A-rank Hunter on vacation probably has his phone and pager turned off while he enjoys himself.
And if the people here rush in, there’s a good chance they’ll die without rescuing anyone.
Am I right?”
“W-We don’t know that—”
“Come on.
What we don’t know is how long the people inside can hold out.”
He gasped.
“It’s been fifteen minutes since the readings first started rising.
Your team members could be dying in there right now.”
“W-Wait.”
The B-rank Hunter barely managed to stop me before continuing in a trembling voice.
“I know.
I know that too.
But... letting an outsider intervene would be a serious violation of Guild policy.”
“So?”
“Everyone here, including me, desperately wants to ask you for help.
But we can’t.
You already know that.
You’ve heard about it.”
Anyone who worked as a Hunter had to know how strict and difficult Ares Guild’s rules were.
Lee Jungryong had selected only the most capable Hunters from each rank and locked them inside a tall, enormous cage.
The fact that no Guild would accept a Hunter expelled from Ares Guild wasn’t some vague urban legend.
“Fuck...”
Sighs and curses came from all around me.
I looked at the Ares Guild members, then asked abruptly, “One person?
Or two?”
“Huh?
What are you—”
“I have a feeling two people have died while you’ve been hesitating.”
“M-Mr.
Jin Taekyung!”
“Hey, you by the measuring device.
What’s the reading now?”
A C-rank Hunter who had kept chewing his nails in front of the device even after I arrived answered with something close to a scream.
“Three times!
It’s passed three times the average magical power level!”
Everyone there knew what that meant.
A Mutated Gate.
The third Mutated Gate to erupt in the week since the new year began.
I clicked my tongue softly and looked straight at the Branch Leader.
“What are you waiting for?
Open it.”
“I wasn’t going to enter without the person in charge’s consent because it would be illegal.
But people need to be saved, don’t they?
So just say that I barged in while making a huge fucking scene and open it right now.”
He squeezed his eyes shut, his clenched fists trembling.
As I turned away from the silent Branch Leader, a trembling voice came from behind me.
“Let’s say...
I gave my consent.”
I’d thought he was a complete moron.
Maybe he was only a fool.

The Peace Guild will take you in.”

chapters.title: Chapter 562
paragraphs: The wasteland stretched endlessly in every direction.
There was no sun, but a dark light made of magical power hung in the air. Hundreds of Orcs roamed in packs, hunted by the Hunters who came here.
Or rather, that was how it used to be.
Boom. Boom. Boom.
The ground trembled. The magical power saturating the wasteland swelled as though it might burst at any moment, squeezing the breath from their lungs.
The Hunters panted raggedly, their breath carrying a sickly sweet smell.
More than a hundred Orcs lay sprawled around them. The Hunters stood back-to-back in a circle, but beyond the bodies, a monster army ten times that size was advancing.
“T-Team Leader.”
“Don’t worry. We’ll get out of here, whatever it takes.”
The Team Leader’s answer sounded hollow.
The one who had asked and the one who had answered both had some idea of the truth. None of them would leave this place alive today.
Even if they miraculously broke through the monster army’s encirclement, there was one opponent they would never be able to bring down.
—Kraaaargh!
The Orc Lord.
At the roar of the powerful mutant said to be born only once in a million, more than a thousand Orcs shrieked and struck their weapons together.
—Chweeek!
Clang! Crash-crash-crash!
Despair flickered in the Hunters’ eyes.
It’s over.
Under the Orc Lord’s command, the monster army had grown stronger. The Orcs were no longer a rabble roaming in groups of a few dozen, and the Hunters numbered fewer than twenty.
We can’t win this.
The thought flashed through every mind at once.
It would have been no different even if they could overwhelm Hunters of the same rank. Their pride in belonging to Ares Guild crumbled before the death bearing down on them.
“...Damn Mutated Gate.”
As someone muttered those words, the monsters filling the area began charging all at once.
At their head was the Orc Lord, the bastard they couldn’t kill hard enough.
—Karchwi! Kalipto!
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Shouting something unintelligible in the Demon Realm language, its massive body hurtled toward them.

The raid Team Leader gritted his teeth, raised his shield, and charged to meet it. His team members called out from behind him, but he focused every ounce of strength and attention on the enemy ahead.
“Come on!”
It was a great shout, forced out to drive away his fear.
Red light flashed in the Orc Lord’s eyes. The enormous ax in its hands came down toward the crown of the Team Leader’s head.
Whooosh—crash!
One strike. That was all it took.

The blow was unbelievably fast and powerful. With a thunderous roar, it shattered the Tower Shield reinforced with high-grade enhancement magic. The Team Leader’s eyes widened, the pain of his broken arms forgotten.
Whoooosh.
The ax had not touched him, but already it felt as though his side had been cut open.
His life flashed before his eyes, and the world slowed. A second blow was coming to split his body in two at the waist.
No. Not the second blow. The last.
The Team Leader closed his eyes. He had no desire to spend the final moment of his life looking at that ugly, fucking monster.
And in the next moment, along with the pitch-black darkness blocking his vision, a sharp sound of something cutting through the air pierced his ears.
Fwoooooosh—crack!
The pain he had been waiting for never came. It felt so strange that he wondered if this could really be death.
The Team Leader cracked his eyes open and gaped.
Less than five paces away, the Orc Lord’s three-meter-tall body stood motionless.
Its head was gone.
The world seemed to stop.
Humans and monsters alike stood frozen, staring. At that moment, only one thing moved across the endless wasteland.
Rrrrrr.
A single spear that had blown apart the Orc Lord’s head, pierced through the ground, and now trembled violently.
The Hunters knew who owned that spear, with its soft, almost mystical glow.
Jin Taekyung!
Along with the name that flashed through their minds like lightning, the spear lodged deep in the ground shot upward and flew into someone’s grasp.
Fwoooooosh—tap.
As though by agreement, they slowly turned their heads. Only then did they realize that the shadow of death looming over them had vanished without a trace.
“Little lambs wandering through the Mutated Gate. Run like fuck and get behind me.”
Tap. Tap.
The middle-aged man walked with a confident, unhurried stride.
That did not change when he entered the skyscraper overlooking the Blue House and the National Assembly.
“If you’re a Guild member, please show your access pass—”
“I haven’t seen you before. New here?”
“Pardon? Yes, I am.”
“Thought so. You must be new if you’re acting like this. Looks like your Team Leader didn’t tell you.”
The Security Team Hunter, who had been staring blankly at the middle-aged man, sucked in a startled breath.
“Oh! I’m sorry. I didn’t recognize you—”
“It’s fine. I’m busy, so let me through.”
“Y-Yes, sir.”

The checkpoint that everyone, Guild member or outsider, had to pass through could not stop the middle-aged man. He glanced at the young Hunter bowing hurriedly to him and continued toward his destination.
A voice was already coming through the tiny communicator implanted beneath his ear in a simple operation.
“He’s waiting for you.”
The middle-aged man barely moved his lips.
“Where?”
“Section A.”
The skyscraper rose 150 stories, but Section A appeared on neither its building plans nor its signs. Only a tiny fraction of its countless Guild members were allowed into that space.
The middle-aged man was one of them.
“Have the Teleport ready.”
“It’s ready. By the way, that new Security Team recruit, Deputy Team—ah, sorry. Team Leader.”
“It’s fine. Don’t worry about it.”
Even I’m not used to it yet, so what can you expect?
Before he could finish the thought, the voice continued.
“In any case, I’ll inform the Security Team Leader and have the recruit disciplined.”
Not a report. Not a suggestion. A notification.
At some point, that had become normal, but it still felt strange to him. He frowned faintly.
“Do we really need to go that far?”
“Team Leader?”
“...Never mind. Handle it as you see fit.”
“Yes. I’ll deal with it appropriately.”
“Appropriately” meant a pay cut at minimum. It might mean a demotion.
He thought of the young man who had stopped him and felt a twinge of discomfort, but there was nothing he could do. That was the policy of the Guild he belonged to.
No. It was their policy.
And ever since that incident, it’s been getting worse.
He had long known that the Guild was ruled with an iron fist, but its grip had tightened even further since the recent unfortunate incident.
Perhaps the new king was impatient because his subjects had yet to fully accept his right to the throne.
The middle-aged man let out a small sigh and spoke as he walked.
“Update me on the VIP.”
“He’s in a bad mood.”
“Am I imagining things, or did you say the same thing yesterday?”
“Well... he read this morning’s papers and—”
“That’s enough. Send me everything the VIP is reading. Scrape it all and send it to me. Right now.”

His magically secured smartphone vibrated as soon as he finished speaking. He tapped the screen lightly. The headlines of more than twenty morning newspapers that had left the presses only two or three hours earlier filled the display.

Unprecedented Crisis... What Do the Successive Mutated Gates Signify? Ominous Signs: Will the Nightmare of China’s Sichuan Province Come to Korea? Emergency Blue House Announcement: “We Have Signed an Agreement with the Peace Guild to Prevent Any Potential Crisis. Results So Far Are Encouraging.” Third Mutated Gate, but Zero Fatalities? Worldwide Praise for the Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team. American Grand Mage Magic Johnson: “The Peace Guild Is a Beacon for a New Era. Jin and Choi Are Good, Upright Young Men.” Former U.S. President Joseph Biden: “South Korea Is an Unquestionable Hunter Powerhouse, Home to Outstanding Young People Who Will Lead This Era. The Choi I Met Recently Is One of Them.” Chinese Chairman Xiao Yang: “Mr. Choi Is Another Unsung Hero. We Remember How He Risked His Life Fighting in Sichuan.” Japanese Prime Minister Shinjiro Koizumi Also Mentions Choi on Social Media: “As Far as I Know, Choi Is Korean. Therefore, He Is Not Japanese.” Korean Netizens React: “Thank God He Isn’t One of Our Idiots.” Remarks by World Leaders Spark Unprecedented Interest: “Who on Earth Is This Choi?” Sources Identify Him as Peace Guild Team Leader Choi Minwoo... S-Rank Hunter Jin Taekyung to Attend New Year’s “Communicating with the People” Press Conference with the President This Morning! ... ... ...
“...Whew.”
After reading them all, the middle-aged man rubbed his dry eyes. The fatigue he had forgotten came rushing back.
“Damn it.”
“Have you finished reading?”
“Yes. I’d have been better off not reading them.”
“I’m sorry to interrupt, but you should hurry.”
“I was about to. I’m almost there.”
Tap.
He stepped onto a faintly glowing magic circle. After he authenticated his fingerprint and infused the circle with mana, it recognized him and released a brilliant flash.
Flash!
A sensation like his entire body floating into the air seized him amid a dazzling halo of light.
The next moment, he opened his eyes and knew the Teleport to Section A had succeeded.
White marble and Magic Gems adorned the room. Around a dozen men and women in lightweight tailored suits bowed to him.
“Welcome, Team Leader.”
Many people, speaking with one voice.
He glanced at the subordinates moving like machines and slowly stepped off the magic circle.
“Where’s the VIP?”
“Alone in his private office.”
“Without security? I clearly told you to keep at least three people stationed in the hallway—”
Boom!
A muffled crash from somewhere cut him off. He could guess what had happened and clicked his tongue.
“I’ll go see him. Leave one person here and clear Section A.”
“Yes.”
His subordinates moved in perfect order as soon as he gave the command. Leaving them behind, he headed down the wide corridor.
At least fifty Magic Traps guarded it against intruders, but the access card around his neck concealed a device that let him pass safely through the minefield.
Bzzzt.
Head of Security Go Se-won
A red glow swept past him, and the mana churning on every side settled instantly.
Go Se-won crossed the seemingly endless corridor with practiced ease and stopped before a firmly closed door.
Knock, knock.
“It’s Go Se-won.”
An irritable voice came from the other side.
“Come in.”
Go Se-won slowly took hold of the knob and pushed the door open.
The office looked as though a bomb had gone off. In the middle of the wreckage, a man sat on a sofa, staring at him with a red glow in his eyes.
“You’re later than usual.”
Go Se-won bowed his head without a word. Amid the scattered debris, a nameplate gleamed.
Ares Guild Vice Guild Master Go Jun

It might mean a demotion.
He thought of the young man who had stopped him and felt a twinge of discomfort, but there was nothing he could do.
That was the policy of the Guild he belonged to.
No.
It was their policy.
And ever since that incident, it’s been getting worse.
He had long known that the Guild was ruled with an iron fist, but its grip had tightened even further since the recent unfortunate incident.
Perhaps the new king was impatient because his subjects had yet to fully accept his right to the throne.
The middle-aged man let out a small sigh and spoke as he walked.
“Update me on the VIP.”
“He’s in a bad mood.”
“Am I imagining things, or did you say the same thing yesterday?”
“Well... he read this morning’s papers and—”
“That’s enough.
Send me everything the VIP is reading.
Scrape it all and send it to me.
Right now.”
His magically secured smartphone vibrated as soon as he finished speaking.
He tapped the screen lightly.
The headlines of more than twenty morning newspapers that had left the presses only two or three hours earlier filled the display.
Unprecedented Crisis...
What Do the Successive Mutated Gates Signify?
Ominous Signs: Will the Nightmare of China’s Sichuan Province Come to Korea?
Emergency Blue House Announcement: “We Have Signed an Agreement with the Peace Guild to Prevent Any Potential Crisis.
Results So Far Are Encouraging.” Third Mutated Gate, but Zero Fatalities?
Worldwide Praise for the Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team.
American Grand Mage Magic Johnson: “The Peace Guild Is a Beacon for a New Era.
Jin and Choi Are Good, Upright Young Men.” Former U.S.
President Joseph Biden: “South Korea Is an Unquestionable Hunter Powerhouse, Home to Outstanding Young People Who Will Lead This Era.
The Choi I Met Recently Is One of Them.” Chinese Chairman Xiao Yang: “Mr.
Choi Is Another Unsung Hero.
We Remember How He Risked His Life Fighting in Sichuan.” Japanese Prime Minister Shinjiro Koizumi Also Mentions Choi on Social Media: “As Far as I Know, Choi Is Korean.

Therefore, He Is Not Japanese.” Korean Netizens React: “Thank God He Isn’t One of Our Idiots.” Remarks by World Leaders Spark Unprecedented Interest: “Who on Earth Is This Choi?” Sources Identify Him as Peace Guild Team Leader Choi Minwoo...
S-Rank Hunter Jin Taekyung to Attend New Year’s “Communicating with the People” Press Conference with the President This Morning! ... ... ...
“...Whew.”
After reading them all, the middle-aged man rubbed his dry eyes.
The fatigue he had forgotten came rushing back.
“Damn it.”
“Have you finished reading?”
“Yes.
I’d have been better off not reading them.”
“I’m sorry to interrupt, but you should hurry.”
“I was about to.
I’m almost there.”
Tap.
He stepped onto a faintly glowing magic circle.
After he authenticated his fingerprint and infused the circle with mana, it recognized him and released a brilliant flash.
Flash!
A sensation like his entire body floating into the air seized him amid a dazzling halo of light.
The next moment, he opened his eyes and knew the Teleport to Section A had succeeded.
White marble and Magic Gems adorned the room.
Around a dozen men and women in lightweight tailored suits bowed to him.
“Welcome, Team Leader.”
Many people, speaking with one voice.
He glanced at the subordinates moving like machines and slowly stepped off the magic circle.
“Where’s the VIP?”
“Alone in his private office.”
“Without security?
I clearly told you to keep at least three people stationed in the hallway—”
Boom!
A muffled crash from somewhere cut him off.
He could guess what had happened and clicked his tongue.
“I’ll go see him.
Leave one person here and clear Section A.”
“Yes.”
His subordinates moved in perfect order as soon as he gave the command.
Leaving them behind, he headed down the wide corridor.
At least fifty Magic Traps guarded it against intruders, but the access card around his neck concealed a device that let him pass safely through the minefield.
Bzzzt.
Head of Security Go Se-won
A red glow swept past him, and the mana churning on every side settled instantly.
Go Se-won crossed the seemingly endless corridor with practiced ease and stopped before a firmly closed door.
Knock, knock.
“It’s Go Se-won.”
An irritable voice came from the other side.
“Come in.”
Go Se-won slowly took hold of the knob and pushed the door open.
The office looked as though a bomb had gone off.
In the middle of the wreckage, a man sat on a sofa, staring at him with a red glow in his eyes.
“You’re later than usual.”
Go Se-won bowed his head without a word.
Amid the scattered debris, a nameplate gleamed.
Ares Guild Vice Guild Master Go Jun

chapters.title: Chapter 563
paragraphs: “You’re later than usual.”
Go Jun was wrong. Go Se-won’s watch was always accurate, and there was still plenty of time before he was due at work.
The one who was different today wasn’t Go Se-won. His superior was simply in an unusually foul mood.
Go Se-won bowed his head and kept his reply brief.
“I’m sorry.”
“Enough. Sit down.”
Being allowed to share Go Jun’s sofa was a privilege reserved for his closest aides. But before Go Se-won could sit on the Italian leather, he realized his superior’s anger was far from spent.
“Go Hyeon-woo, Rough News.”
The reporter, a man in his early thirties who had been given the floor, continued smoothly on the holographic TV.
“Just ten days into the new year, we’ve already had three Mutated Gates. What are your thoughts on that, Mr. President?”
Go Se-won glanced to the side.
Go Jun’s face was rigid, his eyes bloodshot. He was glaring at someone in the broadcast.
Ah.
Go Se-won remembered an article he had seen on his way in: Jin Taekyung and the President were holding an official New Year’s press conference.
He had more or less guessed what was happening, but watching the broadcast in his current state was no different from forcing Go Jun to swallow deadly poison.
Like showing a snuff film to a child.
Go Se-won had made up his mind and was bending down to pick up the remote from the floor when—
“Head of Security.”
Go Jun’s sharp voice cut in. He kept his eyes on the TV.
“Leave it.”
“...I’m only putting it back.”
Go Se-won hesitated, brushed the glass shards off the remote, and set it on the table in front of the sofa. On the TV, a man in his early forties had begun to speak.
“That’s a good question.”
He had a pleasant voice and a kind face, though there was nothing weak about him.
Baek Hanseong, Korea’s twenty-seventh President and the youngest ever elected at forty, continued in a gentle tone.
“As those of you who saw the Blue House’s official announcement yesterday afternoon will know, these successive Mutated Gates...”

His calm, unflustered manner inspired trust. Baek Hanseong was known for speeches that held an audience with his voice and slipped in humor so subtly it was hard to tell whether he was joking. Of course people listened.
By the time his lengthy speech—almost like the one he had given when announcing his presidential campaign—ended, the reporters broke into vigorous applause.
“It’s a campaign rally in there.”
Go Jun spat out the words, anger and mockery mingling in his voice. Then he muttered,
“How many of those bastards haven’t taken our fucking money, huh?”
“They couldn’t even breathe properly when Master was around. The youngest president in history? Anti-Ares Guild? That bastard Baek Hanseong was still beneath Master’s feet in the end.”
Humiliation and rage poured from his voice—emotions that had never been visible in him before.
Go Se-won lowered his eyes. His thoughts turned cold.
It’s true. Though it’s all in the past now.
Lee Jungryong’s influence had been immense.

Even before Cheon Taemin vanished, he had taken little interest in worldly affairs, like an immortal above the clouds. Lee Jungryong had remained on the ground, enjoying a position equal to—or greater than—a president’s or king’s.
Yes. That was how it was back then...
Politicians, business leaders, even the masters of the great Guilds that had risen into a new ruling class had bowed to Lee Jungryong.
He was a hero who had accomplished extraordinary deeds at Cheon Taemin’s side. As the vanished savior’s sworn brother, entrusted with full authority, he had been all but a pope.
Another Vatican.
The people of Korea called this 150-story skyscraper a second Blue House. In truth, it had been closer to the Vatican, where the pope lived.
Even people who freely cursed the incompetent government and lawmakers had been reluctant to speak against Ares Guild. Its name had been practically sacrosanct.
But...
“This world! The entire world! Is changing even now! We have entered a new phase!”
As the President’s voice rang out over unending applause, everything was changing.
With the fall of the giant that was Lee Jungryong, the shadow he had cast was beginning to lift.
And at the center of all these events, one person’s presence was exerting a powerful influence.

“But, my fellow citizens! The government and I will do everything in our power to keep you safe! Together with the young man seated beside me, we will protect Korea from every threat, at home and abroad!”
President Baek Hanseong did not say the young man’s name. He didn’t need to.
In the past few months, that man in his late twenties had become one of the most famous people in human history.
“Waaaaah!”
“Jin Taekyung! Jin Taekyung!”
“Fuck! Fucking fuck!”
Cheers louder than any before shook the press conference hall.
The young man who had been sleeping with his chin propped at an angle suddenly opened his eyes. Then he began clapping at a frantic speed while staring at the President.
“That was truly an incredible speech, Mr. President. Especially your final words. They moved me so deeply that I feel—”
“Um, that last part was about you, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
“Ah, wait a moment. My stomach really is churning. I think I’m suddenly getting motion sickness.”
“All of this is being filmed. Please wipe the drool off your face first—”
“Edit this out. Please. Okay?”
“I told you several times before we started. We’re live.”
“Right. Wow. Fuck, I’m screwed.”
“It’s live. I said it’s live, please. Hunter Jin Taekyung. Hello?”
The sight of the sweating President in his forties and the young hero in his twenties was broadcast in its entirety.
It was a broadcasting accident that would go down in the history of Korean television, but no one would scold or curse Jin Taekyung for it.
Even now, the people caught on camera were not frowning. They were smiling as they chanted his name.
Jin Taekyung.
Watching them, Go Se-won realized that the young man and the crowd’s reaction to him resembled something he had thought of only moments ago.
...Sacrosanct?
Compared to the sun that was Cheon Taemin, Jin Taekyung was still only a torch.
But one thing was undeniable. Jin Taekyung was walking the same path as the man remembered as an immortal hero.
And perhaps, regardless of what Jin Taekyung wanted, everything around him was trying to make him a second Cheon Taemin.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! I heard you suppressed all three Mutated Gates that appeared this time by yourself! Would you say a few words about that?”
“I wasn’t alone. There were two of us, though—”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! Kim Jin-mu, Mudang Daily!”
“I have a question about the Mutated Gates!”
Reporters with microphones swarmed toward him. Camera flashes went off without pause.
Go Se-won listened to questions flying in from every direction and felt a sudden sense of déjà vu.
This is...
Something was wrong with the flow of it. It looked natural at first glance, but everyone was being drawn in a direction someone had chosen for them.
Then an unfamiliar reporter shouted a question, and a chill ran down Go Se-won’s spine.
“I have a question about the third Mutated Gate you suppressed two days ago! According to information obtained by our newspaper, that Gate was being handled by a famous Guild—”
That’s it. So that’s what this is.
The moment enlightenment flashed through him, Go Se-won hurriedly reached for the remote.
Crunch!
Go Jun crushed the remote and the table beneath it. His eyes flashed red.
“I’m sure I told you to leave it.”
“But, Vice Guild Master...”
“I won’t say it twice.”
The blood vessels in his superior’s eyes had burst. The voice that followed was so chilling that it raised goose bumps.
“Stay still. Unless you want to die.”
Go Se-won swallowed a breath without meaning to and leaned back against the sofa as though his half-raised body had collapsed.
On the holographic TV, exactly what he had feared was happening.
“That’s right. Ares Guild handled that Gate. Well, it’s technically on a permanent lease, but as everyone knows, that’s practically ownership.”
The great Guilds’ monopoly on Gates was an open secret. Everyone knew; no one said it aloud.
Jin Taekyung had just exposed it without hesitation at a live, official Blue House press conference. And he wasn’t stopping there.
“What exactly happened? The magical power readings kept climbing, and no rescue team came.”
The reporters lunged at their prey. Quite a few had once taken Ares Guild’s dirty money, but money always gave way to more money.
“Wait. Are you saying a rescue team didn’t arrive even after you waited?”
Jin Taekyung nodded.
“Yes. They still hadn’t come fifteen minutes after the initial situation began. In the meantime, the magical power readings kept rising until the Gate became a Mutated Gate.”
“Does that mean it could have been dealt with before the Gate fully mutated if the rescue team had arrived on time?”
“Well, I can’t be a hundred percent certain, but if they had sent in even one A-rank Hunter early on, there probably would have been a high chance of resolving it without outside assistance.”
“Unlike the other Mutated Gates, the Guild responsible for this one has enormous numbers of Hunters and considerable financial resources. Why do you think it failed to send a rescue team in time?”
“The reason... Well, I’m not sure.”
Jin Taekyung thought for a moment, then tossed out an answer as though it were nothing.
“That family seems to be having a lot of trouble these days. Or should I say, the boss? Their management has changed, too, so I imagine there was probably some confusion here and there.”
Crack!
Something beside Go Se-won splintered. He closed his eyes.
It’s over.
An enormous Guild with vast manpower and capital. A change in management.
Those two clues were enough. Anyone who knew anything would understand without searching online. Even if no one had named it yet...

“It was a serious mistake, but what could I do? Fortunately, I happened to be there, so no one died. Personally, I’m just glad about that. Oh, and while I have this opportunity, I’d like to once again offer my deepest condolences to the deceased.”
“An excellent answer, Hunter Jin Taekyung. I’m certain the deceased would be grateful and proud of you.”
Damn it.
Go Se-won swore inwardly and opened his eyes.
Korea’s youngest President had the microphone again. He was delivering the final blow.

“Fortunately, we were able to bring this incident to an end without any fatalities, but our government intends to take the initiative and begin a thorough investigation. As President of Korea—and as a citizen—I find this Guild’s negligent response deeply regrettable. However, the wishes and legacy of the deceased, who was a great hero, have been passed on in their entirety to Hunter Jin Taekyung—”
The President’s words did not reach the end.
No—in precise terms, Go Se-won could no longer hear them.
He threw up his guard on instinct. Powerful mana shot out like a beam of light, shattering the holographic TV and tearing through everything around it.
Kwa-gwa-gwa-gwang!
The layered protective magic circles installed by ten high-ranking mages broke apart. Bulletproof glass and everything else shattered, then scattered into dust.
At the center of the destruction stood Go Jun, his eyes blood-red.
“How dare you! How dare you! How dare you—!”
Bang! Bang! Kwaaaang!
Everything had a limit.
Those last words had set fire to all the anger Go Jun had swallowed in the days since becoming Vice Guild Master.
“I’ll kill him! I’ll kill him no matter what!”
Kwaaaang!
Go Jun was Lee Jungryong’s de facto successor. But those who watched today’s press conference would see it differently.

They would believe that Jin Taekyung was the new hero—and the only person who had inherited the will of Cheon Taemin, who had still not revealed himself, and Lee Jungryong, who had died only recently.
“Jin Taekyung! Jin Taekyuuung!”
Go Jun screamed the name as though coughing up blood, all reason gone.
Go Se-won watched him, his gaze sinking deep.

chapters.title: Chapter 564
paragraphs: When a company grows, what’s the first thing it should do?
Everyone would answer differently, but every CEO has a dream tucked away somewhere in their heart.
Build a headquarters of their own.
Or should I call it an expansion in this case?
I was walking through the Guild House when I stopped and looked down at the work going on below.
“Hey, can somebody lift these materials with gravity magic?”
“All right, listen up. Any former tanks here? Hands up.”
“Me.”
“Over here, too. Why?”
“Why do you think? I’m putting you to work. Five F-ranks, over here. Bring an E-rank or two as well.”
Grrrind. Boom!
Smooth marble rose and fell through the air, while every swing of the muscle-bound giants’ sledgehammers smashed apart the solid concrete walls.
More than a hundred workers bustled about. They were all Awakened, which probably explained their astonishing pace.
Of course, their wages were astonishing too. But to a young tycoon with deep pockets, they were pocket change.
“The Guild House is getting cramped now that we have more people.”
Team Leader Choi had dropped that remark a few days ago and immediately taken action.
I’d heard he bought up all the nearby land, paying above market value for it, and started a massive expansion. I wasn’t going to argue.
It’s not my money.
Besides, I had other uses for my own money.
My fifty trillion won in untaxed assets was shrinking bit by bit as I spent it, but what I’d used so far was a drop in the ocean compared to what remained.
Fifty trillion won...
Even thinking about it again, it was an absurd amount of money. Like the figure of a man gradually approaching from beyond the corridor.
Swoosh.
A huge man glided through the air like a ghost and spoke without warning.
“Hey, I watched the press conference.”
Wait. What are you doing here, hyung?
I stared at Magic Johnson in disbelief before I finally managed to speak.
“What is it?”
“Why?”
“Why? That’s what I want to ask you. Why are you here again today?”
“I had something to take care of.”
“You didn’t come to use the bathroom, did you?”
“Of course not. I came to give Choi something. I figured I’d check on the progress while I was here.”
“Do you put emails in your cereal and eat them?”
“You’re not uncomfortable because I’m here, are you?”
“You didn’t think I was comfortable, did you?”
Magic Johnson let out a heavy sigh at my immediate reply.
“Hey, Jin. Harsh words hurt sensitive people like me.”
“...Hurt?”
I looked at his thick neck and iron-hard, bronze-colored arms.
He looks like a knife couldn’t cut him.
Damn, that Black dude is jacked.
With a build like that, he could quit being a mage and become a melee Hunter right now.

I wasn’t exaggerating, either. Search for “Magic Johnson’s staff,” and you’d get page after page of videos. Practically everyone knew the story of how he’d caved in an ogre’s skull with a single blow from a staff made for casting magic. People in fitness communities were still arguing over how much the thing weighed.
And he’s calling himself sensitive? Give me a break.
Magic Johnson caught the meaning of my lingering stare and shook his head.
“Not my body. My heart. The heart’s what matters, Jin.”
“Someone with a sensitive heart wouldn’t have survived the Great Cataclysm. You’re still alive and people call you a hero because you’re strong.”
“Hmm. I can’t tell if that was a compliment or an insult.”
“Take it as a compliment.”
Magic Johnson gave me a suspicious look, then went on.
“Anyway, I watched the press conference. There was a lot to read into it.”
The press conference...
I scratched the back of my head, embarrassed.

The official Blue House press conference I’d attended at the President’s request had caused an enormous stir. I’d heard domestic viewership had topped seventy percent, and it had made headlines abroad too.
Even two days later, related searches were holding firm near the top of the real-time rankings. They’d probably still be there a week from now.
“The broadcast mishap probably helped, and the ratings were pretty good. I didn’t know you watched it, Johnson.”
“What you’re up to is always news in the United States, Jin. President Baek’s final words must have meant a great deal to certain people. Me included.”
“Oh, that.”
“I wondered why he was praising Mr. Lee so much. Then he landed one hell of a blow, didn’t he?”
“Well, I wasn’t the one who landed it... But I bet it got under Go Jun’s skin.”
We weren’t living in the Warring States period, but anyone inheriting an organization that big still needed legitimacy.
And Go Jun, the new Vice Guild Master of Ares Guild, didn’t have much of it.

“Ares Guild is a vast empire. Even if he inherited the shares according to the will, he didn’t inherit all of Mr. Lee’s influence. If they had shared blood, he would at least have met certain expectations in Asian society. But he doesn’t, does he?”
“Lee Jungryong did have a son, but I heard he died young. He was an ordinary person who never Awakened, though, so he couldn’t have succeeded Lee even if he were still alive.”
Modern Guilds were like Murim sects. A bookish scholar couldn’t become the Sect Leader of Huashan; a Guild Master needed the power and authority of a Hunter.
Magic Johnson knew that as well as anyone. He nodded.

“True. Sseokkochoon, on the other hand, has the skill, whatever his faults as a person. I heard he passed the S-rank Hunter qualification assessment with an incredible score. The news got buried almost immediately under everything else that’s been happening, of course.”
“His name is Go Jun, not Sseokkochoon. And anyway, that bastard was Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security.”
“That’s nowhere near enough. He needs the support of the other founding heroes who made Ares Guild what it is today. But...”
“He didn’t have time.”
“Exactly. Time. Mr. Lee probably wrote that will to prepare for the worst without ever imagining he’d die so easily.”
But he had died in the end, and Go Jun had inherited the crown before he could firmly establish himself as the successor.
Being Head of Security was proof that he had been one of Lee Jungryong’s closest aides, but there were many difficulties involved in inheriting an enormous organization like Ares Guild.
Even with Lee Jungryong’s will, it would not be easy for elderly veterans to respectfully serve a fresh-faced man in his thirties as their superior.
On top of that, Go Jun himself had rapidly fallen apart since Lee Jungryong’s death.
And in the middle of all that, his legitimacy was openly denied during an official Blue House press conference with seventy percent viewership...
President Baek Hanseong’s remark had been both subtle and sharp.
He had indirectly criticized Ares Guild over the Mutated Gate while praising Lee Jungryong’s achievements and presenting me as the man who would carry on his legacy.
The whole thing was staged.
The press conference had been a joint production by President Baek Hanseong, who had shown an anti-Ares stance since his days as a lawmaker, and Team Leader Choi.
They’d won over reporters, fed them questions, and steered the conversation where they wanted it to go. The script and cast had been prepared from start to finish.

If Lee Jungryong had still been alive, they would have scrapped the plan. But Go Jun lacked the power to put down the new underdog’s rebellion, so we finished the shoot without a hitch—with a domestic rating of seventy percent and the foreign press shining its spotlight on us.
“Either way, it’s another small victory. We should have a glass of champagne. Where’s Choi?”
“He was busy before, but lately he’s been swamped. If we’re lucky, he might be in his office.”
“He’s not.”
Magic Johnson shrugged.
“I just stopped by there on my way here.”
“Ah. Something else must have come up.”
That was nothing new. Team Leader Choi might have held a team leader’s title, but he’d effectively been the Guild Master from the start. By now, the public saw him that way too.
He was probably one of the busiest people in Korea.
“Hey, Jin. Want to walk with me?”
“Sure. As long as we stay away from secluded spots.”
“You’ve gotten funnier.”
“...Tell me that was a joke.”
I walked faster without answering. Magic Johnson followed, stepping through the air as if he were floating, and grumbled.
“Jin, why do you keep making me out to be some kind of weirdo?”
“Because you keep saying weird things.”
“I’m joking, obviously. Besides, I have preferences. You’re not my type. That guy over there, maybe.”
I followed his gaze to a tall, handsome man walking past.
“I haven’t seen him before. New Guild member?”
“Someone might mistake you for a member of our Guild. How many people here do you even know?”
“That’s ridiculous! You think I wouldn’t remember a handsome man like that?”
Why is he so adamant about it?
He had an uncanny eye for this sort of thing. I sighed and answered.
“I don’t really know his name, but he is new. C-rank, I think?”
“I don’t know who his former Guild Master was, but he must be crying tears of blood. With looks like that, he’d draw plenty of attention. He could do well as a star Hunter.”
“His former Guild Master is probably crying blood over something else. He was humiliated at the press conference.”
“Oh. Then was he...?”
“Yeah. He used to belong to Ares Guild.”
Leaving Ares Guild for Peace Guild meant more than a simple transfer. Magic Johnson seemed to understand.
“Living proof that the impregnable fortress is starting to shake. How many have come over from Ares so far?”
“Not many. Around ten.”
“The number isn’t the point. It proves a crack has opened.”
I gave a small nod. If outsiders could see the crack, it was probably much bigger on the inside.
Of course, we can’t rule out the possibility that Go Jun sent him deliberately as a spy.
That was why he had been accepted only after a thorough verification process, and I heard they planned to deploy him in actual operations little by little.
Even with the System, I couldn’t read people’s minds. Team Leader Choi’s intelligence network would be a great help there.
“What’s that place?” Magic Johnson asked. “The security looks serious.”
I’d been walking in silence, lost in thought. I looked up and saw the titanium-alloy door he was pointing at.
“Oh, that? It’s a training room.”
“The training room? A training room?”
“Yeah.”
“My goodness. What kind of training room needs security like that?”
Magic Johnson gave an incredulous laugh.
“Five overlapping spells? I can understand not wanting anyone to watch you train, but isn’t that excessive inside a Guild House?”
“Who knows?”
I kept my answer short. The room had been prepared for only a handful of people.
More specifically...
For people training in the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique.
I hadn’t even told Magic Johnson about it. Access was limited to Team Leader Choi, Butler Kim, Song Song, and Im Kkeokjeong.
“Judging by the security, it doesn’t seem like a space open to every Guild member.”
I nodded at his observation.
“That’s exactly right. It’s for the Guild’s founding members, including me.”
“Hmm. A secret, then. Now you’ve awakened my curiosity as a mage.”
“Put it back to sleep.”
“That’s cruel. I can’t even take a quick look?”
I hesitated, then waved him off.
“No. Someone’s inside.”
“Who? Choi?”
“No.”
A sudden bitterness came over me.
“Someone who needs to train more desperately than anyone.”
“There is someone like that.”

I couldn’t see him now, but I could picture him clearly: a middle-aged Hunter training over and over, sweat pouring off him like rain. He tried harder than anyone to act as though he was fine, even as he willed himself back onto his feet with his spirit brutally crushed.
Maybe it’s time to start that...
The thought that flashed through my mind slowly took shape as Magic Johnson spoke again.
“Can’t be helped. Give this to Choi when you see him.”
“Huh? Give him what?”
“This.”
Swoosh.
A small object slipped inside my clothes on a faint current of qi.
I felt the chip and looked up. The Grand Mage’s face had turned grave.
“It’s not just Korea and the United States. Magical power readings are soaring all over the world. Up seven percent from last year. That lucky number has never felt so ominous.”

chapters.title: Chapter 565
paragraphs: After Magic Johnson left, I texted Team Leader Choi, who still wasn’t answering his phone, then headed straight for my private office on the top floor of the Guild House.
Bang.
Hearing the door slam shut behind me, I dropped heavily onto the floor.
The place was over a hundred pyeong, but all it held was a small desk and a single chair. It was called an office. Really, it was a training ground.
I immediately took out my smartphone and inserted the chip.
Click.
The latest model I’d bought recently had every feature imaginable, including holographic video playback, which had become common over the past decade or so.
Bzzzz.
Light spilled from the phone’s projector with a faint hum. I quickly used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to draw the blackout curtains, then focused on the footage filling the dark office.
Crackle. Crackle.
Static.
Boom! Kraaang!
A deafening roar.
Shrieeeek!
A monster’s cry.
“Aaaah!”
A human scream.
It all mingled before my eyes, then scattered. The place, lined with tents and buildings of every size, had become a horrific battlefield.
Mutated Gate.
The words flashed through my mind.
Then—
“In the name of Allah!”
“Waaaaah!”
A group in military caps and turbans charged forward, shouting at the top of their lungs. They looked Arab, and their bodies were soaked in someone else’s blood.
There was even a child among them, no older than an elementary school student.
A child...

There was no way these people were regular soldiers. Their mismatched clothing had already told me as much. They had to be Arab rebels—the kind who had stained the Middle East with blood even before the Great Cataclysm.
Then, the next moment—
“Aaaah! G-God is great!”
Along with the terrified cry of a little boy, countless firearms in their hands opened fire.
Rat-tat-tat-tat!
Whoosh! Boom!
Enough firepower to riddle ordinary humans with holes poured out at once. But their enemies were neither ordinary nor human.
Kraaang!
A huge blaze rose from the explosion. The rebels stood panting as black smoke filled the area. Then the smoke parted, and a flash of light cut through it.
Whoosh. Shing!
One strike was enough. Dark red magical power swept outward in a crescent, cutting through everything in its path.
Necks, waists, chests. The wounds differed, but the result was the same.
Death.
Splaaash!
A beat later, fountains of blood stained the sand red.
The surviving rebels stared wide-eyed at the grisly deaths of nearly twenty comrades.
“M-Masoud!”
“My God...”
But their god neither appeared nor answered his followers. In his place came a monster clad from head to toe in green armor.
Chirr. Chiriririk.
A triangular head. Two quivering antennae. Forelegs curved like scythes.
It was a mantis, enormous enough to look down at a grown man. Powerful magical power radiated from its body, which bore not a scratch from the rebels’ attack.
“G-Giant Mantis...”
Someone groaned the name. The huge foreleg swept through the air again.
Whoom. Shing!
A rebel frozen in place split down the middle. Magical power shot from the foreleg like an arrow, tearing through everything around it.
Shing! Shing! Kraaang!
People. Weapons. Even the tanks hastily sent into battle could not stop it.
Explosions and screams rang out as the attacks cut in every direction. Before long, there were five Giant Mantises, and they leaped among the humans.
Chit-chit-chit!
Chiriiit!
Crack! Splaaash!
With every strange cry, limbs flew from the roughly hundred rebels, and blood sprayed across the sand.
Those who fought while calling on their god and those who fled in terror alike fell in the desert, never to rise again.
“Aaah! Aaaaah!”
Shunk!
A scythe-like foreleg slashed through the rebel’s back and shattered his breastbone.
Having struck down the last rebel still resisting, the Giant Mantis suddenly turned. A red eye protruding from the side of its head fixed on the camera.
It found the camera.
It saw the camera, and I saw it.
Then, just as the Giant Mantis sensed something strange and cautiously began approaching the camera—
“May the flames of God descend upon this place. Fire Rain!”
Fwoosh!
An aged voice rang out. At the same instant, dozens of fireballs formed from mana came hurtling over the Giant Mantis’s shoulder like meteors.
Chiririririt!
It shrieked and swung a foreleg at them.
Boom!
The impact dyed the screen—no, everything around it—red. Dozens of Hunters appeared in the distance and raced across the battlefield through the bursting fireballs.
“Allahu Akbar!”
“God is great! Kill every one of those devils!”
Krrk, chiiit!
Humans and monsters. Monsters and humans.
The two sides began killing each other again. But I couldn’t watch the battle to its end.
Crackle. Crackle. Pop!
In an instant, the hologram filling the room vanished amid a burst of heavy static.
“...Whew.”
I let out the breath I’d been holding and picked up the phone I’d set aside. The list on the chip held more than twenty videos I hadn’t watched yet.
Fuck. How long has it been since the last batch? And there’s already more.
Worldwide magical power readings had risen seven percent over the previous year.
Some idiots might call that only seven percent. But a drop of even a few percentage points in the air’s oxygen concentration would cause an uproar. This was proof that things were going to hell.
No. Maybe...
This could be the beginning of the second Great Cataclysm.
As I watched the remaining videos one by one, my fears began to take shape.
Europe. The Middle East. West Africa. Southeast Asia... What is this, some kind of worldwide festival?
Changes were already happening all over the world at once.

A new Gate appeared among the green hills of Switzerland, where I could picture Patrache running around with a dog biscuit in his mouth. Elsewhere, rebels and regular soldiers rained shells on each other while monsters poured from low-rank Gates left unattended.
A few places had been prepared well enough to suppress the outbreaks early. In more than half the videos, though, the monsters were defeated only after causing considerable damage.
This...
I kept replaying the footage, my brow furrowing. The damage wasn’t simply due to poor Gate defenses.
But insight wasn’t the only thing that came to me then.
Ding.
I heard the faint chime of the elevator, followed by the presence of two people drawing closer. Recognizing my uninvited guests, I reached out.
Fwoosh.
A warm breeze swept through the room. Qi flowed from my palm and gently pushed the door open, revealing familiar faces.
“What took you so long? I texted you ages ago.”
“I’m sorry. I couldn’t be reached for a while.”
I’d been about to lay into the latecomers, but I tilted my head.
“Couldn’t be reached? Did you go into a Gate or something?”
“Something like that.”
“...Either you did or you didn’t. What’s ‘something like that’ supposed to mean?”
“Butler Kim and I had somewhere to stop. It was important, so it couldn’t be helped.”
Team Leader Choi stepped inside as he answered. Butler Kim followed, closed the door, and gave me a slight nod.
Haven’t seen him in a while.
Butler Kim had hardly shown his face at the Guild lately. What important business had the two of them been handling?
It had been about a week since I’d seen him, and the question lingered. But something more urgent needed our attention. Team Leader Choi knew it too.
“We can discuss this later. For now, we should check the information Mr. Johnson gave us.”
“Oh. Here.”
I played the footage again. By the time they’d gone through every video and the attached materials, both their faces had hardened.
“Worldwide magical power readings up seven percent?”
Butler Kim’s usually gentle voice came out cracked.
“Young Master.”
“Yes. It’s progressing faster than we expected. This is serious.”
Seven percent wasn’t merely a rise. Surge was closer to the mark.
And that sharp change in magical power levels was especially obvious in the footage.
“The monsters...”
I nodded and finished Team Leader Choi’s thought.
“Yeah. They’ve gotten fucking strong.”
Rising magical power readings meant stronger monsters. The Giant Mantis in the first video had held its own even after taking a hit from Fire Rain.
It was like watching Chikorita get a tan from Charizard’s flames.
Type advantages were supposed to mean something. But as magical power readings climbed, the monsters were growing strong enough to shrug those advantages off.
In a situation this fucked, places that kept their precious Hunters deployed in minimal numbers as a precaution were bound to be overwhelmed.
To sum it up...
“We’re fucked. It’s five minutes to a complete shitshow.”
Things were moving at a ridiculous pace. Keep this up, and monsters might be part of the weather forecast by the end of the year.
A pretty weathercaster would point to a map of the Korean Peninsula no bigger than a booger and explain it all:

“Tomorrow, goblins are expected to fall in Cheorwon, Gangwon Province, instead of heavy snow. They’re expected to pile up to a height of twenty meters, so residents should grab their shields and antidotes and evacuate immediately.”
Fuck. Heavy snow is annoying enough. Now monsterfall? Seriously?
Just imagining monsters pouring down from the sky made my heart shrivel.
Of course, I wasn’t going to sit around twiddling my thumbs until then. I had to stop Korea from turning into Hell Peninsula, whatever it took.
I’d kept this possibility in mind, but... it’s definitely happening too fast.
I’d thought we had a little more time. The prospect of bringing forward that thing—the plan I’d been working on little by little since Murim—weighed on me.
That was when Team Leader Choi spoke.
“At this point, we can’t keep it hidden any longer.”
He turned off the hologram. His voice was low.
“It’s already beyond what can be concealed at a national level. The longer we wait to tell people, the worse the confusion will be.”
This wasn’t a wave that would pass. It was a tsunami that might sweep whole cities away.
“What are you planning to do, Team Leader Choi?”
“Gate defenses come first right now. We need a breakwater before the tsunami hits.”
“Strengthen the Gate defenses?”
“That will leave us with fewer Hunters for raids, and we won’t be able to make full use of all the Gates Peace Guild owns. But I know which matters more.”
“That’s a relief.”
I let out a quiet laugh. Team Leader Choi knew where to draw the line. He had grand ambitions of swallowing Ares Guild, but he also knew when to push forward and when to stop.
That’s the biggest difference between him and Lee Jungryong.

“Yes?”

What?
My eyes widened. Team Leader Choi went on.
“I told you I had important business to take care of.”
“Then that important business was...?”

“A major figure in Ares Guild. A war hero who helped my maternal grandfather bring the Great Cataclysm to an end. Once the friend Lee Jungryong trusted most. And now the leader of the largest faction within Ares threatening Go Jun.”
His voice was gentler than ever, with thorns hidden beneath it.
“Everything crumbles from the inside.”

sentences.text: After Magic Johnson left, I texted Team Leader Choi, who still wasn’t answering his phone, then headed straight for my private office on the top floor of the Guild House.
Bang.
Hearing the door slam shut behind me, I dropped heavily onto the floor.
The place was over a hundred pyeong, but all it held was a small desk and a single chair.
It was called an office.
Really, it was a training ground.
I immediately took out my smartphone and inserted the chip.
Click.
The latest model I’d bought recently had every feature imaginable, including holographic video playback, which had become common over the past decade or so.
Bzzzz.
Light spilled from the phone’s projector with a faint hum.
I quickly used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to draw the blackout curtains, then focused on the footage filling the dark office.
Crackle.
Crackle.
Static.
Boom!
Kraaang!
A deafening roar.
Shrieeeek!
A monster’s cry.
“Aaaah!”
A human scream.
It all mingled before my eyes, then scattered.
The place, lined with tents and buildings of every size, had become a horrific battlefield.
Mutated Gate.
The words flashed through my mind.
Then—
“In the name of Allah!”
“Waaaaah!”
A group in military caps and turbans charged forward, shouting at the top of their lungs.
They looked Arab, and their bodies were soaked in someone else’s blood.
There was even a child among them, no older than an elementary school student.
A child...
There was no way these people were regular soldiers.
Their mismatched clothing had already told me as much.
They had to be Arab rebels—the kind who had stained the Middle East with blood even before the Great Cataclysm.
Then, the next moment—
“Aaaah!
G-God is great!”
Along with the terrified cry of a little boy, countless firearms in their hands opened fire.
Rat-tat-tat-tat!
Whoosh!
Boom!
Enough firepower to riddle ordinary humans with holes poured out at once.
But their enemies were neither ordinary nor human.
Kraaang!
A huge blaze rose from the explosion.
The rebels stood panting as black smoke filled the area.
Then the smoke parted, and a flash of light cut through it.
Whoosh.
Shing!
One strike was enough.
Dark red magical power swept outward in a crescent, cutting through everything in its path.
Necks, waists, chests.
The wounds differed, but the result was the same.
Death.
Splaaash!
A beat later, fountains of blood stained the sand red.
The surviving rebels stared wide-eyed at the grisly deaths of nearly twenty comrades.
“M-Masoud!”
“My God...”
But their god neither appeared nor answered his followers.
In his place came a monster clad from head to toe in green armor.
Chirr.
Chiriririk.
A triangular head.
Two quivering antennae.
Forelegs curved like scythes.
It was a mantis, enormous enough to look down at a grown man.
Powerful magical power radiated from its body, which bore not a scratch from the rebels’ attack.
“G-Giant Mantis...”
Someone groaned the name.
The huge foreleg swept through the air again.
Whoom.
Shing!
A rebel frozen in place split down the middle.
Magical power shot from the foreleg like an arrow, tearing through everything around it.
Shing!
Shing!
Kraaang!
People.
Weapons.
Even the tanks hastily sent into battle could not stop it.
Explosions and screams rang out as the attacks cut in every direction.
Before long, there were five Giant Mantises, and they leaped among the humans.
Chit-chit-chit!
Chiriiit!
Crack!
Splaaash!
With every strange cry, limbs flew from the roughly hundred rebels, and blood sprayed across the sand.
Those who fought while calling on their god and those who fled in terror alike fell in the desert, never to rise again.
“Aaah!
Aaaaah!”
Shunk!
A scythe-like foreleg slashed through the rebel’s back and shattered his breastbone.
Having struck down the last rebel still resisting, the Giant Mantis suddenly turned.
A red eye protruding from the side of its head fixed on the camera.
It found the camera.
It saw the camera, and I saw it.
Then, just as the Giant Mantis sensed something strange and cautiously began approaching the camera—
“May the flames of God descend upon this place.
Fire Rain!”
Fwoosh!
An aged voice rang out.
At the same instant, dozens of fireballs formed from mana came hurtling over the Giant Mantis’s shoulder like meteors.
Chiririririt!
It shrieked and swung a foreleg at them.
Boom!
The impact dyed the screen—no, everything around it—red.
Dozens of Hunters appeared in the distance and raced across the battlefield through the bursting fireballs.
“Allahu Akbar!”
“God is great!
Kill every one of those devils!”
Krrk, chiiit!
Humans and monsters.
Monsters and humans.
The two sides began killing each other again.
But I couldn’t watch the battle to its end.
Crackle.
Crackle.
Pop!
In an instant, the hologram filling the room vanished amid a burst of heavy static.
“...Whew.”
I let out the breath I’d been holding and picked up the phone I’d set aside.
The list on the chip held more than twenty videos I hadn’t watched yet.
Fuck.
How long has it been since the last batch?
And there’s already more.
Worldwide magical power readings had risen seven percent over the previous year.
Some idiots might call that only seven percent.
But a drop of even a few percentage points in the air’s oxygen concentration would cause an uproar.
This was proof that things were going to hell.
No.
Maybe...
This could be the beginning of the second Great Cataclysm.
As I watched the remaining videos one by one, my fears began to take shape.
Europe.
The Middle East.
West Africa.
Southeast Asia...
What is this, some kind of worldwide festival?
Changes were already happening all over the world at once.
A new Gate appeared among the green hills of Switzerland, where I could picture Patrache running around with a dog biscuit in his mouth.
Elsewhere, rebels and regular soldiers rained shells on each other while monsters poured from low-rank Gates left unattended.
A few places had been prepared well enough to suppress the outbreaks early.
In more than half the videos, though, the monsters were defeated only after causing considerable damage.
This...
I kept replaying the footage, my brow furrowing.
The damage wasn’t simply due to poor Gate defenses.
But insight wasn’t the only thing that came to me then.
Ding.
I heard the faint chime of the elevator, followed by the presence of two people drawing closer.
