chapters.title: Chapter 566
paragraphs: What Team Leader Choi told me was the last thing I’d expected.
If magical power readings hadn’t been rising so sharply, I might have found this even more interesting.
A traitor?
A few Ares Guild members had come over to our side after the recent incident, but those were ordinary transfers. Rank-and-file Guild members like them were a dime a dozen at Ares.
A traitor on the inside was another matter.
Especially if he’s a big shot.

In Murim terms, he was a master of the previous generation. Having lived through the Great Cataclysm already made him interesting enough, but he was also the head of an internal faction powerful enough to threaten Go Jun.
Oh, now that’s appetizing.
“...Mr. Jin Taekyung?”
“Oh. Yes? What is it?”
“Here, take this first.”
It was a handkerchief. I blinked at him, and Team Leader Choi pointed awkwardly at my chin.
“I don’t know why, but there’s a lot of drool around your mouth.”
“It looks like it’s about to dr—ugh.”
What was with the ugh? A man could drool a little.
I wiped my mouth with my sleeve and got straight to the point.
“So who is he? The traitor.”
“Traitor. I doubt he’d like hearing that. How should I put it... He’d probably prefer to be called a business partner. Or Ares Guild’s next Vice Guild Master.”

“What kind of bullshit is that? It sounds like you’ve more or less struck a deal with him already. If it looks like betrayal, I’m calling him a traitor. Is he just telling himself otherwise to feel better?”
Team Leader Choi wasn’t the one who answered.
Butler Kim had been listening quietly. Now he spoke in a low voice.
“He craves honor.”
“Honor?”
“As people grow old and death draws closer, they often begin to cling to honor. No... Looking back on the life he’s led, greed might be the better word.”
Had I ever heard Butler Kim speak so harshly about anyone?
Lee Jungryong was the only person who came to mind. But what Butler Kim had shown Lee was anger. What he felt toward this man sounded more like contempt.
He almost never shows his feelings this openly.
From everything I’d seen and heard, Butler Kim was practically up there with Jesus and Buddha. Sure, he seemed to have had a fiery temper when he was young, but that was a long time ago.
Who the hell is this guy?

Judging by how severely he was criticizing the man’s entire life, they clearly knew each other well. But there were so many Ares Guild executives who wielded considerable influence that no name immediately came to mind.
As if he’d read my mind, Team Leader Choi spoke.
“Director Song. Song Cheonwoo is that kind of man.”
“Song Cheonwoo. Song Cheonwoo...”
The name sounded vaguely familiar. I searched for it on my phone and found a short profile.
Calling it a profile was generous. It had his date of birth, a few lines about his life, and two photos of the same man side by side at the top of the page, one from his younger days.
Still, it gave me something.
“Huh? Wait, is this guy...?”
“Have you seen him before?”
“I think so. There’s a framed picture of him in the hallway at the Hunter training center. Isn’t there?”
“You probably remember correctly. He briefly served as head of the Hunter training center a little over twenty years ago.”
“Oh.”
That was before the rules for the position had been properly established, but even then, only a top ranker with an impressive record could become head of the Hunter training center.
He really is a big deal.

For someone with his reputation, though, there was barely anything about him online. A man like this had to have plenty of accomplishments and stories to his name, yet his biography was only two or three lines long. His profile hadn’t even been updated in three years.
Three years ago?
Even a B-list celebrity would have more written about them. I frowned and tapped around for another source.
Bzz.
My phone vibrated faintly. A notification appeared on the screen.
Team Leader Choi └ Team Leader Choi: [File attached]
“What’s this all of a sudden?”
“I thought it would be faster. I doubt you’ll find much detail about him through an Internet search.”
“Come on. In this day and age?”
“Then I’ll delete the attachment.”
“But since you went to the trouble of sending it, I’ll read it.”
“Listen until someone finishes speaking Korean.”
Having offered Team Leader Choi that valuable advice, I opened the file. Unlike the online profile, it ran to dozens of pages.
I started taking in the information on the screen as fast as I could.
Name: Song Cheonwoo. Age: seventies.

He was an A-rank Hunter, naturally. Twenty years ago, he’d ranked as high as third in Korea. The two people ahead of him had been Cheon Taemin and Lee Jungryong, which told me he was a formidable fighter in his own right.

During the Great Cataclysm, he’d taken part in dozens of major battles. His work had apparently been more prominent overseas than at home: he’d received medals from eight countries, including the United Kingdom, Germany, and France.
And the rest of his career? There was too damn much to go through line by line.
“That’s some résumé. How did I not remember him?”
“He isn’t as well known in Korea as you might think. Most of his notable work was overseas, and he spent very little time working here after the war.”
“Ah. Right.”
His stint as head of the Hunter training center stood out, but according to the file, he’d resigned voluntarily before serving even half of his four-year term.
The official reason was his health, but...
“Two months later, appointed Director of Ares Guild’s European regional branch.”
I read the line aloud. Team Leader Choi nodded.
“That was his last position here. From twenty years ago until now, he’s remained the Director of Ares’s European regional branch. That’s why younger Hunters like you and me know so little about him.”
“Leave yourself out of it. You probably know Song Cheonwoo better than almost anyone. Am I wrong?”
“What makes you think so?”
“Who do you take me for, an idiot? Cheon Tae—sorry. Anyway, you seem to have quite a connection with that person, and Butler Kim knows him too, so there has to be a link. To give one more example...”
“What would that be?”
I didn’t have to think long. I pulled up a fairly recent memory and tossed out a phrase.
“Director of the European regional branch.”
“You told me that when you were at Ares, they kept shuttling you between overseas branches. I think Europe was one of them.”
A faint smile touched Team Leader Choi’s lips. I’d got it right.
“You remembered.”
“I keep telling you I’m not that stupid.”
“You’re right. Song Cheonwoo followed my maternal grandfather long before I was born. When I was assigned to the European branch five years ago, Song used his authority as Director to keep me close.”
“So did you know each other personally...?”
“On second thought, ‘keep me close’ isn’t the right expression. I should say he kept me under surveillance and isolated me.”
“...So you weren’t close at all. Got it. Go on.”
“From what I saw of him, Song Cheonwoo’s abilities don’t match the scale of his ambition. Though his rival at the time may simply have been too formidable.”
His rival? I didn’t have to think about that one.
“Lee Jungryong.”
“A mountain can have only one master. Even if they were once friends, one of them had to leave.”
Now it made sense. Why a man of Song Cheonwoo’s stature had left Korea so soon after the war. Why he’d spent twenty years stuck in an impressive-sounding post overseas.
He was demoted.
There was no other way to put it. Lee Jungryong had won their power struggle inside Ares Guild and exiled his rival to Europe. Over time, Song had faded from people’s memories.
No. Knowing Lee Jungryong, he’d made sure Song was forgotten.
Which means this file...
It wasn’t a collection of Internet gossip. Experts had compiled and polished this investigation. It went beyond research and came close to surveillance.
So that’s why he sent it separately.
Unlike the online profile, whose updates had stopped five years ago, the final page of the file dealt with recent events.

November 15, 2046. Discussed retirement at a party hosted by the British ambassador. Audio file attached. November 28, 2046. Purchased a two-story mansion of approximately 300 pyeong in Samseong-dong, Seoul. Appears intended as a residence after retirement. January 1, 2047. Arrived through Incheon International Airport. Met secretly with key members of Ares Guild’s board of directors. Exact number and names attached in supplementary materials. January 2, 2047. Attended Lee Jungryong’s funeral. Held a second meeting with major political and business figures and key members of the Guild. January 4, 2047. Ares Guild’s board held an official meeting to appoint a Vice Guild Master. Go Jun’s appointment was approved after three revotes.
The file was packed with information on Song Cheonwoo’s movements over the past two months. Just reading it, I could see exactly how his thinking had changed.
“Song Cheonwoo’s got his heart set on a comeback.”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“In November, he subtly expressed his intention to resign in a private setting, and he even purchased a mansion in Korea where he could stay after retirement. But...”
“Lee Jungryong died.”
“Yes. No one could have expected that. To a man on the verge of retirement, it must have looked like one last chance.”
“And his opponent wasn’t Lee Jungryong anymore. It was Go Jun. With you on his side, he must have thought he could win.”

Go Jun had needed three revotes to secure the Vice Guild Master position. That alone was proof. Song Cheonwoo, seventy-something and about to retire, had been gathering support wherever he could for one last shot.
“Pretty energetic for a man his age.”
Team Leader Choi gave a quiet laugh.
“That’s the magic of power, isn’t it? It’s given me an opportunity too.”
“Sure. That’s all well and good, but...”
What was this feeling? My mouth felt gritty, as though I’d chewed a handful of sand.
I stared at Song Cheonwoo’s face on the screen. Then Team Leader Choi spoke softly beside me.
“And if this works... a grandparent and grandchild may finally see each other again after a long time.”
What hand?
I blinked at him. A moment later, I understood.
“No way.”
The savior of the twenty-first century. The immortal hero who had saved humanity and would live forever in its memory—yet had vanished one day behind an invisible curtain.
Cheon Taemin.
He hadn’t shown himself even when his only blood relative was in danger. Not even after Lee Jungryong died.
And his maternal grandson, born of the hero’s blood, spoke with the smile gone from his face.
“Song Cheonwoo knew where my maternal grandfather was.”
Go Se-won, the Head of Security, gazed at the teacup in front of him.
The cup, once warm, had gone cold. Tea-leaf dregs floated in the little tea he’d deliberately left behind.
Looks just like me.
He’d been staring at the cup for over an hour since making his report. At this point, he was almost getting attached to it.

But there was nothing else he could do. His job was to report the facts as they were, not to give orders. And considering the gravity of what he’d reported, he was fortunate his superior hadn’t smashed everything around him as he had last time.
He’s thinking it over. The longer he thinks, the better the decision should be.
His superior’s next words proved how badly he’d misjudged the situation.
“Kill him.”
“Sir?”
“I said kill him. His children. His grandchildren. His daughters-in-law. All of them.”
Thud.
A file folder slipped off the table, struck the floor, and fell open.
Go Jun stared at the three Korean characters spelling Song Cheonwoo, then at the photograph of a man with prominent cheekbones. Fire flickered in his eyes.
“Has this old bastard gone senile...?”

It had his date of birth, a few lines about his life, and two photos of the same man side by side at the top of the page, one from his younger days.
Still, it gave me something.
“Huh?
Wait, is this guy...?”
“Have you seen him before?”
“I think so.
There’s a framed picture of him in the hallway at the Hunter training center.
Isn’t there?”
“You probably remember correctly.
He briefly served as head of the Hunter training center a little over twenty years ago.”
“Oh.”
That was before the rules for the position had been properly established, but even then, only a top ranker with an impressive record could become head of the Hunter training center.
He really is a big deal.
For someone with his reputation, though, there was barely anything about him online.
A man like this had to have plenty of accomplishments and stories to his name, yet his biography was only two or three lines long.
His profile hadn’t even been updated in three years.
Three years ago?
Even a B-list celebrity would have more written about them.
I frowned and tapped around for another source.
Bzz.
My phone vibrated faintly.
A notification appeared on the screen.
Team Leader Choi └ Team Leader Choi: [File attached]
“What’s this all of a sudden?”
“I thought it would be faster.
I doubt you’ll find much detail about him through an Internet search.”
“Come on.
In this day and age?”
“Then I’ll delete the attachment.”
“But since you went to the trouble of sending it, I’ll read it.”
“Listen until someone finishes speaking Korean.”
Having offered Team Leader Choi that valuable advice, I opened the file.
Unlike the online profile, it ran to dozens of pages.
I started taking in the information on the screen as fast as I could.
Name: Song Cheonwoo.
Age: seventies.
He was an A-rank Hunter, naturally.
Twenty years ago, he’d ranked as high as third in Korea.
The two people ahead of him had been Cheon Taemin and Lee Jungryong, which told me he was a formidable fighter in his own right.
During the Great Cataclysm, he’d taken part in dozens of major battles.
His work had apparently been more prominent overseas than at home: he’d received medals from eight countries, including the United Kingdom, Germany, and France.
And the rest of his career?
There was too damn much to go through line by line.
“That’s some résumé.
How did I not remember him?”
“He isn’t as well known in Korea as you might think.
Most of his notable work was overseas, and he spent very little time working here after the war.”
“Ah.
Right.”
His stint as head of the Hunter training center stood out, but according to the file, he’d resigned voluntarily before serving even half of his four-year term.
The official reason was his health, but...
“Two months later, appointed Director of Ares Guild’s European regional branch.”
I read the line aloud.
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“That was his last position here.
From twenty years ago until now, he’s remained the Director of Ares’s European regional branch.
That’s why younger Hunters like you and me know so little about him.”
“Leave yourself out of it.
You probably know Song Cheonwoo better than almost anyone.
Am I wrong?”
“What makes you think so?”
“Who do you take me for, an idiot?
Cheon Tae—sorry.
Anyway, you seem to have quite a connection with that person, and Butler Kim knows him too, so there has to be a link.
To give one more example...”
“What would that be?”
I didn’t have to think long.
I pulled up a fairly recent memory and tossed out a phrase.
“Director of the European regional branch.”
“You told me that when you were at Ares, they kept shuttling you between overseas branches.
I think Europe was one of them.”
A faint smile touched Team Leader Choi’s lips.
I’d got it right.
“You remembered.”
“I keep telling you I’m not that stupid.”
“You’re right.
Song Cheonwoo followed my maternal grandfather long before I was born.
When I was assigned to the European branch five years ago, Song used his authority as Director to keep me close.”
“So did you know each other personally...?”
“On second thought, ‘keep me close’ isn’t the right expression.
I should say he kept me under surveillance and isolated me.”
“...So you weren’t close at all.
Got it.
Go on.”
“From what I saw of him, Song Cheonwoo’s abilities don’t match the scale of his ambition.
Though his rival at the time may simply have been too formidable.”
His rival?
I didn’t have to think about that one.
“Lee Jungryong.”
“A mountain can have only one master.
Even if they were once friends, one of them had to leave.”
Now it made sense.
Why a man of Song Cheonwoo’s stature had left Korea so soon after the war.
Why he’d spent twenty years stuck in an impressive-sounding post overseas.
He was demoted.
There was no other way to put it.
Lee Jungryong had won their power struggle inside Ares Guild and exiled his rival to Europe.
Over time, Song had faded from people’s memories.
No.
Knowing Lee Jungryong, he’d made sure Song was forgotten.
Which means this file...
It wasn’t a collection of Internet gossip.
Experts had compiled and polished this investigation.
It went beyond research and came close to surveillance.
So that’s why he sent it separately.
Unlike the online profile, whose updates had stopped five years ago, the final page of the file dealt with recent events.
November 15, 2046.
Discussed retirement at a party hosted by the British ambassador.
Audio file attached.
November 28, 2046.
Purchased a two-story mansion of approximately 300 pyeong in Samseong-dong, Seoul.
Appears intended as a residence after retirement.
January 1, 2047.
Arrived through Incheon International Airport.
Met secretly with key members of Ares Guild’s board of directors.
Exact number and names attached in supplementary materials.
January 2, 2047.
Attended Lee Jungryong’s funeral.
Held a second meeting with major political and business figures and key members of the Guild.
January 4, 2047.
Ares Guild’s board held an official meeting to appoint a Vice Guild Master.
Go Jun’s appointment was approved after three revotes.
The file was packed with information on Song Cheonwoo’s movements over the past two months.
Just reading it, I could see exactly how his thinking had changed.
“Song Cheonwoo’s got his heart set on a comeback.”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“In November, he subtly expressed his intention to resign in a private setting, and he even purchased a mansion in Korea where he could stay after retirement.
But...”
“Lee Jungryong died.”
“Yes.
No one could have expected that.
To a man on the verge of retirement, it must have looked like one last chance.”
“And his opponent wasn’t Lee Jungryong anymore.
It was Go Jun.
With you on his side, he must have thought he could win.”
Go Jun had needed three revotes to secure the Vice Guild Master position.
That alone was proof.
Song Cheonwoo, seventy-something and about to retire, had been gathering support wherever he could for one last shot.
“Pretty energetic for a man his age.”
Team Leader Choi gave a quiet laugh.
“That’s the magic of power, isn’t it?
It’s given me an opportunity too.”
“Sure.
That’s all well and good, but...”
What was this feeling?
My mouth felt gritty, as though I’d chewed a handful of sand.
I stared at Song Cheonwoo’s face on the screen.
Then Team Leader Choi spoke softly beside me.
“And if this works... a grandparent and grandchild may finally see each other again after a long time.”
What hand?
I blinked at him.
A moment later, I understood.
“No way.”
The savior of the twenty-first century.
The immortal hero who had saved humanity and would live forever in its memory—yet had vanished one day behind an invisible curtain.
Cheon Taemin.
He hadn’t shown himself even when his only blood relative was in danger.
Not even after Lee Jungryong died.
And his maternal grandson, born of the hero’s blood, spoke with the smile gone from his face.
“Song Cheonwoo knew where my maternal grandfather was.”
Go Se-won, the Head of Security, gazed at the teacup in front of him.
The cup, once warm, had gone cold.
Tea-leaf dregs floated in the little tea he’d deliberately left behind.
Looks just like me.
He’d been staring at the cup for over an hour since making his report.
At this point, he was almost getting attached to it.
But there was nothing else he could do.
His job was to report the facts as they were, not to give orders.
And considering the gravity of what he’d reported, he was fortunate his superior hadn’t smashed everything around him as he had last time.
He’s thinking it over.
The longer he thinks, the better the decision should be.
His superior’s next words proved how badly he’d misjudged the situation.
“Kill him.”
“Sir?”
“I said kill him.
His children.
His grandchildren.
His daughters-in-law.
All of them.”
Thud.
A file folder slipped off the table, struck the floor, and fell open.
Go Jun stared at the three Korean characters spelling Song Cheonwoo, then at the photograph of a man with prominent cheekbones.
Fire flickered in his eyes.
“Has this old bastard gone senile...?”

chapters.title: Chapter 567
paragraphs: “Has this old man gone senile...?”
Go Se-won had lost count of how many times he’d faced those red eyes.
Go Jun’s gaze had gone beyond ominous. It was chilling now, and Go Se-won swallowed before he realized he was doing it.
But he was the Head of Security.

He was the only person who could put the brakes on Go Jun’s rampage, if only for a moment. And after all that deliberation, his superior was about to make a disastrous move. Go Se-won had a duty to talk him out of it.
“Vice Guild Master.”
Go Jun looked at him. A chill ran down Go Se-won’s spine, but he managed to speak.
“What you just said... Were you serious?”
Go Jun frowned.
“Of course not. Do I look like that much of an idiot to you, Team Leader Go?”
“Oh.”
Go Se-won had waited for the answer with a sinking feeling, so he let out a quiet sigh of relief.
Come to think of it, the idea was absurd.
Go Jun had grown far more violent lately, but surely he wouldn’t order every member of Song Cheonwoo’s family killed...
“Don’t kill them. Capture them and bring them here.”
“Excuse me?”
“Didn’t you hear me?”
Of course he had.
Go Se-won was an A-rank Hunter who could hear a mosquito’s wings flutter from ten meters away.
He asked again because he’d heard something he would rather not have heard at all.
“Would you repeat that, please?”
Bang! Crack!
The table, replaced only a few days ago, was smashed to pieces again. Flames blazed in Go Jun’s eyes.

“I said bring them here. I don’t care if it’s the grandchild Song Cheonwoo fusses over every day or some white grandmother he met at a retirement community in Europe. Anything I can use to get a grip on that old man’s life!”
His shout rang through the room, the veins standing out on his neck. Then his voice dropped.
“So, Team Leader Go. Send the men out and bring them here. Now.”
“What? Didn’t you hear me this time either?”
There would not be a third warning.
Realizing that there was nowhere left to retreat, Go Se-won lowered his head slightly.
“No, sir. I heard you clearly.”
“Then get moving. Ah, where did you say that old man’s family lived?”
“On the outskirts of London. The whole family lives together in a huge mansion converted from a castle.”
A life worthy of European nobility.
Song Cheonwoo had been able to live that way after losing the power struggle within Ares because Lee Jungryong had allowed it and supported him.
Old affection between friends? Mercy? To Lee Jungryong, those words were about as useful as cabbage.
He could afford to look down on a rival several moves behind him. That arrogance was the ease of a man with overwhelming power.
He kept his only political rival completely under his thumb. His successor’s first thought is to kidnap the man’s family.
It came down to temperament. To the difference in what each man was made of.
Go Se-won pushed the thought from his mind and continued.

“There are about thirteen of them, counting his children, their spouses, and his grandchildren. Some of the grandchildren commute to school by helicopter or Teleportation magic circle. We receive updates on their locations in real time.”
“You’ve taken measures? Since when?”
“Since he entered the country. I reported it at the time, but you seemed extremely busy, so I took care of it on my own authority.”
“You’re good at your job, Team Leader Go. I thought you’d lost your touch after getting married.”
“...Thank you.”
Praise and a jab in the same breath. Go Se-won bowed his head again. Go Jun looked down at him, then muttered in a cold voice.
“Come to think of it, what an ungrateful old man. He should have thanked me for letting him keep his position this long. And he stabs me in the back?”
Song Cheonwoo should have retired before the new year.
But the Monster Wave in China and Lee Jungryong’s death had rekindled the ambition the old lion had never quite abandoned. The hyenas caught its scent and quietly lined up behind him.
The influential members of the elder generation, just before a sweeping change of generations.
They were the pack of hyenas.
“Damn old bastards.”
Go Jun sprang to his feet and began pacing. Then he spoke again.
“What about him?”
Him.
He hadn’t said a name, but Go Se-won knew immediately whom he meant.
The greatest threat wasn’t the old lion leading the hyenas. It was the young male lion prowling the grassland beyond Ares Guild’s high fences, waiting for his chance.
“Choi Minwoo has returned to Peace Guild.”
“You’re certain he met that old man, Song Cheonwoo?”
Go Se-won answered at once.
“They met in secret and concealed themselves with advanced illusion magic, but yes. We’re certain.”
“What about Director Hong? Can we trust him?”
Director Hong was one of the elders who, like Song Cheonwoo, had been approaching honorary retirement. He was also the helpful informant who had told them about today’s meeting.
Go Se-won nodded.
“Yes. He read the situation quickly.”
“He’s always been quick on the uptake. Still, don’t let your guard down. He’s known Song Cheonwoo for over thirty years.”
“We’re watching his every move without letting him notice.”
Betrayal upon betrayal. Everyone was scrambling to get what they wanted. Director Hong had simply chosen comfort and survival for the years he had left.
“And the security team?”
“All thirty members are on constant standby.”
The security team was handpicked from Ares Guild’s elite. Every member was an A-rank Hunter. Their abilities went without saying, and their loyalty was just as impressive.
The master they served had changed suddenly, but these were men who would handle a murder without batting an eye.
And I’m no different.
Go Se-won had done all kinds of dirty work under Lee Jungryong.
Sometimes he was disgusted by what he’d become, but until now, he’d managed to live with it.
That work had made him wealthier than most people could dream of being. It had also let him meet his beautiful, loving wife after he turned forty and finally get married.
But...
Have I been doing this too long?
Maybe this was the hypocrisy of a man who had forgotten what it meant to go hungry. Maybe it was the disgust he’d spent years suppressing.
Or maybe it was his son, who had only just started walking, and his wife, who had recently become pregnant with their second child.
Song Cheonwoo’s youngest grandson is about Sangho’s age, isn’t he?
The thought of ordering his men to abduct a child too young to speak left him uneasy.
No. We’ll be lucky if it ends with kidnapping.
Go Jun had become a different man in the past month or two. No one knew what he might do next, now that he’d grown so violently ruthless.
Even Lee Jungryong, who had never been particular about his methods, had left children alone...
“Team Leader Go.”
Go Se-won straightened at his superior’s voice.
“Yes, Vice Guild Master.”
“Prepare the security team. You know what I mean, don’t you?”
The gentleness in Go Jun’s voice made Go Se-won’s hair stand on end. After a brief silence, he answered.
“Yes.”
“I’d like results as soon as possible. Is that too much to ask?”
Go Se-won already knew his answer.
He was just another piece of shit in the same shit pit. He’d stepped into the mud long ago. It was too late to turn back.
“No, sir. I’ll bring you good news by tomorrow at the latest.”
“Good. You may go.”
That was the end of the conversation.
Go Se-won walked out of the office on stiff legs and raised a hand to his ear.
Beep.
The communicator he’d switched off for a while gave a faint chirp and lit up.
“Report the current personnel.”
As soon as the brief command ended, a sharp voice came through the communicator.
“Team One, all members standing by. Nothing to report.”
“Team Two, all members standing by. Nothing to report.”
“Team Three, all members standing by. Nothing to report.”
The three teams had thirty members in total. Even within Ares Guild, where only the best were gathered, they had been chosen from among the best of the best.

Go Se-won possessed overwhelming skill befitting the Head of Security, but even he could not easily guarantee victory if five or more of these men joined forces. No matter how thoroughly the target had prepared, there was no way to stop them.
“Orders from the Vice Guild Master. Finish your preparations and assemble in one hour. Our final destination is...”
Go Se-won paused, then said in a low voice,
“London, United Kingdom.”
They wouldn’t need passports for this trip.
Advanced illusion magic and special makeup concealed their faces, names, and even fingerprints. Exactly one hour later, they gathered before a long-distance Teleportation magic circle.
Then they walked into the dazzling light.
Whoosh!
The next morning, Go Jun received the news he’d been waiting for from his Head of Security.
“It was a success. Of the security team’s thirty members, two were killed, but the rest—”
“What about Song Cheonwoo’s family?”
“...We captured them all alive. Teams One and Two have stayed behind, disguised as the existing security personnel. They’ve taken control of the mansion and are keeping watch.”
“Well done. I knew I could count on you, Team Leader Go.”
“The team paid a heavy price. We made the most of our advantage and took them by surprise, but security at the mansion was tighter than expected. Two of our men were killed...”
“It’s fine. You took care of the aftermath, right?”
After a short silence, Go Se-won answered.

“Yes. We’ve taken control of their communications network, and we used enchantment magic to learn every code word and reporting procedure. Even if someone contacts them, they’re unlikely to suspect much.”
“How long can you keep it up?”
“Four days at most.”
“That’s long enough to finish this. Contact that old man, Song Cheonwoo. Tell him Lunar New Year is coming and it’s been too long since we saw each other.”
Go Jun laughed aloud, imagining the look on the old traitor’s face when they met. Then he looked up.
“Oh, and Team Leader Go.”
Go Se-won had been watching his superior with an unreadable expression. He quickly composed himself.
“Yes, Vice Guild Master.”
“Sorry. The good news made me forget.”
“Oh.”
“You know how distracted I’ve been lately. You understand, don’t you?”
“Not at all, sir!”
His answer came out more forcefully than before.
Of course. No matter how much he’s changed, he wouldn’t do that.
Go Se-won waited for the words he’d been hoping to hear. Instead, Go Jun’s next remark stopped him cold.
“You’re always working hard. Take this for yourself.”
Slide.
Go Jun set a spotless white envelope on the table.
Considering the nature of the matter, it obviously contained a check for a substantial sum. Judging from his experience, it was probably at least ten billion won.
But an envelope of bonus money wasn’t what he’d wanted.
Still...
“Thank you, Vice Guild Master.”
Go Se-won accepted the envelope politely and bowed deeply.
By then, his gaze had grown deep and unreadable as he stared at the man reflected in the spotless, gleaming marble.
Martial arts are made up of countless movements.
Thrusting and cutting. Striking and smashing.
Link movements like those together, and they become a form.
Whoosh! Bang!
I punched into empty space. Compressed air exploded, and my hair fluttered.
I continued through the forms against an imaginary opponent.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh! Slash!
Everything I’d seen and learned firsthand, every insight I’d gained, flowed into the forms. One led naturally into the next without pause.
Forms linked together. A combat sequence.
Boom-boom-boom!
The edge of my hand. My elbow. My shoulder. Every part of my body turned and twisted as I struck in every direction.
Learning martial arts had taught me once again that a weapon didn’t have to be a blade.
Anything that can hurt an enemy is a weapon.
That was why training mattered. With enough of it, you could break a neck with one finger or split a rock with a rusty carving knife.
Whoom! Bang!
My heel came down like lightning and slammed into the ground. That strike would have crushed the skull of even an A-rank monster with a hard outer shell.
But there were no enemies to bring down here.
The hundred or so corpses—human or monster—existed only in my imagination.
I let out a quiet breath.
Clap, clap, clap.
A vigorous round of applause rang out from behind me.

The next morning, Go Jun received the news he’d been waiting for from his Head of Security.
“It was a success.
Of the security team’s thirty members, two were killed, but the rest—”
“What about Song Cheonwoo’s family?”
“...We captured them all alive.
Teams One and Two have stayed behind, disguised as the existing security personnel.
They’ve taken control of the mansion and are keeping watch.”
“Well done.
I knew I could count on you, Team Leader Go.”
“The team paid a heavy price.
We made the most of our advantage and took them by surprise, but security at the mansion was tighter than expected.
Two of our men were killed...”
“It’s fine.
You took care of the aftermath, right?”
After a short silence, Go Se-won answered.
“Yes.
We’ve taken control of their communications network, and we used enchantment magic to learn every code word and reporting procedure.
Even if someone contacts them, they’re unlikely to suspect much.”
“How long can you keep it up?”
“Four days at most.”
“That’s long enough to finish this.
Contact that old man, Song Cheonwoo.
Tell him Lunar New Year is coming and it’s been too long since we saw each other.”
Go Jun laughed aloud, imagining the look on the old traitor’s face when they met.
Then he looked up.
“Oh, and Team Leader Go.”
Go Se-won had been watching his superior with an unreadable expression.
He quickly composed himself.
“Yes, Vice Guild Master.”
“Sorry.
The good news made me forget.”
“Oh.”
“You know how distracted I’ve been lately.
You understand, don’t you?”
“Not at all, sir!”
His answer came out more forcefully than before.
Of course.
No matter how much he’s changed, he wouldn’t do that.
Go Se-won waited for the words he’d been hoping to hear.
Instead, Go Jun’s next remark stopped him cold.
“You’re always working hard.
Take this for yourself.”
Slide.
Go Jun set a spotless white envelope on the table.
Considering the nature of the matter, it obviously contained a check for a substantial sum.
Judging from his experience, it was probably at least ten billion won.
But an envelope of bonus money wasn’t what he’d wanted.
Still...
“Thank you, Vice Guild Master.”
Go Se-won accepted the envelope politely and bowed deeply.
By then, his gaze had grown deep and unreadable as he stared at the man reflected in the spotless, gleaming marble.
Martial arts are made up of countless movements.
Thrusting and cutting.
Striking and smashing.
Link movements like those together, and they become a form.
Whoosh!
Bang!
I punched into empty space.
Compressed air exploded, and my hair fluttered.
I continued through the forms against an imaginary opponent.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Slash!
Everything I’d seen and learned firsthand, every insight I’d gained, flowed into the forms.
One led naturally into the next without pause.
Forms linked together.
A combat sequence.
Boom-boom-boom!
The edge of my hand.
My elbow.
My shoulder.
Every part of my body turned and twisted as I struck in every direction.
Learning martial arts had taught me once again that a weapon didn’t have to be a blade.
Anything that can hurt an enemy is a weapon.
That was why training mattered.
With enough of it, you could break a neck with one finger or split a rock with a rusty carving knife.
Whoom!
Bang!
My heel came down like lightning and slammed into the ground.
That strike would have crushed the skull of even an A-rank monster with a hard outer shell.
But there were no enemies to bring down here.
The hundred or so corpses—human or monster—existed only in my imagination.
I let out a quiet breath.
Clap, clap, clap.
A vigorous round of applause rang out from behind me.

chapters.title: Chapter 568
paragraphs: Clap, clap, clap.
A vigorous round of applause rang out. At the same time, the voice of someone I’d been aware of for a while echoed through the room.
“Impressive. Very impressive.”
Click.
Shiny black dress shoes came toward me. The man wearing them had on suit pants with razor-sharp creases and a leather coat that reached his knees. He stopped in front of me.
“Mr. Jin, I’ve heard a great deal about you... but coming all the way here was worth it. You’re even more impressive than I expected.”
I had no idea what was going on, and it must have shown. He answered with an easy smile.
“There’s no need to be so flustered. The time has simply come.”
“The time has come?”
“Yes. Did you think you were the only hero in this world?”
“What?”
“From this moment on, you’ve become part of a much greater world. You simply don’t know it yet.”
A sharp current ran through my entire body. I let out a low groan and glared at the unwelcome guest.
“What the hell are you?”
“Not many people know my true identity.”
He gave a quiet laugh and continued.
“As for who I am...”
“No, I’m asking what the hell you’re doing.”
“Huh?”
His eyes went round, as if this wasn’t how the scene was supposed to go. I stared at him for a moment, then waved a hand.
“Never mind. Keep going. You’ve still got lines left, right?”
“Can I?”
“Sure. Finish them.”
He cleared his throat and gave me a solemn look.
“My name is King Fury. Director of Barrier...”
Wham!
“Urgh.”
I punched him in the face. The Skeleton King staggered like a drunk, and I followed up with a string of punches.
Wham! Wham! Crack!
“Urgh! Ugh! Wait! Wait! My jawbone!”
“Like hell I’m waiting, you fucker.”
This guy needed a beating.
While some people were working their asses off day and night to build a bright future even in times like these, he had suddenly popped up dressed like a movie character.
I’d wondered why he was wearing a leather coat all of a sudden.
“Having fun? Are superhero movies that much fun?”
The Skeleton King, who’d been getting pummeled nonstop, suddenly set his face and raised a thumb.
“Fucking awesome.”
“I hate them three thousand.”
“What the hell is wrong with you?”
“Wait! You’ve cracked a bone!”
Wham! Wham!
“How can you call yourself human? Huh?”
“I—I’m a monster!”
“This bastard only claims he’s a monster when it suits him. Is your species a buffet? You just pick whichever one you want?”
Wham! Wham!
“Wait! Stop for real this time! I’ve got an orbital fracture!”
That was a surprisingly precise diagnosis for a monster.
The medical terminology made my fist hesitate. The Skeleton King promptly slipped away, trembling with humiliation.
“You vile human. You aren’t even a person.”
“My God. Did a monster just say that to me?”
“You devil. When Judgment Day comes, may you be cast into hell.”
“Have you been going to church lately? That’s a strange choice of words for you.”
The Skeleton King froze for an instant, then cleared his throat.
“A human woman...”
“What?”
“A beautiful human woman spoke to me first. I met her at the crosswalk up ahead. She said if I followed her, we could all sing songs and eat good food.”
“So I went. It wasn’t particularly fun, but it wasn’t bad. A man called a pastor must have recognized my nobility, because he even presented me with a gift.”
“My God.”
An undead monster had gone to church. Was this for real?
While I was still at a loss for words, the Skeleton King lowered the collar of his coat, which he’d turned up like a middle-aged man from forty years ago.
“Heh heh. Behold.”
I’d doubted my ears before. Now I doubted my eyes.
Peeking proudly out from between the coat collars was none other than a cheap cross necklace.
“This is the symbol of a noble king.”
Wasn’t it a symbol of exorcism?

For a moment, I wondered whether he’d met an exorcist rather than a pastor. But Magic Johnson’s illusion magic was flawless. There wasn’t the slightest hint that anything about the Skeleton King was out of place.
His social media followers, whose numbers had grown exponentially, were proof of that.
Click.
“...You’re taking a selfie right now? Want me to smash your phone?”
“I bought it with my own money. A vile human has no right to say anything, so keep your mouth shut.”
A monster who’d adapted to capitalism. Maybe that was the real monster.
And since he’d bought it himself, I couldn’t argue. It wasn’t even some undisclosed sponsorship. He’d paid for it with the money he’d recently received from the Peace Guild.

“I’m quite a high earner among humans now. I hear the people of this world sort themselves into classes by annual income. Mine is a full six hundred million won! Heh heh. And I’ll be making that much for the next ten years!”
Welcome to ten years of slavery.
If the Skeleton King were a Hunter, he’d qualify for S-rank with room to spare. Yet Team Leader Choi had him working for a mid-level Hunter’s salary.
Team Leader Choi’s cruelty made me want to give Hyuk Mujin’s balls a sharp tap.
“What’s that look for?”
“Nothing. Don’t worry about it. Keep earning lots of money.”
The Skeleton King narrowed his eyes and looked me up and down.
“Suspicious. And not just now. You’ve been acting strangely these past few days.”
“Who? The undead monster who went to church?”
“You, vile human!”
He shouted, then went on.

“You keep getting lost in thought even inside Gates. A man without so much as a finger joint’s worth of culture starts drawing pictures and taking notes. Yesterday, you even turned down an emergency rescue call, so I had to go in person!”
For a monster, he was pretty perceptive. Maybe because I’d spent more time with him than anyone else lately.
I scratched my chin and looked at him.
“I get what you’re trying to say. So?”
“Huh?”
“What do you want from me? I’m not allowed to think? I can’t draw a few pictures and take notes?”
“I—I didn’t say that.”
He faltered, then rallied.
“Even so, that emergency rescue call—”
“I put it off because I could. They still had you.”
“Wha—what?”
“It wasn’t a Mutated Gate, and from how much the magical power reading had risen, I figured it would be fine. So I sent you instead.”
“You sent me in your place?”
He blinked at me, mouth hanging open.
“Why?”
“Because I trust you to handle it.”
“I’d been going with you just in case. But I’ve seen what you can do, and after hearing what other people had to say, I figured you could go alone.”
The Skeleton King was a Named Monster in every sense of the word.
He had possessed powerful abilities even back when he was called a Warlord, but after his battle with the Arch Lich, he had evolved into an even more powerful being.
An ordinary Named Monster wouldn’t stand a chance against him.
From what I’d seen firsthand, his physical abilities were exceptional. He could also use his own Authority to raise a one-man army.
In that respect, none of the S-rank Hunters alive today could match him. Though a Grand Mage like Magic Johnson, who could dominate an entire battlefield, might be another story.
And there’s me, too.
The Skeleton King was an undead Lü Bu who could sweep a Gate by himself. There was only one reason I’d kept someone that powerful at my side.
His complete and utter lack of social skills.
He’d never come right out and announced what he was, but he went around advertising that he was born to be a monster.

If I had taken him to the official Blue House press conference last time, he would have referred to President Baek Hanseong as a “human male.” Then the Liberation Army, led by the Lady of the House, would surely have risen up, waving Korean flags and demanding that they investigate the identity of that long-nosed bastard.
But now...
“This hyung can finally relax. You even went to church, you little punk. Go on, live a little more freely from now on.”
Pat, pat.
I patted his shoulder. The Skeleton King’s eyes widened—perhaps at the warmth of my touch, or perhaps at one word I’d said.
“F-freely?”
“Yeah. You’ve reached the point where I can trust you with things. You deserve that much freedom.”
“Vile human. Weren’t you keeping watch on me?”
“Keeping watch?”
I gave a quiet laugh.
“After you saved my life in China?”
“That...”
“Sure, you owe me too. Neither of us needs to say it out loud. Just know I’ve always been grateful.”
His golden eyelids quivered. He looked at me with an expression I couldn’t quite place, then opened his mouth, eyes wet.
“Vile human.”
“Oh, shit. Don’t say anything.”
“But I have to say this.”
“Don’t. Seriously. I hate this kind of mood.”
I could almost hear soft background music playing somewhere. I looked off toward the distant mountains, uncomfortable, as his voice reached me.
“Then can I go to a club tonight?”
“That mage tricked me into going to a gay bar twice. This time, I intend to enjoy some noble bump-and-grind at a club.”
Noble bump-and-grind, my ass.
Give me back my emotions, you bastard.
“Please, vile human. I swear I’ll be back before midnight!”
“Fine. Go.”
“R-really?”
“Yeah. Go. If you want to die.”
“You crazy bastard. A club? What kind of trouble would you get into there?”
Hearing that he had gone to a gay bar twice did make me feel a little sorry for him, but the Skeleton King still wasn’t socially developed enough for that.
This had nothing to do with the fact that I’d never been to one myself.
...Really.
“Why? How can this happen when I’m so handsome!”
As the Skeleton King howled in anguish, the smartphone in his hand vibrated.
Bzzzz.
His face crumpled when he checked the screen. I didn’t need to look to know why. It might as well have been projected as a hologram.
“Emergency call?”
“...Damn it.”
Talk about timing. I checked the call details, then looked up at him.
“What are you waiting for?”
“I refuse, vile human. You go this time.”
“What are you talking about? One look tells me all I need to know. You can handle this by yourself.”
“Damn it! Why do you get to play around here while I work?”
Play around? Who?
But he had no way of knowing what I was doing.
I gave a quiet laugh and raised a hand instead of answering. He caught the hint and darted out the door.
Bang!
The door slammed shut and did not open again from sunset until the following morning.
And then...
Inhale. Exhale.
Whoosh. Boom!
In that quiet, isolated room, I circulated my qi and trained without pause.
It was a long journey in search of a path I’d never taken, with the faintest thread of a clue in my grasp.
A pale face. Trembling fingertips.
When had it started? A drop of cold sweat that had run down the back of his neck while he listened fell with a soft plop.
“W-what did you just say?”

He had the imposing build of a man whose age of seventy seemed impossible, along with the face of a middle-aged man. But the voice that slipped between his lips was as faint as that of someone standing on the brink of death.
What he’d just heard was that shocking.
“Th-that is...”
Even remembering what he had heard made his vision swim. The old man barely pulled himself together and forced out his trembling voice.
“You—you kidnapped our children?”
“‘Kidnapped’ sounds rather unpleasant. Someone might get the wrong idea.”
“Y-you dare...”
“So let’s call it protection.”
Across a table laden with an elaborate feast, Go Jun answered brightly and took a bite of steak.
Juice from the rare beef ran down his angular jaw. His next words, added almost in passing, cut into the old man’s ears.
“For now, at least.”
Go Jun smiled with pleasure at the frozen face of the old man, Song Cheonwoo.

chapters.title: Chapter 569
paragraphs: Thud.
The door closed behind Song Cheonwoo with a sound like thunder. His sturdy frame—hard to believe he was seventy—staggered.
Slide. Tap.
Neither his powerful mana nor the experience he had gained through a lifetime of hardship was any use to him now.
He braced himself against the wall and stared at the floor. A pair of black dress shoes stepped into view.
“Are you all right?”
At the sound of the businesslike voice, Song looked up, saw who the shoes belonged to, and gritted his teeth.
“Does this look all right to you?”
Head of Security Go Se-won bowed beneath his furious glare.
“I’m sorry if that sounded insensitive.”
“Spare me the words you don’t mean. Before I break your neck!”
“I wouldn’t recommend it. You’d have nothing to gain and plenty to lose.”
Go Se-won gave a gentle wave of his hand. At the far end of the hallway, the security-team members who had started toward them stopped.
“They’re my men. As you know, Director, they’re quite capable. And when the situation calls for it, they don’t care what they have to do.”
“Please don’t misunderstand me. I only mean that I don’t want you to make matters worse.”
Crack.
The marble beneath Song’s hand, reinforced by magic, split in a spiderweb of cracks. He glared at Go Se-won through bloodshot eyes and forced the words through his teeth.
“So you kidnapped my children? They had nothing to do with this. They’d done nothing wrong.”
“They were exceptionally well guarded for people who supposedly had nothing to do with it. That means you had at least considered the possibility, Director.”
Two security-team members had died despite the whole team taking part in the attack. Given that they were among the best Ares Guild had to offer, it was no fewer than two.
“I regret what happened to your family. But if you suspected this might happen, you should have sent even more people to protect them.”
“I shouldn’t have said that. I apologize.”
Go Se-won meant it. Song Cheonwoo was already like an old lion whose death had been decided. There was no need for Go Se-won to drive the knife in himself.
Would he believe me if I said it slipped out because I felt sorry for him?
Go Se-won was a father too. His first son had been born after he turned forty, and his second child was due in a few months. Both were already more precious to him than anything.
He would give his life for his children’s safety and happiness. That was what it meant to be a father. A parent.
But Song Cheonwoo had weighed his ambition against his family’s safety. Then again, if he had imagined the worst, he would never have tried to make an enemy of Go Jun.
...Not that I’m one to talk.
Go Se-won felt like a pathetic villain.
For well over a decade, he had lived more like a fixer than a Hunter. Ever since Lee Jungryong had noticed him and brought him into the security team, his main targets had been people, not monsters.
He was the one who had ordered his men to kidnap Song Cheonwoo’s family and then cleaned up the aftermath.
And I have the nerve to lecture him.
They were all pieces of shit in the same shit pit.

Song Cheonwoo had let ambition consume him on the verge of retirement and brought danger upon himself. Go Jun swung his blade without caring what it took to get his way. And Go Se-won had become the sword in his superior’s hand and kidnapped Song’s family.
A war between bastards. In the end, there’ll be a winner and a loser.
And he was nothing more than a component.
He was swallowing the bitter thought when—
Grab!
A hand far too strong to belong to a seventy-year-old man seized his collar.
“Team Leader!”
“Enough. Stay at your posts.”
Go Se-won stopped his men and calmly looked up at Song Cheonwoo, who stood a full head taller than him.
“I told you. You stand to lose more than you’d gain.”
“You bastards dare lay a hand on my children...!”
“The Vice Guild Master is listening inside. I don’t know what the two of you discussed, but I hope there won’t be any more unnecessary sacrifices.”
Go Jun held his family’s lives in his hands. Go Se-won was telling him not to make Go Jun angry.
Song understood at once. His eyelids trembled, and though he kept glaring at Go Se-won through clenched teeth, his grip slowly loosened.
“You made the right choice.”
“...Shut your mouth. I’d like nothing more than to smash your face in right now.”
“I’m sure you would.”
A bitter smile touched Go Se-won’s lips. He would have felt the same in Song’s place.

And even twenty years after leaving active service, Song Cheonwoo was still an extraordinary fighter. His ability simply hadn’t matched his ambition. The fact that he had once been Lee Jungryong’s political rival said enough about him.
Which is why Go Jun chose a method this dirty.
Go Se-won disliked it. But dirty as it was, it would work.
Song Cheonwoo would be eliminated soon, and it would look so natural that no one would suspect a thing.
“Follow me. I’ll escort you outside.”
Go Se-won bowed slightly and started down the hallway. Song cast one last glare at the closed door, then followed.
Step. Step.
Go Se-won had sent his men away. Only their footsteps sounded in the hallway until Song broke the silence.
“What you said earlier. Was it true?”
“You said you didn’t know what Go Jun and I had discussed. Was that true?”
Go Se-won considered the question for a moment, then nodded.
“I see. From what I found out about you, I suppose you were never much of a strategist.”
“What do you mean?”
“It seems he doesn’t trust you as much as I thought. Or perhaps he wanted to hide it even from his closest aide.”
Song gave a weak, hollow laugh at Go Se-won’s frown.
“Go Se-won.”
In the brief span of time between one breath and the next, he seemed to have aged ten years. No—twenty. He continued in a desolate voice.
“There’s such a thing as a line a person shouldn’t cross. You know that?”
“...If you’re criticizing the Vice Guild Master, I’d ask you to stop.”
“Criticizing him? That’s a much gentler word than I’d expected. Far too gentle for that bastard Go Jun.”
“I understand how you feel. But no one involved in this has the right to condemn anyone else. I know you haven’t lived a particularly clean life either, Director.”
“Heh. True. There was a time when I’d use any means necessary to get what I wanted. But I never went this far.”
Song laughed again, empty and almost unhinged. Go Se-won fell silent.
Song wasn’t talking only about the kidnapping.
What is it?
His heart pounded. A current ran down his spine.
This was a warning. A danger signal telling him not to listen.
But his body moved contrary to his thoughts.
“What limit are you talking about, Director?”
“A monster who has forgotten even the most basic duty of being human.”
“What?”
Step.
Song stopped before the Teleportation magic circle leading outside. He stared at it for a moment before speaking again.
“The boundary between human and monster. That bastard Go Jun... has already become a monster.”
The old man’s empty gaze drifted through the air. As though searching through memories of a brilliant past, he took a weary step toward the magic circle and left Go Se-won with one last plea.
“I apologize for what I did to you. So please, don’t let those children die for nothing.”
Flash!
Before Go Se-won could ask what he meant, Teleportation magic manifested, and dazzling radiance swallowed Song Cheonwoo’s body.
Go Se-won stood alone, staring in confusion at the spot where Song had been. Then he turned.
The hallway was made entirely of white marble. At the far end of its long stretch stood a closed door. Behind it, someone was probably sipping wine, pleased with himself.
What in the world... have you done?
Go Se-won muttered toward something deep inside his heart.
Section A, which was always filled with light, felt like a pit overflowing with darkness today.
I had no idea how long I’d been shut away in the training ground—or training room, as they called it in the modern world.
One day. Two. Maybe three.
The walls blocked out everything beyond them, and the temperature stayed the same. Once I got absorbed in martial arts, I lost track of time.
Even though I had a smartphone, I never looked at it, so I had no way of knowing. Perhaps they vaguely understood my situation, because no one from the Peace Guild came to see me or contacted me.
Saying it like that made me sound like a complete loner. Which I absolutely wasn’t.
...Probably.
The Skeleton King hasn’t come by once since then, either.

It was good news in one sense: he seemed to be handling things better than I’d expected. But it also meant the emergency rescue team was busier, and more Gates were showing signs of abnormal activity. I couldn’t exactly celebrate.
What I could celebrate was that my own attempt was nearly complete.
It’s not finished yet, though.
I had never tried anything like this before, and the process so far had been anything but easy.
The pressure of having to create something exceptional while the current situation was on the verge of exploding may have contributed as well.
What I have now might be good enough...
Should I just take the plunge and go with it?
I’d asked myself that dozens, maybe hundreds of times. I was going over it again when the training room door opened with a familiar mechanical sound.
“So this is where you were. I need your help, as it happens.”
Step. Step.
Combat boots polished to a shine. A skin-tight blue suit. A shield with a skull on it.
I gave him a look colder than the snow piled on the roof of King Sejong Station in Antarctica.
“Look at this fucking bastard.”
“You heard from Director King Fury, didn’t you?”
“...Are you playing two roles now?”
“Heh heh. Surely a citizen of the United States of America ought to be King-tin America.”
“This bastard keeps changing his name however he wants. I’m going to beat you so badly you’ll want to go back to the glacier.”
“I can do this all day.”
Whoosh! Boom!
White Flame shot toward him like a streak of light. Its spearhead grazed his neck and pierced the training room wall, burying the shaft.
The Skeleton King looked from the spear to me, then muttered, “All day might be difficult...”
“Cut the bullshit. Why are you here? If you dropped by because you were bored, I’ll kill you. Seriously.”
He answered in a hurry.
“N-no, that’s not it. It’s a mission. A mission!”
“A mission?”
“That is correct, wicked human.”
He nodded.
“It isn’t an ordinary Mutated Gate. The magical power reading is enormous.”
Damn it.

chapters.title: Chapter 570
paragraphs: Eight in the morning.
The new year had arrived, but people’s daily routines hadn’t changed. Office workers in neat suits hurried to work with tired faces, and the roads were packed with cars.
Honk! Hooonk!
At the constant blare of horns, the middle-aged man driving a midsize van rolled up his half-open window and grumbled.
“Fuck. Even the Great Cataclysm couldn’t get this goddamn road fixed. Are we supposed to drive on it or not?”
Swearing behind the wheel was practically inevitable. Especially in Busan.
He laid on the horn at a compact car trying to cut in without signaling.
Honk!
Then again, if its driver had any sense, he wouldn’t have needed to honk.

The compact car flashed its high beams in broad daylight to celebrate its successful lane change and cruised away. The middle-aged man spotted the message plastered across its rear window and swore again.
A child is on board.
“Goddamn it. Is the kid on fire? Is that why you’re driving like that?”
Only then did he realize he’d cursed aloud. He glanced at the passenger seat and cleared his throat.
“Ahem. That slipped out.”
The young man beside him answered calmly.
“It’s all right. It happens.”
He spoke to the driver, but his eyes remained on the view outside. The middle-aged man glanced at him.
“Your name was... Dongseok, right?”
“Yes.”
“That’s a relief. With things blowing up all over the place these days, it’s hard enough to remember someone’s full name.”
“It happens. Don’t worry about it.”
“Ah, I don’t know if I told you last time, but my name is...”
“I’ll call you Team Leader. That’s easier for me.”
The Team Leader blinked, taken aback by the prompt answer. Lee Dongseok added, just as abruptly, “And, Team Leader.”
“Uh, yeah?”
“The light’s changed.”
Hoooonk!
The horn behind them snapped the Team Leader back to his senses. He stepped on the gas, and as the van lurched forward, he frowned.
What a rude little shit.
But he soon reconsidered. So what if Dongseok was rude? They’d only be working together for a day. As long as he did his job, that was enough.
He’s a hundred times better than a rookie who shakes in his boots or some loudmouth who can’t back up his talk.
The Team Leader was a C-rank Hunter who had worked freelance for years. He knew a capable fighter with lousy manners was preferable to someone pleasant and polite who couldn’t fight.
At least he won’t shit the bed and disappear like that bastard a little while ago.
A team member had made a major mistake inside a Gate and then gone into hiding, leaving them in need of a temporary replacement. Lee Dongseok was the man they’d found.

His résumé gave them nothing to complain about, and from what the Team Leader could judge for himself, Dongseok was a skilled Hunter. Skilled enough that it seemed strange for him to be freelancing.
Well, I’m not complaining.
Finding people was hard enough these days. Even now, the DJs chatting quietly on the radio were discussing the main reason Hunters were in short supply.

“We have a comment from Shin Ayoung, a woman in her twenties who lives in Pocheon, Gyeonggi Province. ‘A Mutated Gate appeared near my home three days ago. It happened only ten minutes away, and I’ve been so anxious I can’t sleep.’”
“Oh, no... You live right near it? That’s awful.”
“I remember seeing that on the news. Apparently it was extremely dangerous. There could have been a lot of casualties.”
“Thank goodness they stopped it just before it became a Monster Wave.”
The Team Leader turned up the volume.
As a Hunter, there was no way he could have missed the Pocheon Mutated Gate incident three days earlier. Even Dongseok, who had been staring out the window, seemed to be listening.
“Fortunately, there were no deaths this time either.”
“That’s right. They stopped the Monster Wave, so there were no civilian casualties, and the Mutated Gate was dealt with quickly.”
“That was Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team, wasn’t it?”
“Yes. Hunter Jin Taekyung didn’t go himself, but Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team did an impressive job.”
“Rising magic power readings have become a serious problem here and overseas. Of all the countries in the world, ours has been recognized for responding the fastest and suffering the least damage.”
“It really is remarkable. And it isn’t just Hunter Jin Taekyung and Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team. All the Hunters fighting monsters under these circumstances deserve our...”
As the DJ went on, the Team Leader stole another glance at Dongseok.
“Come to think of it, you’re pretty impressive yourself, Dongseok.”
“What do you mean?”
“Going on raids at a time like this isn’t easy.”
As magic power readings rose, monsters grew stronger. Mutated Gates, which had once appeared only once or twice a year, now made the nine o’clock news headlines about every three days.
The Team Leader turned the wheel and continued. “I’m doing it for my family, but you’re still in your twenties. You don’t have a household to support. Is it youthful ambition or something?”
“No.”
“Hm?”
“I’m doing what needs to be done. I have to do it.”
His answer was firm, his eyes suddenly bright with resolve. The Team Leader blinked at this unfamiliar side of him.
“R-really?”
“Yes.”
“Well. Good for you. That’s some dedication to your job.”
Dongseok’s response had caught him off guard. So had the determination in his eyes. Sense of duty was about the only way to describe it.
What’s with this guy?
A rude young man burning with a sense of justice? A kid dreaming of becoming a hero in troubled times? Whatever it was, he was an odd one.
The Team Leader eased onto the brakes. When he parked in the Gate management office lot and got out, the team members who recognized the van came over.
“Hey, Team Leader Kim. You made it.”
“You’re here, hyung.”
“You’re early, oppa. But who’s that with you...?”
“This is Dongseok. You know—the temporary guy I told you about.”
“Ah, is that right? I could tell at a glance. He looks just like someone from Seoul.”
“I think he is. Dongseok, these are the rest of the team...”
The Team Leader naturally turned his head, then blinked. Something about Dongseok didn’t look right.
“Dongseok. Are you feeling sick?”
“Hey. Dongseok?”
Dongseok stood staring silently at the Gate, his face rigid. He wiped the cold sweat from his forehead.
“No. I just got a little nervous all of a sudden.”
“Hmm. You’re all right, though?”
“Yes. There’s no problem.”
The Team Leader eyed him doubtfully, but they were already at the Gate. The manager responsible for Siren’s Black River, the C-rank Gate in Haeundae, was ambling over from a distance.
“Oh, Team Leader Kim. You’re here.”
“Yes. We’re a little late.”
“No trouble, right? Got everyone?”
The Team Leader glanced at Dongseok and nodded.
“Of course.”
“You sure? You know they’ve tightened the regulations. If something goes wrong, you and I both...”
“I know, I know. Have you ever seen me or my team cause trouble? You’re going to inspect everything anyway.”
“With things the way they are lately, I can’t help worrying. And yes, I was going to inspect you.”
The inspection was quick. The manager checked everything, finishing with Dongseok, then grinned.
“All right. Go on in.”
With permission granted, the team began moving, talking noisily among themselves. Everyone except Dongseok.
At the back of the group, he stared at the Gate with trembling eyes.
Thump. Thump.
His heart hammered. He’d suffered from cold hands and feet since his days at the orphanage, but now his palms were so clammy with cold sweat he might have developed hyperhidrosis.
Don’t get nervous. Not until the very end.
He had a mission. A mission he absolutely had to complete.
Dongseok took a deep breath. At the front of the group, the Team Leader suddenly looked back.
“Dongseok. You really are okay, right?”
“You don’t look good, and you took your time answering. Your mind isn’t somewhere else, is it?”
“No.”
The Team Leader would never know that Dongseok had been slow to answer because he still wasn’t used to the name, not because his mind was elsewhere.
And Lee Dongseok—or rather, the man behind that name—had not forgotten his purpose for a single moment.
“Don’t worry. I’ll definitely do it.”
“What?”
For a moment, the Team Leader looked baffled. Then he gave Dongseok a look that said What an oddball and turned away.
They stood at the entrance to the Gate.
“All right, before we go in—everyone together. Safety first, today too!”
“Safety first!”
The chant rang out, and the Team Leader stepped toward the entrance.
“Let’s go in!”
Whoosh!
The rippling magical power swallowed them one after another.
As the others hurried inside, Dongseok lifted his head and looked at the sky.
It was a January morning. The sky was blue, and the wind was still cold.
And... this might be the last sky he ever saw.
“I have a mission for you.”
A voice he had heard several days earlier seemed to reach him on the wind, along with his own answer.
“I’ll do it.”
“Your life could be at risk.”
“The former Vice Guild Master saved my life in the first place.”

He had been told that his mother, whose face he had never seen, gave birth to him in a subway restroom. Wrapped in toilet paper and thrown into a trash can, the newborn survived by sheer luck. He was sent to an orphanage secretly supported by Lee Jungryong, where he grew up healthy and strong.
“If I can help... I’ll do anything.”
To him, Lee Jungryong was a father, and Ares Guild was the home he’d shared with that father. He could do anything for him.
“Leave it to me.”
At his resolute answer, the other person had smiled broadly. Then he had handed him something—an object now kept deep in his subspace pocket.
“You must succeed.”
That was the last thing he’d said. After receiving his orders, Dongseok changed everything, including his face and name, and went down to Busan with that precious, dangerous object in his possession.
“I... will definitely do it.”
His turn had come.
He fought down his fear, steadied himself with those murmured words, and stepped toward the rippling field of magical power.
Whoosh!
About an hour later, the people outside the Gate saw what happened.
Beep beep beep beep!
The magic power reading climbed at a frantic pace. Then a change began too quickly for anyone to stop.
Kiiiiing.
A rift tore open in the air, and a dense breath of death blanketed the sandy beach of Haeundae.
After arriving in Busan through three Teleportation magic circles, I knew at once.
No—I could feel it.
“Aaaaaah!”
“Aaargh!”
Kwaaaang!
