sentences.text: Eight in the morning.
The new year had arrived, but people’s daily routines hadn’t changed.
Office workers in neat suits hurried to work with tired faces, and the roads were packed with cars.
Honk!
Hooonk!
At the constant blare of horns, the middle-aged man driving a midsize van rolled up his half-open window and grumbled.
“Fuck.
Even the Great Cataclysm couldn’t get this goddamn road fixed.
Are we supposed to drive on it or not?”
Swearing behind the wheel was practically inevitable.
Especially in Busan.
He laid on the horn at a compact car trying to cut in without signaling.
Honk!
Then again, if its driver had any sense, he wouldn’t have needed to honk.
The compact car flashed its high beams in broad daylight to celebrate its successful lane change and cruised away.
The middle-aged man spotted the message plastered across its rear window and swore again.
A child is on board.
“Goddamn it.
Is the kid on fire?
Is that why you’re driving like that?”
Only then did he realize he’d cursed aloud.
He glanced at the passenger seat and cleared his throat.
“Ahem.
That slipped out.”
The young man beside him answered calmly.
“It’s all right.
It happens.”
He spoke to the driver, but his eyes remained on the view outside.
The middle-aged man glanced at him.
“Your name was...
Dongseok, right?”
“Yes.”
“That’s a relief.
With things blowing up all over the place these days, it’s hard enough to remember someone’s full name.”
“It happens.
Don’t worry about it.”
“Ah, I don’t know if I told you last time, but my name is...”
“I’ll call you Team Leader.
That’s easier for me.”
The Team Leader blinked, taken aback by the prompt answer.
Lee Dongseok added, just as abruptly, “And, Team Leader.”
“Uh, yeah?”
“The light’s changed.”
Hoooonk!
The horn behind them snapped the Team Leader back to his senses.
He stepped on the gas, and as the van lurched forward, he frowned.
What a rude little shit.
But he soon reconsidered.
So what if Dongseok was rude?
They’d only be working together for a day.
As long as he did his job, that was enough.
He’s a hundred times better than a rookie who shakes in his boots or some loudmouth who can’t back up his talk.
The Team Leader was a C-rank Hunter who had worked freelance for years.
He knew a capable fighter with lousy manners was preferable to someone pleasant and polite who couldn’t fight.
At least he won’t shit the bed and disappear like that bastard a little while ago.
A team member had made a major mistake inside a Gate and then gone into hiding, leaving them in need of a temporary replacement.
Lee Dongseok was the man they’d found.
His résumé gave them nothing to complain about, and from what the Team Leader could judge for himself, Dongseok was a skilled Hunter.
Skilled enough that it seemed strange for him to be freelancing.
Well, I’m not complaining.
Finding people was hard enough these days.
Even now, the DJs chatting quietly on the radio were discussing the main reason Hunters were in short supply.
“We have a comment from Shin Ayoung, a woman in her twenties who lives in Pocheon, Gyeonggi Province.
‘A Mutated Gate appeared near my home three days ago.
It happened only ten minutes away, and I’ve been so anxious I can’t sleep.’”
“Oh, no...
You live right near it?
That’s awful.”
“I remember seeing that on the news.
Apparently it was extremely dangerous.
There could have been a lot of casualties.”
“Thank goodness they stopped it just before it became a Monster Wave.”
The Team Leader turned up the volume.
As a Hunter, there was no way he could have missed the Pocheon Mutated Gate incident three days earlier.
Even Dongseok, who had been staring out the window, seemed to be listening.
“Fortunately, there were no deaths this time either.”
“That’s right.
They stopped the Monster Wave, so there were no civilian casualties, and the Mutated Gate was dealt with quickly.”
“That was Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team, wasn’t it?”
“Yes.
Hunter Jin Taekyung didn’t go himself, but Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team did an impressive job.”
“Rising magic power readings have become a serious problem here and overseas.
Of all the countries in the world, ours has been recognized for responding the fastest and suffering the least damage.”
“It really is remarkable.
And it isn’t just Hunter Jin Taekyung and Peace Guild’s Emergency Rescue Team.
All the Hunters fighting monsters under these circumstances deserve our...”
As the DJ went on, the Team Leader stole another glance at Dongseok.
“Come to think of it, you’re pretty impressive yourself, Dongseok.”
“What do you mean?”
“Going on raids at a time like this isn’t easy.”
As magic power readings rose, monsters grew stronger.
Mutated Gates, which had once appeared only once or twice a year, now made the nine o’clock news headlines about every three days.
The Team Leader turned the wheel and continued.
“I’m doing it for my family, but you’re still in your twenties.
You don’t have a household to support.
Is it youthful ambition or something?”
“No.”
“Hm?”
“I’m doing what needs to be done.
I have to do it.”
His answer was firm, his eyes suddenly bright with resolve.
The Team Leader blinked at this unfamiliar side of him.
“R-really?”
“Yes.”
“Well.
Good for you.
That’s some dedication to your job.”
Dongseok’s response had caught him off guard.
So had the determination in his eyes.
Sense of duty was about the only way to describe it.
What’s with this guy?
A rude young man burning with a sense of justice?
A kid dreaming of becoming a hero in troubled times?
Whatever it was, he was an odd one.
The Team Leader eased onto the brakes.
When he parked in the Gate management office lot and got out, the team members who recognized the van came over.
“Hey, Team Leader Kim.
You made it.”
“You’re here, hyung.”
“You’re early, oppa.
But who’s that with you...?”
“This is Dongseok.
You know—the temporary guy I told you about.”
“Ah, is that right?
I could tell at a glance.
He looks just like someone from Seoul.”
“I think he is.
Dongseok, these are the rest of the team...”
The Team Leader naturally turned his head, then blinked.
Something about Dongseok didn’t look right.
“Dongseok.
Are you feeling sick?”
“Hey.
Dongseok?”
Dongseok stood staring silently at the Gate, his face rigid.
He wiped the cold sweat from his forehead.
“No.
I just got a little nervous all of a sudden.”
“Hmm.
You’re all right, though?”
“Yes.
There’s no problem.”
The Team Leader eyed him doubtfully, but they were already at the Gate.
The manager responsible for Siren’s Black River, the C-rank Gate in Haeundae, was ambling over from a distance.
“Oh, Team Leader Kim.
You’re here.”
“Yes.
We’re a little late.”
“No trouble, right?
Got everyone?”
The Team Leader glanced at Dongseok and nodded.
“Of course.”
“You sure?
You know they’ve tightened the regulations.
If something goes wrong, you and I both...”
“I know, I know.
Have you ever seen me or my team cause trouble?
You’re going to inspect everything anyway.”
“With things the way they are lately, I can’t help worrying.
And yes, I was going to inspect you.”
The inspection was quick.
The manager checked everything, finishing with Dongseok, then grinned.
“All right.
Go on in.”
With permission granted, the team began moving, talking noisily among themselves.
Everyone except Dongseok.
At the back of the group, he stared at the Gate with trembling eyes.
Thump.
Thump.
His heart hammered.
He’d suffered from cold hands and feet since his days at the orphanage, but now his palms were so clammy with cold sweat he might have developed hyperhidrosis.
Don’t get nervous.
Not until the very end.
He had a mission.
A mission he absolutely had to complete.
Dongseok took a deep breath.
At the front of the group, the Team Leader suddenly looked back.
“Dongseok.
You really are okay, right?”
“You don’t look good, and you took your time answering.
Your mind isn’t somewhere else, is it?”
“No.”
The Team Leader would never know that Dongseok had been slow to answer because he still wasn’t used to the name, not because his mind was elsewhere.
And Lee Dongseok—or rather, the man behind that name—had not forgotten his purpose for a single moment.
“Don’t worry.
I’ll definitely do it.”
“What?”
For a moment, the Team Leader looked baffled.
Then he gave Dongseok a look that said What an oddball and turned away.
They stood at the entrance to the Gate.
“All right, before we go in—everyone together.
Safety first, today too!”
“Safety first!”
The chant rang out, and the Team Leader stepped toward the entrance.
“Let’s go in!”
Whoosh!
The rippling magical power swallowed them one after another.
As the others hurried inside, Dongseok lifted his head and looked at the sky.
It was a January morning.
The sky was blue, and the wind was still cold.
And... this might be the last sky he ever saw.
“I have a mission for you.”
A voice he had heard several days earlier seemed to reach him on the wind, along with his own answer.
“I’ll do it.”
“Your life could be at risk.”
“The former Vice Guild Master saved my life in the first place.”
He had been told that his mother, whose face he had never seen, gave birth to him in a subway restroom.
Wrapped in toilet paper and thrown into a trash can, the newborn survived by sheer luck.
He was sent to an orphanage secretly supported by Lee Jungryong, where he grew up healthy and strong.
“If I can help...
I’ll do anything.”
To him, Lee Jungryong was a father, and Ares Guild was the home he’d shared with that father.
He could do anything for him.
“Leave it to me.”
At his resolute answer, the other person had smiled broadly.
Then he had handed him something—an object now kept deep in his subspace pocket.
“You must succeed.”
That was the last thing he’d said.
After receiving his orders, Dongseok changed everything, including his face and name, and went down to Busan with that precious, dangerous object in his possession.
“I... will definitely do it.”
His turn had come.
He fought down his fear, steadied himself with those murmured words, and stepped toward the rippling field of magical power.
Whoosh!
About an hour later, the people outside the Gate saw what happened.
Beep beep beep beep!
The magic power reading climbed at a frantic pace.
Then a change began too quickly for anyone to stop.
Kiiiiing.
A rift tore open in the air, and a dense breath of death blanketed the sandy beach of Haeundae.
After arriving in Busan through three Teleportation magic circles, I knew at once.
No—I could feel it.
“Aaaaaah!”
“Aaargh!”
Kwaaaang!
The countless screams and tremendous din coming from far away.
And...
Kuuung!
The immense magical power shaking the earth.
“...Fuck.”

chapters.title: Chapter 571
paragraphs: Busan.
Before and after the Great Cataclysm, it had been one of the three most populous cities in the country.
A very long time ago, a handsome, clever elementary school student on a family trip to Busan spent his nights practically glued to the window.
“Taekyung, what are you looking at?”
“That leg! It’s sparkling! It’s pretty!”
“Whoa, you’re right. Is she a fit model?”
“...Not that kind of leg, Dad.”
“Oh.”
“That bridge over there! The long, sparkly one!”
“Aha. Gwangan Bridge?”
“Gwangan Bridge? What’s that?”
“It’s the name of that bridge. You saw it earlier, but it’s even prettier at night, isn’t it?”
“Yeah! I want to go! Take me to Gwangan Bridge right now!”
My father looked at his demanding young son as though he couldn’t have loved him more.
“Oh, my boy. Your dad’s exhausted from driving all day, and look at you thinking only of yourself. Who did you get that from?”
“Then can I ask Mom what a fit model is?”
“...You really are my son. Pack your bag.”
It was one of the moments I would never forget. Walking hand in hand with my dejected father to Gwangan Bridge left a vivid impression on my young mind.
The bridge was impossibly huge and glittering. Beside me was my father, who was always too busy for us to spend much time together.
I even got him to carry me on his shoulders by threatening him, despite his complaints about a bad disc in his neck. What more could I have wanted?
“Dad, let’s come back next week! And the week after that! And next month too! You have to carry me on your shoulders again!”
“Haha. What am I going to do? If we do what you want, I don’t think I’ll make it here next month.”
“Why?”
“Because at this rate, my neck will break the week after next. How many bowls of rice have you been eating a day lately, Taekyung?”
“I haven’t had much of an appetite, so only five!”
“...That’s my good boy. No wonder the night sky looked yellow.”
It was a happy memory. We talked about all sorts of things that day, and when we got back to the hotel, I excitedly told my little sister Hayeon and Mom all about it.
Watching me, my father rubbed his neck, gave a quiet laugh, and made a promise.
“When Hayeon’s a little older and you’re in middle school, let’s come back to see the ocean. All right?”
“Really?”
“Of course. Here—promise.”
He never got to keep that promise.
As his two children grew, there were more and more expenses. When my mother fell ill from pushing herself too hard at her side job, my father grew busier still.
Then, on an ordinary day, an extraordinary accident took his life.
But I remembered his promise.
My father was no longer with us, yet even after more than twenty years, the Gwangan Bridge I’d seen as a child remained vividly etched in my mind.
And now—
Ruuuumble.
Gwangan Bridge was collapsing before my eyes.
“Ah.”
A sigh escaped between my lips before I could stop it.
My mind screamed at me to get over there with everything I had, but my body wouldn’t move. It was as if an invisible hand held me in place.
It’s... already too late.
I wasn’t the only one thinking it.
The Skeleton King, who had come with me, and the mage who had brought us here watched with exhausted eyes as the disaster unfolded several kilometers away.
“N-no!”
The cry of the mage whose name I did not know was hollow, and the scene spread out in the distance below us was overwhelming.
That’s...
A wave.
A wave dozens of meters high had struck the place where my father’s promise could never be kept, the bridge crossed by thousands—tens of thousands—of vehicles every day.
Whoooosh!
Carrying tremendous weight and force, the wave slammed into the middle of Gwangan Bridge, a suspension bridge thirty-five meters high and 7,420 meters long.
Spray burst in every direction, and screams were swallowed by blinding white foam. Hundreds of cars cruising along at the speed limit were flung away like toys.
Boom! Crash!
With a deafening roar, the suspension bridge’s towers and anchors shattered.
Hundreds of cables snapped. No longer holding up the bridge, they became gigantic whips lashing out in every direction.
Whoooooosh—boom!
It happened in an instant.
People and cars that looked like ants were swept away by the cables and vanished.

Red blood flowed where they had stood, unable even to leave a final scream behind. Chain explosions, the screams of those who had survived by sheer luck, and the frantic blaring of car horns all reached my heightened senses.
Honk! Hooooonk!
“Back up! Back the fuck up, you bastard!”
“Aaaaaaah!”
“Please! Please get my child out! There’s a kid here...!”
I felt dazed, as though I were dreaming.
An advanced civilization built on magic and science was crumbling like a sandcastle.

Gwangan Bridge, which held my childhood memories, collapsed beneath the weight of destruction and death. Those who survived abandoned their cars and ran for their lives, crying desperately for someone to help them.
“Save me! Please save me!”
“Mommy!”
Their screams woke me from where I stood frozen like a statue.
“Ah.”
I had to save them. I had to stop this disaster.
I’d been still for only a few dozen seconds, but hundreds had already died. If I hesitated any longer, thousands—tens of thousands—would die.
Smack!
I slapped both cheeks as hard as I could. The sharp pain brought me back to my senses.
I spat out the blood from my split mouth and grabbed the Skeleton King by the collar.
Grab!
“W-what?”
“I’m going. Get a grip.”
“W-wait. Where are you—”
Before he could finish, I took a running start and threw him out the window with all my strength.
No. I launched him.
Crash! Whoooosh!
The magically reinforced floor-to-ceiling glass shattered, and the Skeleton King shot out like a cannonball.
Hearing his scream disappear into the wind, I kicked off the ground with all my strength as well.
I did not forget to leave one instruction for the mage, who had already collapsed from exhaustion.
“Call for rescue using my name. Anywhere—right now!”
I didn’t know whether he’d heard me properly in his exhausted state, or where he would send the request.
Nothing mattered more than what was happening in front of me.
Boom!
The force of my leap made the high-rise building where the Teleport Magic Formation had been installed tremble.
As I shot through the sky, an angry shout reached me.
“You lunatic!”
The Skeleton King. He had fashioned wings of bone with his own power and was flapping toward me at high speed.
Or he would have been, if I hadn’t blocked his path.
“Go somewhere else.”
“What?”
“It’s too widespread. We split up and cover it.”
A Monster Wave—and in Busan, of all places, with its dense population.

It might have been different in a desert or a sparsely populated military zone like the ones I’d seen in Magic Johnson’s footage. Here, thousands of people were packed into a radius of just a few kilometers.
I had to keep the disaster from spreading, no matter what it took.
“I’ll take the bridge first. You...”
“Damn it. Got it.”
I didn’t have time to say more, but the Skeleton King understood.
He swallowed hard and looked far below.
His gaze swept over the road swallowed by screams and chaos and the people running for their lives. Then it suddenly began to tremble.
“Fuck. What are those?”
“What do you think?”
I answered shortly, pulled a spare spear from my Inventory, and aimed it at the ground.
Through my greatly enhanced eyesight, it looked as grotesque as any other monster. The scales covering its entire body and the fins extending down to its jaw were repulsive.
Merman.
An aquatic monster that lived in places like the sea.
It had the form of a male merperson, but it was neither beautiful nor kind like the ones in fairy tales.
The hundreds of Mermen surging out of the sea and descending on the people below made that clear enough.
“Ssssss!”
“Karruk!”
They charged with unintelligible cries, barnacle-covered tridents flashing in their hands.
Beyond those flashing points sat a little girl, collapsed on the ground and crying.
“Waaaaah! Mommy!”
“Minhee!”
The child’s cries. Her parents’ screams as they turned back.
And hundreds of monsters rushing toward their first prey.
Now.
I shifted my weight.
My body, angled through the wind, turned sharply downward. Internal energy flowed through my dantian and burst from my feet.
Bang!
I began a steep descent, using Stepping on Empty Air to kick off the air itself.
But no matter how quickly I hurried, the girl would inevitably die before I arrived if things continued like this.
Go.
With a short breath, I hurled the spear I’d aimed at the ground.
Whoooosh!
A single spear plunged down like a bolt of lightning from an unreachable height.
Cutting through the wind, erasing space, carrying the two characters for certain death—
It pierced its target.
Splurch! Crunch-crunch-crunch!
The Merman leading the charge toward the girl, along with a dozen or so monsters around it, turned into a handful of blood.
Hundreds of Mermen stopped at once and stared up at the sky, mouths hanging open.
As I met their gazes, half ferocity and half confusion, I muttered, “What are you looking at, you sons of bitches?”
Inventory Open. Summon.
Click.
The instant two spears appeared in my hands, my arms were already swinging toward the ground.
Boom! Crack!
Scales harder than steel shattered, and fins tore apart.
One Merman, lucky enough to lose only half its body, let out a mournful death cry.
“Krruk, krruruk!”
So noisy.
Inventory Open. Summon.
Whoosh! Boom!
It was around noon, with the sun high overhead. Fireworks erupted where none belonged.
Sticky blood trickled down the railing of the tilted Gwangan Bridge.
More. More. One more time.
Open. Summon. And summon. Summon again.
It happened in the blink of an eye. The System operated instantly, and my movements were faster than the wind and more powerful than lightning.
As soon as I thought of it, my hand shot out. In only a few seconds, I seized dozens of spears and hurled them at the ground.
Die.
Whoooosh—boom-boom-boom!
They split apart. They burst.
Those who tried to block the spears died along with their tridents. Those who tried to run died before they could take a step.
When the girl who had been crouched and crying just three meters away began to hiccup, there was nothing left around her.
“Hic. Sob.”
She looked about nine years old. Sobbing hiccups escaped through the little hands clamped over her mouth.
What did she see when she looked at me with those enormous eyes?
A monster that had defeated monsters? Or an angel come down from the sky?
I didn’t know. But one thing was certain.
Unlike me... you won’t have any good memories of this place.
A bitter taste filled my mouth. I landed lightly and, instead of trying to comfort her, crooked a finger.
Shhh.
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space. Qi reached out gently and pushed the girl toward her parents, who were running to her with anguished cries.
But that family’s ordeal wasn’t over.
Ruuuumble.
The sea had turned black beneath the sun.
I stared at the thing hidden inside another wave rising dozens of meters high and lowered the spearhead of White Flame.

He swallowed hard and looked far below.
His gaze swept over the road swallowed by screams and chaos and the people running for their lives.
Then it suddenly began to tremble.
“Fuck.
What are those?”
“What do you think?”
I answered shortly, pulled a spare spear from my Inventory, and aimed it at the ground.
Through my greatly enhanced eyesight, it looked as grotesque as any other monster.
The scales covering its entire body and the fins extending down to its jaw were repulsive.
Merman.
An aquatic monster that lived in places like the sea.
It had the form of a male merperson, but it was neither beautiful nor kind like the ones in fairy tales.
The hundreds of Mermen surging out of the sea and descending on the people below made that clear enough.
“Ssssss!”
“Karruk!”
They charged with unintelligible cries, barnacle-covered tridents flashing in their hands.
Beyond those flashing points sat a little girl, collapsed on the ground and crying.
“Waaaaah!
Mommy!”
“Minhee!”
The child’s cries.
Her parents’ screams as they turned back.
And hundreds of monsters rushing toward their first prey.
Now.
I shifted my weight.
My body, angled through the wind, turned sharply downward.
Internal energy flowed through my dantian and burst from my feet.
Bang!
I began a steep descent, using Stepping on Empty Air to kick off the air itself.
But no matter how quickly I hurried, the girl would inevitably die before I arrived if things continued like this.
Go.
With a short breath, I hurled the spear I’d aimed at the ground.
Whoooosh!
A single spear plunged down like a bolt of lightning from an unreachable height.
Cutting through the wind, erasing space, carrying the two characters for certain death—
It pierced its target.
Splurch!
Crunch-crunch-crunch!
The Merman leading the charge toward the girl, along with a dozen or so monsters around it, turned into a handful of blood.
Hundreds of Mermen stopped at once and stared up at the sky, mouths hanging open.
As I met their gazes, half ferocity and half confusion, I muttered, “What are you looking at, you sons of bitches?”
Inventory Open.
Summon.
Click.
The instant two spears appeared in my hands, my arms were already swinging toward the ground.
Boom!
Crack!
Scales harder than steel shattered, and fins tore apart.
One Merman, lucky enough to lose only half its body, let out a mournful death cry.
“Krruk, krruruk!”
So noisy.
Inventory Open.
Summon.
Whoosh!
Boom!
It was around noon, with the sun high overhead.
Fireworks erupted where none belonged.
Sticky blood trickled down the railing of the tilted Gwangan Bridge.
More.
More.
One more time.
Open.
Summon.
And summon.
Summon again.
It happened in the blink of an eye.
The System operated instantly, and my movements were faster than the wind and more powerful than lightning.
As soon as I thought of it, my hand shot out.
In only a few seconds, I seized dozens of spears and hurled them at the ground.
Die.
Whoooosh—boom-boom-boom!
They split apart.
They burst.
Those who tried to block the spears died along with their tridents.
Those who tried to run died before they could take a step.
When the girl who had been crouched and crying just three meters away began to hiccup, there was nothing left around her.
“Hic.
Sob.”
She looked about nine years old.
Sobbing hiccups escaped through the little hands clamped over her mouth.
What did she see when she looked at me with those enormous eyes?
A monster that had defeated monsters?
Or an angel come down from the sky?
I didn’t know.
But one thing was certain.
Unlike me... you won’t have any good memories of this place.
A bitter taste filled my mouth.
I landed lightly and, instead of trying to comfort her, crooked a finger.
Shhh.
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.
Qi reached out gently and pushed the girl toward her parents, who were running to her with anguished cries.
But that family’s ordeal wasn’t over.
Ruuuumble.
The sea had turned black beneath the sun.
I stared at the thing hidden inside another wave rising dozens of meters high and lowered the spearhead of White Flame.

chapters.title: Chapter 572
paragraphs: How did this happen?
The thing blinked slowly as the question formed in its mind.
It had lived its entire life driven by instinct. Now, with intelligence far beyond anything it had known before, everything was confusing.
But it soon understood what had happened.
—Hu. Man.
Yes. That human.
Humans were small, strangely shaped creatures. Accursed things that occasionally invaded the black sea where it lived and stirred it up.
For countless years, the thing had fought them, driven by instinct and rage. Today had been no different.
But...
—What. Was. That. Human?
Several dozen humans had invaded the black sea.
Their weapons and magic brought down even the Mermen with their magnificent fins and the Sirens whose beautiful songs lured humans to them. Blood spilled into the water.
Then, as the thing sensed defeat and fought desperately on, one human stepped forward.
“Let’s stop here.”
He looked ordinary. Smaller than a Merman, and nowhere near as beautiful as a Siren.
Yet the thing knew instinctively: of everyone there, this was the only human who could kill it on his own.
The other humans, however, were different.
“Mr. Dongseok, sorry, what did you just say?”
“What are you doing in the middle of a raid, you crazy bastard? Move it!”
“That’s going to be difficult. I have something I need to do.”
“Something you need to do? Mr. Dongseok, what does that mean?”
“I told you. I’m going to see it through.”
“Wait. Mr. Dongseok, I’m asking because I really don’t understand what’s going on here...”
Shing.
“M-Mr. Dongseok?”
“T-Team Leader Kim! That guy...!”
Whoosh—slash!
Confusion turned to uproar, uproar to a fight, and the fight to a battle. The battle brought death.
Crack-crack-crack!
“Ghk, krrk...!”
One against many. But the difference in strength was overwhelming.
In moments, the human had killed everyone who stood in his way. He came to a stop before the thing, which lay wounded where it had fallen.
Then he held out an object containing a power both irresistibly alluring and terrifyingly strong, and spoke words the thing could not understand.
“Absorb it. It’s a gift from that person to you.”
The thing had no choice. Exhausted by the long battle, it had neither the strength nor the energy to kill the human before it.
Its mind filled with the scent of what he held out.
Magic power.
That was exactly what it was: the primordial power the thing had possessed since birth, and a meal so tempting it could not resist.
Whoooooosh.
When the brief meal ended, the thing realized it had changed.
Its body had grown beyond comparison with what it had been, and immense magic power overflowed from within. The vast black sea it had known all its life looked strangely unfamiliar.
Almost as if...
“It’s cramped, isn’t it?”
The human’s voice came from far below. Without thinking, the thing nodded.
Yes. Cramped. The black sea that had once seemed so vast was now too small and shabby for it.
What should it do?
“Go outside. There’s a wider sea.”
The answer could not have been clearer. Reborn as something new, the thing looked down at the human who had solved its problem.
—Thank. You.
And that was the end.
Crack! Crunch!
The human who had seemed so powerful was no match for what the thing had become. It wrapped him up, crushed his tiny body in an instant, and stirred the power lying within itself.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The black sea—everything the thing had ever known—began to shake.

Waves filled with magic power swallowed the human corpses and woke countless Mermen and Sirens sleeping in the deep sea. Amid savage roars and beautiful songs, magic power surged beyond its former limits. A dozen or so whirlpools rose around the thing and swept outward in every direction.
Whooooooosh!
A storm tore through the once-calm black sea and ripped open space itself.
Beyond the rift lay blinding light and a world the thing had never seen.
Whoosh!
Nothing could contain its magic power now.
Knowing its time had come, the thing became a single enormous wave and moved toward the new sea, carrying the countless Mermen and Sirens clinging to its body.
Crack! Whooooooosh!
The sunlight it felt for the first time was painfully hot. The endless blue sea was impossibly vast. And the sight of humans frozen in fear was enough to rouse the savagery it had briefly forgotten.
—Kill. Them.
A Monster Wave. The beginning of another disaster.
—Aah, aaaaaah!
Humans fleeing the Sirens’ alluring songs turned back as if bewitched. The Mermen fell upon them.
Stab! Stab-stab-stab!
Screams and death swept across the sandy beach. Humans with special abilities came running, but they were no match for the thing.
Whoom—crack!
One Strike.
A single powerful sweep of its leg crushed a dozen or so humans to powder. What insignificant, feeble creatures humans were.
—To. A. Wider. Place.
The vast blue sea was the thing’s now, and nothing stood in its way. It sent nearly a thousand of its followers ashore, one after another, then swam on beneath the surface.
Whoooooosh.
Easy. Everything was astonishingly easy.
Humans were weak, and it was strong. It would make those worthless things understand.
The thing roused the magic power coiled within its body. At the same time, it churned the water with limbs that had multiplied from eight to dozens.
Whooooooosh!
A wave dozens of meters high rose and hurtled forward.
Nothing could stop a wave carrying that much magic power. Everything human hands had built broke apart and sank.
The long, enormous structure built over the sea was no exception.
Ruuuumble!

The wave slammed into the suspension bridge called Gwangan Bridge. The wide-ranging defensive magic installed for emergencies shattered under its immense power, and the bridge broke precisely at its middle.
“Aaaaaah!”
“S-Save me...!”
Honk! Hooooonk!
The thing surveyed what it had made: the collapsing bridge, the terrified humans screaming, the noise pouring from objects it could not identify.
It was all satisfying.
At least until that happened.
Whoooosh! Boom!
In an instant, flashes of light rained down from the sky without pause, reducing some two hundred Mermen to pools of blood.
And then the thing noticed the presence of a human floating high above.
—Sky?
Could humans fly?
The question had barely formed when the human descended gently and landed.
Splash.
The human stepped into a pool of green blood and stared straight at it. Sunlight shattered against the spearhead he held at an angle.
The thing groaned at the painfully bright glare. Then it made its decision.
—I. Will. Kill. You.
A savage red light flashed in the eyes on either side of its head. With a surge of immense magic power, dozens of legs struck the water.
Rumble! Whooooooosh!
Another enormous wave rose. The disaster it had summoned blotted out the sun, and the thing charged with a vast roar.
—Grrrrrrooooooar!
There, in the path of the terror of the sea—the Kraken—stood a human.
Of course the wave that struck Gwangan Bridge hadn’t formed naturally.
Soon after the Great Cataclysm, many structures had been rebuilt to combine the best of magic and science. Gwangan Bridge, one of Busan’s landmarks, was no exception.
But the fact that the powerful defensive magic on Gwangan Bridge was shattered by that wave...
The answer was clear. There was more than salt and seaweed in that water.
Something had torn through the boundary between worlds and emerged into ours.
I breathed out and tightened my grip on my spear.
“Come at me, you octopus bastard.”
The Kraken took me up on it.
Whoooooosh!
Dozens of tentacles came at me with a tremendous shriek of displaced air. Their evenly spaced suction cups were so large they looked like black holes.
Damn it.
Who the hell said octopuses only had eight arms?
Internally clicking my tongue at the greater-than-expected number, I circulated internal energy through my legs.
Crack. Boom!
Spiderweb cracks raced across the hard ground, which burst apart beneath me. The recoil launched me between the Kraken’s enormous tentacles.
An arc of White Flame slashed down like a flash of lightning.
Slash!
Three or four tentacles as thick as logs were cleanly severed.
They were only the relatively thin tips, but anyone would feel that pain.
The Kraken’s tentacle, which had been about to strike the section of Gwangan Bridge where I had stood only moments earlier, twitched and trembled before slapping against the surface of the water.
Splash!
I had avoided the attack, but it was not over.
This is a bad place to fight.
Gwangan Bridge had already collapsed, almost split in two, but survivors were still scattered everywhere nearby. The screams coming from behind me were proof enough.
If I fought the Kraken here, there was a high chance of causing many unexpected casualties.
At this rate...
The battlefield, the surroundings, what I needed to do—there was only one answer.
Step. Tap.
The tip of my foot gently touched empty air.
Stepping on Empty Air. It consumed internal energy at a punishing rate, so I couldn’t keep it up for long. I had no intention of dragging this fight out anyway.
Whoooooosh!
Nothing made an easier target than someone hanging in midair.
The Kraken’s tentacles swept toward me as if dancing. I brought my spearhead down at an angle.
Fwoosh—shhhhhk!
Blue flames split into dozens of streaks and shot through the air.
However strong the Kraken was, it couldn’t withstand Force.
Slash! Splash!
The tentacles swinging at me from every direction were severed in a single stroke.
Sizzle.
The Scorching Yang Qi carried by the Force burned the flesh even as it cut through. The Kraken roared in agony.
—Grrrrrrooooooar!
Of all kinds of pain, burns were the most agonizing.
I didn’t miss the moment it faltered.
Bang!
Compressed air burst beneath my toes. The spearhead held upright plunged down, slicing through the fierce wind.
At its tip was the face of a gigantic octopus.
Shhhhhhhk!

chapters.title: Chapter 573
paragraphs: Everything had an order and a progression.
Mutated Gates were no exception.
When a magical power reading crossed a certain threshold, an alarm sounded and everyone nearby received an evacuation order.
But the ordinary Grade C Gate had become a Mutated Gate and then a Monster Wave in just a few dozen seconds.
The reading was so far beyond anything on record that the Gate management office could only suspect a measurement error.
Their deliberation lasted less than a minute. Then the Kraken tore through space into this world and smashed the Gate management office before anything else.
Boom!
And the flames of disaster spread in every direction in an instant.
The Kraken was the terror of the black sea, a king of immense power. And a king like that had savage, loyal soldiers.
—Ssssss!
Fins moved without pause. Gills opened and closed.
A Merman appeared, making a strange cry, and the intersection crowded with cars and people fell silent.
“What is that...?”
The question went unfinished.
Whoosh—crack!
It happened in an instant.
A barnacle-covered trident pierced through a human body and continued flying, punching straight through even a vehicle waiting at the light.
Boom!
Vehicle fragments flew in every direction with the sound of an explosion.
As people stared at the impossible sight, alarms around the intersection sounded and warnings arrived on their smartphones.
Weeeeeeeeng!
Ding. Beep-beep. Bzzzz.
The noise broke the silence.
People looked from the burning car to the Merman standing in the road. Only then did they realize the danger was right in front of them.
“M-Monster!”
“It’s a Monster Wave!”
“Aaaaaaaah!”
The crowds scattered, screaming.
All they could think about was getting away from the monsters and staying alive. Rules and laws meant nothing now.
“Fuck, move!”
“W-wait...!”
Crash! Crack!
“Graaagh!”
People knocked one another down. A car sped through a red light and struck a pedestrian in the crosswalk.
Hooooonk! Thud!
“Ghk!”
After the Great Cataclysm, Korea had become the most densely populated country in the world.
An intersection in Busan, the country’s second-largest city, plunged into chaos and terror.
But there were exceptions.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Figures pushed against the current of the fleeing crowd.
There were only four of them, but their calm eyes and lightning-fast movements marked them as seasoned Hunters.
“Three o’clock!”
“Okay. All at once?”
“Cut down the ones in front first.”
“Don’t let them scatter!”
They had never met, but a few words were enough.
Each had spent anywhere from one to ten years fighting monsters. They knew exactly what they had to do.
If we don’t stop them here... we’re finished.
We have to hold them back somehow.
Fortunately, only around a dozen Mermen had appeared at the intersection.
None of the four was a particularly high-Grade Hunter, but against that many, they might be able to hold out and buy time.
“Surround them!”
They charged toward the Mermen. Then they stopped, despair taking hold.
Thud. Thud-thud. Thud-thud-thud!
—Ssssit!
—Ssssss!
The asphalt trembled beneath the weight of hundreds of Mermen charging toward them.
The first group had only been the vanguard. The main force had arrived.
And even this many might be just a fraction of it.
We’re finished.
All four thought the same thing.
Fighting a dozen Mermen would have meant risking their lives. For four low-to-mid-Grade Hunters, taking on this many was nearly impossible.
No—it was impossible without high-Grade Hunters to back them up.
“W-we could hold out until reinforcements arrive...”
“Hold out?”
A middle-aged Hunter muttered through clenched teeth in response to someone’s almost desperate suggestion.
“We’d get hacked to death a thousand times faster.”
“...Damn it.”
His entire body felt as heavy as cotton soaked in water. He had to fight, but he could not bring himself to do it.
They had families. They wanted to live. Only their duty and resolve as Hunters kept them from backing away.
But they would not be able to hold themselves back much longer.
—Aah, aaaaaah!
When had she appeared?
A song spread from atop a tall building. Its singer was a pale beauty wearing a pearl crown, her long, flowing hair covering her naked body.
A Siren.
A witch whose beautiful voice bewitched listeners and led them to ruin. The queen of the black sea.
There was only one, but her haunting, powerful voice filled the wide intersection.
People who had been screaming as they fled looked up at the half-human, half-bird monster floating like an angel. They stopped, rapture on their faces.
The Hunters gritted their teeth against her magic, but it did no good.
Drip. Drip.
Blood slipped between their clenched teeth and ran down their chins.
The song burrowed into their ears. Their grips on their weapons weakened, and the hundreds of Mermen drawing closer blurred before their eyes.
“God... damn it.”
They could see death coming. Neither they nor the nearly thousand civilians around them would escape it.
And the massacre wouldn’t end here. Even if high-Grade Hunters arrived, they couldn’t protect every one of Busan’s millions of citizens.
Fuck. I didn’t think I’d die like this.
It was too late. There was nothing he could do.
The middle-aged Hunter had given up. He was staring at the Siren through blurred eyes when—
—Aah, aaaaaah...!
Fwooooosh—crack!
Something shrieked through the air, and the song cut off.
Dark blue blood, the color of the sea, burst from the Siren. Her beating wings snapped, and the half-human, half-bird monster fell from the sky onto the asphalt.
Whoooosh—thud!
“Huh?”
—Ssssit?
With the enchanted song gone, their minds cleared.
The surviving humans and the Mermen who had watched their queen die stared at the fallen Siren.
Her eyes were frozen wide. The impact had knocked off her pearl crown and spread her hair apart, revealing something long and pointed jutting out between her breasts.
Was that...?
“Bone?”
The question had barely left the middle-aged Hunter’s lips when—
Whooooooosh!
A strange noise rang out, and a shadow fell over everyone’s heads.
Everyone looked up.
Something enormous and pure white covered the sky far above them. At its center stood a man.
“This body. Descends.”
The arrogant yet powerful voice pierced everyone’s ears.
When golden hair flashed briefly in their vision, the unidentified man pointed toward the hundreds of Mermen and continued speaking.
“You. Die.”
The Mermen’s eyes widened. At the same instant, the white mass casting its shadow over them flashed.
Papapapapat!
Bone. It was bone.
Sharper than spearheads and as fast as arrows, bone fragments rained down on the intersection.
Fwooooosh! Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Thousands of bone fragments fired at once smashed scales and tore through fins.
A Merman that barely managed to knock away several bone fragments with its spear was immediately turned into a pincushion by another fragment that came flying at it, then collapsed.
Thud-thud-thud!
The downpour of bones struck monsters alone.

Thump. Thump. Crash!

No. They had melted.
One Merman, apparently their commander, let out an urgent cry.
—Ssssit, ssssssit!
—Sss. Ssssit!

That damned human. He puts me through all this?

Whoooooosh!
Gwooooooar!
Boom! Krrrrr-boom!

Slash!

I dodged an incoming tentacle and stepped on empty air, leaping higher. Beneath my feet was a gigantic pair of eyes.
Time to finish this.
Fwoosh.

Fire Dragon Divine Spear, Third Form: Takoyaki.

sentences.text: Everything had an order and a progression.
Mutated Gates were no exception.
When a magical power reading crossed a certain threshold, an alarm sounded and everyone nearby received an evacuation order.
But the ordinary Grade C Gate had become a Mutated Gate and then a Monster Wave in just a few dozen seconds.
The reading was so far beyond anything on record that the Gate management office could only suspect a measurement error.
Their deliberation lasted less than a minute.
Then the Kraken tore through space into this world and smashed the Gate management office before anything else.
Boom!
And the flames of disaster spread in every direction in an instant.
The Kraken was the terror of the black sea, a king of immense power.
And a king like that had savage, loyal soldiers.
—Ssssss!
Fins moved without pause.
Gills opened and closed.
A Merman appeared, making a strange cry, and the intersection crowded with cars and people fell silent.
“What is that...?”
The question went unfinished.
Whoosh—crack!
It happened in an instant.
A barnacle-covered trident pierced through a human body and continued flying, punching straight through even a vehicle waiting at the light.
Boom!
Vehicle fragments flew in every direction with the sound of an explosion.
As people stared at the impossible sight, alarms around the intersection sounded and warnings arrived on their smartphones.
Weeeeeeeeng!
Ding.
Beep-beep.
Bzzzz.
The noise broke the silence.
People looked from the burning car to the Merman standing in the road.
Only then did they realize the danger was right in front of them.
“M-Monster!”
“It’s a Monster Wave!”
“Aaaaaaaah!”
The crowds scattered, screaming.
All they could think about was getting away from the monsters and staying alive.
Rules and laws meant nothing now.
“Fuck, move!”
“W-wait...!”
Crash!
Crack!
“Graaagh!”
People knocked one another down.
A car sped through a red light and struck a pedestrian in the crosswalk.
Hooooonk!
Thud!
“Ghk!”
After the Great Cataclysm, Korea had become the most densely populated country in the world.
An intersection in Busan, the country’s second-largest city, plunged into chaos and terror.
But there were exceptions.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Figures pushed against the current of the fleeing crowd.
There were only four of them, but their calm eyes and lightning-fast movements marked them as seasoned Hunters.
“Three o’clock!”
“Okay.
All at once?”
“Cut down the ones in front first.”
“Don’t let them scatter!”
They had never met, but a few words were enough.
Each had spent anywhere from one to ten years fighting monsters.
They knew exactly what they had to do.
If we don’t stop them here... we’re finished.
We have to hold them back somehow.
Fortunately, only around a dozen Mermen had appeared at the intersection.
None of the four was a particularly high-Grade Hunter, but against that many, they might be able to hold out and buy time.
“Surround them!”
They charged toward the Mermen.
Then they stopped, despair taking hold.
Thud.
Thud-thud.
Thud-thud-thud!
—Ssssit!
—Ssssss!
The asphalt trembled beneath the weight of hundreds of Mermen charging toward them.
The first group had only been the vanguard.
The main force had arrived.
And even this many might be just a fraction of it.
We’re finished.
All four thought the same thing.
Fighting a dozen Mermen would have meant risking their lives.
For four low-to-mid-Grade Hunters, taking on this many was nearly impossible.
No—it was impossible without high-Grade Hunters to back them up.
“W-we could hold out until reinforcements arrive...”
“Hold out?”
A middle-aged Hunter muttered through clenched teeth in response to someone’s almost desperate suggestion.
“We’d get hacked to death a thousand times faster.”
“...Damn it.”
His entire body felt as heavy as cotton soaked in water.
He had to fight, but he could not bring himself to do it.
They had families.
They wanted to live.
Only their duty and resolve as Hunters kept them from backing away.
But they would not be able to hold themselves back much longer.
—Aah, aaaaaah!
When had she appeared?
A song spread from atop a tall building.
Its singer was a pale beauty wearing a pearl crown, her long, flowing hair covering her naked body.
A Siren.
A witch whose beautiful voice bewitched listeners and led them to ruin.
The queen of the black sea.
There was only one, but her haunting, powerful voice filled the wide intersection.
People who had been screaming as they fled looked up at the half-human, half-bird monster floating like an angel.
They stopped, rapture on their faces.
The Hunters gritted their teeth against her magic, but it did no good.
Drip.
Drip.
Blood slipped between their clenched teeth and ran down their chins.
The song burrowed into their ears.
Their grips on their weapons weakened, and the hundreds of Mermen drawing closer blurred before their eyes.

They could see death coming.

Even if high-Grade Hunters arrived, they couldn’t protect every one of Busan’s millions of citizens.

It was too late.

chapters.title: Chapter 574
paragraphs: Squelch!
The blade of White Flame pierced the enormous eye. The Kraken, terror of the sea, shuddered in agony.
But its pain was far from over.
Boom!
Flames burst forth, evaporating the blood. Powerful qi surged down the spearhead and tore through the Kraken’s insides.
A full three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi had done more than roast one of its eyes. It was enough to inflict grievous internal injuries.
—Gwooooooar!
Roaring in pain unlike anything it had ever felt, the Kraken whipped its eight tentacles in every direction.
It was trying to shake me off.
I held on, driving the spearhead deeper, and slammed my fist into its enormous eye.
Whoom! Thud!
With a divine weapon like White Flame in hand, I had little reason to use my fists or feet. But a fist thrown with strength and speed far beyond human limits was a deadly weapon in its own right.
Thud! Thud! Thuuud!
My fists came down like streaks of light, and the Kraken’s massive body writhed again.
—Ghk, gwooooooar!
Boom! Splash!
Its eight tentacles hammered the sea, throwing up walls of water and raising waves.
I got drenched in salt water and licked my lips. The briny taste spread across my tongue.
“Stay still. I’m not done yet.”
How many people had died or been injured in this Monster Wave?
The collapse of Gwangan Bridge alone had already caused hundreds of casualties. Every one of them was someone’s father or mother, or a child so precious someone couldn’t bear to see them hurt.
You have to pay.
The Kraken had destroyed more than a bridge.
Hundreds of precious lives had sunk beneath the white foam. So had promises made to people who would never be seen again.
Crack!
I tightened my grip on the spear shaft and sent internal energy surging through the mythical monster’s body like an electric current.
Boom.
A small explosion sounded somewhere deep beneath its wet, glistening skin.
“Gaaaaaah! Hu. Maaaan!”
I had aimed for its head to end things quickly. But perhaps because of its enormous size, even a devastating blow couldn’t kill it instantly.
I answered without the slightest hesitation.
“Give up. You’re going to die here anyway.”
That much wasn’t going to change.
I felt the Kraken stiffen at my flat response. It must have been startled to hear a human speaking the Demon Realm language, which only highly intelligent monsters could use.
“You. Are. Clearly. Human.”
“Of course I’m human, you fucking bastard. Do I look like an octopus to you?”
It was all thanks to the System’s Integrated Language Pack, but I saw no reason to explain that to it.
Instead, while it hesitated, I drove a fist toward the area above its eye.
Fwoosh.
Blue flames flickered over my clenched fist.
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist—the technique that had once turned Tibet’s Potala Palace into a “Crash Mansion.”
The hammer of Scorching Yang Qi pierced the Kraken’s skin, protected though it was by magical power.
Gwaaaaaang!
Keep striking even the hardest rock, and eventually it will break.
With enough internal energy behind it, the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist could bring down not just a rock, but a monster hundreds of times larger than a human.
Fwoosh!
Blue blood surged upward, and the Kraken’s body trembled.
It had thrashed so violently that every yacht and fishing boat moored nearby was smashed to pieces. Now, instead of a thunderous roar, it let out a faint groan.
“...You. Human.”
“Shut your mouth.”
At last, I could see the end of this fight.
Sensing victory, I yanked White Flame from its eye at lightning speed and brought it down.
Or I was about to.
“Did you. Humans. Not give me. Power?”
The spearhead stopped in midair, just short of piercing the Kraken’s head.
Countless thoughts flashed through my mind. I stared at it in confusion.
“What did you just say?”
Its limp body stirred at my question.
The Kraken was laughing. I was sure of it.
“Interesting.”
“Answer my question. Before it stops being interesting.”
“Did I not. Tell you? You were the ones. Who gave me power.”
“What do you mean by—”
Something felt wrong. As I tried to ask again, the Kraken drew a ragged breath and spoke.
“It must be cramped. Isn’t it?”
“Go outside. There’s a wider sea.”
I froze.
That wasn’t the Kraken’s voice. It wasn’t the Demon Realm language, either.
Unlike its halting speech until now, this voice flowed smoothly. It was unmistakably—
Korean?
Yes. It was definitely Korean.
The Kraken was imitating someone I didn’t know. No—it was closer to replaying a memory exactly as it had happened.
The unfamiliar voice that followed confirmed it.
“The one who gave me power. The one who led me outside.”
Blue blood ran like a tear from its charred eye.
The Kraken looked at me with that eye—already dead, yet still full of hatred and despair—and continued.
“They were all human.”
At the word human, a chill so cold it made me shudder climbed my spine.
Things that hadn’t quite made sense flashed through my mind, one after another.
The Monster Wave had moved so quickly that no one could respond.
The Kraken was extraordinarily powerful, even for a named monster.
And the Kraken itself had admitted that someone else was involved.
If all of that is true...
Someone deliberately caused the Monster Wave.
My teeth clenched at the thought. An artificially caused Monster Wave? It shouldn’t have been possible. It should never be allowed to happen.
But...
Damn it. It is possible.
The total amount of magical power determined whether a Gate mutated or a Monster Wave occurred.
If the magical power exceeded the amount a Gate could contain, the two phenomena described above would occur.
And there was a way to raise that amount artificially.
Magic Gems.
The scattered pieces fell into place.
If it absorbed a Magic Gem containing a monster’s magical power—an unpurified Magic Gem that had not undergone the purification process at human hands—it could be the only answer to this mystery.
But who? Why?
Someone had made the Kraken absorb a Magic Gem, turning it into a named monster. Then they had brought about a Monster Wave and unleashed this disaster.
It was terrorism. An atrocity no human should have been capable of committing.
Who would do that?
The hand holding White Flame trembled. Question after question crowded my mind, leaving it dark as a sky covered in clouds.
Ironically, only one creature could answer them.
“...Tell me. Everything you saw and heard.”
I spat out the words. The Kraken gave a low, rumbling laugh.
“Why. Should I?”
“Because if you don’t tell me right now, I’ll kill you.”
“How frightening. Truly frightening.”
The mockery was obvious.
I pressed the spearhead farther in, but it only laughed through the pain and refused to yield.
“Ask. Your own kind.”
“You fucking octopus.”
“Kill. Me. Human.”
I clenched my teeth, fighting the urge to put a hole through the damned octopus’s head right then and there.
Grind.
I had to kill it. I knew I did.
I had watched it all with my own eyes—the Kraken sacrificing hundreds of people.
If I included the other monsters under its command, the number of casualties might exceed several thousand.
Even now, someone somewhere in this city was probably screaming as they died.
But...
“...Fuck.”
I couldn’t kill the Kraken.
For what it had done, I wanted to beat it to death a hundred times over. A thousand times. But finding the person behind this damned disaster mattered more.
If I couldn’t catch the bastard who had made the Kraken absorb a Magic Gem and brought about the Monster Wave, this would only be the beginning.
And people would die every time.
Was it the internal energy I’d spent? Or the unexpected existence of a traitor? My body felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton, and fatigue hit me all at once.
Sunlight beat down on my head.
Fuck. Of course the weather’s nice.
It was a damn beautiful day and a god-awful situation.
I let out a rough breath and pulled White Flame from the Kraken’s head.
Fsssh!
Blue blood gushed around the white spearhead as it came free.
I have to keep this thing alive.
The only witness—and the only one who could testify—was a monster.
Exhaustion weighed on me as I loosened my grip on the spear shaft.
Slide.
And that was both the only miscalculation I made in this battle and the most painful mistake.
Whoooooosh!
It happened in an instant.
The Kraken’s massive body, limp as though half-dead, thrashed. All eight tentacles came flying at me.
“Hup!”
Tap-tap. Whoosh!
I belatedly came to my senses, stepped on the Kraken’s head, and launched myself into the air.
For a heartbeat, I thought I’d dodged the ambush.
Then I realized what the Kraken had really intended.
Fwoooooosh!
Black liquid spread through the air for dozens of meters in every direction.
It had planned this from beginning to end. With my guard down, I had no room to dodge all of it.
Splash!
Even moving as fast as I could, I couldn’t avoid all of it as it spread across such a wide area.
And the instant the black liquid—perhaps roughly the amount in a cup of milk—touched my entire body, an unexpected System alert rang out.
Beep.

System You have come into contact with Kraken’s Ink! Kraken’s Ink is a deadly poison with tremendous toxicity! Status Abnormality: Poisoned has been applied! Status Abnormality: Paralyzed has been applied! Strength temporarily decreases significantly! Agility temporarily decreases drastically! Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons begins resisting! Using internal energy can rapidly drive out the poison!
My body grew heavy along with the System alert.
The black liquid was ink—and a deadly poison at that.
Damn it.
Why had I let my guard down? Why hadn’t I suspected it right to the end?
The regret was bitter, but it was too late.
I drew up Scorching Yang Qi to counter the poison and put on the Myriad-Poison Ring from my Inventory.
Ding.
Another System alert sounded, and purification began.
But that was another mistake. The Kraken had seized the moment I let my guard down, and I wasn’t its target.
Splashhhhh!
Its massive body shot forward like a ray of light, throwing up waves.
Gwangan Bridge lay ahead. Survivors were still there, waiting to be rescued.
“Human! Try. To. Kill. Me!”
There was scarcely time to think. Countless thoughts flashed through my mind, but the answer had been decided from the start.
A Murim warrior fought. A Hunter had to fight and protect people at the same time.
Crack.
I tightened my grip on the spear shaft, still cold despite all the blood it had soaked up.
In midair, I drew back my shoulder and twisted my waist. Internal energy raced through my coiled muscles and acupoints toward the spearhead.
Fwoosh.
Blue flames burned beneath the blazing sun. Sunlight shattered against the spearhead.
And then...
Now.
Die.
I swung my arm with every intention of killing it. The spear, engulfed in hellfire, shot forward as a beam of light.
Whooooooosh! Boom!
Compressed air burst outward, and the sea split apart.
At the end of its path was the Kraken’s enormous body, bearing down on the survivors.
Boom!
Blue blood fell like rain.

The Kraken was imitating someone I didn’t know.
No—it was closer to replaying a memory exactly as it had happened.
The unfamiliar voice that followed confirmed it.
“The one who gave me power.
The one who led me outside.”
Blue blood ran like a tear from its charred eye.
The Kraken looked at me with that eye—already dead, yet still full of hatred and despair—and continued.
“They were all human.”
At the word human, a chill so cold it made me shudder climbed my spine.
Things that hadn’t quite made sense flashed through my mind, one after another.
The Monster Wave had moved so quickly that no one could respond.
The Kraken was extraordinarily powerful, even for a named monster.
And the Kraken itself had admitted that someone else was involved.
If all of that is true...
Someone deliberately caused the Monster Wave.
My teeth clenched at the thought.
An artificially caused Monster Wave?
It shouldn’t have been possible.
It should never be allowed to happen.
But...
Damn it.
It is possible.
The total amount of magical power determined whether a Gate mutated or a Monster Wave occurred.
If the magical power exceeded the amount a Gate could contain, the two phenomena described above would occur.
And there was a way to raise that amount artificially.
Magic Gems.
The scattered pieces fell into place.
If it absorbed a Magic Gem containing a monster’s magical power—an unpurified Magic Gem that had not undergone the purification process at human hands—it could be the only answer to this mystery.
But who?
Why?
Someone had made the Kraken absorb a Magic Gem, turning it into a named monster.
Then they had brought about a Monster Wave and unleashed this disaster.
It was terrorism.
An atrocity no human should have been capable of committing.
Who would do that?
The hand holding White Flame trembled.
Question after question crowded my mind, leaving it dark as a sky covered in clouds.
Ironically, only one creature could answer them.
“...Tell me.
Everything you saw and heard.”
I spat out the words.
The Kraken gave a low, rumbling laugh.
“Why.
Should I?”
“Because if you don’t tell me right now, I’ll kill you.”
“How frightening.
Truly frightening.”
The mockery was obvious.
I pressed the spearhead farther in, but it only laughed through the pain and refused to yield.
“Ask.
Your own kind.”
“You fucking octopus.”
“Kill.
Me.
Human.”
I clenched my teeth, fighting the urge to put a hole through the damned octopus’s head right then and there.
Grind.
I had to kill it.
I knew I did.
I had watched it all with my own eyes—the Kraken sacrificing hundreds of people.
If I included the other monsters under its command, the number of casualties might exceed several thousand.
Even now, someone somewhere in this city was probably screaming as they died.
But...
“...Fuck.”
I couldn’t kill the Kraken.
For what it had done, I wanted to beat it to death a hundred times over.
A thousand times.
But finding the person behind this damned disaster mattered more.
If I couldn’t catch the bastard who had made the Kraken absorb a Magic Gem and brought about the Monster Wave, this would only be the beginning.
And people would die every time.
Was it the internal energy I’d spent?
Or the unexpected existence of a traitor?
My body felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton, and fatigue hit me all at once.
Sunlight beat down on my head.
Fuck.
Of course the weather’s nice.
It was a damn beautiful day and a god-awful situation.
I let out a rough breath and pulled White Flame from the Kraken’s head.
Fsssh!
Blue blood gushed around the white spearhead as it came free.
I have to keep this thing alive.
The only witness—and the only one who could testify—was a monster.
Exhaustion weighed on me as I loosened my grip on the spear shaft.
Slide.
And that was both the only miscalculation I made in this battle and the most painful mistake.
Whoooooosh!
It happened in an instant.
The Kraken’s massive body, limp as though half-dead, thrashed.
All eight tentacles came flying at me.
“Hup!”
Tap-tap.
Whoosh!
I belatedly came to my senses, stepped on the Kraken’s head, and launched myself into the air.
For a heartbeat, I thought I’d dodged the ambush.
Then I realized what the Kraken had really intended.
Fwoooooosh!
Black liquid spread through the air for dozens of meters in every direction.
It had planned this from beginning to end.
With my guard down, I had no room to dodge all of it.
Splash!
Even moving as fast as I could, I couldn’t avoid all of it as it spread across such a wide area.
And the instant the black liquid—perhaps roughly the amount in a cup of milk—touched my entire body, an unexpected System alert rang out.
Beep.
System You have come into contact with Kraken’s Ink!
Kraken’s Ink is a deadly poison with tremendous toxicity!
Status Abnormality: Poisoned has been applied!
Status Abnormality: Paralyzed has been applied!
Strength temporarily decreases significantly!
Agility temporarily decreases drastically!
Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons begins resisting!
Using internal energy can rapidly drive out the poison!
My body grew heavy along with the System alert.
The black liquid was ink—and a deadly poison at that.
Damn it.
Why had I let my guard down?
Why hadn’t I suspected it right to the end?
The regret was bitter, but it was too late.
I drew up Scorching Yang Qi to counter the poison and put on the Myriad-Poison Ring from my Inventory.
Ding.
Another System alert sounded, and purification began.
But that was another mistake.
The Kraken had seized the moment I let my guard down, and I wasn’t its target.
Splashhhhh!
Its massive body shot forward like a ray of light, throwing up waves.
Gwangan Bridge lay ahead.
Survivors were still there, waiting to be rescued.
“Human!
Try.
To.
Kill.
Me!”
There was scarcely time to think.
Countless thoughts flashed through my mind, but the answer had been decided from the start.
A Murim warrior fought.
A Hunter had to fight and protect people at the same time.
Crack.
I tightened my grip on the spear shaft, still cold despite all the blood it had soaked up.
In midair, I drew back my shoulder and twisted my waist.
Internal energy raced through my coiled muscles and acupoints toward the spearhead.
Fwoosh.
Blue flames burned beneath the blazing sun.
Sunlight shattered against the spearhead.
And then...
Now.
Die.
I swung my arm with every intention of killing it.
The spear, engulfed in hellfire, shot forward as a beam of light.
Whooooooosh!
Boom!
Compressed air burst outward, and the sea split apart.
At the end of its path was the Kraken’s enormous body, bearing down on the survivors.
Boom!
Blue blood fell like rain.

chapters.title: Chapter 575
paragraphs: I didn’t need to see it up close or rush over to check for a pulse.
The moment the blue-flame-wreathed spearhead drove into the Kraken’s body, I knew.
It’s over.
Slash! Boom!
The spear cut through it, and fire qi exploded from within.
The monster’s head, some ten meters tall, burst like a balloon. Blue blood that hadn’t evaporated rained down over the sea.
And then—
Whoooooosh—
As the Kraken’s enormous body finally collapsed, a clear chime rang in my ears.
Ding.

System You have defeated Lv. 140 ‘King of the Black Sea’ Kraken! You have gained a large amount of EXP! Myriad-Poison Ring has detoxified all poison within your body! Status Abnormality: Poisoned disappears! Status Abnormality: Paralyzed disappears!
Even with the System telling me I’d defeated the Kraken, my mouth felt as gritty as if I were chewing sand.
Damn it.
I should have kept it alive. Somehow, I should have kept it alive long enough to learn who was really behind this.
But one moment of carelessness had brought about consequences I couldn’t undo. The Kraken was dead, and the question remained unanswered.
If it had attacked me directly, I might have had a chance to capture it, but...
Too late now.
The Kraken had been smarter than I’d thought.
It knew I was stronger than it, even poisoned. It knew it couldn’t escape.
That was why it had gone after the survivors instead of me. It would rather die than be captured.
Faced with its final desperate move, I’d had only one choice.
“...Phew.”
I sighed, looking at the Kraken’s corpse half-submerged in the sea.
There had been no other choice. If I hadn’t killed it with that one strike, someone would have died right in front of me.

People talked about sacrificing the small for the sake of the greater good, but that was just a pretty phrase. In the end, it was still a sacrifice—doing nothing while someone died pointlessly, despite having the power to prevent it.
I shouldn’t have let my guard down. Not until it was over...
But what was done was done.
I was anxious and regretful that I had ultimately failed to uncover the truth behind the disaster. But I did not regret killing the Kraken.
People had survived because of my choice.
“Over here! Please, help us!”
“Cough! Please, my child...”
“Mom! Mooooom!”
Maybe fighting as far away from them as I could had helped.
Hundreds of people had been killed or injured before I’d even arrived, but there were still more survivors waiting to be rescued.
Their desperate cries came from the choppy water and the broken Gwangan Bridge. I forced down my exhaustion and shot toward them.
Fwoooooosh!
The briny, refreshing smell of the sea filled my nose.
I raced across the water like a gust of wind. Passing the Kraken’s floating corpse, I reached the survivors and began pulling them up.
“It’s dangerous out there, so everyone needs to stay here. If you still have the strength, help me rescue the others first.”
A young man who looked relatively unharmed spat out seawater.
“Cough. B-but shouldn’t we run somewhere else...?”
“Run?”
“Y-yes.”
I raised a hand and pointed. Black smoke rose between the densely packed buildings all around us.
Ordinary civilians couldn’t hear what I could, but my senses had already told me what was happening.
Hssssss!
“Tank! Three steps forward!”
“The building! The building is collapsing! The civilians are in danger!”
“Aaaaaagh!”
Rumble! Boom!
Faint screams and crashes. Humans and monsters were fighting in the streets not far away—and in several places at once.
“There are monsters in every direction. Still want to go?”
“...No. I’ll stay here.”
At least he caught on quickly.
The Kraken was dead, but this was far from over. If I was going to get this chaos under control, I had a busy day ahead of me.
Fwoooooosh! Boom!
The survivors stared, dazed, as I kicked off the water and shot into the sky.
Everyone ate. But who you ate with, and where, made a difference to how formal the meal was.
By that measure, the breakfast shared by the two people sitting across from each other had been formal indeed.
The late-starting breakfast had continued for a full two hours amid quiet conversation. By then, a beautifully decorated dish of sujeonggwa had been placed on the spotless white tablecloth.
“Since Seollal is just around the corner, I had tteokguk prepared... I’m not sure whether the meal suited your taste, Team Leader Choi.”
Choi Minwoo wiped his mouth with a napkin before answering the gentle, courteous voice.
“It was excellent, Mr. President. Thank you for taking such care.”
“Ha-ha. I’m glad.”
The middle-aged man across from him, President Baek Hanseong, smiled warmly.

“You’ve been so busy lately that I was worried you weren’t eating properly. So I repeatedly impressed upon the head chef here at the Blue House that you were an important guest and that he needed to take special care with your meal.”
“Important guest” was no empty compliment.
An invitation to breakfast at the Blue House already marked a person as powerful and influential. A meal alone with the President meant something more.
Baek Hanseong valued Choi Minwoo that highly.
“You eat well. It’s nice to see. Makes me proud, too.”
Choi Minwoo dipped his head.
“Thank you. Still, I don’t go hungry as often as you seem to think, Mr. President. I feel I may have caused you unnecessary concern.”
“Oh? Well, I suppose you have a personal chef.”
“No. Someone has been making my meals for me lately.”
“Someone making your meals... Ah, do you mean...?”
Choi Minwoo gave a small nod.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung’s mother cooks for me.”
“My goodness. His mother does it herself?”
“Yes. I’ve tried to refuse—it doesn’t feel right—but she won’t hear of it.”
President Baek Hanseong let out a quiet exclamation.
He already knew Jin Taekyung’s family was staying temporarily at Choi Minwoo’s estate. Hearing Choi himself speak about it, though, gave that fact new significance.
If she’s even cooking for him... They’re closer than I thought.
Jin Taekyung and Choi Minwoo. Choi Minwoo and Jin Taekyung.

From President Baek Hanseong’s perspective, the two men were not only enormous fish he could never afford to let go, but also the only means of restraining the Ares Guild, which wielded tremendous influence.
Jin Taekyung, with his extraordinary standing. Choi Minwoo, Cheon Taemin’s maternal grandson and only living blood relative.
With those two on his side, Baek could rise still higher. After becoming the youngest president in Korea’s history, he might well become the first to win reelection under the amended law.
Whatever it takes, I have to bring them both over to my side.
While President Baek Hanseong entertained thoroughly political thoughts, Choi Minwoo was thinking about something completely different as he drank his coffee.
She said she was making dinner tonight... Kimchi stew, was it?
Strange. He had just finished breakfast, yet his stomach felt empty.
He wanted Jin Taekyung’s mother’s kimchi stew more than the tteokguk the Blue House head chef—a master of Korean cuisine—had prepared with such care.
Fluffy white rice from a pressure cooker of a kind rarely seen these days. Pork cooked until tender, and well-aged kimchi.
And the people huddled around the same table, frantically moving their spoons.
Hmm.
As Choi Minwoo realized he was unconsciously smacking his lips, he let out a faint, bemused laugh.
So that’s what it is.
He wasn’t particularly fond of tteokguk or kimchi stew. Nor was he looking forward to dinner because her cooking was better than the Blue House chef’s.
He simply liked being there. The warm food, shared with warm people.
Home.
And family.
Choi Minwoo had lost both before he was as tall as the chair he sat in now. He had thought he could never have them again.
No. I do still have one family member.
A hero who had saved humanity. A living savior.
But a man who had been unable to protect his own family.
Choi Minwoo thought of the last time he had seen his maternal grandfather—a meeting he could no longer remember.
Soon... I’ll see you again.
At the thought of the grandfather who had shut himself away for decades, a feeling he couldn’t name rose within him.
Noticing that Choi Minwoo’s mood had changed, President Baek Hanseong asked with concern, “Is something troubling you?”
“Ah. No. It’s nothing.”
“Ha-ha. I see. Well, now that we’ve finished eating, there’s something important I’d like to discuss with you, Team Leader—”
The door flew open.
President Baek stopped mid-sentence. He frowned at the aide who had entered without knocking.
“I thought I told everyone not to come in.”
“I’m sorry. I tried to avoid it, but you weren’t answering...”
“Answering? Of course not. My phone’s on silent.”
With an important conversation under way, taking out a smartphone would have been discourteous, given who was at the table.
“Huff... I’m sorry. But it’s urgent.”
The aide was breathing hard, sweat beading on his forehead.
Sensing something was wrong, Choi Minwoo took the smartphone from inside his suit jacket. He had more than ten missed calls from Butler Kim and a string of text messages.
Dread rose in him.
Don’t tell me...
He opened the messages. One of his neatly groomed eyebrows twitched.
Butler Kim └ Butler Kim: Butler Kim └ Butler Kim: Emergency Monster Wave in Busan └ Butler Kim: Extra-large named monster sighted └ Butler Kim: Young Master, where are you? └ Butler Kim: Young Maᄂter
The messages were from Butler Kim. They were short, but there was nothing small about the news.
A Monster Wave? In Busan?
Busan was Korea’s second-largest city, home to millions. An extra-large named monster could cause an enormous loss of life just by doing a forward roll.
And what the aide said next made matters worse.
“The emergency alert was delayed for about ten minutes. The Monster Wave happened so suddenly, and the Gate management office and all the surrounding facilities were destroyed...”
“You idiot! Do you hear yourself?”
“I-I’m sorry.”
Sweat poured down the aide’s face as he continued.
“But according to the report that came in one minute ago, the extra-large named monster has been subdued. Hunter Jin Taekyung happened to arrive at the scene just in time...”
“What? Are you certain?”
“Yes. The remaining monsters are being dealt with, and survivors are being rescued.”
“...Phew. At least that’s a relief.”
President Baek Hanseong exhaled in relief, while Choi Minwoo rose from his seat without hesitation.
The worst of the immediate crisis might have passed, but this was no time to sit and talk.
“I’ll be going, Mr. President.”
“Of course. We’ll speak another time.”
They exchanged brief farewells. Choi Minwoo had just left the Blue House when—
Bzzzzzt.
The smartphone he had turned back on began vibrating forcefully again.
Team Leader Choi thought he knew who was calling and answered at once.
“Yes, Butler Kim. I’m on my way ri—”
“It’s me.”
Choi Minwoo stopped dead.
Song Cheonwoo’s aged voice came through the phone.
“Let’s talk for a moment. It’s urgent.”

chapters.title: Chapter 576
paragraphs: Click.
The short call ended. The signal ringing from the smartphone stopped, but the hand Choi Minwoo had raised to his ear did not come down easily.
He crossed the Green Garden in front of the Blue House residence, his expression conflicted. His steps had slowed. One thought filled his mind.
Song Cheonwoo wants to meet me. Right now.
Song Cheonwoo—the Trojan horse who could get him inside the impregnable fortress that was the Ares Guild.
Choi had been waiting for him to make contact. He simply had not expected it today, much less an immediate meeting.
He went over their brief conversation again.
What should I do?

Busan. And Song Cheonwoo.

Crunch.

A familiar face was waiting outside the main gate, beside the Blue House security office.
“Young Master.”
Choi greeted Butler Kim with a nod and stepped through the gate.

A sleek limousine, five black SUVs, and around twenty Hunters waited by the roadside. Every one of them was skilled enough to count among the elite of the Peace Guild, which had grown considerably. The Equipment they wore showed they were ready for battle.
Butler Kim’s next words confirmed Choi’s suspicion.
“We were waiting to escort you.”
“I’m sorry. Given where I was, I failed to check in time. More importantly, I heard that Mr. Jin Taekyung defeated a named monster. What is the current situation?”
“As you said, the named monster that appeared during this wave, the Kraken, has been eliminated. However, over a thousand Mermen have spread throughout Haeundae and Gwangalli.”
“The damage must be severe,” Choi said quietly.

Busan might not have been as large as Seoul, but it was Korea’s second-largest city, with a population approaching five million. For a thousand monsters to appear there, especially monsters strengthened by the recent rise in magic power, was nothing short of a disaster.
But Butler Kim calmly shook his head.
“It isn’t something to celebrate, but fortunately, casualties are far lower than we expected.”
“Even if Mr. Jin Taekyung defeated the Kraken, he couldn’t have stopped all thousand Mermen.”
“Skel—no. The Stone King was there.”
“Ah.”
The face of the blond foreigner who always wore an arrogant, self-assured expression flashed before Choi Minwoo’s eyes. He gave a small exclamation and nodded.
With him there, it’s possible.
Only a handful of people knew the truth about the undead monster caught in an identity crisis between monster and American. Choi also knew he was every bit as powerful as an S-rank Hunter.
“Yes. Fortunately, thanks to the efforts of those two, the damage is not particularly severe.”

It was extraordinary luck. Jin Taekyung and the Skeleton King were each a one-man army. And unlike the Skeleton King, whose abilities came with various restrictions, Jin Taekyung ranked among the strongest in Korea. No, in the entire world.
Except for one person...
