“About five minutes ago, we dispatched the emergency rescue team and three teams we had standing by to Busan. The Guilds and Hunters based there, along with outside reinforcements, are doing everything they can to keep the damage from spreading.”

Choi knew by heart how many Gates, Guilds, and Hunters there were across Korea. He blinked a few times as he calculated, then asked, “They’ll have the monsters contained within two hours at the latest. Correct?”
“Yes. Of course, rescuing the victims afterward will take considerable time as well...”
“Then we can’t call Mr. Jin Taekyung or the Stone King away under the circumstances.”
“Forgive me, Young Master, but call them away for what?”
“Never mind. Let’s go.”
Choi’s reply was quiet and final, but his lips moved again as he walked toward the limousine.
The words reached Butler Kim’s ear through what could no longer properly be called message magic. It was Sound Transmission.
—He has requested a meeting.
Butler Kim’s eyes trembled. Choi had not named him, but there was no mistaking who he meant.
—Song Cheonwoo?
—Yes.
—Young Master, it may be dangerous. The Busan Monster Wave is already nearing its end. We could go back to the Guild House instead—
—He spoke about my maternal grandfather’s safety. And about a trap Go Jun is setting.
Choi watched Butler Kim’s face go rigid and continued quietly.
—I have to meet him. Right now.
The B-rank Gate in Pyeongchang, Gangwon Province, known as Yeti’s Winter Range, was not an especially appealing raid site.
Even with exceptional physical abilities and Magic Equipment, fighting furry giants on a snowy mountain where your feet sank with every step was hardly pleasant.
Still, not everyone avoided Yeti’s Winter Range. Some Hunters continued to visit despite the recent, repeated rises in magic power. The group that had just ridden the lift down was among them.
“Damn it. No entry, all of a sudden?”
“Right? Hey, Team Leader, are we getting paid for today?”
“...You’re worse than a yeti. We couldn’t even get into the Gate because the magic power went up, and you’re asking about pay? Have you got no shame?”
“Aw, I got my hopes up for nothing. By the way, who were those people up there? The handsome guy wearing the mask looked kind of familiar.”
“Beats me. How would I know—huh?”
The thirty-odd Hunters came down the path grumbling. Their Team Leader, walking at the front, suddenly widened his eyes.
A man was walking up toward them at an unhurried pace.
“Tsk, tsk. Looks like he’s going to strike out too.”
The man had obviously come for a raid. The Team Leader called out to him. He looked to be in his forties.
“Yeti raid?”
The middle-aged man paused at the abrupt question, then nodded without a word.
The Team Leader clicked his tongue. “Then you’re out of luck too, Boss. Don’t bother going up. They’ve closed it off.”
“They say the magic power reading suddenly went up or something. Anyway, entry’s prohibited. That’s why we got turned back too.”
“...Hello? Did you hear me?”
The Team Leader frowned when he sensed something strange. Without answering a single word, the middle-aged man who had merely listened to him walked past the group.
Step. Step.
“What’s with that guy?” the Team Leader muttered as the man receded up the path.
To the middle-aged man, however, the Team Leader’s goodwill was nothing more than needless meddling.
Clatter.
The man rode the lift up with a slight jolt and found dozens of pairs of eyes waiting for him.
A Hunter who looked quite capable stepped forward to bar his way.
“Sorry, but due to the rise in the magic power reading, you can’t enter the Gate—”
“He’s my guest.”
At the quiet voice, the twenty-odd Hunters standing like a wall parted to let him through.
Two people stood at the end of the path they made.
“You’re late.”
At Choi Minwoo’s flat voice, the middle-aged man whose appearance had been changed by an illusion spell—Song Cheonwoo—finally parted his tightly closed lips.
“I had to be careful. And you were the one who chose this place, Minwoo.”
“I wasn’t the one who suggested meeting at a Gate. Surely that gave me the right to choose which one.”
“We had to avoid wiretapping and any other surveillance. None of it will work once we’re inside.”
“Then there should be no problem. This Gate belongs to the Peace Guild. It’s a suitable place for both of us to be cautious.”
“...Both of us? You suspect me?”
It was Butler Kim, standing quietly behind Choi, who answered.
“Why should the Young Master trust you?”
“Come now, Hwajong.”
“Do not call me by my name. Whatever relationship we had ended long ago.”
Song Cheonwoo’s eyelids trembled at Butler Kim’s glacial stare.
Once, they had been close enough to call each other brothers. Then their paths had split between loyalty and ambition.
As an icy chill settled between them, a quiet voice rang out.
“I believe there’s something more important we need to discuss first.”
The words were gentle, but they cut to the point. Both men backed down. Choi glanced from one to the other, then turned toward the Gate entrance, where a field of magic power shimmered.
“You two will come inside with me. The other Guild members will keep anyone else from entering.”
Choi went first. Butler Kim and Song Cheonwoo followed.
Whoooooosh.
Cold, sticky magic power enveloped them. When they opened their eyes again, a world of white stretched before them.
Yeti’s Winter Range.
Snowdrifts lay in every direction across its steep slopes. Somewhere in the mountains, a monster roared.
—Kraaaaaaaar!
The three men remained unmoved by the bitter cold and the chilling cry. They were far too powerful to fear a mere yeti. Besides, they had come for a private conversation, not a raid.
“Tell me about my maternal grandfather’s safety,” Choi said. “And the trap Go Jun is preparing.”
Song gave a bitter smile at the direct demand.
“Although I have not watched you for long... your personality has not changed.”
“Just get to the point. I don’t think I’m asking much.”
Song let out a shallow breath. White mist rose into the wind as he spoke, his voice sounding older than before.
“Would you walk with me a little? I’d like to speak to you alone.”
Butler Kim frowned. Choi answered evenly.
“Is that necessary?”
“You still suspect me.”
“I still have no reason to trust you.”
“This Gate belongs to the Peace Guild, not to me or Ares. You chose it yourself. How could I have set a trap here?”
“I’m not stupid enough to try something against my only ally.”
Choi had been looking out across the snowy mountains. He turned and studied Song’s eyes. They did not waver in the slightest.
“Very well.”
“Young Master,” Butler Kim said.
“Don’t worry. I won’t go far.”
“...Then I’ll follow at a distance.”
Song nodded and slowly drew the weapon at his waist.
“I suppose I can’t stop you doing that. Suit yourself.”
“You—!”
“Don’t misunderstand.”
Thud.
What Butler Kim feared did not happen. Song drove his weapon deep into the snow for them to see, and Choi started walking.
Crunch. Crunch.
Snow crumbled beneath their feet as they walked side by side.
After a few steps, Song finally broke his silence.
“There’s a secret area inside Ares Guild headquarters. Only a handful of people can enter.”
“Are you referring to Area A?”
Song’s eyes widened at the unexpected question.
“I knew the area existed and what it was called,” Choi said calmly. “I couldn’t find out anything more.”
“...Impressive. How did you learn even that?”
“I put in more effort than you might imagine. What I need now isn’t praise, though. I need details. What does Area A have to do with my maternal grandfather’s safety?”
“Because that person is there.”
Crunch.
Choi stopped dead at those two words. After a moment of silence, he began walking again.
“That information is not certain.”
“Why do you say that?”
“You were pushed out of the Ares Guild’s inner circle long ago, Director Song.”
“...That stings. But you’re right. I can’t be certain.”
“I also can’t see why my maternal grandfather would be there. No—I can’t understand it.”
“A reason...”
Song sighed softly.
“You wouldn’t understand. No one knows what happened to that person—not even you.”
“What are you—”
Choi Minwoo turned to him with a questioning expression. Then, at the next words, he froze.
“It happened more than twenty years ago. That person lost consciousness.”

chapters.title: Chapter 577
paragraphs: Choi Minwoo’s face had gone rigid. His eyes trembled faintly as he stared at Song Cheonwoo.
“What... do you mean?”
“You may find it hard to believe, but it’s true.”
Song continued with a sigh.
“It happened suddenly, one day. No one saw it coming.”
Choi clenched his fists without realizing it.
He did not trust Song Cheonwoo, but he could sense no trace of a lie in the old man before him.
Then is it really true?
His heart sank. A bead of cold sweat rolled down the back of his neck.
He barely managed to force the words past his tightly pressed lips.
“But I’ve never heard anything like that from anyone. Not even Butler Kim, who was my maternal grandfather’s closest aide...”
Before Choi could finish, Song shook his head.
“It isn’t that he chose not to tell you. He couldn’t.”
“Then...”
“I’m sorry.”
Wouldn’t and couldn’t. A small difference in words, but an enormous difference in meaning. Choi understood what Song was saying and glared at him.
“You hid it from Butler Kim too? Something this important?”
The old man nodded quietly. When he spoke, his voice sounded older than ever.
“Hwajong was always loyal. And he gave that same loyalty to a child born after the war—a boy who lost his parents in an accident and was left alone.”
“Even on the day everything changed, your grandfather’s most loyal aide was at your side.”
Choi turned his head without realizing it.
Far across the snow, Butler Kim stood watching them.
If the howling blizzard had not swallowed Song’s voice, that loyal servant would have come flying over to kill the traitor.
“Is that why you asked me to walk with you alone?”
“I had no choice. If he’d heard us, we couldn’t have continued this conversation.”
“If Butler Kim had heard about my maternal grandfather back then, you two would already have...”
His usual calm composure was gone.
Blue fire seemed to flicker in Choi’s eyes. Song could not bring himself to meet his gaze and looked away.
“At first, we were only bewildered. We thought he would regain consciousness soon, so we kept it strictly confidential.”
Crunch.
Song took a weary step and continued.
“But then a month passed. Half a year. A year. And a strange thought occurred to me. What if... he never woke up?”
Song Cheonwoo and Lee Jungryong.
What the two men had scarcely dared consider at first hardened into certainty as time passed. Then that certainty gave way to something else.
“Another year passed, and we recognized the greed in each other.”
The greed to fill the place left vacant by Cheon Taemin, a man no one had dared challenge. The desire to become master of the great fortress that was Ares Guild.
“The purge began quietly one day. Unlike Kim Hwajong, who had already drifted away from Ares Guild, several of his closest aides knew of his condition. They died in Gates.”
Choi bit down hard on his lip.
From ancient times to the present, death had been the surest way to bury the truth.
Lee Jungryong and Song Cheonwoo had chosen that path to usurp the throne of a king who was still alive.
Crack.
Choi’s smooth lips split, and red blood ran down his chin. As he walked, his angry steps crushed the drops falling onto the white snow.
“You managed to survive, Regional Director. You really do have a stubborn hold on life.”
Song answered his cutting words in a weak voice.
“Getting rid of me wouldn’t have been easy for Lee Jungryong. Besides, we’d both covered ourselves in filth fighting over Ares Guild. He must have judged that I was unlikely to talk. He was right.”
Knowing the truth was reason enough to be killed. Having wallowed in the mud together could be reason enough to be spared.
And to Choi, Song Cheonwoo had never seemed capable of fighting Lee Jungryong to the bitter end.
“Was the European regional director’s position the price of that deal?”
“Yes. It saved my life and my family’s.”
Choi drew a deep breath. At last, the pieces of the puzzle that had eluded him fell into place.
Why Lee Jungryong, cold and thorough as he was, had kept Song Cheonwoo alive.
And why Choi’s grandfather, his only blood relative and a symbol to the world, had not appeared in more than twenty years.
—Kraaaaaaar!
A yeti roared somewhere in the mountains, as if giving voice to Choi’s feelings.
Damn it.
Crack.
The bones in his tightly clenched fist shifted audibly.

He wanted to scream. To ask why they had done it, and what they had hoped to gain. He wanted to shout at the top of his lungs, seize the old man walking ahead by the collar, draw the sword at his waist, and stab him in the back.
But...
Swish. Thud.
His hand moved toward the hilt, then fell away before it reached it.
Not yet. Song Cheonwoo would answer for what he had done, but only after Choi had confirmed all the facts.
Choi forced his pounding heart to settle and spoke in a trembling voice.
“Why did my grandfather collapse?”
Crunch.
Song’s footsteps stopped. Ahead of him, the ground gave way to empty air.
A crevasse—the kind of fissure found in snowy mountains and glaciers—cut through the mountain. It was enormous, and its depths were too dark to fathom.
“Why. Why, you ask...”
Song Cheonwoo stared down at the darkness spread before his feet and muttered in a low voice.
“I don’t know.”
“Be clear. Do you not know, or do you want to pretend you don’t?”
“Do you think Lee Jungryong or I pulled some kind of trick? On him, of all people?”
“That...”
Choi fell silent. He remembered who his grandfather was.
Cheon Taemin. Humanity’s immortal hero. The first and last Hunter to defeat the countless monsters that had descended upon Earth, along with their lord, the Demon King Asmodeus.
The people he saved had given him the name Slayer. It was also a mark of the reverence Hunters held for a man whose strength none of them could approach.
“I respected him, and I feared him. Lee Jungryong felt the same. If we hadn’t, we wouldn’t have waited years for him to wake up.”
It was true. Even after Cheon Taemin, the object of their respect and fear, collapsed, Song Cheonwoo and Lee Jungryong had been unable to act easily.
Before they revealed their greed, they needed two years, countless experiments to verify his condition, and a certainty still tinged with unease.
“Then what could have...?”
At Choi’s bewildered question, Song shook his head.
“No one can guess the reason. But one thing is certain. He is still alive.”
Song had answered the question Choi meant to ask next. Choi gathered his thoughts.
“What makes you so sure?”
“If he’d died, Lee Jungryong would have had no reason to keep me alive this long.”
“But I do not know exactly where he is being kept. For now, I merely suspect Area A.”
“Area A...”
Choi murmured the name and raised his head. Song stood at the edge of the crevasse, gazing down into it.
“I have a few more questions.”
“Ask me anything.”
Choi studied his back in silence, then said, “I want to know why.”
“Why are you telling me all this now? We’re working together, but before long, I’ll be your rival again. Why give me information this important?”
The enemy of my enemy is my ally. That was all Choi Minwoo and Song Cheonwoo were to each other.
They had joined forces temporarily to bring down Go Jun and claim Ares Guild. Nothing more, nothing less.
Which made Song’s behavior all the harder to understand.
He’s changed.

Their last secret meeting had been barely a week ago. Song had been cautious then, faintly wary in both word and deed. As a man who had once been Lee Jungryong’s political rival, he knew their alliance would end the moment it achieved its goal.
So why?
Information about Cheon Taemin’s whereabouts was a secret within a secret. Considering the confrontation that would come later, it was also a powerful weapon that could force Choi Minwoo to withdraw.
It was not something he could simply disclose on a passing impulse.
Choi’s fingertips touched his sword hilt. Song, who had been staring silently into the depths, slowly turned around.
“The reason.”
The old man’s voice was calm now. The hesitation and faint tremor it had held when they met outside the Gate were gone.
Choi felt Song’s gaze move to his hand.
“Call it atonement.”
Choi tightened his grip on the sword. “Atonement for what?”
“I wanted to tell you someday, even if it was late. About the wrongs I committed against him—and against you.”
“More than twenty years late.”
“Yes. But I had no choice.”
“That’s an excuse.”
Choi’s answer was firm.
Then—
Rrrrrumble!
The snow-covered mountain trembled beneath its blanket of white. An avalanche was taking place beyond the crevasse, which stretched dozens of meters across.
Fur-covered giants rode atop the surging waves of snow.
—Kraaaaaaaaaar!
—Kauu!
Their savage roars shook the mountain. There were hundreds of yetis charging toward them.
“That’s strange,” Choi murmured.
“What is?”
“Yetis usually live in groups of around a dozen.”
“Yes. They used to.”
Crunch. Shing.
With the crevasse at his back, Song stepped forward. Choi drew the sword at his waist—a sword left behind by a hero who had fulfilled his duty even in death.
“That’s a fine sword,” Song Cheonwoo muttered, taking another step.
Behind Choi, someone was already hurtling toward them.
“Young Master!”
At the old servant’s shout, Song muttered, “Understand. I had no choice.”
And then—
BOOM!
A thunderous explosion erupted, and a blizzard came whirling.

sentences.text: Choi Minwoo’s face had gone rigid.
His eyes trembled faintly as he stared at Song Cheonwoo.
“What... do you mean?”
“You may find it hard to believe, but it’s true.”
Song continued with a sigh.
“It happened suddenly, one day.
No one saw it coming.”
Choi clenched his fists without realizing it.
He did not trust Song Cheonwoo, but he could sense no trace of a lie in the old man before him.
Then is it really true?
His heart sank.
A bead of cold sweat rolled down the back of his neck.
He barely managed to force the words past his tightly pressed lips.
“But I’ve never heard anything like that from anyone.
Not even Butler Kim, who was my maternal grandfather’s closest aide...”
Before Choi could finish, Song shook his head.
“It isn’t that he chose not to tell you.
He couldn’t.”
“Then...”
“I’m sorry.”
Wouldn’t and couldn’t.
A small difference in words, but an enormous difference in meaning.
Choi understood what Song was saying and glared at him.
“You hid it from Butler Kim too?
Something this important?”
The old man nodded quietly.
When he spoke, his voice sounded older than ever.
“Hwajong was always loyal.
And he gave that same loyalty to a child born after the war—a boy who lost his parents in an accident and was left alone.”
“Even on the day everything changed, your grandfather’s most loyal aide was at your side.”
Choi turned his head without realizing it.
Far across the snow, Butler Kim stood watching them.
If the howling blizzard had not swallowed Song’s voice, that loyal servant would have come flying over to kill the traitor.
“Is that why you asked me to walk with you alone?”
“I had no choice.
If he’d heard us, we couldn’t have continued this conversation.”
“If Butler Kim had heard about my maternal grandfather back then, you two would already have...”
His usual calm composure was gone.
Blue fire seemed to flicker in Choi’s eyes.
Song could not bring himself to meet his gaze and looked away.
“At first, we were only bewildered.
We thought he would regain consciousness soon, so we kept it strictly confidential.”
Crunch.
Song took a weary step and continued.
“But then a month passed.
Half a year.
A year.
And a strange thought occurred to me.
What if... he never woke up?”
Song Cheonwoo and Lee Jungryong.
What the two men had scarcely dared consider at first hardened into certainty as time passed.
Then that certainty gave way to something else.
“Another year passed, and we recognized the greed in each other.”
The greed to fill the place left vacant by Cheon Taemin, a man no one had dared challenge.
The desire to become master of the great fortress that was Ares Guild.
“The purge began quietly one day.
Unlike Kim Hwajong, who had already drifted away from Ares Guild, several of his closest aides knew of his condition.
They died in Gates.”
Choi bit down hard on his lip.
From ancient times to the present, death had been the surest way to bury the truth.
Lee Jungryong and Song Cheonwoo had chosen that path to usurp the throne of a king who was still alive.
Crack.
Choi’s smooth lips split, and red blood ran down his chin.
As he walked, his angry steps crushed the drops falling onto the white snow.
“You managed to survive, Regional Director.
You really do have a stubborn hold on life.”
Song answered his cutting words in a weak voice.
“Getting rid of me wouldn’t have been easy for Lee Jungryong.
Besides, we’d both covered ourselves in filth fighting over Ares Guild.
He must have judged that I was unlikely to talk.
He was right.”
Knowing the truth was reason enough to be killed.
Having wallowed in the mud together could be reason enough to be spared.
And to Choi, Song Cheonwoo had never seemed capable of fighting Lee Jungryong to the bitter end.
“Was the European regional director’s position the price of that deal?”
“Yes.
It saved my life and my family’s.”
Choi drew a deep breath.
At last, the pieces of the puzzle that had eluded him fell into place.
Why Lee Jungryong, cold and thorough as he was, had kept Song Cheonwoo alive.
And why Choi’s grandfather, his only blood relative and a symbol to the world, had not appeared in more than twenty years.
—Kraaaaaaar!
A yeti roared somewhere in the mountains, as if giving voice to Choi’s feelings.
Damn it.
Crack.
The bones in his tightly clenched fist shifted audibly.
He wanted to scream.
To ask why they had done it, and what they had hoped to gain.
He wanted to shout at the top of his lungs, seize the old man walking ahead by the collar, draw the sword at his waist, and stab him in the back.
But...
Swish.
Thud.
His hand moved toward the hilt, then fell away before it reached it.
Not yet.
Song Cheonwoo would answer for what he had done, but only after Choi had confirmed all the facts.
Choi forced his pounding heart to settle and spoke in a trembling voice.
“Why did my grandfather collapse?”
Crunch.
Song’s footsteps stopped.
Ahead of him, the ground gave way to empty air.
A crevasse—the kind of fissure found in snowy mountains and glaciers—cut through the mountain.
It was enormous, and its depths were too dark to fathom.
“Why.
Why, you ask...”
Song Cheonwoo stared down at the darkness spread before his feet and muttered in a low voice.
“I don’t know.”
“Be clear.
Do you not know, or do you want to pretend you don’t?”
“Do you think Lee Jungryong or I pulled some kind of trick?
On him, of all people?”
“That...”
Choi fell silent.
He remembered who his grandfather was.
Cheon Taemin.
Humanity’s immortal hero.
The first and last Hunter to defeat the countless monsters that had descended upon Earth, along with their lord, the Demon King Asmodeus.
The people he saved had given him the name Slayer.
It was also a mark of the reverence Hunters held for a man whose strength none of them could approach.
“I respected him, and I feared him.
Lee Jungryong felt the same.
If we hadn’t, we wouldn’t have waited years for him to wake up.”
It was true.
Even after Cheon Taemin, the object of their respect and fear, collapsed, Song Cheonwoo and Lee Jungryong had been unable to act easily.
Before they revealed their greed, they needed two years, countless experiments to verify his condition, and a certainty still tinged with unease.
“Then what could have...?”
At Choi’s bewildered question, Song shook his head.
“No one can guess the reason.
But one thing is certain.
He is still alive.”
Song had answered the question Choi meant to ask next.
Choi gathered his thoughts.

“If he’d died, Lee Jungryong would have had no reason to keep me alive this long.”

For now, I merely suspect Area A.”

Song stood at the edge of the crevasse, gazing down into it.

chapters.title: Chapter 578
paragraphs: BOOOOM!
The ground heaved under a massive wave of energy called mana, and the snow thrown into the air rose like a colossal wall.
The moment everything turned white—
Rrip.
A dazzling streak of light tore through Song Cheonwoo’s sleeve and shot outward.
The slender, razor-sharp blade was an unusual weapon, modified for this one strike.
I’m sorry.
With that brief apology, unheard by anyone, Song Cheonwoo moved like a flash.
Swish.
He lowered his stance, straightened his rear leg, bent his front leg at an angle, and put his strength behind the thrust.
The motion flowed as smoothly as water, perfected through more attempts than anyone could count. Wrapped in blinding aura, the blade pierced through space.
SHWAAA!
A sharp whistle tore through the air, as though it could cut anything in its path.
Song Cheonwoo had retired from active duty and was nearing seventy, but no one could deny his strength.
The instincts engraved in his body by the Great Cataclysm—and the tremendous mana coiled within him—defied the passing years.
There was no way a youngster who wasn’t even thirty could block his strike.
It’s over.
Song Cheonwoo was certain.
Until, an instant later, something stopped his blade as it pierced the wall of wind and snow.
SKRAAAK!
A powerful resistance ran up the blade. Song Cheonwoo’s eyes flew wide as a thunderous roar rang out.
BOOOOM!
Mana collided with mana. The gale from the impact clawed at everything around them.
The wall of snow collapsed, and snow scattered through the air.
Beyond it was a pair of deep, steady eyes.
“So this was the trap Go Jun prepared.”
Song Cheonwoo let out a low groan. Choi Minwoo had caught the strike with the flat of his sword.
“How did you...?”
It was impossible. Song Cheonwoo clearly remembered Choi Minwoo’s stay at the European regional branch several years earlier, when he had still been in his early twenties.
The youngster had possessed outstanding natural talent, but his skills had fallen far short of it.
Yet now...
Rrrrrumble.
Song Cheonwoo could feel the strength behind Choi’s sword pressing against his own.
The young man facing him was no longer a youngster. He had become a formidable fighter.
And Song Cheonwoo’s plan had suffered a major setback.
So blood really does tell.
Cheon Taemin.
The name weighed on his heart, and suddenly his sword felt heavier too. But he had come too far to turn back.
He had crossed the river long ago and sunk his own boat. If he wanted to protect the family Go Jun held captive, he could not retreat.
I have to kill him here. No matter what.
Song Cheonwoo clenched his teeth. Mana surged through his sturdy body, seemingly untouched by age.
His wrist traced an arc, and the sharp tip of his sword slid across the flat of Choi Minwoo’s blade.
Clack. Swish!
It missed by a hair. The tip grazed past Choi Minwoo’s neck and stabbed into empty air.
Sword pressure split the skin of his neck, sending a stream of blood into the air.
Someone watching cried out.
“Young Master!”
The shout held grief, urgency, and fury.
The newcomer closed the hundreds of meters between them in an instant. With a flick of his sleeve, the surrounding air grew hot.
Fwoooosh!
Flames made of mana erupted and rose between Song Cheonwoo and the others. The snow on the mountain melted and evaporated.
Through the scorching heat, Song Cheonwoo saw the old butler approaching beyond Choi’s shoulder. Choi backed away, steadying his breath.
“So you’ve come.”
Song Cheonwoo looked calmly at Butler Kim.
Once, they had called each other older and younger brother. Butler Kim had been one of the few comrades Song trusted to watch his back on the battlefield.
For both of them, that belonged to the past.
“I resented you, but I never hated you. But...”
Fwoosh.
A fierce heat burst forth. Flames formed in midair, coiled around Butler Kim’s hands, and took on a new shape.
Song Cheonwoo gazed wistfully at the man now holding a whip of fire in each hand.
“Now you finally look like yourself. The Kim Hwajong I knew.”
Butler Kim—no, Kim Hwajong—gripped the fiery whips and stepped forward.
Thud.
Lava seemed to boil in eyes that had always been calm.
The old butler, who had preserved his loyalty without wavering through all the years that had passed, had returned to the vigorous figure he had been in the past.
“Shut your fucking mouth, you piece of shit.”
Choi Minwoo stared, mouth open. He had never seen Kim Hwajong like this.
Swish! FWOOSH!
Following the arc of the sword as it swung, the wall of fire separating the three of them split apart.
And Choi Minwoo saw it.
Song Cheonwoo was watching them with a calm expression. Somehow, a pure white necklace now hung around his neck.
That’s...
Song Cheonwoo spoke the name of the necklace Choi knew so well.
“It’s a Yeti’s Necklace. When you told me to come here, I thought it was bound to be useful.”
Song Cheonwoo turned his head. Beyond the crevasse, hundreds of yetis were surging down the mountain with the avalanche.
“And this time, it seems I was right. Don’t you agree?”
—Kyaaaaaaar!
Watching the hundreds of yetis charge toward them, Choi Minwoo felt his grip tighten around his sword.
A Yeti’s Necklace.
Choi Minwoo knew what the little necklace did. So did Kim Hwajong.
Only a few months earlier, Won Myunghoon had prepared the magic item to trap Jin Taekyung in the Black Wyvern’s nest.
A slave’s mark that draws in dragonkin monsters.
Even monsters had their hierarchies.
Yetis, the giants of the snowy mountains, were slaves and prey to dragonkin. But the Yeti’s Necklace did more than attract dragonkin monsters.
It marked its wearer as a slave of the dragonkin—and, to yetis, as one of their own.
Choi Minwoo’s shout toward Song Cheonwoo never finished.
RUMBLE! Rat-a-tat!
An enormous avalanche swept forward. Hundreds of yetis raced across it as though riding a wave, then leaped over the crevasse.
Song Cheonwoo was closest, but while he wore a necklace carrying a yeti’s scent, he was no different from one of their own.
—Kraaaaaar!
The savage roar shook the snowfield.
Song Cheonwoo glanced at the hundreds of shadows leaping over his head and charging toward the other two before speaking.
“Hwajong. You’d better stay out of this.”
“You fucking bastard! I’ll tear you apart!”
Kim Hwajong roared and swung his whips of fire.
Whoooosh! BOOM!
Flames of tremendous heat swept through the air, burning everything they touched. But the hundreds of yetis had been strengthened by magical power, and the deaths of their own kind did not slow them.
If anything, the magical power rising from them grew more ferocious.
—Kraaaaaar!
There were too many.
Kim Hwajong bit down on his lip. Then Choi Minwoo’s quiet voice reached him.
“It’s all right, Butler Kim.”
“Young Master!”
“The yetis will only make my fight harder.”
“Go. I’ll take care of things here.”
Kim Hwajong stopped before he could argue.
For a moment, the old butler looked into Choi Minwoo’s unwavering eyes. Then, without a word, he kicked off the ground.
He swung the fiery whips in both hands, drawing the hundreds of yetis after him.
RUMBLE!
—Kyaaaa!
The yetis moved away in pursuit of the heat. At the same time, Song Cheonwoo stepped forward.
Crunch.
He took one step through the snow. His hand blurred, and his aura-wrapped sword tore through the air on every side.
SHWAAAAK! Slice!
Aura was the essence of mana’s true power.
The razor-sharp, destructive energy surged outward, cleaving through space. Wind, snow, rock—none of them could stop it.
Only another aura could.
Swish! Slice!
Sword strikes slashed through the air without pause. Skin split, and drops of blood flew.
Choi Minwoo narrowly avoided the streaks of light cutting across him. His eyes grew steady, and he tightened his grip on his sword.
Whoooosh.
Hero’s Soul. The sword left behind by a noble hero trembled.
Pure white aura, resembling the snowy mountain, coiled around the blade and surged upward. Choi Minwoo gripped the sword tightly with both hands and smoothly rotated his upper body.
Shiiiiing.
Aura against aura. Light against light.
The instant two flashes of different colors met—
RUMBLE-RUMBLE-RUMBLE!
A massive shock wave shook the mountain. Snowdrifts within dozens of meters turned to powder and scattered.
Two pale figures streaked through the white.
Swish, swish, swish!
BOOM! CRASH!
Two figures. Two swords. Their auras cut through the air and collided.
Each clash sent out another tremendous shock wave, sweeping away snow and tearing up the ground.
Red liquid dropped onto the dark green ground, revealed for the first time in ages beneath the snow.
Trickle.
Choi Minwoo felt hot blood run down his wrist. His shoulder throbbed, and cold sweat gathered on his forehead until it touched his eyebrows.
He had no time to stop the bleeding or wipe away the sweat.
The man facing him was still raining down sword strikes filled with killing intent.
SHIIING! Slice!
The attack missed by a hair. Solid rock split like tofu.
Choi Minwoo exhaled sharply as he dodged. His opponent’s face came into view, his killing intent so fierce it made Choi’s whole body prickle.
Song Cheonwoo.
A hero of the Great Cataclysm, once counted among the greatest Hunters alongside Lee Jungryong. His skill was terrifying.
It was one reason he had survived despite knowing a truth that could never be allowed into the open.
Shing!
Choi Minwoo jerked his head aside. Fierce wind sent strands of hair flying. A moment slower, and it would have been his neck.
So why didn’t he feel the terror of death he had felt in Sichuan?
Heh.
A quiet laugh escaped him instead. He had suddenly remembered a conversation with someone who wasn’t here.
“This might sound a little crazy, but sometimes I start laughing when I’m in a situation where I feel like I’m going to die.”
“You really are quite insane.”
“But... whenever I start laughing, I always end up winning somehow.”
Choi Minwoo didn’t know why that passing conversation had come to mind now.
But at last, he felt he understood a little of what the man had meant.
I won’t die.
It was faith in himself. The will to keep fighting until the very end.
Choi Minwoo had made that insight his own when, exhausted and wounded, he had walked toward thousands of monsters.
Shing. Slice!
Burning pain shot through his thigh.
Choi Minwoo twisted, staggered, and Song Cheonwoo pressed his attack even harder.
Swish, swish, swish! Slice!
This time, it was his arm.
Thunk!
Then his side.
Choi Minwoo endured the pain and kept moving forward.
He met the rain of sword strikes, taking one step, then another. The sword in his hand trembled.
Whoooom.
Hero’s Soul. The sword passed down to him from a hero who had fulfilled his duty even after becoming a vengeful spirit.
A legendary blade that granted greater power to one worthy of wielding it.
Fwoooooom!
The blade shuddered. Brilliant light swelled around its aura.
Song Cheonwoo’s eyes widened.
“One last question.”
Choi Minwoo’s gaze was cold, but his voice burned.
He put all his strength into a single strike.
“Have you forgotten whose blood flows through my veins?”
Shiiing!
A massive streak of light cleaved through space.
Within the blinding flash that filled his vision, Song Cheonwoo felt a bolt of lightning cut across his chest.
Slice!

—Kraaaaaar!
The savage roar shook the snowfield.
Song Cheonwoo glanced at the hundreds of shadows leaping over his head and charging toward the other two before speaking.
“Hwajong.
You’d better stay out of this.”
“You fucking bastard!
I’ll tear you apart!”
Kim Hwajong roared and swung his whips of fire.
Whoooosh!
BOOM!
Flames of tremendous heat swept through the air, burning everything they touched.
But the hundreds of yetis had been strengthened by magical power, and the deaths of their own kind did not slow them.
If anything, the magical power rising from them grew more ferocious.
—Kraaaaaar!
There were too many.
Kim Hwajong bit down on his lip.
Then Choi Minwoo’s quiet voice reached him.
“It’s all right, Butler Kim.”
“Young Master!”
“The yetis will only make my fight harder.”
“Go.
I’ll take care of things here.”
Kim Hwajong stopped before he could argue.
For a moment, the old butler looked into Choi Minwoo’s unwavering eyes.
Then, without a word, he kicked off the ground.
He swung the fiery whips in both hands, drawing the hundreds of yetis after him.
RUMBLE!
—Kyaaaa!
The yetis moved away in pursuit of the heat.
At the same time, Song Cheonwoo stepped forward.
Crunch.
He took one step through the snow.
His hand blurred, and his aura-wrapped sword tore through the air on every side.
SHWAAAAK!
Slice!
Aura was the essence of mana’s true power.
The razor-sharp, destructive energy surged outward, cleaving through space.
Wind, snow, rock—none of them could stop it.
Only another aura could.
Swish!
Slice!
Sword strikes slashed through the air without pause.
Skin split, and drops of blood flew.
Choi Minwoo narrowly avoided the streaks of light cutting across him.
His eyes grew steady, and he tightened his grip on his sword.
Whoooosh.
Hero’s Soul.
The sword left behind by a noble hero trembled.
Pure white aura, resembling the snowy mountain, coiled around the blade and surged upward.
Choi Minwoo gripped the sword tightly with both hands and smoothly rotated his upper body.
Shiiiiing.
Aura against aura.
Light against light.
The instant two flashes of different colors met—
RUMBLE-RUMBLE-RUMBLE!
A massive shock wave shook the mountain.
Snowdrifts within dozens of meters turned to powder and scattered.
Two pale figures streaked through the white.
Swish, swish, swish!
BOOM!
CRASH!
Two figures.
Two swords.
Their auras cut through the air and collided.
Each clash sent out another tremendous shock wave, sweeping away snow and tearing up the ground.
Red liquid dropped onto the dark green ground, revealed for the first time in ages beneath the snow.
Trickle.
Choi Minwoo felt hot blood run down his wrist.
His shoulder throbbed, and cold sweat gathered on his forehead until it touched his eyebrows.
He had no time to stop the bleeding or wipe away the sweat.
The man facing him was still raining down sword strikes filled with killing intent.
SHIIING!
Slice!
The attack missed by a hair.
Solid rock split like tofu.
Choi Minwoo exhaled sharply as he dodged.
His opponent’s face came into view, his killing intent so fierce it made Choi’s whole body prickle.
Song Cheonwoo.
A hero of the Great Cataclysm, once counted among the greatest Hunters alongside Lee Jungryong.
His skill was terrifying.
It was one reason he had survived despite knowing a truth that could never be allowed into the open.
Shing!
Choi Minwoo jerked his head aside.
Fierce wind sent strands of hair flying.
A moment slower, and it would have been his neck.
So why didn’t he feel the terror of death he had felt in Sichuan?
Heh.
A quiet laugh escaped him instead.
He had suddenly remembered a conversation with someone who wasn’t here.
“This might sound a little crazy, but sometimes I start laughing when I’m in a situation where I feel like I’m going to die.”
“You really are quite insane.”
“But... whenever I start laughing, I always end up winning somehow.”
Choi Minwoo didn’t know why that passing conversation had come to mind now.
But at last, he felt he understood a little of what the man had meant.
I won’t die.
It was faith in himself.
The will to keep fighting until the very end.
Choi Minwoo had made that insight his own when, exhausted and wounded, he had walked toward thousands of monsters.
Shing.
Slice!
Burning pain shot through his thigh.
Choi Minwoo twisted, staggered, and Song Cheonwoo pressed his attack even harder.
Swish, swish, swish!
Slice!
This time, it was his arm.
Thunk!
Then his side.
Choi Minwoo endured the pain and kept moving forward.
He met the rain of sword strikes, taking one step, then another.
The sword in his hand trembled.
Whoooom.
Hero’s Soul.
The sword passed down to him from a hero who had fulfilled his duty even after becoming a vengeful spirit.
A legendary blade that granted greater power to one worthy of wielding it.
Fwoooooom!
The blade shuddered.
Brilliant light swelled around its aura.
Song Cheonwoo’s eyes widened.
“One last question.”
Choi Minwoo’s gaze was cold, but his voice burned.
He put all his strength into a single strike.
“Have you forgotten whose blood flows through my veins?”
Shiiing!
A massive streak of light cleaved through space.
Within the blinding flash that filled his vision, Song Cheonwoo felt a bolt of lightning cut across his chest.
Slice!

chapters.title: Chapter 579
paragraphs: Slice!
The instant a streak of light cut across his chest, Song Cheonwoo felt his vision dim.
It’s hot.
It was lightning.
The kind of lightning even a hero of old—one who had left his mark on the chaotic, perilous Great Cataclysm—had been unable to stop.
Song stared at the sword in his hand, his eyes trembling. Only seconds ago, it had shone with aura. Now something sharper and more destructive had cut it in half.
Clang.
The sword slipped from his grip and clattered across the ground. A beat later, pain swept through his body.
“Cough.”
Drip, drip.
Dark red blood spilled from his mouth, staining the snow. His clothes and armor split diagonally, exposing his bronze-colored torso. A fine line across his skin and taut muscles glowed red.
SHWAAA!
An enormous amount of blood burst forth like a waterfall.
It ran from his left chest to his right hip. The injury left by that bolt of lightning was devastating. It would never heal.
Song staggered backward as the strength drained from his body.
Crunch.
His unsteady foot came down on blood-soaked snow.
One step. Two steps. Three steps. And then...
Fsssh.
At the sound of piled snow falling away, Song barely managed to steady himself. A massive crevasse gaped behind him.
He could retreat no farther. There was nowhere to go forward, either.
Damn it.
His chest felt hollow. Perhaps that was the life still draining out of him.
Song raised his head. Someone was walking slowly toward him.
Choi Minwoo.
The only blood descendant of that person, whom Song had always respected and feared. He remembered the quiet words he had heard just before the lightning struck.
“Have you forgotten whose blood flows through my veins?”

But now Song saw someone else in the young man before him. Someone who was not here, who existed only in his memories. Someone he could not have watched from nearby without feeling both reverence and fear.
Song realized something he had long forgotten: Cheon Taemin’s blood flowed through Choi Minwoo’s veins.
“...Hyung?”
The word escaped between ragged breaths.
Through Song’s blood-red vision, the young man holding a brilliantly shining sword looked like his maternal grandfather. His somber eyes seemed to ask why Song had changed sides.
“Don’t come closer. Stay away!”
Song shouted with what little strength he had left and swung his sword. Or thought he did.
The hand that had dropped it moments earlier was empty. It swept through the air until someone’s firm grip stopped it.
Whooom. Thud.
Choi Minwoo seized Song’s wrist and squeezed.
Crunch.
Bones shifted out of place, and Song screamed.
“GRAAAAAH!”
Thud.
Unable to bear the pain, Song fell to his knees. Choi gazed down at him, his eyes steady. What he saw now was not Song Cheonwoo, but an old man.
Zzt, zzt, zzt.
The radiance surrounding Hero’s Soul slowly faded. The fight had already been decided.
“Stop. It’s over,” Choi said quietly.
Song went rigid. He had lost? Impossible. It could not happen. It should not happen.
But there was no denying it.
His trembling gaze lifted to Choi, whose calm expression made the bloody fight they had just fought seem unreal.
“How? How did you...?”
“I’m not sure.”

Choi felt the immense power flowing through his body. Only a few months ago, he had been unable to sense it. It was the only gift his maternal grandfather had left him—and Jin Taekyung had torn open the wrapping and returned it to its rightful owner, along with a way to put the gift to good use.
“Perhaps... because I was stronger than you.”
That was not all. Choi had believed in himself and acted with an upright heart. In return, the sword imbued with a hero’s soul had granted its worthy wielder even greater strength.
He looked down at Song, his gaze unwavering.
“I won, and you lost. That is all that remains between us.”
The old man’s trembling gaze gradually settled. A hoarse voice came through his bloodstained lips.
“Yes. You’re right. Though I didn’t expect this outcome.”
“Neither did I. I never thought we’d end up here.”
Anger. Hostility. A faint trace of pity for a man who had fallen so far. Choi felt all of them, but above all, he wanted to know why.
Why had Song done this? And could Choi believe what Song had told him earlier?
“Why did you do it? If we’d worked together, driving Go Jun out and taking control of Ares Guild wouldn’t have been difficult.”
“I know,” Song answered hollowly. “I thought so too.”
“Then why?”
“I had no choice. It was an offer I couldn’t refuse.”
Choi already knew who had made that offer.
“Go Jun. Was it all on his orders? Our alliance, everything up to now?”
“Cough. Orders?”
Song spat out more blood and gave a feeble laugh. He was plainly laughing at Go Jun.

“If it were Lee Jungryong, perhaps. But that bastard is nothing more than a powerful, immature brat. I may be a despicable and pathetic old man, but I haven’t fallen so low that I would submit to the orders of some young punk. My alliance with you was entirely my own decision.”
“Then—”
“I told you. It was an offer I couldn’t refuse.”
Choi looked into Song’s fading eyes and suddenly understood what the old man still had left—and what the offer must have involved.
“Your family.”
Song gave a small nod.
“I didn’t realize until after I lost to Lee Jungryong. I’d forgotten what mattered most.”

His had been a hard-fought life. Before the Great Cataclysm, he had worked day and night to support his family. During it, he had been unable to leave the battlefield. Afterward, he had begun another struggle to reach the center of power.
Losing that political struggle to Lee Jungryong had reminded him how precious his family was. Then Lee’s death had rekindled his ambition, and Song had forgotten them again.
“My absence was the root of all this. I suppose this is the price an old man paid for reaching too greedily after ambition too late in life.”
“You’re probably right.”
Choi’s answer was cold. Hearing Song lament his own choices stripped away the last of his pity.
“Because of you and Lee Jungryong, I lost the only family I had.”
His voice was cold, but fury burned beneath it.

Because of two adults’ ambitions, a child too young to know what ambition meant had been left little better than an orphan. Before he could even understand that his parents were dead, his maternal grandfather had disappeared too. Choi had lived all these years resenting him.
“...I’m sorry. It was my fault.”
“Then I suppose you wouldn’t have any objections if I burned you to death right now. Would you?”
The voice came from somewhere above them. It was not Choi’s.
Crunch.
Kim Hwajong stepped onto the ground, covered from head to toe in blue yeti blood. Flames burned in the old butler’s eyes, matching the whip of fire in his hand.
“Hwajong. It’s you.”
“Shut your fucking mouth, you bastard. Do you know how much the Young Master—”
Kim looked ready to swing the whip, but a slight glance from Choi stopped him. The old butler pressed his lips together and stepped back.
Choi turned to Song.
“Then is everything you told me about my maternal grandfather a lie as well?”
“I wish it were a lie. But it is all true. I’ve already come too far.”
Kim frowned, unable to understand what Song meant. Choi let out a breath, torn between relief and disappointment.
His grandfather was alive. That was welcome news, even if he had been unconscious for more than twenty years.
But that could wait. For now, Choi had to decide what to do with Song.
—Young Master.
Kim’s message spell carried pride in Choi, fury toward Song, and a faint hope. Choi shook his head. He knew what the old butler wanted to say.
—Butler Kim. That isn’t possible.
—What do you mean, it isn’t possible?
—Give me a potion. We need to treat him just enough to keep him alive.
Kim looked ready to protest, but Choi’s calm gaze made him hold back. He knew Song was a crucial witness—and, while alive, evidence in his own right.
He simply wished it weren’t so.
“Butler Kim.”
“Damn it. All right.”
Kim cursed as he handed over a mid-grade potion. Choi’s eyes widened.
“Did you just swear in front of me?”
“Yes, I did. Why?”
“I’d heard a little about this, but you’re nothing like the man I remember.”
“This is who I am. When you were little, I watched what I did and said in case you picked it up from me.”
“Why stop now...?”
“You’re almost thirty now. Since things have come to this, learn from me if you want to learn. Or don’t.”
Is this really the man who’s been by my side since I was a child?
Choi let out a quiet laugh at the old butler’s gruff tone.
“Butler Kim.”
“What? And stop laughing. That’s no way to treat an elder.”
“Thank you. For becoming my only family.”
“I’ve always wanted to tell you that.”
After saying it, Choi could not bring himself to meet the old butler’s eyes. He turned away without another word.
At the end of the path before him, an old man lay buried in the snow, waiting for death.
Click.
Choi pulled the stopper from the potion. Its delicate, fresh scent drove back the smell of blood.
Song watched him approach through eyes that seemed about to close for good.
“Are you... going to save me?”
“Do you want to live?”
“I... That’s...”
Choi felt a surge of disgust at his hesitation.
“If I had my way, I would kill you a hundred times, a thousand times over.”
“B-but my family...”
“There must be a way to help them. We’ll deal with it once we’re out of here.”
“Choose.”
Song hesitated, then nodded with a look of resignation.
Choi gazed at him coldly and slowly tipped the potion.
Hiss.
The wound began to close the moment the milky liquid touched it. It was an extremely weak recovery, but to someone, it was a lifeline that could give them enough strength for one final effort.
Crack!
Where had that strength come from?
Amid the snow exploding in every direction, Song Cheonwoo launched himself with superhuman force and slipped into the enormous crevasse.

chapters.title: Chapter 580
paragraphs: News spread quickly: a Named Monster called the Kraken had landed in Busan at the head of thousands of Mermen.
Go Se-won was one of the few who heard about it before the breaking news appeared.
A Monster Wave...
He was human, too. Busan was a major city with a population approaching five million. He had never met any of those people, but the thought of countless civilians dying still left him uneasy.
At least Jin Taekyung is there.
Step. Step.
Guild members moving through headquarters hurriedly cleared a path when they saw Go Se-won.
He strode past them and muttered, “Security Team. Respond.”
Beep.
A faint tone sounded in his earpiece, followed at once by replies.
“Team Three. Transmission complete.”
“Team Two. Transmission complete.”
“Team One. Transmission complete.”
“I’m going to see a VIP. Open Area A and report your current locations and personnel.”
Go Se-won intended to ask his superior for permission to send the security teams to Busan.
It would help rescue people, and it would also help repair Ares Guild’s recently damaged image.
But as the team leaders reported in one after another, he frowned.
“All of Team Three are monitoring the target’s family in London.”
“All of Team Two have returned from London and are standing by in headquarters’ Area A.”
“Team One has nine members present. We’ve returned from London and are standing by on the hundredth floor of headquarters.”
“Team Leader of Team One. Say that again. What did you say?”
“Team One has nine members present. We’re standing by on the hundredth floor—”
“Forget the rest.”
Go Se-won stepped onto a magic circle as he spoke in a quiet voice.
Whoosh.
White light flared as the Teleport spell activated, taking him to Area A.
“Why nine instead of ten?”
“An urgent matter came up.”
“An urgent matter. Who’s missing?”
“Kim Ho-jung.”
“Kim Ho-jung?”
“Yes.”
Listening to the Team Leader’s dry voice, Go Se-won crossed the hallway in Area A. His mood soured with each sharp click of his dress shoes.
“That’s strange. I don’t recall receiving a report.”
“My apologies.”
“I’m asking for a reason, not an apology. Did he leave without permission?”
“Of course not.”
Of course he didn’t.
The security team was a pack of hunting dogs raised by the late Lee Jungryong.
For a long time, Lee Jungryong had secretly operated enormous orphanages and children’s homes, instilling loyalty in orphans who had nowhere else to go.
Go Se-won had been one of them. So had the others.
Team One, in particular, was made up of only the most loyal and capable. A member going AWOL was less likely than a Monster Wave.
Especially a member like Kim Ho-jung.
Which means...
Ares Guild had plenty of senior executives and elders, but the security team took orders from only two people.
Kim Ho-jung had vanished without reporting to Go Se-won, one of those two. That could mean only one thing.
Step.
His unimpeded stride came to an abrupt halt.
Go Se-won silently stared at a door with no nameplate or decoration when a bright voice rang out from beyond it.
“Come in. Don’t loiter out there.”
Go Se-won swallowed and opened the door. His one direct superior was waiting in the neatly kept room.
“Nice weather today. Don’t you think, Team Leader Go?”
“Yes.”
Go Se-won bowed briefly, his gaze sweeping the room.
The pleasant smile at Go Jun’s lips. The whiskey glass in his hand. And the object he was rolling around in his other hand.
What is that?
Go Jun was not acting like himself. Everything about the room felt unfamiliar and unsettling.
Perhaps it was the noise working its way into Go Se-won’s ears.
Grind. Grate.
Go Jun’s voice mingled with the irritating friction.
“You don’t need to worry about Kim Ho-jung, Team Leader Go. I gave him a separate assignment.”
“I see.”
“Aren’t you curious what it was?”
Their eyes met. Go Jun’s looked unusually red today. Go Se-won lowered his head politely.
“No. If it was your order, Vice Guild Master, I’m sure you had a reason.”
“That’s good to hear. I thought you’d been feeling a little slighted lately. I am younger than you, after all, and you were always particularly devoted to Master.”
“How could I? It’s true that I owe the former Vice Guild Master a great deal, but that does not diminish my loyalty.”
“Is that so? Then that’s a relief.”
Grind.
Go Jun rubbed the object in his hand again. Smiling, he swirled his glass.
“It’s a nice day. Care to join me for a drink?”
Go Se-won answered evenly. “I’m sorry, but...”
“You mean you won’t drink? What a shame. It’s good liquor.”
Go Jun leisurely emptied his glass. Go Se-won watched him in silence before suddenly speaking.
“There’s an urgent matter I need to report.”
“Go on.”
“In Busan...”
Go Se-won trailed off. Beside the glass Go Jun had set down was a holographic PC.
The paused screen showed an enormous octopus and the shattered remains of Gwangan Bridge.
“What about Busan?”
After a moment, Go Se-won murmured, “You already know.”
Go Jun gave a low laugh.
“I did. Before anyone else.”
His voice was as cheerful as ever. Go Se-won’s heart sank.
As the unease he had tried to dismiss revealed its true shape, he forced himself to speak calmly.
“Then is Kim Ho-jung... in Busan right now?”
“I seem to remember you saying you weren’t curious a moment ago.”
“I’m sorry. That slipped out.”
“It’s fine. You need to know anyway.”
Go Jun answered pleasantly as he filled his empty glass with whiskey.
“That’s right. Kim Ho-jung is in Busan on my orders.”
He paused to think, then added, “Though he might not be there anymore.”
“Don’t just stand there. Sit down and have a drink. My neck hurts from looking up at you.”
This time Go Se-won could not refuse. No, he had no reason to. He needed a drink to steady himself.
Gulp, gulp.
He drained the strong whiskey in one go. Only then did he feel able to breathe.
Holding the empty crystal glass, he hesitated before forcing out the words.
“Vice Guild Master. I don’t know how you managed to cause this, but it won’t do much damage to them.”
“Why do you think that?”
“Because he’s—because Jin Taekyung is there. He even killed an Arch Lich. He’s already bringing the Monster Wave under control. This will only add to the Peace Guild’s Fame.”
“Yes. Jin Taekyung. Quite a man.”
Go Se-won had risked his superior’s anger by mentioning the name. Instead, the smile stayed on Go Jun’s face.
And that gentle smile made Go Se-won feel even more uneasy.
“Vice Guild Master. Don’t tell me...”
“If you want to capture the commander, you have to lure out the general. There’ll be an uproar if anyone finds out, but no consequences to worry about afterward.”
“We can’t do anything about Jin Taekyung right now. Choi Minwoo is another matter. Don’t you agree?”
Grind. Grate.
Along with the irritating sound of friction, one name flashed through Go Se-won’s mind like a bolt of lightning.
“Song Cheonwoo. It’s Song Cheonwoo.”
“Correct. I’ll give you another drink as your reward.”
Go Se-won accepted it, hiding the tremor in his fingers. He could not begin to grasp how far things had gone wrong.
Even now, though, he was certain his superior’s plan would fail.
“...Choi Minwoo is a cautious man. On the surface, he is the master of the Peace Guild, and he also has Kim Hwajong, who has served him loyally at his side for a long time.”
“I know. Master told me about Kim Hwajong more than once. And with the other guards there, Song Cheonwoo can’t manage it alone.”
“Vice Guild Master. Then why in the world—”
GRRAAATE!
The loud sound of friction drowned out Go Se-won’s voice.
Go Jun gave a quiet laugh instead of answering and opened his hand. At last, Go Se-won saw what he had been holding.
It was the size of an egg, and the darkness inside looked as though someone had gathered up the abyss and sealed it there.
“A Magic Gem...”
An ordinary Magic Gem would not have surprised him.
But the one in Go Jun’s palm could only have come from a Named Monster. It was what people called an S-grade Magic Gem.
Pure, unrefined magical power swirled inside.
“V-Vice Guild Master.”
Only now did Go Se-won understand how Go Jun had been able to cause the Monster Wave artificially.
At the dread in his voice, Go Jun murmured, “Choi Minwoo will die today. He will.”
And Choi Minwoo’s killer would be one of two: an old man whose family had been taken hostage, or another being whose identity even Go Jun could not clearly determine.
“One thing is certain. Song Cheonwoo has no choice.”
Go Jun murmured the words quietly, then smiled with satisfaction.
He reached up out of habit to stroke the old necklace around his neck. Darkness flickered in his eyes.
If anyone had asked how Song Cheonwoo could still move in his condition, he would have answered in one word.
Will.
That was all it was: the last of his strength, drawn out by sheer force of will. The old man, now entering his seventies, threw himself toward death with everything he had left.
Flash! Whoosh!
The world slowed.
The cold touch of snow vanished. For an instant, his whole body felt weightless.
In that moment, split into fragments of a second, Song Cheonwoo met two pairs of eyes staring wide at him.
Choi Minwoo and Kim Hwajong. Their eyes seemed to ask the same thing.
Why?
Song answered them silently.
Because there’s no other way.
A few days earlier, he might have taken Choi Minwoo’s hand.
But the last time he had faced Go Jun, the man had become... a monster.
Song had seen madness in his eyes. If Song left this place alive, Go Jun would kill his family without a moment’s hesitation.
Neither the Peace Guild, nor even Jin Taekyung or “that person,” could resolve that problem.
So this is how it ends.
With that fleeting thought, Song fell toward the pitch-black darkness.
He could see no end to it. It looked like a monster’s gaping maw—and like his own life.
Was it Nietzsche?
Someone had said that if you gazed into the abyss, you became the abyss yourself.
Song understood that now, but too late. Everything was already too late.
SHWAAAA!
A cold, fierce wind battered him.
Through its howl, he seemed to hear a conversation from a few days ago.
“This.”
“Keep it with you. You know how dangerous it is, Director. Expensive, too.”
“...You bastard. You’re insane.”
“Then you’ll have to go insane as well. If you want to save your family.”
The man had been insane, and it had been an insane conversation.
Song had agonized over it, each day feeling like ten years. Yet in the end, he had never used it.
Was that the last thing I did right?
The wind grew fiercer. Song sensed something drawing near in the darkness and closed his eyes.
Crack! Crunch, crunch, crunch!
His long fall ended.
His neck broke first. Then the bones throughout his body shattered.
Then, through his fading consciousness, Song heard something growl.
—Grrrr.
It was the eerie cry of a monster unlike any he had heard before.
He wanted to say something, but the being that had crouched in the abyss for so many years allowed its prey no last words.
CRUNCH!
Darkness came.
Enormous teeth crushed his lifeless body and swallowed his blood.
They swallowed the thing deep in his pocket, too—the thing he had refused to use to the very end, wanting to die a human rather than a monster.
Whoosh.
Darkness itself turned to light and burst forth.
