chapters.title: Chapter 581
paragraphs: Whump! BOOM!
A whip of fire lashed the ground. Piled snow melted, and yeti blood boiled. Kim Hwajong’s voice came through his clenched teeth as if he were chewing the words before spitting them out.
“Song Cheonwoo, you fucking bastard...”
The old butler’s wide-open eyes were fixed on the spot where someone had been lying only seconds ago.

If this was how it was going to end—if that bastard was going to meet a death like this—Hwajong should have killed him with his own hands. But Song Cheonwoo had summoned the last of some unknown strength, thrown himself into the deep crevasse, and met the death he had chosen for himself.
It was too good an end for a traitor. Worse still...
“We’ve lost an important witness. I’m sorry, Young Master.”
“No.”
Choi Minwoo shook his head at Kim Hwajong’s sigh-like murmur. His gaze remained fixed on the crevasse whose depth could not be estimated.
“You have nothing to apologize for, Butler Kim. I should have been more careful.”
Victory dulled vigilance. Perhaps all the more so after a fight that had been anything but easy. Choi poured the potion—still more than three-quarters full—over himself.
Hiss.
The sound of flesh burning filled the air as his wounds began to close little by little. Feeling a faint pain, he continued.
“Song Cheonwoo must have thought this was the only way to save his family.”
“I understand his situation, but... he must have been more desperate than we realized.”
Kim Hwajong muttered roughly, “Damn fool. There wasn’t even any guarantee this would save his family. Why do it?”
“He must have been that afraid. People cling to hope even in despair, don’t they?”

Choi answered quietly and took his eyes off the crevasse. He could not tell exactly how deep it was, but the drop had to be hundreds of meters. Song had already been at death’s door. His chances of surviving the fall were close to zero.
“We should call the Guild members. No—it would be faster to have the Guild House send people.”
After more than twenty years together, Kim Hwajong knew at once what he meant.
“You want to recover his body?”
“I don’t know if we can, but we have to try. Song Cheonwoo is still Ares Guild’s European regional branch director.”

Death would not erase his position. If they could prove even half of what had happened here, the repercussions would reach beyond the impregnable fortress that was Ares Guild and shake Go Jun himself.
“Attempted murder, murder-for-hire—whatever the charge, it will stain even Ares Guild’s Vice Guild Master. Especially now.”
A fortress built through decades of effort did not crumble easily. But Go Jun was different. Choi Minwoo intended to use every bit of power at his disposal to unseat him as lord of that fortress.
“We’re going to be busier than ever. Both of us.”
Kim Hwajong smiled with pride.
“I’ve been waiting for this day.”
“I’m glad. That you’re always at my side.”
“Then put me to work before I get any older, Young Master. We’ll make that bastard Go Jun regret doing this.”
“That’s the plan.”
Choi nodded and walked away from the crevasse. Whether from his fierce fight with Song or the blood he had lost, exhaustion swept through him and made every step heavy.
Then, as his consciousness gradually grew hazy and he retraced the path he had taken, Choi Minwoo came to an abrupt stop.
Splash.
Muddy water mixed with snow and blood sprayed around him. Kim Hwajong, who had been following behind him, asked in confusion,
“Young Master?”
Choi Minwoo did not answer. He silently stared down at his foot, half-submerged in a puddle of murky water, then suddenly muttered,
“Regret.”
“Yes?”
“You said we’d make Go Jun regret doing this.”
“I did. Is there a problem...?”
“We left out why. Why did Go Jun do it?”
Choi looked at the puddle. A single step had splashed the water and sent ripples across it. Why, then, had Go Jun sent Song Cheonwoo, a member of Ares Guild, to assassinate him?
Because Song was powerful? Because he was a traitor?
Neither.
It’s a trap.
The thought struck like lightning. Choi began to tremble.
Not from the shock of his realization, and certainly not from exhaustion.
No. His body was not the only thing that had been trembling from the beginning.
Rumble...
Fresh ripples spread across the puddle as it was settling, and a heap of snow that had yet to melt collapsed. The ground was shaking. Terrified yetis cried out across the trembling mountain.
At the center of it all came a tremendous rumble.
Crack—RUMBLE, RUMBLE!
Choi and Kim Hwajong turned together. The ground split in a spiderweb of cracks, thin fractures running back toward the darkness behind them.
Crack! Crack-crack-crack!
The crevasse.
An enormous darkness whose end could not be seen opened its jaws. Darkness poured from the widening gap.
Darkness—no. Immense magical power shook the mountain and tore through space-time.
SHWAAAA!
And the two men saw what lay beyond the split in space: a boundless blue sky and buildings.
The world they had lived in. The world they were meant to go on living in.
“...Monster Wave.”
Two worlds that touched but should never have been connected had become linked. A roar announcing the beginning of the disaster reverberated in every direction.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
Facing the abyss as it finally revealed itself, Kim Hwajong stepped in front of his young master, his gaze darker than ever.
Step.
A snowstorm swept around them. Blackened by magical power, it was no longer white—or beautiful.
“Team Leader, how about a drink?”
A team member came over with a soju bottle and an easy grin. The Team Leader answered curtly.
“No, asshole.”
Despite his words, his glass was already being raised ever so slightly. The team member grinned as if he knew everything and filled the empty glass.
Glug, glug, glug.
The Team Leader threw back the full glass in one gulp, then dipped a piece of flounder sashimi deep in the spicy-sweet sauce and swallowed it. The chewy bite lifted his mood a little.
“...Shit. At least it tastes good.”
“Right? This place is famous in the Hunter community.”
“Really?”
“Yeah. Search for it and you’ll find plenty of reviews. People say it’s perfect for a drink after a raid.”
“Of course the drinks taste good to them. They finish a raid and pick up plenty of Magic Gems. They didn’t come away empty-handed like me.”
“...Oh, boy. Here he goes again.”

The Team Leader smacked his lips. If he belonged to a Guild, it would hardly matter whether a raid came to nothing. But he led a freelance Hunter team. That meant paying the daily wages of everyone laughing and chatting around him, even if the money had to come out of his own pocket.
Including this shameless bastard who had come over to him.
“You’re not mad, are you, Team Leader?”
“Forget it, punk. Pour me another.”
“Yes, sir.”
The team member snapped a salute and poured. The Team Leader gave a quiet laugh and looked out beyond the railing.
The raid had fallen through, but drinking while looking over the landscape, white from a recent snowfall, was not so bad.
Pyeongchang really does have nice scenery. The scenery, anyway.
That was probably why they had built so many ski resorts around here.
He kept emptying his glass as he took in the view. The crowds at the ski resort and the gondolas running nonstop up and down the mountain showed just how little sense those people had.
“Hey. Isn’t this funny?”
The team member looked up from the sashimi he had been devouring.
“What is?”
“There’s a Gate right up on that mountain, and magical power has risen by seven percent. They’re still out there doing this shit.”
Worse, when he came down and checked the news, he had learned that a Monster Wave had broken out in Busan. The Team Leader shook his head.
“Then again, when COVID broke out while I was a kid, there were idiots who still went skiing.”
“Melona?”
“...Never mind. Just keep stuffing your face.”
He sighed and drained his glass. Thinking about what must be happening in Busan made his chest tighten.
“Uh—uh-oh! Oh, whoa! Whoa, whoa, whoa!”
“What?”
“...Why is she doing that again?”
Everyone turned toward the outburst. A female Hunter in her twenties, who had been deep in thought for a while, was waving her smartphone wildly.
“Wow! No way! This is insane!”
The Team Leader looked at her with concern.
“Yeah. Seems like it.”
“No, not that! I told you earlier, didn’t I? I thought I recognized that masked, incredibly handsome guy up there!”
The Team Leader recalled the Hunters they had encountered, particularly the young man at the back.
“Yeah. Thanks to them, our raid was a bust.”
“But it’s him! Wow, that’s incredible. Kim Sohye, how did you spot him? Are your eyes really that good?”
“I’m about to lose my mind listening to you. Could you please tell me what you’re talking about?”
“Look! Right here!”
She thrust the phone in front of his face. He frowned, then saw the face on the screen and opened his eyes wide.
“What the hell? Is this for real? They do look alike, I guess...”
“I’m telling you, it’s him! You don’t trust me, Team Leader?”
“No.”
“Ah, damn it! This time I’m certain, so believe me! I’ve got an eye for this that I honed through thirty years of idol fandom!”
“You’re twenty-five. Was your father a fan too?”
“Anyway, I’m right! If I’m wrong, you don’t have to pay me today!”
A slave to capitalism had put her day’s wages on the line. Only then did the Team Leader start to believe her. He was curious, too.
If it’s true... why would someone that important come all the way here?
Beside a face handsome enough to belong to a celebrity, the phone displayed a short article.
Peace Guild Team Leader Choi Minwoo: “The Emergency Rescue Team Is for Everyone”
A big shot. A very big shot.
The Team Leader had not seen the masked man’s face clearly, but the calm eyes and distinctive air in the photograph did seem familiar.
If it really was him, the other Hunters must be Peace Guild members too.

Choi Minwoo had become famous enough recently that the Team Leader had heard about him several times. But even if only half of those stories were true, the man should have been too busy to breathe. Why would he lead his Guild members to a B-grade Gate in Pyeongchang?
Wait. Then that older man I saw on the way down...
Before he could finish the thought—
RUMBLE, RUMBLE, RUMBLE!
A tremendous vibration began to sweep through the area. For an instant, every sound fell silent, and everyone turned their heads in the same direction as if they had planned it.
The Team Leader noticed what was wrong first. He had already been looking there before the shaking began.
...That place...
The place he had climbed toward with such high hopes, only to come back down empty-handed.
The B-grade Gate known as Yeti’s Winter Range.

The next moment, what appeared in the Team Leader’s widened eyes was part of the mountain slowly collapsing, with pitch-black darkness settling over it. Amid the wreckage of collapsing gondolas and buildings, a dreadful roar shook him to his core.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
A Monster Wave.
And there were still people inside the Gate.
Overcome by suffocating terror, the Team Leader forced out a voice he had barely managed to squeeze together.
“Report it! Right now!”
A frightened question came back.
“W-where?”
“The Hunter Association, the Peace Guild, Jin Taekyung—anywhere! Right now!”

sentences.text: Whump!
BOOM!
A whip of fire lashed the ground.
Piled snow melted, and yeti blood boiled.
Kim Hwajong’s voice came through his clenched teeth as if he were chewing the words before spitting them out.
“Song Cheonwoo, you fucking bastard...”
The old butler’s wide-open eyes were fixed on the spot where someone had been lying only seconds ago.
If this was how it was going to end—if that bastard was going to meet a death like this—Hwajong should have killed him with his own hands.
But Song Cheonwoo had summoned the last of some unknown strength, thrown himself into the deep crevasse, and met the death he had chosen for himself.
It was too good an end for a traitor.
Worse still...
“We’ve lost an important witness.
I’m sorry, Young Master.”
“No.”
Choi Minwoo shook his head at Kim Hwajong’s sigh-like murmur.
His gaze remained fixed on the crevasse whose depth could not be estimated.
“You have nothing to apologize for, Butler Kim.
I should have been more careful.”
Victory dulled vigilance.
Perhaps all the more so after a fight that had been anything but easy.
Choi poured the potion—still more than three-quarters full—over himself.
Hiss.
The sound of flesh burning filled the air as his wounds began to close little by little.
Feeling a faint pain, he continued.
“Song Cheonwoo must have thought this was the only way to save his family.”
“I understand his situation, but... he must have been more desperate than we realized.”
Kim Hwajong muttered roughly, “Damn fool.
There wasn’t even any guarantee this would save his family.
Why do it?”
“He must have been that afraid.
People cling to hope even in despair, don’t they?”
Choi answered quietly and took his eyes off the crevasse.
He could not tell exactly how deep it was, but the drop had to be hundreds of meters.
Song had already been at death’s door.
His chances of surviving the fall were close to zero.
“We should call the Guild members.
No—it would be faster to have the Guild House send people.”
After more than twenty years together, Kim Hwajong knew at once what he meant.
“You want to recover his body?”
“I don’t know if we can, but we have to try.
Song Cheonwoo is still Ares Guild’s European regional branch director.”
Death would not erase his position.
If they could prove even half of what had happened here, the repercussions would reach beyond the impregnable fortress that was Ares Guild and shake Go Jun himself.
“Attempted murder, murder-for-hire—whatever the charge, it will stain even Ares Guild’s Vice Guild Master.
Especially now.”
A fortress built through decades of effort did not crumble easily.
But Go Jun was different.
Choi Minwoo intended to use every bit of power at his disposal to unseat him as lord of that fortress.
“We’re going to be busier than ever.
Both of us.”
Kim Hwajong smiled with pride.
“I’ve been waiting for this day.”
“I’m glad.
That you’re always at my side.”
“Then put me to work before I get any older, Young Master.
We’ll make that bastard Go Jun regret doing this.”
“That’s the plan.”
Choi nodded and walked away from the crevasse.
Whether from his fierce fight with Song or the blood he had lost, exhaustion swept through him and made every step heavy.
Then, as his consciousness gradually grew hazy and he retraced the path he had taken, Choi Minwoo came to an abrupt stop.
Splash.
Muddy water mixed with snow and blood sprayed around him.
Kim Hwajong, who had been following behind him, asked in confusion,
“Young Master?”
Choi Minwoo did not answer.
He silently stared down at his foot, half-submerged in a puddle of murky water, then suddenly muttered,
“Regret.”
“Yes?”
“You said we’d make Go Jun regret doing this.”
“I did.
Is there a problem...?”
“We left out why.
Why did Go Jun do it?”
Choi looked at the puddle.
A single step had splashed the water and sent ripples across it.
Why, then, had Go Jun sent Song Cheonwoo, a member of Ares Guild, to assassinate him?
Because Song was powerful?
Because he was a traitor?
Neither.
It’s a trap.
The thought struck like lightning.
Choi began to tremble.
Not from the shock of his realization, and certainly not from exhaustion.
No.
His body was not the only thing that had been trembling from the beginning.
Rumble...
Fresh ripples spread across the puddle as it was settling, and a heap of snow that had yet to melt collapsed.
The ground was shaking.
Terrified yetis cried out across the trembling mountain.
At the center of it all came a tremendous rumble.
Crack—RUMBLE, RUMBLE!
Choi and Kim Hwajong turned together.
The ground split in a spiderweb of cracks, thin fractures running back toward the darkness behind them.
Crack!
Crack-crack-crack!
The crevasse.
An enormous darkness whose end could not be seen opened its jaws.
Darkness poured from the widening gap.
Darkness—no.
Immense magical power shook the mountain and tore through space-time.
SHWAAAA!
And the two men saw what lay beyond the split in space: a boundless blue sky and buildings.
The world they had lived in.
The world they were meant to go on living in.
“...Monster Wave.”
Two worlds that touched but should never have been connected had become linked.
A roar announcing the beginning of the disaster reverberated in every direction.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
Facing the abyss as it finally revealed itself, Kim Hwajong stepped in front of his young master, his gaze darker than ever.
Step.
A snowstorm swept around them.
Blackened by magical power, it was no longer white—or beautiful.
“Team Leader, how about a drink?”
A team member came over with a soju bottle and an easy grin.
The Team Leader answered curtly.
“No, asshole.”
Despite his words, his glass was already being raised ever so slightly.
The team member grinned as if he knew everything and filled the empty glass.
Glug, glug, glug.
The Team Leader threw back the full glass in one gulp, then dipped a piece of flounder sashimi deep in the spicy-sweet sauce and swallowed it.
The chewy bite lifted his mood a little.
“...Shit.
At least it tastes good.”
“Right?
This place is famous in the Hunter community.”
“Really?”
“Yeah.
Search for it and you’ll find plenty of reviews.
People say it’s perfect for a drink after a raid.”
“Of course the drinks taste good to them.
They finish a raid and pick up plenty of Magic Gems.
They didn’t come away empty-handed like me.”
“...Oh, boy.
Here he goes again.”
The Team Leader smacked his lips.
If he belonged to a Guild, it would hardly matter whether a raid came to nothing.
But he led a freelance Hunter team.
That meant paying the daily wages of everyone laughing and chatting around him, even if the money had to come out of his own pocket.
Including this shameless bastard who had come over to him.
“You’re not mad, are you, Team Leader?”
“Forget it, punk.
Pour me another.”
“Yes, sir.”
The team member snapped a salute and poured.
The Team Leader gave a quiet laugh and looked out beyond the railing.
The raid had fallen through, but drinking while looking over the landscape, white from a recent snowfall, was not so bad.
Pyeongchang really does have nice scenery.
The scenery, anyway.
That was probably why they had built so many ski resorts around here.
He kept emptying his glass as he took in the view.
The crowds at the ski resort and the gondolas running nonstop up and down the mountain showed just how little sense those people had.
“Hey.
Isn’t this funny?”
The team member looked up from the sashimi he had been devouring.
“What is?”
“There’s a Gate right up on that mountain, and magical power has risen by seven percent.
They’re still out there doing this shit.”
Worse, when he came down and checked the news, he had learned that a Monster Wave had broken out in Busan.
The Team Leader shook his head.
“Then again, when COVID broke out while I was a kid, there were idiots who still went skiing.”
“Melona?”
“...Never mind.
Just keep stuffing your face.”
He sighed and drained his glass.
Thinking about what must be happening in Busan made his chest tighten.
“Uh—uh-oh!
Oh, whoa!
Whoa, whoa, whoa!”
“What?”
“...Why is she doing that again?”
Everyone turned toward the outburst.
A female Hunter in her twenties, who had been deep in thought for a while, was waving her smartphone wildly.
“Wow!
No way!
This is insane!”
The Team Leader looked at her with concern.
“Yeah.
Seems like it.”
“No, not that!
I told you earlier, didn’t I?
I thought I recognized that masked, incredibly handsome guy up there!”
The Team Leader recalled the Hunters they had encountered, particularly the young man at the back.
“Yeah.
Thanks to them, our raid was a bust.”
“But it’s him!
Wow, that’s incredible.
Kim Sohye, how did you spot him?
Are your eyes really that good?”
“I’m about to lose my mind listening to you.
Could you please tell me what you’re talking about?”
“Look!
Right here!”
She thrust the phone in front of his face.
He frowned, then saw the face on the screen and opened his eyes wide.
“What the hell?
Is this for real?
They do look alike, I guess...”
“I’m telling you, it’s him!
You don’t trust me, Team Leader?”
“No.”
“Ah, damn it!
This time I’m certain, so believe me!
I’ve got an eye for this that I honed through thirty years of idol fandom!”
“You’re twenty-five.
Was your father a fan too?”
“Anyway, I’m right!
If I’m wrong, you don’t have to pay me today!”
A slave to capitalism had put her day’s wages on the line.
Only then did the Team Leader start to believe her.
He was curious, too.
If it’s true... why would someone that important come all the way here?
Beside a face handsome enough to belong to a celebrity, the phone displayed a short article.
Peace Guild Team Leader Choi Minwoo: “The Emergency Rescue Team Is for Everyone”
A big shot.
A very big shot.

The Team Leader noticed what was wrong first.

chapters.title: Chapter 582
paragraphs: What could they call it?
Choi Minwoo, Kim Hwajong, and the twenty elite Peace Guild Hunters guarding the Gate from outside all had the same question. None of them could answer it.
They could only stare in disbelief at it, now standing in their world.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
A thunderous roar shook the sky.
It was a hippopotamus, an elephant, an ox, and a rhinoceros all at once. Yet it was none of them.
It was too enormous, too powerful, to be called a beast.
Whoooosh. CRUNCH!
A single step—and the impact was tremendous.

Its huge foreleg crushed the Gate control station beneath a shadow that stretched more than ten meters in every direction. The ground shook as if an earthquake had struck. The cable running down the mountain snapped, and a gondola fell.
Then, from a memory long buried, Kim Hwajong recalled a monster’s name.
“...Behemoth.”
Behemoth. Or Behemos.
A monster whose name came from the Hebrew word for “beast.” Traces of the mythical creature that had risen from the deep, dark abyss could even be found in the Bible.
Look at Behemoth. Just as I made you, I made it too. It grazes grass like an ox.
But the Bible was wrong.
Kim Hwajong did not know what being had made the monster before him, but Behemoth was nothing like a peaceful creature that grazed on grass and drank from ponds.
CRUNCH! CRRRUNCH!
—Kwooh! Kwoooooh!
Behemoth was not the only thing to emerge from the Gate.
Some two hundred yetis fled into the world, their cries sounding like screams. They were Behemoth’s first targets.
The enormous creature trampled and devoured them without mercy, though they were both its kind and its subordinates.
SHAAK! Thud-thud-thud!
Blue blood fell like rain.
Four legs like temple pillars stamped across the earth. Each time tusks resembling an elephant’s ivory scraped the ground, severed monster limbs and blood flew into the air.
A trembling voice escaped someone’s lips.
“T-This...”
The sight alone was enough to bring despair.
Everyone stood frozen, staring blankly as the yetis met their gruesome deaths.
Then—
FWOOOOSH!
Beyond the black mist that had settled around them, dazzling light surged upward. Its warmth pushed back the mist, spreading little by little.
Only then did the onlookers release the breaths they had been holding and search for its source.
Twenty-odd pairs of eyes found a young man holding a sword that blazed with light. His own eyes shone brighter than ever.
“Everyone, behind me.”
The moment his calm voice reached them, the Peace Guild Hunters realized they had broken free of the Fear emanating from Behemoth.
And one person watching the scene trembled with emotion.
This is...
The feeling was deeply familiar and achingly distant. Kim Hwajong remembered a face whose features had grown faint with time and murmured, “So you were here.”
Past and present overlapped. What Kim Hwajong saw reflected in his eyes was Cheon Taemin and Choi Minwoo at the same time—and Choi Minwoo and Cheon Taemin at the same time.
Song Cheonwoo had seen the same thing and felt despair. But even in this perilous moment, joy welled up from deep within the old butler’s chest.
He took his place beside the young man, who had stood alone in the light.
FWOOSH!
Long, fierce whips of flame formed in his hands. Choi Minwoo met his gaze, his expression composed.
“We have to stop it. No matter what it takes.”
There was no retreat in his voice. Below them, screams were already rising from those who had noticed what was happening.
“Aaaah!”
“A-Aaaah!”
—GRAAAAAAAH!
As Behemoth slaughtered the yetis, its roar sent the snow piled on the mountain sliding down like a wave.
More than a thousand people were scattering in every direction, their shrill screams carrying up the slope. Even if luck let them escape the monster for now, they would be its next targets.
Choi Minwoo, Kim Hwajong, and the Peace Guild Hunters knew it. They also knew they could not take on the monster by themselves.
“T-Team Leader.”
They all possessed the strength of high-level Hunters, but their opponent was a monster that appeared only in mythology.
Choi Minwoo answered the frightened voice.
“I won’t force you. If you want to run, run.”
Before anyone could begin to murmur, he continued quietly.
“But don’t forget the choice you made here. Ask yourselves whether you can still call yourselves Hunters.”
The wavering in their eyes stopped. The sword in Choi Minwoo’s hand shone brighter than ever.
[Hero’s Soul]. An ego sword that granted power worthy of a hero only to those who qualified.
Hummm. Fwoooosh.
The blade shook fiercely. Light burst from it in a flash, driving back the darkness, and its warmth enveloped them all.
By then, Choi Minwoo’s eyes had turned golden. Reflected in them was Behemoth, which had finished devouring every last one of its kind.
“Wasn’t the power we received given to us for a day like this?”
Not one person here was an exception. Each had been chosen one day by someone unknown and given power beyond the ordinary.
And that power came with duty and a sense of responsibility.
Hunters.
Swords that defended humanity. Shields against the threats it faced. Guardians who had to stand at the forefront of every battle against monsters.
Their wealth and fame might have dulled that ideal, but its pure essence remained.
“Attack formation. Take your positions.”
Step.
Choi Minwoo advanced. The light moved with him, and Kim Hwajong and the twenty Hunters followed.
They formed an arrowhead as they approached. Their figures appeared in the enormous eyes of the monster that had just finished its first meal in this new world.
—G. R. A. A. A. A. H.

Behemoth let out a cry that sounded almost like a sneer. Though it had devoured hundreds of yetis, it was still hungry—ready to trample, chew, and swallow the humans approaching it with their irritating light.
—Come. Hu. Mans.
No one there understood Behemoth’s Demon Realm language.
But its meaning reached them all.
Shing. Fwoosh.
Weapons were drawn. Magic surged up through staffs and hands.
Twenty-two Hunters shone in the deep darkness, bathed in the sword’s radiance. They were drawn taut as a bowstring, and Choi Minwoo’s shout loosed them.
“Charge!”
Their battle cry was loud enough to leave their ears ringing. Together, they shot forward as a single arrow.
SHWAAAAAAK!
A streak of light cut through the darkness. At its tip, the monster roared as if the sound had been dragged up from the abyss.
—KWOAAAAAAH!
The next moment—
BOOOOM! CRRRUNCH!
Shouts and roars, light and darkness, collided.
—Kik!
“Shut your mouth, you fucking bastard.”
Wham!
The Merman’s head vanished with a heavy impact.
I didn’t bother checking whether it was dead. Before the body hit the ground, I launched myself forward and cut off the fleeing Mermen.
“You shit all over the place, and now you’re running? What kind of business ethics is that? Huh?”
—K-Kiiik.
Their cries were desperate pleas to live. Too late. They were monsters, and I was human.
Besides, if they had crawled all the way to Busan and shit everywhere, they had to pay compensation for it.
An eye for an eye. A life for a life.
I swung White Flame without hesitation.
Whoosh!
Flames surged along the spearhead and swept sideways.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail. The fire dragon’s tail, packed with immense heat, lashed some fifty Mermen in a single stroke. Screams rose with the horrific stench of burning flesh.
—KIEEEEEEK!
A pitiful death cry.
I flashed past the nearest Merman.
Slice.
Through my heightened senses, I felt its head lift into the air and heard the faint sound of the cut.
But I wasn’t done.
Some five hundred Mermen had gathered here, looking for a way out. That meant some five hundred monsters I had to kill.
Slice. Slice. Shhhhhk!
Limbs flew amid sprays of blood. Everything in my spear’s path was severed. From my outstretched palm burst the force of Flame Divine Palm, burning some twenty Mermen.
Fwoosh! KRAAAASH!
It was hot.
The asphalt melting under the extreme heat was hot. So were the tires of the car spinning uselessly after slamming into the side of a bus.
And my heart, as I looked at the driver dead behind the wheel, his foot still on the accelerator.
Drip. Drip.
Blood ran down the hood from the shattered windshield. Even a state-of-the-art airbag had apparently failed to stop the trident that had pierced the glass and lodged in the driver’s chest.
The middle-aged man’s eyes were empty, their light gone. A family photograph hung from the rearview mirror like a talisman, soaked in blood.
Middle-aged parents. A boy who looked to be in elementary school, and a girl who looked younger still.
The worst fucking part was that everyone in the photograph was inside the car. None of them was smiling anymore. All of them were covered in blood.
“You fucking bastards!”
Fwoosh! KRAAAASH!
The flames blazed fiercer and swallowed the monsters.
I cut through the path they made, swinging my spear. I cut, split, tore, and smashed without stopping.
Amid the heat and the evaporating blood, a thought came to me.
Maybe.
Maybe they had been on a trip too. Maybe this was their first family trip to Busan in years, and they had been laughing and chatting when the monsters appeared.
Maybe the father and son had looked toward nearby Gwangan Bridge and made a promise they would never get to keep.
Crack!
My fist punched through hard scales and crushed bone and flesh.
I watched the Merman silently as it let out a short groan. Then I grabbed the warm, pulpy thing my hand had touched and tore it out.
SPURT! Thud!
Green blood splashed across my face as I pulled my hand out. The stench was horrific, but I was already drenched in blood.
Eyes wide, I dropped the heart I had just ripped out onto the fallen Merman’s body.
Plop.
I didn’t like the disbelief in its eyes or the look on its face, as though it thought it had been wronged. So I stomped on it.
CRUNCH. Pop.
Only then did I realize no more monsters were coming at me. None were fleeing. None were alive.
I stood in a pool of green blood, breathing hard, when—
“...Wicked human. You.”
“Why?”
The Skeleton King met my eyes as I turned. It sighed.
“No. Never mind.”
For a moment, I wondered what I looked like to it. I didn’t ask. The eyes of the hundred or so Hunters behind it gave me a fair idea.
“We’re done here.”
At the dry voice that sounded strangely unfamiliar even to me, a Hunter who appeared to be a superior jolted and answered, “Huh? Ah, yes. Yes.”
“How are things elsewhere?”
“T-Those were the last ones. We were gathering our forces to hit them all at once, but...”
Gulp.
He swallowed and went on.
“It looks like everything has been taken care of.”
“Good, then. You worked hard too.”
I patted the Skeleton King’s shoulder and started walking again. When someone asked where I was going, I answered briefly.
“To save people. The ones dying right now. The ones who’ve survived this long.”
I was tired—more mentally than physically. But I couldn’t rest.
Somewhere, people were still waiting for rescue, facing the terror of death. I had to save at least one of them.
And then—
Splash.
My foot left a print of green blood on the city asphalt.
Bzzzt. Bzzzt.
An irritating electronic buzz sounded, and a billboard high on a building flickered. Through the static appeared a familiar face.
A face so handsome it was almost irritating.
Team Leader Choi.
A small inset image appeared beside him, along with a caption.
Peace Guild Hunter Choi Minwoo. Caught up in the Monster Wave in Pyeongchang...
God fucking damn it.

Each had been chosen one day by someone unknown and given power beyond the ordinary.
And that power came with duty and a sense of responsibility.
Hunters.
Swords that defended humanity.
Shields against the threats it faced.
Guardians who had to stand at the forefront of every battle against monsters.
Their wealth and fame might have dulled that ideal, but its pure essence remained.
“Attack formation.
Take your positions.”
Step.
Choi Minwoo advanced.
The light moved with him, and Kim Hwajong and the twenty Hunters followed.
They formed an arrowhead as they approached.
Their figures appeared in the enormous eyes of the monster that had just finished its first meal in this new world.
R.
A.
A.
A.
A.
H.
Behemoth let out a cry that sounded almost like a sneer.
Though it had devoured hundreds of yetis, it was still hungry—ready to trample, chew, and swallow the humans approaching it with their irritating light.
—Come.
Hu.
Mans.
No one there understood Behemoth’s Demon Realm language.
But its meaning reached them all.
Shing.
Fwoosh.
Weapons were drawn.
Magic surged up through staffs and hands.
Twenty-two Hunters shone in the deep darkness, bathed in the sword’s radiance.
They were drawn taut as a bowstring, and Choi Minwoo’s shout loosed them.
“Charge!”
Their battle cry was loud enough to leave their ears ringing.
Together, they shot forward as a single arrow.
SHWAAAAAAK!
A streak of light cut through the darkness.
At its tip, the monster roared as if the sound had been dragged up from the abyss.
—KWOAAAAAAH!
The next moment—
BOOOOM!
CRRRUNCH!
Shouts and roars, light and darkness, collided.
—Kik!
“Shut your mouth, you fucking bastard.”
Wham!
The Merman’s head vanished with a heavy impact.
I didn’t bother checking whether it was dead.
Before the body hit the ground, I launched myself forward and cut off the fleeing Mermen.
“You shit all over the place, and now you’re running?
What kind of business ethics is that?
Huh?”
—K-Kiiik.
Their cries were desperate pleas to live.
Too late.
They were monsters, and I was human.
Besides, if they had crawled all the way to Busan and shit everywhere, they had to pay compensation for it.
An eye for an eye.
A life for a life.
I swung White Flame without hesitation.
Whoosh!
Flames surged along the spearhead and swept sideways.
Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
The fire dragon’s tail, packed with immense heat, lashed some fifty Mermen in a single stroke.
Screams rose with the horrific stench of burning flesh.
—KIEEEEEEK!
A pitiful death cry.
I flashed past the nearest Merman.
Slice.
Through my heightened senses, I felt its head lift into the air and heard the faint sound of the cut.
But I wasn’t done.
Some five hundred Mermen had gathered here, looking for a way out.
That meant some five hundred monsters I had to kill.
Slice.
Slice.
Shhhhhk!
Limbs flew amid sprays of blood.
Everything in my spear’s path was severed.
From my outstretched palm burst the force of Flame Divine Palm, burning some twenty Mermen.
Fwoosh!
KRAAAASH!
It was hot.
The asphalt melting under the extreme heat was hot.
So were the tires of the car spinning uselessly after slamming into the side of a bus.
And my heart, as I looked at the driver dead behind the wheel, his foot still on the accelerator.
Drip.
Drip.
Blood ran down the hood from the shattered windshield.
Even a state-of-the-art airbag had apparently failed to stop the trident that had pierced the glass and lodged in the driver’s chest.
The middle-aged man’s eyes were empty, their light gone.
A family photograph hung from the rearview mirror like a talisman, soaked in blood.
Middle-aged parents.
A boy who looked to be in elementary school, and a girl who looked younger still.
The worst fucking part was that everyone in the photograph was inside the car.
None of them was smiling anymore.
All of them were covered in blood.
“You fucking bastards!”
Fwoosh!
KRAAAASH!
The flames blazed fiercer and swallowed the monsters.
I cut through the path they made, swinging my spear.
I cut, split, tore, and smashed without stopping.
Amid the heat and the evaporating blood, a thought came to me.
Maybe.
Maybe they had been on a trip too.
Maybe this was their first family trip to Busan in years, and they had been laughing and chatting when the monsters appeared.
Maybe the father and son had looked toward nearby Gwangan Bridge and made a promise they would never get to keep.
Crack!
My fist punched through hard scales and crushed bone and flesh.
I watched the Merman silently as it let out a short groan.
Then I grabbed the warm, pulpy thing my hand had touched and tore it out.
SPURT!
Thud!
Green blood splashed across my face as I pulled my hand out.
The stench was horrific, but I was already drenched in blood.
Eyes wide, I dropped the heart I had just ripped out onto the fallen Merman’s body.
Plop.
I didn’t like the disbelief in its eyes or the look on its face, as though it thought it had been wronged.
So I stomped on it.
CRUNCH.
Pop.
Only then did I realize no more monsters were coming at me.
None were fleeing.
None were alive.
I stood in a pool of green blood, breathing hard, when—
“...Wicked human.
You.”
“Why?”
The Skeleton King met my eyes as I turned.
It sighed.
“No.
Never mind.”
For a moment, I wondered what I looked like to it.
I didn’t ask.
The eyes of the hundred or so Hunters behind it gave me a fair idea.
“We’re done here.”
At the dry voice that sounded strangely unfamiliar even to me, a Hunter who appeared to be a superior jolted and answered, “Huh?
Ah, yes.
Yes.”
“How are things elsewhere?”
“T-Those were the last ones.
We were gathering our forces to hit them all at once, but...”
Gulp.
He swallowed and went on.
“It looks like everything has been taken care of.”
“Good, then.
You worked hard too.”
I patted the Skeleton King’s shoulder and started walking again.
When someone asked where I was going, I answered briefly.
“To save people.
The ones dying right now.
The ones who’ve survived this long.”
I was tired—more mentally than physically.
But I couldn’t rest.
Somewhere, people were still waiting for rescue, facing the terror of death.
I had to save at least one of them.
And then—
Splash.
My foot left a print of green blood on the city asphalt.
Bzzzt.
Bzzzt.
An irritating electronic buzz sounded, and a billboard high on a building flickered.
Through the static appeared a familiar face.
A face so handsome it was almost irritating.
Team Leader Choi.
A small inset image appeared beside him, along with a caption.
Peace Guild Hunter Choi Minwoo.
Caught up in the Monster Wave in Pyeongchang...
God fucking damn it.

chapters.title: Chapter 583
paragraphs: Team Leader Choi. Pyeongchang. Monster Wave.
The three words hit me all at once, leaving my thoughts in a jumble.
But the footage filling the electronic billboard gave me no time to think.
—Kwooooom!
“Aaaahhh!”
“An avalanche!”
People fled, screaming.
They hadn’t even thought to take off their ski equipment. They waddled forward, stumbled, and fell as a vast mass of snow and shattered rock came pouring down behind them.
—BOOOM!
The snow swept over dozens of people like a wave. Blood sprayed amid the thunderous roar.
A building crushed by the falling rock went up in flames. Beyond the surging fire lay the source of it all.
—Ruuuumble!
The sun had not yet set, but the sky above that place was dark.
Black clouds hung over a mountain peak I didn’t recognize. Each flash of dazzling light between them brought a tremendous tremor and a deafening boom.
A Monster Wave.
I knew it instinctively. Where light and darkness met, a battle was deciding the fate of thousands.
And Team Leader Choi, Butler Kim, and the Peace Guild Hunters were risking their lives against a named monster.
An announcer’s voice came through the static.
“The government has declared the Pyeongchang area of Gyeonggi Province a disaster zone and dispatched emergency support forces. Meanwhile, the Monster Wave in Busan...”
I had no reason to listen any longer. No time, either.
I spun toward the Hunters staring blankly at the billboard high on the building and shouted.
“Mages!”
“Y-Yes?”
“Mages, step forward! We have to get to Pyeongchang with Teleport! Right now!”
My shout, charged with internal energy, jolted them as though they’d woken from a nightmare. A few raised their hands hesitantly.
One A-grade mage and six B-grade mages. But their faces were grim.
“I-I’m sorry, but it would be difficult for us to cast Teleport on our own.”
“What?”
“We’ve all just fought monsters. Our mana fatigue is severe, and we’d have to draw a Teleport magic circle. Under these circumstances...”
Their voices trailed off as they looked around.
Victims’ bodies and monster carcasses lay everywhere. The roads had been torn apart.
Teleport was notoriously difficult even for high-ranking mages. These were about the worst conditions imaginable for casting it.
Skeleton King had been watching. Now he spoke, his face twisted.
“You stupid hu—bastards. Do you think this is the time to worry about conditions? Do it. Please? Fuck. Being polite is hard.”
He was barely holding back his anger, but the menacing aura leaking from him made the mages swallow hard.
“B-But we can’t help it. It’s too dangerous.”
“We can’t do it. Even if we somehow succeeded, it’s over 250 kilometers from Busan to Pyeongchang. We can’t cover that distance in a single jump.”
“Try! Just find some way to try!”
Skeleton King had said exactly what I wanted to say.
But I knew the mages weren’t making excuses. They weren’t Magic Johnson.
The dark-skinned Grand Mage who had sent me into a chaotic battlefield in Sichuan, China, without even a magic circle was probably on another continent by now.
Damn it.
Sticky blood dripped from my clenched fist. I couldn’t tell if it was mine or a monster’s. Maybe both.
“Is there another way?”
A middle-aged Hunter who seemed to be the highest-ranking one there answered anxiously.
“We contacted headquarters a little while ago. They’re looking for a high-ranking mage in Busan who can cast Teleport, but...”
His voice trailed off. His face was grim.
That told me enough. I urged him again to hurry, then clenched my teeth.
Damn it.
Their opponent was a named monster. One as powerful as the Kraken, or worse.
How much longer could they hold out against a monster whose might was conveyed even through the footage? How many of them would survive?
Just a little longer. Please, hold out a little longer.
I made the plea silently, knowing it would never reach them, and sat down cross-legged.
Until they found a mage, I needed to recover whatever strength I could.
“Whew.”
I closed my eyes and tried to calm the anxiety and rage boiling inside me. Darkness filled my vision.
Through it flashed the faces of those fighting in a darkness deeper still.
Please... survive.
Until I get there.
Whoooosh.
Powerful internal energy, carrying my desperate wish, spread through every limb and bone.
The trunk swept through the air, long and enormous.
Like an elephant’s, it knocked aside the incoming spells and arrows, then came hurtling toward the ground.
Whoooosh!
A deep shadow fell across the people below. Choi Minwoo gritted his teeth, sprang forward, and shouted.
“Scatter!”
Fwap-fwap-fwap!
Figures leaped like the wind and scattered in every direction. They moved like the high-ranking Hunters they were, at the top of the Hunter hierarchy.
But if they were A-grade Hunters, the enemy before them was a named monster out of ancient myth.
—GRAAAAAAAH!
Behemoth.
The monster that had risen from the depths of the abyss into the mortal world roared. Its powerful Fear seized souls and stilled movement, shaking the Hunters as they fled.
“Gasp!”
Two Peace Guild Hunters had strayed beyond the light of Hero’s Soul. They caught their breath sharply.
Without their extensive combat experience and strong wills, they might have fainted or gone mad on the spot.
But even the momentary chaos brought on by Fear was enough for the cunning monster to achieve the result it wanted.
“No!”
Behemoth moved half a beat before Choi Minwoo’s warning. That was enough to seal their fate.
Whoom—CRUNCH!
A gust of wind erupted from empty air and slammed into the earth.
Their armor bore high-level defensive magic. Their muscles had been trained to their limits, and their vitality was tenacious.
None of it could withstand the blow. It broke and crushed everything.
“Ghk. Cough!”
Dark red blood burst out with their dying cries. Bones, flesh, even their organs had ruptured. Not even a top-grade potion could save them.
For an instant, Choi Minwoo met both pairs of fading eyes. He gritted his teeth.
Again...!
They had died. Died, and died again.
Trampled beneath enormous forefeet. Impaled on tusks. Crushed by that swinging trunk.
Of the twenty-two Hunters, including himself and Kim Hwajong, more than half had died horribly. Without the potions they’d brought, he would have watched even more of them die.
And now the potions were nearly gone.
Damn it.
Choi Minwoo clenched his teeth. The ache from a broken molar had faded without his noticing. He could no longer feel the blood running from his split lip.
Only anger and determination remained.
They kept him from collapsing in despair. They drove him past his fear and toward Behemoth.
“Young Master!”
Whoosh!
Kim Hwajong’s anguished cry fell behind him as he kicked off the ground, mana surging through his steps.
He shot forward like a ray of light. Something split the air above his head, and Choi Minwoo twisted aside with all his strength.
Whoom—BOOOM!
The ground shook. Snow scattered, and shards of rock scraped his forehead. Red blood ran across his vision. The sword gripped in both hands blazed with pure white light.
Fwoooosh—slash!
The thick darkness split.
A streak of light cut through the air and slashed Behemoth’s two pillar-like forelegs. Green blood gushed from the deep wounds.
Fwoooosh!
Drenched from head to toe, Choi Minwoo let out the breath he’d been holding.
He wanted to dodge the blood, but he couldn’t. His body shook from the strength he had spent in that brief attack, much like Behemoth’s staggering legs.
“Two of its four legs...”
He murmured through a vision stained entirely green.
Fifteen Hunters. Far too high a price compared with his own life.
Still, Behemoth’s scream of pain was not unpleasant to hear.
—GRAAAAAAAH! “Hu. Man!”
“...I hear you. No idea what you’re saying, though.”
Choi Minwoo’s answer came out weak.
The pain and exhaustion he’d pushed aside rushed back at once. The light of Hero’s Soul in his hands was fading, ready to go out.
Hold on a little longer. Just a little longer.
But that was asking too much.

His fatigue had been building since his bloody fight with Song Cheonwoo. With the healer dead and the potions gone, there was nothing to stop the bleeding or tend his injuries. They were finally bringing him down.
Ssssh.
The world tilted.
No. The world wasn’t tilting.
Choi Minwoo was.
As his view slowly turned over, he saw something enormous flying toward him.
Whoooosh!
He felt the wind of a blow that would crush his entire body, and closed his eyes.
BOOOM!
With a thunderous crash, the only light vanished.
A cloud of snow and dirt rose through the dense black fog.
Ruuumble!
Behemoth’s strongest blow yet shook the entire mountain.
The surviving Peace Guild Hunters stared in despair. What little hope they had held onto had vanished with the light.
With the young man who had led them.
It’s over. All of it.
They all knew.
The world itself might not end, but the world they knew would end here today.
Strangely, they felt calm as they faced it.
They had done their duty, at least. Their duty as people and as Hunters. They had given everything to a sense of purpose that wealth and fame had made them forget for a while.
They had no regrets.
“Fuck. I signed the contract on my house two days ago.”
A snort of laughter escaped the Hunters at someone’s mutter.
“Crazy bastard.”
“If you’re scared, go. Nobody’s stopping you.”
But no one moved. Not even the Hunter who had spoken first.
He looked down at his trembling legs and said bluntly, “How are we supposed to leave? I’d rather die fighting.”
They all felt the same. Thousands of people were still evacuating behind them.
The comrades who had fallen, and Choi Minwoo, who had charged Behemoth to the end, had died protecting those people.
“We’ve got money, and we’ve got pride.”
“Still, what a shitty day to die. Can’t even see the sky through this fucking fog.”
“Why’d that elephant bastard suddenly stop moving?”
The few who remained steeled themselves to charge Behemoth. Just as they were about to rush forward, a quiet voice spoke.
“You needn’t die.”
At the quiet voice, the thick fog parted. It was fire, not light, that drove back the abyssal darkness.
Fwoooosh!
A man appeared through the fog amid fierce flames and continued,
“At least, you don’t.”
The Hunters’ trembling eyes took in a middle-aged man with half-gray hair.
Kim Hwajong had disappeared into the fog after Choi Minwoo. He looked very different now.
“...Guild Master. Your arm.”
“I’m fine.”
His left arm had been torn off. Even so, Kim Hwajong smiled faintly through his exhaustion.
He had lost an arm, but he had saved something far more precious.
He passed the person cradled in his right arm to the Hunters.
“Leave this place at once. Take the Young Master with you.”
“B-But...”
“That’s an order from your Guild Master.”
Grrrrr.
The monster gave a low laugh. It had spotted the prey that had escaped it by a hair.
Kim Hwajong’s smile disappeared.
“Go!”
The force of his shout left the Hunters no room to argue. They clenched their teeth, took Choi Minwoo’s limp body, and gave a brief bow before launching themselves down the steep slope.
Shhhh-shhhh-shhk!
Kim Hwajong watched them slide away. A faint smile returned to his lips.
You must make it out safely. You must.
When he turned away after murmuring the small plea that would never reach them, hellfire flickered in his one remaining hand.
“Come on, you fucking bastard.”
—GRAAAAAAAH!
Behemoth’s enormous eyes and Kim Hwajong’s flame-filled gaze collided in midair.
The old butler had sent everyone away and stood alone at the edge of the cliff. He began to recite what might be his final spell.
“Hellfire of the underworld, descend upon this place.”
Hell Fire.
Ruuuuumble!

The Hunters’ trembling eyes took in a middle-aged man with half-gray hair.
Kim Hwajong had disappeared into the fog after Choi Minwoo.
He looked very different now.
“...Guild Master.
Your arm.”
“I’m fine.”
His left arm had been torn off.
Even so, Kim Hwajong smiled faintly through his exhaustion.
He had lost an arm, but he had saved something far more precious.
He passed the person cradled in his right arm to the Hunters.
“Leave this place at once.
Take the Young Master with you.”
“B-But...”
“That’s an order from your Guild Master.”
Grrrrr.
The monster gave a low laugh.
It had spotted the prey that had escaped it by a hair.
Kim Hwajong’s smile disappeared.
“Go!”
The force of his shout left the Hunters no room to argue.
They clenched their teeth, took Choi Minwoo’s limp body, and gave a brief bow before launching themselves down the steep slope.
Shhhh-shhhh-shhk!
Kim Hwajong watched them slide away.
A faint smile returned to his lips.
You must make it out safely.
You must.
When he turned away after murmuring the small plea that would never reach them, hellfire flickered in his one remaining hand.
“Come on, you fucking bastard.”
—GRAAAAAAAH!
Behemoth’s enormous eyes and Kim Hwajong’s flame-filled gaze collided in midair.
The old butler had sent everyone away and stood alone at the edge of the cliff.
He began to recite what might be his final spell.
“Hellfire of the underworld, descend upon this place.”
Hell Fire.
Ruuuuumble!

chapters.title: Chapter 584
paragraphs: Ruuuuumble!
A pillar of fire shot into the sky. The mountain shook. For hundreds of meters in every direction, the air boiled with heat so intense that snow, dirt, and rock melted away.
Lava flowed across a land of death. Above the ground where everything else had evaporated, two figures stood like towers.
—Hu. Man. How. Dare. You!
The mythical monster raged, its body charred black. The half-gray-haired old butler regarded it calmly.
Hell Fire.

Even the hellfire summoned from the depths of hell had failed to bring Behemoth down. One of its enormous tusks had melted away without a trace, and its entire body was charred black, but the monster remained standing.
And yet...
“You’re a tough bastard.”
Kim Hwajong did not retreat. He could not.
He tightened his grip on his Magic Staff with his one remaining hand.
Fwoosh.
Flames engulfed the short, slender staff. When they passed, the staff that emerged was longer and thicker.
It was the cherished weapon with which he had reduced countless monsters to ash during the chaotic years of the Great Cataclysm—the weapon that had earned its master the name Hellfire Mage.
Kim Hwajong pointed the reddish staff at Behemoth and muttered,
“Stop. You’re not going anywhere.”
—Old. Man!
Behemoth roared. The black mist hanging over the area stirred like a living creature and shot toward Kim Hwajong.
Sssshhhh!
It was a rope that could bind his whole body and a blade that could tear through flesh and crush it.
Kim Hwajong watched it close in from every direction. Then the staff in his bloodied hand struck the ground.
BOOM!
A deep rumble sent a wave spreading outward. Flames rose around Kim Hwajong and joined into a single ring.
Fwoosh—FWOOSH!
Before fire was a symbol of destruction, it was a force of purification.
The instant the black mist touched the flames, it crumbled away like ash.
The enormous eyes of the monster looking down upon the earth reflected the figure of a lone human standing tall.
—What. Is. This?
Even Behemoth had not expected it.
Its opponent was a mere human. Yet the small, insignificant creature had wounded it—and now had nullified its attack.
—You. Hu. Man!
A roar laden with powerful Fear shook the entire area. But though fire flickered in Kim Hwajong’s eyes, his heart was utterly calm.
The monster had misjudged one thing.
It did not realize that the old human standing before it possessed none of the fear that everyone carried deep in their hearts.
I’m glad, Young Master.
Kim Hwajong smiled at the words that would never reach him. His only fear was moving farther from this disaster even now.
As long as that child, Choi Minwoo, could survive... it did not matter what happened to him.
Even if I die here.

He could be crushed beneath the monster’s feet, impaled on its tusks and killed without a final word, or reduced to ash after wringing every last bit of strength from his body and mana. It would be all right.
If the Young Master is safe, that is enough for me.
Kim Hwajong gripped his staff with a glad heart.
Mana poured into the tip of his reddish weapon in an amount that had already pushed him beyond his limits. It grew hot, then burst forth as flame.
“Sweep it away.”
Fire Wave.
At the brief incantation, a wave of fire surged forward.
Behemoth stood in its path. With an enraged cry, it swung its trunk, shaped like an elephant’s but dozens of times larger.
FWOOSH!
A powerful rush of wind slammed into the wave of fire. The blistering heat died in an instant, and invisible blades of wind raked everything around them.
Ssshhh-shhk! Slash!
The ground split and tore like paper. Kim Hwajong had already escaped by the narrowest margin.
A low voice escaped between the old butler’s lips as he charged toward Behemoth’s flank.
“Shoot forth.”
Blaze.
BOOM!
Flames burst from the tip of the foot he planted.
The blast sent Kim Hwajong forward like a streak of fire. A dense shadow fell over his head.
Whoooosh!
Instinct beat reason by half a step. Fire Shield. At the silent, unspoken spell, layer upon layer of fiery shields formed above him.
In the next instant, tremendous pressure crushed down on the more than twenty overlapping shields.
CRRRRUNCH!
They shattered and scattered.
The overwhelming force and weight—and the immense magical power behind them, whose limits he could not begin to fathom—broke through the shields and sent his mana reeling.
Ptooey!
Dark red blood sprayed from Kim Hwajong’s lips.
His vision blurred as the spell collapsed. But instead of crumpling where he stood, he clenched his teeth and threw himself aside, almost falling.
CRACK! THUD!
The defensive spell had bought him a moment.
Behemoth’s trunk swept past by a hair and smashed into the ground. Hundreds of fragments flew outward, scraping across Kim Hwajong’s calf.
The pain felt like a burn. But instead of groaning, the old butler exposed his bloodstained teeth and smiled.
“Didn’t I tell you? You’re not going anywhere.”
His staff gave off searing heat. A sphere of flame appeared in midair and swelled.
Kim Hwajong coughed up blood.
“Burst. Barrage of fire.”
Flame Cannon.
Dazzling light-flames erupted as the spell was completed.
The ultimate fire spell, carrying power faster and more formidable than any cannon, shot toward the monster’s two forelegs—the same forelegs that Choi Minwoo had already cut halfway through.
FWOOSH—BOOOOOOM!
Behemoth’s cry vanished beneath a blast that shook the entire area.
The fire that tore through space burst open the wounds that had not yet healed and swept through the inside of the legs.
Sizzle.
Agonizing pain surged from its forelegs, now blackened like charcoal. Behemoth roared.
—GRAAAAAAAAAAH!
Ruuuuumble!
At last, its two forelegs gave way.
The mythical monster that had risen from the abyss into this world dropped to its forelegs like a collapsing temple.
Its immense weight shook the earth. A great cloud of dust rose.
And the man who had brought Behemoth to its knees laughed as he spat blood.
“Ha! Hahahaha!”
It was the laughter of a Hunter once called the greatest fire mage, and the relief of a butler who had done his duty.
That’s enough. That’s enough.
Half of Behemoth’s four legs were useless.
Unless it grew wings, it could no longer pursue Choi Minwoo. No small number of others would survive because of it, too.
Kim Hwajong smiled at the dark shadow flying toward him.
Still, just a little... I wish...
CRACK! Sssshhhh!
His vision flashed white. An enormous blow engulfed him in pain and sent him flying like a cannonball.
BOOM!
With a thunderous crash, his back smashed into solid rock and broke. Something unstoppable surged up from deep inside him.
“Gueeeeeegh!”
The old butler looked down at what he had vomited, the light fading from his eyes. Small pieces of his organs lay in the pool of dark red blood.
His ears felt blocked, as though his eardrums had burst. Through his blurred vision, a memory from long ago rose like a haze.
“Your fire magic is impressive. Were you an arsonist before this?”
“...What kind of crazy shit is that? If you’re not going to help, get lost.”
“Fortunately, I won’t have to ‘go out,’ then. I’m going to help you and everyone here.”
“Hmm. That changes things. What’s your name?”
“Cheon Taemin.”
He had not known that this man, who looked absurdly young for his age, would become the idol to whom Kim Hwajong would devote his entire life.
But that became reality soon enough.
One year, two years, five years... By the end of the long, terrible Great War, Kim Hwajong had become Cheon Taemin’s shadow.
“What am I supposed to do now?”

The Great Cataclysm had changed Kim Hwajong’s life completely, just as it had changed so many others. He had waited so long for peace, yet when it finally came, he did not know what to do with himself.
Cheon Taemin answered his question with one of his own.
“What do you want to do?”
“I don’t know. But I’ll do anything you ask.”
“Then join the Guild. I need you. I’ve brought Jungryong and Cheonwoo in too.”
“That Peace Guild thing?”
“Yes.”
“The name’s pretty damn lame. How about Ares instead? The god of war from Greek mythology. Ares.”
“Ares, huh? Not bad. I’ll take your suggestion, so join the Guild. I’ll make sure you never have to worry about retirement.”
“...Office work really doesn’t suit me. All right, Guild Master.”
“I’ve told you to call me hyung about five thousand times over the last five years. You never change.”
As Taemin had said, Kim Hwajong never did.
Not even after his relationship with his two trusted comrades and closest sworn brothers grew distant, and after it became difficult to see Cheon Taemin’s face.
Peace had come, but Kim Hwajong’s fiery temper remained, and he still swore constantly.
He decided to change only after a child born amid everyone’s blessings lost both parents in an unexpected accident.
“Hello.”
“...Hello.”
Only a few people had gathered for the funeral. The boy, no more than four or five years old, looked lonely.
He clung to the leg of his maternal grandfather, now his only family, and greeted Kim Hwajong with a somber face. The sight pained the aging man.
Perhaps that was why, when Cheon Taemin came to him a few days later, he accepted without hesitation.
“Could you take care of Minwoo? Of the boy?”
The immortal hero who had become a symbol of humanity was always busy. Even after the Great Cataclysm ended, Cheon Taemin lived as though something were chasing him.
In his place, Kim Hwajong became family to the child left alone.
“Good day, Young Master.”
Neat hair and clothes. A gentle voice. A smile at the corners of his mouth.
That was how the Hellfire Mage, who had set a page of the Great Cataclysm ablaze, became Butler Kim.
“Young Master, you mustn’t run! You’ll hurt yourself—oh dear.”
“Young Master. Being a picky eater is bad for your health. Please eat.”
“Young Master, please don’t cry.”
Young Master. Young Master. Young Master...
Time flowed like a river.
The boy grew into a young man, and white frost settled over Kim Hwajong’s hair.
Even after Cheon Taemin vanished without a trace, Kim Hwajong remained steadfast in his place.
His Young Master no longer ran about recklessly, ate every kind of food without complaint, or cried while thinking of the parents who had left him too soon.
Then, one day, Kim Hwajong saw traces of someone he had not seen in a long time in the grown young man’s face.
“You said you were going to create a Guild.”
“Yes. I’m sorry to ask, Butler Kim, but I need you to serve as Guild Master.”
“If that is what you wish, Young Master, I will do anything. But what do you intend to name the Guild?”
“The Peace Guild. I’m going to call it the Peace Guild.”
“Butler Kim, why do you look so... displeased?”
What could he say? So many thoughts came at once that the old butler hesitated. Then he burst out laughing.
“Not at all. The Peace Guild. What a wonderful name.”
And so the past met the present.

From the founding of the Peace Guild onward, Kim Hwajong greeted each day with joy and memories. His Young Master, who had worn a cold, rigid mask, softened after finding “comrades” for the first time in his life. The Guild grew day by day.
Kim Hwajong thought there would be nothing but good days ahead. From then on. Forever.
He thought he would stay beside his Young Master and watch him grow.
Today really was... the best day of my life.
Cough.
Kim Hwajong laughed as he vomited blood mixed with pieces of his organs.
There was only one reason he could laugh as he died: something his Young Master had said to him today.
“Thank you. For becoming my only family.”
And what else had the Young Master said?
“I’ve always wanted to tell you that.”
Yes. That was it.
Kim Hwajong raised his head, coughing. Thick black mist filled his fading vision.
Somewhere beyond it, his only hope—and his only fear—was probably alive and leaving this place.
“I want to... see you.”
The words trembled between his bloodied lips.
The mythical monster smiled in satisfaction at the dying old butler and opened its jaws.
FWOOSH.
A tremendous gust swept through the entire area.
The flames that had yet to go out, someone’s scattered limbs and blood, even the rocks—all were drawn in.
They spun like a tornado inside Behemoth’s mouth.
“Young... Master.”
No. That was not it. Though his words would never reach him, this was his final greeting.
A faint smile touched his wrinkled lips.
“Minwoo.”
At the very moment his fading voice escaped—
Sssshhhh—FLASH!
A burst of light erupted in midair and turned the whole world white.

chapters.title: Chapter 585
paragraphs: Whoooosh!
A fierce rush of air sounded overhead. Thousands of people who had been screaming and fleeing in every direction stopped in their tracks. One tourist looked up at the sky and spoke in a daze.
He wasn’t the only one wondering.

The civilians fleeing the monster, the hundreds of reinforcements dispatched to stop it, even the Peace Guild Hunters hurrying down the mountain to fulfill their Guild Master’s final wish—they all saw it and had the same question.
What is that?

But they saw it from different places and with different eyes. To the civilians, the streak of light crossing the sky was simply a mystery. The high-ranking Hunters among the reinforcements felt a powerful surge of mana far above them for the briefest instant.
Closer still, the Peace Guild Hunters on the mountainside realized how the light had appeared out of thin air.
...Teleport?
Who? How? Why?
Questions raced through countless minds. But no one saw and felt what was happening more clearly than Kim Hwajong.
On the brink of death, the old butler recognized the blue light spreading across the sky, pressing down on the black mist of magical power.
That’s...
Power, pure and more destructive than anything else.
Flame. It was flame.

Brighter than sunlight and as fierce as the sun itself, it streaked across the sky. For a moment, a face seemed to pass through Kim Hwajong’s blurred vision—a face somewhere inside that blinding light, too bright to look at directly.
Yes. It’s you.
His smile deepened. The primordial monster risen from myth opened its enormous jaws toward the oncoming light.
Whoooooom—
The wind split. The air scattered. Inside jaws wide enough to swallow a mountain, an abyssal power churned.
But the light did not stop. It grew sharper and larger, becoming blue-white flame that surged through the air.
Gooooong.
The world stopped. Two forces that swallowed all space and sound as they advanced collided.
And in the next moment, Kim Hwajong could see. He could hear.
Fwooooosh!
Darkness torn to shreds beneath the blue sky.
Blue-white flames burning through everything in their path. And in that dazzling, silent world, one voice ringing clear.
“One Annihilation.”
Space warped. Unprecedented flames fell like a meteor and pierced Behemoth’s jaws before they could close, passing through its body.
As the monster toppled with a death cry like thunder, the old butler forgot his pain and laughed aloud.

Even the greatest master in the world could not escape death. Neither could an ancient monster that belonged in a myth. Not when a full-powered One Annihilation had entered through its mouth and pierced its entire body.
Bewilderment and death settled together in the eyes of a monster unlike any I had ever seen or heard of. It stared at me vacantly as its enormous body slowly tipped over.
Krrrrrrrung!
The mountain shook when its lifeless body hit the ground. Huge clouds of dust rose all around me, and I gritted my teeth against the pain and fatigue rolling over me in waves.
I can’t collapse.
One Annihilation was a double-edged sword. It poured out all the user’s strength at once.
But I couldn’t fall yet. Not now. Fortunately, I had a power ordinary people didn’t.
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System You have defeated Lv. 150 Behemoth! You have acquired an enormous amount of EXP and Fame! Level Up! The Status effect Exhaustion has been removed! The Status effect Internal Energy Depletion has been removed! Some fatigue and Status effects have disappeared due to the effects of Level Up! ... ... ...
Damn it.
I barely managed to steady myself.

Leveling up was one of the System’s most broken features, but unless the effects stacked, it couldn’t fix everything. Too much fatigue had built up in my body and mind. The aftereffects of One Annihilation left my hands and feet tingling as if I’d been electrocuted.
Still, I couldn’t stop or collapse. I drew on the internal energy that had filled my dantian with the level-up and sent it surging forward.
Boom!
Compressed air burst outward, scattering the dust. At last I could see a rounded shape covered in white bones.
Step. Step.
My heart pounded with every step across the ruined ground. I couldn’t hide the fear in my ragged breathing.
I was afraid of what I’d find. Afraid he wouldn’t look the way I hoped. Afraid he would say goodbye before I was ready.
Tap. Shrrr...
When I carefully placed my hand against it, the membrane made of bones scattered as though it were melting. And then I could finally see.
Inside was a grim-faced blond foreigner. Leaning against him was a middle-aged man with half-gray hair, each faint breath seeming to be his last.
This is...
For a moment, my heart seemed to stop.

It took only a glance to understand. The top-grade potion bottle lying at the Skeleton King’s feet was empty. The man appeared to have recovered without a mark on him, but strength was already draining from his body.
My vision swam.
“...Butler Kim.”
His half-closed eyelids fluttered at my voice. When his fading gaze met mine, his bloodstained lips curved into a gentle smile.
“You came.”
“Yes. I knew it would be you. That light was so warm.”
I clenched my teeth to hold back a groan. Butler Kim had already accepted what was happening to him. That was probably why he sounded different.
The man before my eyes was neither Butler Kim nor the Guild Master of the Peace Guild. He was simply a human being, Kim Hwajong, saying goodbye.
But...
I’m not ready yet.
I couldn’t accept this sudden farewell. I wasn’t going to smile and let him go. I would do anything to bring Kim Hwajong back—to make him Butler Kim, the Guild Master, again.
“But I’m a little cold now. I was so warm before.”
I took his hand and slowly sent Scorching Yang Qi into him.
“It’s because we’re up on the mountain. You’ll warm up soon.”
“Will I?”
I forced a smile.
“Yes. It’s still winter.”
As the warmth seeped into him, Kim Hwajong smiled faintly.
“It really is. Just as you said.”
“You’ll be all right. Don’t worry. I’ll take care of—”
My voice failed me, and not only because my chest had tightened. The internal energy I’d sent through him had shown me the state of his body.
What in the world...
Everyone was born with innate qi, the root and source of all the body’s energy. Almost none remained in Kim Hwajong.
No. Even what little remained was slowly burning away.
Like a dying flame.
Jeok Cheongang’s innate qi had been damaged in Henan, but not to this extent. Kim Hwajong’s condition was beyond repair.
I could tell from what my internal energy revealed.
What it had taken for him to face Behemoth. What he had sacrificed to hold back the monster that had crawled out of the darkness. And who he had burned his one and only life for.
“Young Master... Minwoo. Is the boy safe?”
I made my voice as bright as I could.
“He’s safe. I caught a glimpse of him on the mountainside. He’s fine.”
“Good. That’s good. What a relief.”
What’s a relief? Look what’s happened to you.
I bit my lip rather than say it aloud. Then the Skeleton King’s thought sounded in my head.
—I absorbed the magical power that had seeped into his bones and gave him a top-grade potion, but it was already too late. Even I couldn’t save him.
I knew. I couldn’t blame him when he’d done everything he could. His entire appearance was an illusion made with magic, but the guilt and sorrow on his face were real.
—...I’m sorry, human.
A question occurred to me. It was about everything happening around me.
Why was he the one apologizing? How had Kim Hwajong, who’d eaten with us and laughed with us just a few days ago, ended up lying here beyond recovery?
And why hadn’t I stopped it?
Why?
I had power. The power to stop disasters and prevent tragic deaths.

It had started with a mysterious capsule that appeared in my life one day. It let me change the fate I’d been given and meet people who became precious to me. Now one of those bonds was about to break. One of those people was about to leave me.
So why couldn’t I stop it?
In Shanxi, Henan, Sichuan, Hubei. In Sichuan, in Busan...
I had saved so many lives while traveling between the Murim and the modern world. So why couldn’t I save the one person about to leave before my eyes?
Why?
I was sinking into that question, into helplessness, when—
Ssssh. Tap.
A cold hand covered my trembling fist. Kim Hwajong looked at me, warmth in his eyes.
“It isn’t your fault.”
“You did your best.”
His eyes were no longer clouded. His voice no longer sounded ready to fade. The kindness in his face caught the breath in my throat.
The final rally.
A last flame flaring at the edge of death.
No. I couldn’t let him go yet. I gritted my teeth and sent more internal energy into him, but his body was already at its limit. Strength continued to drain away.
More. Just a little more!
I poured every bit of internal energy in my dantian into him. I held his slowly closing acupoints open and tried to feed the flame dying deep inside his body.
The end came closer rapidly anyway.
“It’s cold. I don’t know if it’s winter, like you said, or if night’s already fallen.”
It couldn’t be either. Scorching Yang Qi was still pouring into him, and the afternoon sun remained in the sky.
Only Kim Hwajong could feel that cold and darkness. Death was freezing his body and drawing a veil over his eyes.
I struggled to speak to the old butler as his breaths grew thinner.
“It’s all right. You’ll see Team Leader Choi soon. Just trust me and...”
Thud.
A hand closed around my wrist. The Skeleton King shook his head, his face grim.
At last I understood. Nothing I said or did could stop this.
It was time to let Kim Hwajong go, so he could leave with whatever peace I could give him.
“Young Master... Minwoo. Is the boy safe?”
His eyes had turned milky. He’d asked me already, but that didn’t matter. I could answer him a hundred times. A thousand.
“He’s safe. Not a hair on his head was harmed.”
“I want to see him. Just once more...”
“You will. He’s already coming.”
“Is that... true?”
“Yes. Ah, there he is.”
It was a lie. A bright red, pure white lie.
On the nameless mountainside swept by a wave of chaos, there were only the three of us and the monster’s corpse.
But Kim Hwajong could no longer tell. With his sight clouded and his mind fading, he reached into empty air as though the person he’d been waiting for would take his hand.
Grab.
At my call and the look that accompanied it, Skeleton King firmly took that hand. The old butler’s eyes curved like crescent moons, and a radiant smile spread across his lips.
“You’ve come.”
And then—
“My grand...son.”
The flame that had burned for one person and refused to go out for this moment finally guttered.
Sssrrk. Tap.
Everything went black.
