chapters.title: Chapter 586
paragraphs: Some truths are cruel and cold.
When people face them, they sometimes turn away, unable—or unwilling—to believe what has happened.
Like me right now.
“...Human.”
Skeleton King’s voice broke the silence. I felt as though I had woken from a long, terrible dream.
And in the next moment, I realized that none of it had been a dream. It was reality.
He’s gone. He really is.
Kim Hwajong’s face was peaceful in death. Joy still lingered in the smile fixed upon his lips—the smile of a man who had fulfilled his final wish before he left.
But I kept sending Scorching Yang Qi through his body, along with questions that could no longer reach him.
Are you still cold? Is it still dark?
Perhaps the old butler I remembered was wandering an endless winter night even now. Shivering, unable to see an inch ahead, searching the darkness for one person.
I couldn’t stop. I had to keep putting warmth into his body as it slowly grew cold.
Thud.
A cold hand came to rest on my shoulder. Skeleton King spoke in a subdued voice.
“Human.”
“Let go.”
“That is enough. Stop.”
He was wrong. It wasn’t enough, so I couldn’t stop.
Just as I was about to roughly shake off the hand on my shoulder, Skeleton King continued.
“He will not be cold anymore, so let that human go... Let that person rest.”
Why did the strength leave my body when I heard that?
I didn’t know.
Perhaps it was because Skeleton King had spoken respectfully of a human for the first time. Perhaps it was because his voice sounded so unusually weak.
Or perhaps it was because of the people who had returned to this nameless mountainside after disaster had swept through it.
Crunch.
Careful footsteps pressed into the snow.
I turned toward the sound and saw five men and women emerge. I recognized their faces from the greetings we’d exchanged once or twice at the Guild House.
Peace Guild members.
They must have realized the situation had changed and come back.

They had already fought Behemoth desperately ahead of me, exhausting themselves and suffering injuries. With vacant eyes, they stared at the monster collapsed before them. Then they turned their heads and looked in this direction.
And—
“No!”
“Guild Master!”
Shouts and screams rang out together.
They hurried over Behemoth’s corpse and found Kim Hwajong in a deep sleep from which he would never wake.
“H-How could this happen?”
“...Damn it. I knew this would happen. I knew it!”
Their voices were filled with grief and tears.
I hadn’t been there, but I could picture what had happened.
He must have told them to go. Told them to run with Team Leader Choi because he was all right.
That was the kind of person Kim Hwajong was.
Someone mattered more to him than his own life: a young man he called Young Master and thought of as his grandson.
I had stood there as though nailed to the ground, watching everything. Then I suddenly opened my mouth.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Y-Yes?”
My voice came out rough and hollow, so unfamiliar it might have belonged to someone else.
“Lay Team Leader Choi down beside him.”
“Hurry.”
The Guild members stared at me for a moment, then understood and nodded. They carefully laid Team Leader Choi, unconscious after exhausting all his strength, on the ground.
The two men lay side by side. They looked nothing alike, yet somehow they resembled each other.
You finally met, the two of you.
Without a word, I placed their hands together.
Maybe it was my imagination, but for an instant Kim Hwajong’s smile seemed to brighten.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung. Wouldn’t it be better to wake the Team Leader...?”
I shook my head at the Guild member who had spoken.
“No.”
“B-But...”
“We can’t. Not right now.”
I cut him off firmly. It wasn’t as though I hadn’t considered it myself.
If Kim Hwajong had still been alive, I would have done whatever it took to wake Team Leader Choi and let them see each other.
But...
It’s too late.

Kim Hwajong was dead. Team Leader Choi’s body was battered, and accumulated fatigue had pushed it to its limit. Even if I forced him awake and gave him a potion, the backlash would come down on him several times harder.
So would the grief and rage.
The dead had found peace after their suffering. The living had to carry theirs on.
I’d learned that three years ago. I couldn’t wake Team Leader Choi in that condition just to tell him something so cruel.
But I could promise him one thing.
Before Team Leader Choi regained consciousness, I would bring him a gift that could soothe even a little of the rage and grief he would feel.
Whoosh! Slash!
The tip of the spear I swung without any preparation split the air, sending a crescent of Force through Behemoth’s enormous body. Skeleton King murmured, almost with a sigh.
“Stop.”
I swung again instead of answering.
Once. Twice. Three times...
Slash! Slash! Fwoosh!
The corpse fell into pieces, and the blood left inside it spurted up like a fountain.
The vast magical power Behemoth had once held was gone. Now it was only meat.
I cut through it without hesitation, like a butcher, until Skeleton King could stand it no longer.
“I said stop! What difference do you think this will—”
“It can make enough of a difference. That’s why I’m doing this.”
“What?”
He stared at me, puzzled.
“What in the world are you talking about?”
I didn’t answer. One step carried me several meters, bringing Behemoth’s corpse right before me.
I studied the remains, cut so thoroughly that nothing of the monster’s former majesty remained. At last, I found what I was looking for.
No—it had made itself known before I found it.
Vrrrr.
A faint vibration passed through the air. With it came a murky, powerful energy.
“...Found it.”
I had worried that it might have been erased by the One Annihilation I had fired earlier, but fortunately, it was unharmed.
I murmured in relief and reached out without hesitation.
Whoosh. Clack!
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space sent it flying into my hand. I stared at it with a solemn gaze.
Item Appraisal.
Ding.

System Item Window Behemoth’s Turbid Abyss Type: Magic Gem Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: None Description: The abyss contained within Behemoth, a Named Monster and primordial beast, and the source of its magical power. For some reason, it absorbed another source of magical power. Its once-pure darkness became turbid and even more powerful. Using it requires an extremely demanding and difficult purification process.
My eyes grew hot as I read the System Window floating before me.
But my mind was colder and clearer than ever as it turned over the information.
Behemoth’s Turbid Abyss.
The System had never lied to me. Not once. Every word of that description had to be true.
It absorbed another source of magical power. For some reason. I see.
The questions that had been drifting through my head for the past several hours, ever since my conversation with Kraken, began to fall into place one after another.
Who had given Kraken a Magic Gem to cause a Monster Wave? Who had ordered him to do it?
Why had Team Leader Choi, busy as he was, left Seoul for Pyeongchang in Gangwon Province? Why had another Monster Wave happened here, of all places?
And what did the description of Behemoth’s Magic Gem mean?
Why? Why? Why?
I asked myself each question and found its answer.
Only a short time passed, though it felt like hours. At last, I had answers to everything.
Everything but the final piece of the puzzle.
Right. One last piece.
I didn’t hesitate. I already knew where to find it.
“Why did you come here today?”
I was speaking to the Peace Guild members. Their eyes turned toward a middle-aged Hunter who seemed to be the most senior among them. He answered grimly.
“Team Leader Choi had someone he needed to meet in secret. A man disguised with illusion magic. He looked very anxious.”
“Who was he?”
“I’m sorry, but none of us know. I don’t know who he was either.”
The middle-aged man was probably telling the truth. But I wasn’t disappointed.
I had heard the man’s identity directly from Team Leader Choi himself not long ago. Even the temporary Head of Security had not been informed.
Song Cheonwoo.
A hero of the Great Cataclysm and Ares Guild’s European regional Director.
And the political rival of both Lee Jungryong and his disciple, Go Jun—two generations of enemies.
But I knew Song Cheonwoo and Team Leader Choi had secretly agreed to work together for the time being. I wasn’t foolish enough to think Song was behind this.
He had no reason. Not one.

Song Cheonwoo was still ambitious after all these years. Whatever else was going on, the idea that he would try to kill Team Leader Choi—a valuable ally in his effort to bring down Go Jun—made no sense.
Someone else was behind everything that had happened today.
Someone who stood to gain more than anyone from the deaths of those two men.
Someone who could use an S-grade Magic Gem of astronomical value and rarity to cause a Monster Wave.
Go Jun.
The final piece fell into place. I knew what I had to do—and that the consequences of my choice could reach the people around me.
Then...
I slowly closed my eyes.
There was no turning back. Right or wrong, I had to do this.
When I opened my eyes again, neither my resolve nor my voice wavered.
“If Team Leader Choi wakes up while I’m gone, please make sure someone tells him.”
“Pardon? Tell him what...?”
“S-grade Hunter Jin Taekyung...”
The unfamiliar, dry voice that sounded as though it belonged to someone else continued.
“...is leaving the Peace Guild as of this moment.”
The frozen expressions of the people before me came into view, along with someone’s face twisted in anger.
“You bastard. Don’t tell me you’re—”
“You stay here. Protect the people and the Guild, just in case.”
The one who had to leave would leave. The one who had to stay would stay.
I shook my head at Skeleton King when he tried to stop me again, then asked the Guild members who had gone rigid like statues.
“Anyone here capable of Teleport? Hands up.”
“H-Hand.”
A mage raised his hand without thinking and asked with a dazed expression,
“B-But where to?”
“Jongno. No...”
I looked at the old butler, asleep forever, and finished.
“Let’s go to Ares Guild.”

sentences.text: Some truths are cruel and cold.
When people face them, they sometimes turn away, unable—or unwilling—to believe what has happened.
Like me right now.
“...Human.”
Skeleton King’s voice broke the silence.
I felt as though I had woken from a long, terrible dream.
And in the next moment, I realized that none of it had been a dream.
It was reality.
He’s gone.
He really is.
Kim Hwajong’s face was peaceful in death.
Joy still lingered in the smile fixed upon his lips—the smile of a man who had fulfilled his final wish before he left.
But I kept sending Scorching Yang Qi through his body, along with questions that could no longer reach him.
Are you still cold?
Is it still dark?
Perhaps the old butler I remembered was wandering an endless winter night even now.
Shivering, unable to see an inch ahead, searching the darkness for one person.
I couldn’t stop.
I had to keep putting warmth into his body as it slowly grew cold.
Thud.
A cold hand came to rest on my shoulder.
Skeleton King spoke in a subdued voice.
“Human.”
“Let go.”
“That is enough.
Stop.”
He was wrong.
It wasn’t enough, so I couldn’t stop.
Just as I was about to roughly shake off the hand on my shoulder, Skeleton King continued.
“He will not be cold anymore, so let that human go...
Let that person rest.”
Why did the strength leave my body when I heard that?
I didn’t know.
Perhaps it was because Skeleton King had spoken respectfully of a human for the first time.
Perhaps it was because his voice sounded so unusually weak.
Or perhaps it was because of the people who had returned to this nameless mountainside after disaster had swept through it.
Crunch.
Careful footsteps pressed into the snow.
I turned toward the sound and saw five men and women emerge.
I recognized their faces from the greetings we’d exchanged once or twice at the Guild House.
Peace Guild members.
They must have realized the situation had changed and come back.
They had already fought Behemoth desperately ahead of me, exhausting themselves and suffering injuries.
With vacant eyes, they stared at the monster collapsed before them.
Then they turned their heads and looked in this direction.
And—
“No!”
“Guild Master!”
Shouts and screams rang out together.
They hurried over Behemoth’s corpse and found Kim Hwajong in a deep sleep from which he would never wake.
“H-How could this happen?”
“...Damn it.
I knew this would happen.
I knew it!”
Their voices were filled with grief and tears.
I hadn’t been there, but I could picture what had happened.
He must have told them to go.
Told them to run with Team Leader Choi because he was all right.
That was the kind of person Kim Hwajong was.
Someone mattered more to him than his own life: a young man he called Young Master and thought of as his grandson.
I had stood there as though nailed to the ground, watching everything.
Then I suddenly opened my mouth.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Y-Yes?”
My voice came out rough and hollow, so unfamiliar it might have belonged to someone else.
“Lay Team Leader Choi down beside him.”
“Hurry.”
The Guild members stared at me for a moment, then understood and nodded.
They carefully laid Team Leader Choi, unconscious after exhausting all his strength, on the ground.
The two men lay side by side.
They looked nothing alike, yet somehow they resembled each other.
You finally met, the two of you.
Without a word, I placed their hands together.
Maybe it was my imagination, but for an instant Kim Hwajong’s smile seemed to brighten.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung.
Wouldn’t it be better to wake the Team Leader...?”
I shook my head at the Guild member who had spoken.
“No.”
“B-But...”
“We can’t.
Not right now.”
I cut him off firmly.
It wasn’t as though I hadn’t considered it myself.
If Kim Hwajong had still been alive, I would have done whatever it took to wake Team Leader Choi and let them see each other.
But...
It’s too late.
Kim Hwajong was dead.
Team Leader Choi’s body was battered, and accumulated fatigue had pushed it to its limit.
Even if I forced him awake and gave him a potion, the backlash would come down on him several times harder.
So would the grief and rage.
The dead had found peace after their suffering.
The living had to carry theirs on.
I’d learned that three years ago.
I couldn’t wake Team Leader Choi in that condition just to tell him something so cruel.
But I could promise him one thing.
Before Team Leader Choi regained consciousness, I would bring him a gift that could soothe even a little of the rage and grief he would feel.
Whoosh!
Slash!
The tip of the spear I swung without any preparation split the air, sending a crescent of Force through Behemoth’s enormous body.
Skeleton King murmured, almost with a sigh.
“Stop.”
I swung again instead of answering.
Once.
Twice.
Three times...
Slash!
Slash!
Fwoosh!
The corpse fell into pieces, and the blood left inside it spurted up like a fountain.
The vast magical power Behemoth had once held was gone.
Now it was only meat.
I cut through it without hesitation, like a butcher, until Skeleton King could stand it no longer.
“I said stop!
What difference do you think this will—”
“It can make enough of a difference.
That’s why I’m doing this.”
“What?”
He stared at me, puzzled.
“What in the world are you talking about?”
I didn’t answer.
One step carried me several meters, bringing Behemoth’s corpse right before me.
I studied the remains, cut so thoroughly that nothing of the monster’s former majesty remained.
At last, I found what I was looking for.
No—it had made itself known before I found it.
Vrrrr.
A faint vibration passed through the air.
With it came a murky, powerful energy.
“...Found it.”
I had worried that it might have been erased by the One Annihilation I had fired earlier, but fortunately, it was unharmed.
I murmured in relief and reached out without hesitation.
Whoosh.
Clack!
Seizing an Object Through Empty Space sent it flying into my hand.
I stared at it with a solemn gaze.
Item Appraisal.
Ding.

System Item Window Behemoth’s Turbid Abyss Type: Magic Gem Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: None Description: The abyss contained within Behemoth, a Named Monster and primordial beast, and the source of its magical power.
For some reason, it absorbed another source of magical power.
Its once-pure darkness became turbid and even more powerful.
Using it requires an extremely demanding and difficult purification process.
My eyes grew hot as I read the System Window floating before me.
But my mind was colder and clearer than ever as it turned over the information.
Behemoth’s Turbid Abyss.
The System had never lied to me.
Not once.
Every word of that description had to be true.
It absorbed another source of magical power.
For some reason.
I see.
The questions that had been drifting through my head for the past several hours, ever since my conversation with Kraken, began to fall into place one after another.
Who had given Kraken a Magic Gem to cause a Monster Wave?
Who had ordered him to do it?
Why had Team Leader Choi, busy as he was, left Seoul for Pyeongchang in Gangwon Province?
Why had another Monster Wave happened here, of all places?
And what did the description of Behemoth’s Magic Gem mean?
Why?
Why?
Why?
I asked myself each question and found its answer.
Only a short time passed, though it felt like hours.
At last, I had answers to everything.
Everything but the final piece of the puzzle.
Right.
One last piece.
I didn’t hesitate.
I already knew where to find it.
“Why did you come here today?”
I was speaking to the Peace Guild members.
Their eyes turned toward a middle-aged Hunter who seemed to be the most senior among them.
He answered grimly.
“Team Leader Choi had someone he needed to meet in secret.
A man disguised with illusion magic.
He looked very anxious.”
“Who was he?”
“I’m sorry, but none of us know.
I don’t know who he was either.”
The middle-aged man was probably telling the truth.
But I wasn’t disappointed.
I had heard the man’s identity directly from Team Leader Choi himself not long ago.
Even the temporary Head of Security had not been informed.
Song Cheonwoo.
A hero of the Great Cataclysm and Ares Guild’s European regional Director.
And the political rival of both Lee Jungryong and his disciple, Go Jun—two generations of enemies.
But I knew Song Cheonwoo and Team Leader Choi had secretly agreed to work together for the time being.
I wasn’t foolish enough to think Song was behind this.
He had no reason.
Not one.
Song Cheonwoo was still ambitious after all these years.
Whatever else was going on, the idea that he would try to kill Team Leader Choi—a valuable ally in his effort to bring down Go Jun—made no sense.
Someone else was behind everything that had happened today.
Someone who stood to gain more than anyone from the deaths of those two men.
Someone who could use an S-grade Magic Gem of astronomical value and rarity to cause a Monster Wave.
Go Jun.
The final piece fell into place.
I knew what I had to do—and that the consequences of my choice could reach the people around me.
Then...
I slowly closed my eyes.
There was no turning back.
Right or wrong, I had to do this.
When I opened my eyes again, neither my resolve nor my voice wavered.
“If Team Leader Choi wakes up while I’m gone, please make sure someone tells him.”
“Pardon?
Tell him what...?”
“S-grade Hunter Jin Taekyung...”
The unfamiliar, dry voice that sounded as though it belonged to someone else continued.
“...is leaving the Peace Guild as of this moment.”
The frozen expressions of the people before me came into view, along with someone’s face twisted in anger.
“You bastard.
Don’t tell me you’re—”
“You stay here.
Protect the people and the Guild, just in case.”
The one who had to leave would leave.
The one who had to stay would stay.
I shook my head at Skeleton King when he tried to stop me again, then asked the Guild members who had gone rigid like statues.
“Anyone here capable of Teleport?
Hands up.”
“H-Hand.”
A mage raised his hand without thinking and asked with a dazed expression,
“B-But where to?”
“Jongno.
I looked at the old butler, asleep forever, and finished.
“Let’s go to Ares Guild.”

chapters.title: Chapter 587
paragraphs: The air. Time.
Everything seemed to have stopped.
That was how it felt to the master of Area A, hidden in the strictest secrecy within Ares Guild in Jongno, Seoul.
How?
The question kept circling through Go Jun’s mind.
He had forgotten Go Se-won was standing beside him. His face rigid, he stared at the holographic television mounted on the wall.
Live footage from dozens of unmanned reconnaissance drones deployed by the government and various media outlets filled the screen.
“Right now, you’re looking at Mount Balwang, near Pyeongchang in Gangwon Province, where the Monster Wave occurred. And...”
It was the voice of the public broadcaster’s nine o’clock news anchor. Usually calm and serious, the unseen man sounded highly agitated.
“Can you see this, everyone? That is the corpse of Behemoth, the Named Monster! Around it, survivors of the disaster are being evacuated by emergency helicopter...”
Go Jun’s eyelids trembled.
The brutally dismembered corpse of the monster. The survivors. The voices of the Peace Guild members and the anchor explaining the situation.
All of it fed his fury.
Bang!
With a thunderous crash, the latest-model holographic television—replaced more than ten times in the past month—burst into dust.
Go Jun did not care.
The instant Choi Minwoo appeared on the screen, being evacuated with a respirator over his face, everything else became meaningless.
He survived. Choi Minwoo survived.
The knowledge weighed on him.
To Go Jun, Choi Minwoo was a bastard who deserved to die. A bastard who had to die.
That was why Go Jun had laid the trap.
He had lured Jin Taekyung to Busan and used Song Cheonwoo to turn his enemies against each other, intending to leave both sides crippled.
But...
What went wrong?
Red light flickered in Go Jun’s eyes. In his hand, two unpurified S-grade Magic Gems ground against each other without pause.
Crk. Crk.
What had he missed?
Crk. Crk.
He had thought the plan was perfect. Perhaps it really had been.
Its one flaw was that someone beyond perfection stood on the other side.
Jin Taekyung.
It had to be him. Behemoth’s magical barrier had kept the media from learning exactly what had happened, but Go Jun had no doubt.
The bastard who had killed his Master, Lee Jungryong—a man who had seemed like a living god—and branded Go Jun with a terror he could never erase had interfered again.
Even after Go Jun had set a trap there was no escaping. Even then, again!
Crkkkk!
Instead of a roar filled with resentment, a chilling grinding sound filled the office.
Go Jun forced down his surging anger and barely managed to speak.
“Song Cheonwoo... What about Song Cheonwoo?”
When no answer came, he roared.
“I asked what happened to him!”
“Team Leader Go! Go Se-won!”
Go Se-won, the Head of Security, had watched his superior’s fury in silence. He answered flatly.
“He isn’t on any of the survivor or casualty lists we obtained.”
“What about the Gate access records?”
“Nothing there either. We believe the Peace Guild, which effectively owns that Gate, deliberately left no traces behind.”
“Of course. That makes sense. Even if Choi Minwoo is a little bastard, he’s extremely careful. Isn’t he?”
When a secret never passed beyond the walls around it, that was both the strength and the weakness of keeping it.

Go Jun raked a hand through his hair. He picked up the whiskey in front of him, drank straight from the bottle, and muttered, “Fine. Things went to hell, but they still can’t do anything about it. Song Cheonwoo can prove his alibi with the stand-in we prepared. If that gets too difficult, we make it look like he acted alone. There’s no trace left in Busan, so we don’t need to worry about that. Right?”

“But, Vice Guild Master, the Pyeongchang incident is too serious to pass off as Song Cheonwoo’s lone crime. According to the information we obtained, Kim Hwajong—the nominal Guild Master of the Peace Guild—died, and Song Cheonwoo is unquestionably a member of Ares...”
“Listen, Team Leader Go.”
A chill seized Go Se-won’s entire body. His frozen figure was reflected in Go Jun’s red eyes.
“Then make it less serious.”
“V-Vice Guild Master.”

“I don’t care if it costs tens of billions or hundreds of billions of won. Throw money at the prosecutors’ office. Threaten the old men sitting in the National Assembly. Grab anyone with a camera or a microphone by the collar. Isn’t that your job?”
Go Se-won’s eyes trembled violently. The malice radiating from one man, along with his horrifying aura, pressed down on him.
How can someone become like this...?
It went beyond surprise. It was horrifying.
Could a person change this much in only a few months? Fall this far?
And what was this overwhelming power bearing down on him?
As he stared at Go Jun in disbelief, Song Cheonwoo’s voice from several days earlier echoed in his mind.
The boundary between human and monster. That bastard Go Jun... has already become a monster.
Song was right. Go Jun—his superior—had already become a monster.

He had exploited his subordinates’ near-religious loyalty and sent them to their deaths. He had deliberately caused two Monster Waves that might have left thousands, tens of thousands, perhaps even hundreds of thousands dead or injured.
All to eliminate his enemies.
A monster that has forgotten even the minimum duty a human being should possess.
Go Se-won was struggling to hide how shaken he felt when Go Jun spoke again.
“Make sure it’s handled. Choi Minwoo survived, but at least we took care of Song Cheonwoo. Get us through this, and there won’t be a problem.”
Go Jun had regained his composure. His voice was cold.
He had failed to bring down the enemy outside Ares, but he had eliminated the one within it. That was half a victory.
Once the fake Song Cheonwoo he had put in place completed his retirement and disappeared, it would all be over.
No rumors or condemnation could bring down Ares Guild.
“Thirty years. It’s been thirty whole years. Politics, business, the prosecutors’ office, the media... They all grew under Ares’s shadow.”
Crk. Crk.
Cheon Taemin had laid the foundation, but after he lost consciousness, Lee Jungryong had built the pillars and roof.
Young politicians Ares had supported long ago had become prime ministers, ruling-party leaders, and opposition heavyweights. It was the same in business, the prosecutors’ office, and the media.

Some portion of the astronomical sums Ares Guild earned from Gates—the diamond mines of this world—had been scattered everywhere as dirty money. Those seeds had grown into a dense forest surrounding an impregnable fortress.
Go Jun was one of the people who knew that fact better than anyone.
Among the things he had inherited from his Master was a ledger packed with records of corruption and weaknesses.
“Even if everyone points fingers at us, this world itself is what protects us.”
In his impatience and anger, he had forgotten how much power he held.
And just as Go Jun’s confidence fully returned and a deep smile spread across his lips—
“You’re wrong.”
“What?”
Go Se-won looked directly at the monster before him—his superior—with an unreadable expression.
“The old politicians raised under Ares’s name, the Prosecutor General, the business and media dynasties dating back to the Japanese occupation—none of them will protect you, Vice Guild Master.”
“Team Leader Go. What are you—”
“Some of what you said is true. Ares won’t fall just because people point fingers and condemn it. But even if the whole world protects you, there’s one person it can’t stop.”
Go Jun froze.
The thought of grabbing the Head of Security by the collar for daring to spout nonsense to his face vanished.
It was because of the name of the one person who had struck him in the mind.
Jin Taekyung.
Go Se-won read the thought in his trembling eyes and continued quietly.
“Have you forgotten who brought down the man who personally cultivated the world you’re counting on?”
The words hit Go Jun like a blow to the back of the head. He clenched his teeth without realizing it.
Unfortunately, the bastard in front of him was not talking nonsense. Every word was true.
Master.
It was true. Lee Jungryong—Ares’s master and a man who had been no different from the king of Korea—had ultimately been killed by Jin Taekyung’s hand.
The whole world had been his, and no one in it had protected him.
Go Jun spoke through clenched teeth, his voice seething.
“Team Leader Go... You bastard.”
“I only said what someone had to say.”
“Shut up.”
“If that is your order, Vice Guild Master, I’ll obey. But please don’t dismiss what I said.”
“I told you to shut your mouth.”
Rumble!
A massive aura burst from Go Jun’s entire body like an explosion. The office shook as though an earthquake had struck.
Go Se-won’s face went pale before that overwhelming power, but his fear was nothing beside the disgust he felt.
Monster.
Go Jun saw it in his eyes and bared his teeth.
“Team Leader Go, have you gone mad? Lost your mind?”
“I only put you in the position of team leader because your abilities were at least useful. Did wearing a title that was never meant for you suddenly make the world look different?”
He gave an angry laugh and went on.
“Team Leader Go, you’re a coward and a piece of trash. You wrapped it in pretty words and called it loyal counsel, but you’re more afraid of Jin Taekyung than you are of my Master and me.”
“...That isn’t true.”
“It’s too late to deny it. Let’s admit what we both know. Yes, that bastard Jin Taekyung is strong. But how long do you think he’ll stay above me? Hmm?”
Crk. Crk!
“It’s only a matter of time. Now that I—now that I’ve decided to kill that bastard—I’ll find a way worthy of it... Damn it. Do you understand?”
Crkkkk!
His chilling voice mingled with the grinding of the Magic Gems. Go Jun glared at Go Se-won, his eyes so red they were nearly the color of blood.
He leaned his upper body forward toward the subordinate who had dared to commit an unforgivable crime. An old necklace slipped out and spun slowly in front of Go Se-won’s eyes.
“Team Leader Go. Go Se-won. You ungrateful piece of trash.”
“A year at most. Jin Taekyung... That bastard you’re so afraid of will die by my hand. Sichuan, Seoul—I don’t care where. I’ll kill him without anyone noticing, the same way Master was killed.”
“Until then, the world is on my side. No one can touch me unless I leave this fortress myself, you stupid bastard.”
The thrill of revenge mingled with his obsession with one man. Go Se-won watched the murk in his eyes for a moment, then spoke.
“A year. That’s a long time.”
“What?”
“I don’t know what method you’ve found, Vice Guild Master, but... Jin Taekyung won’t wait that long.”
“What, do you think he’s going to come charging in right now?”
“Yes.”
At the short answer, Go Jun laughed aloud. He laughed until his face twisted and the office seemed ready to fall apart from the sound. Then, suddenly, his expression sank, and he parted his lips.

“You fucking idiot. This is Ares Guild. Fall forward and you land at the Blue House; fall backward and you land at the National Assembly. Do you really think he’ll do something insane enough to turn the whole world against him?”
“I hear someone I know artificially caused a Monster Wave. Do you really think Jin Taekyung is incapable of doing something less insane than that?”
“And, Vice Guild Master.”
Go Se-won let out a wry laugh despite himself. He remembered what he had learned from watching Jin Taekyung’s every move and investigating his past.
“Jin Taekyung is a lunatic. Didn’t you know?”
“You bas—!”
Go Jun’s eyes flew wide.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Ares Guild headquarters shook. The skyscraper of more than a hundred floors trembled.
As the roar began to fade, Go Se-won’s voice reached him.
“Dealing with that lunatic will probably be my final assignment. Thank you for everything, Vice Guild Master. If I survive, I’ll submit my resignation formally.”
Carrying both his gratitude for everything until now and his disgust toward Go Jun as a human being, Go Se-won bowed deeply. He threw open the door that had been shut tight.
Emergency sirens were waking Ares Guild.

Go Se-won read the thought in his trembling eyes and continued quietly.
“Have you forgotten who brought down the man who personally cultivated the world you’re counting on?”
The words hit Go Jun like a blow to the back of the head.
He clenched his teeth without realizing it.
Unfortunately, the bastard in front of him was not talking nonsense.
Every word was true.
Master.
It was true.
Lee Jungryong—Ares’s master and a man who had been no different from the king of Korea—had ultimately been killed by Jin Taekyung’s hand.
The whole world had been his, and no one in it had protected him.
Go Jun spoke through clenched teeth, his voice seething.
“Team Leader Go...
You bastard.”
“I only said what someone had to say.”
“Shut up.”
“If that is your order, Vice Guild Master, I’ll obey.
But please don’t dismiss what I said.”
“I told you to shut your mouth.”
Rumble!
A massive aura burst from Go Jun’s entire body like an explosion.
The office shook as though an earthquake had struck.
Go Se-won’s face went pale before that overwhelming power, but his fear was nothing beside the disgust he felt.
Monster.
Go Jun saw it in his eyes and bared his teeth.
“Team Leader Go, have you gone mad?
Lost your mind?”
“I only put you in the position of team leader because your abilities were at least useful.
Did wearing a title that was never meant for you suddenly make the world look different?”
He gave an angry laugh and went on.
“Team Leader Go, you’re a coward and a piece of trash.
You wrapped it in pretty words and called it loyal counsel, but you’re more afraid of Jin Taekyung than you are of my Master and me.”
“...That isn’t true.”
“It’s too late to deny it.
Let’s admit what we both know.
Yes, that bastard Jin Taekyung is strong.
But how long do you think he’ll stay above me?
Hmm?”
Crk.
Crk!
“It’s only a matter of time.
Now that I—now that I’ve decided to kill that bastard—I’ll find a way worthy of it...
Damn it.
Do you understand?”
Crkkkk!
His chilling voice mingled with the grinding of the Magic Gems.
Go Jun glared at Go Se-won, his eyes so red they were nearly the color of blood.
He leaned his upper body forward toward the subordinate who had dared to commit an unforgivable crime.
An old necklace slipped out and spun slowly in front of Go Se-won’s eyes.
“Team Leader Go.
Go Se-won.
You ungrateful piece of trash.”
“A year at most.
Jin Taekyung...
That bastard you’re so afraid of will die by my hand.
Sichuan, Seoul—I don’t care where.
I’ll kill him without anyone noticing, the same way Master was killed.”
“Until then, the world is on my side.
No one can touch me unless I leave this fortress myself, you stupid bastard.”
The thrill of revenge mingled with his obsession with one man.
Go Se-won watched the murk in his eyes for a moment, then spoke.
“A year.
That’s a long time.”
“What?”
“I don’t know what method you’ve found, Vice Guild Master, but...
Jin Taekyung won’t wait that long.”
“What, do you think he’s going to come charging in right now?”
“Yes.”
At the short answer, Go Jun laughed aloud.
He laughed until his face twisted and the office seemed ready to fall apart from the sound.
Then, suddenly, his expression sank, and he parted his lips.
“You fucking idiot.
This is Ares Guild.
Fall forward and you land at the Blue House; fall backward and you land at the National Assembly.
Do you really think he’ll do something insane enough to turn the whole world against him?”
“I hear someone I know artificially caused a Monster Wave.
Do you really think Jin Taekyung is incapable of doing something less insane than that?”
“And, Vice Guild Master.”
Go Se-won let out a wry laugh despite himself.
He remembered what he had learned from watching Jin Taekyung’s every move and investigating his past.
“Jin Taekyung is a lunatic.
Didn’t you know?”
“You bas—!”
Go Jun’s eyes flew wide.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
Ares Guild headquarters shook.
The skyscraper of more than a hundred floors trembled.
As the roar began to fade, Go Se-won’s voice reached him.
“Dealing with that lunatic will probably be my final assignment.
Thank you for everything, Vice Guild Master.
If I survive, I’ll submit my resignation formally.”
Carrying both his gratitude for everything until now and his disgust toward Go Jun as a human being, Go Se-won bowed deeply.
He threw open the door that had been shut tight.
Emergency sirens were waking Ares Guild.

chapters.title: Chapter 588
paragraphs: That day, the air in Korea was heavy with unease.
The Monster Waves that had erupted one after another in Busan and Pyeongchang had been successfully contained, but not without a substantial number of casualties.
People who had been going about an ordinary day were confronted with shocking news and began trembling with anxiety.
“Manager, did you see the news?”
“I did. That’s why I dropped everything and came out here.”
“I can’t focus on anything either. What if there’s really a Monster Wave near our homes or workplaces...?”
“Hey, don’t say that. You’ll jinx us. Come on, let’s have a cigarette.”

Office workers escaped their stifling workplaces and headed for cafés. Students made their way home after class. Children, unaware of what had happened, clung to their parents and begged to play longer, while their parents pulled them away just in case.
It was an uneasy afternoon, and people’s hearts were in turmoil. Eyes filled with worry and fear remained fixed on smartphones broadcasting emergency news alerts.
— You are now looking at the collapsed Gwangan Bridge. In the nearby waters lies the corpse of Kraken, the Named Monster responsible for the Busan Monster Wave...

— The number of casualties reported so far is approaching four thousand. Rescue and search operations are still underway. The list of confirmed casualties is available through the Monster Disaster app...

— I’m at Mount Balwang in Pyeongchang, Gangwon Province. The Monster Wave has ended with the death of the Named Monster Behemoth, but the more than seven thousand people visiting the nearby condos and ski resorts remain terrified.
— The Pyeongchang Monster Wave resulted in 371 casualties. Among the forty-five confirmed dead is Mr. Kim Hwajong, Guild Master of the Peace Guild. His death has come as a tremendous shock...
Every report was horrible and shocking. Public broadcasts, cable channels, online news articles—everywhere was in an uproar, as though someone had stirred up a hornet’s nest.
People in the streets swallowed hard at the sight of Gwangan Bridge in ruins. They had no words for a city awash in blood.
Disaster. There was no other word for it.
But the media’s attention did not rest solely on the damage.
No, there was one name no report on the Monster Waves could leave out.

— Nothing like this has happened in Korea since the Great Cataclysm. Two Monster Waves struck just two hours apart and caused tremendous damage, but a flawless initial response brought the chaos under control quickly. Remarkably, one person took part in suppressing both.

— The whereabouts of S-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung, the young hero who appeared like a comet and killed two Named Monsters in a single day, remain unknown. The Peace Guild has yet to issue an official statement...
A hero who had quelled the chaos and then vanished. Of course everyone wanted to know where he had gone.
Within minutes of the government’s announcement that Jin Taekyung’s whereabouts were unknown, media outlets were churning out theories.
He was dead. He was missing. He had fallen unconscious from the strain of battle.
Most of them were Third Rate media companies famous for dealing in rumors and wild gossip, but ordinary people were wondering the same thing.
Did something really happen to him?
A man with no reason to disappear had vanished without a word, without showing his face to anyone.
He was already gone when reinforcements arrived, and the Peace Guild had issued no statement.
As the news swept across Korea and spread overseas, the question grew like a snowball.
That snowball rolled and rolled, growing larger and larger, until it came to a stop amid the skyscrapers of Jongno.
Step.
No one knew when or how he had appeared.
But the people hurrying through the densely packed forest of buildings for their own reasons realized something.
The man whose profile photo filled the screens in their hands was standing before them.
Drip. Drip-drip.
He was red, and he was blue.
Every time he moved, red and blue blood soaked into the sidewalk beneath him. He was covered in the blood of humans and monsters.
At 190 centimeters tall, with a perfectly balanced build, he moved slowly forward, stepping through the blood.
“...Jin Taekyung?”
Someone’s dazed voice broke the sudden silence.
The young hero had finally appeared. But no one cheered, approached him, took out a phone to photograph him, or reported the sighting to the media. They stopped and fell silent.
Perhaps it was the look in his eyes beneath his blood-soaked hair. His gaze had sunk deep.
Step. Step.
Perhaps it was because profound exhaustion seeped from every one of his footsteps.
Huff.
Perhaps it was because the white breath escaping between his split lips carried the sorrow of someone who had lost another person.
But one thing was certain. Everyone in the crowded street understood it instinctively.
They must not stand in his way.
Swish. Swoosh.
Hundreds of people parted to either side.
In place of a prophet’s staff from myth, the young man carried a pure-white spear as he passed through the human sea opened just for him.
People who had watched him go with dazed eyes began to follow.
No one there knew why. They moved as though under a spell. Hundreds joined hundreds more; thousands joined thousands more.
Soon the crowd numbered in the thousands. As if hypnotized, they walked and kept walking.
The great procession had begun when one man started walking. It seemed it might go on forever, until that same man stopped.
Step.
One last step.
The young man suddenly raised his head and looked at the sky.
Five in the afternoon. A January day that had been especially cold, exhausting, and sorrowful was slowly ending in a reddish glow.
But for one person, it was not over.
It’s beginning now.
Sunset light from the west flashed across a skyscraper towering above the rest. The enormous letters mounted at its top reflected in his eyes.
ARES GUILD
An impregnable fortress that could not be brought down, and a magnificent royal palace.
How many Hunters were inside? How many enemies would he have to bring down before he could face the bastard on the throne?
Hundreds? Thousands?
It didn’t matter. Hundreds or thousands.
Beneath the red sky, Jin Taekyung muttered, “Well, this is perfect weather for fucking someone up.”
Whoosh!
Flames the color of the sunset coiled around his arm and surged upward. The entranced crowd drew back with a collective gasp.
At that moment—
“I’m here, you fucking bastard.”
Whoooooosh—BOOM!
An unprecedented force shook the skyscraper.
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
A massive tremor shook everything around me. The area quaked as though an earthquake had struck.
Spiderweb cracks spread across the marble covering the floor without a gap, and the splendid, valuable works of art decorating the lobby fell like a sudden shower onto the cracked marble.
Crack! Crash!
That was what I saw as soon as I entered.
The thing that had just shattered was a plaster statue of some man. I couldn’t remember its name, so I asked someone nearby.
“What was that statue? I saw it in an art textbook. Rodin’s The Man Who Thought of Something?”
“...Ah. Ahh.”
A young Ares Guild member who appeared to belong to the Security Team stammered with a frozen expression.
He looked so pitiful that I changed the question.
“Then what are your personal thoughts on today’s Monster Wave?”
“P-Pardon?”
“Lucky you. Just a grunt who doesn’t know anything.”
That was what saved his life.
Whoosh!
The Finger Qi I fired cut quietly through the air and struck his acupoints.
His body went rigid and collapsed. At the same instant, a streak of light shot toward me from beyond him.
Screeeeech! Boom!
An arrow grazed my ear and smashed into the entrance door. A middle-aged man who looked like an A-rank Hunter stood with his bowstring drawn taut, aiming at me.
And his was hardly the only weapon pointed my way.
Swish, swish, swish!
Dozens of Security Team members and hundreds of other Hunters filled the lobby, watching me with tense faces. Flames and ice gathered in some hands. Others held spears, swords, or bows.
A middle-aged Hunter presumed to be the Security Team Leader spoke in a rigid voice.
“Step back, Mr. Jin.”
Step back?
I couldn’t help letting out a hollow laugh. “That’s going to be difficult.”
“Why are you doing this?”
“I have plenty of reasons. I’m not sure you’d believe them if I told you, though.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, you...!”
I looked across the crowded lobby, my eyes hollow.
Who should I kill, and who should I spare? Which of them is directly connected to what happened today?
It took everything I had to hold back the urge to kill, rising as naturally as breathing.
Don’t forget. I’m not a monster.
If I killed everyone here today, I would become a monster. But I wanted to remain a human being until the end.
At the very least, I didn’t want innocent people dying for what their superior had done.
I thought that was the right thing to do for Kim Hwajong. For everyone.
“Let’s make this easy for everyone.”
I met hundreds of eyes and said, “Bring me Go Jun.”
An invisible resonance swept through the lobby and the hundreds of Hunters.
As the air tingled with it, I continued slowly.
“Right now.”
The Security Team Leader’s face stiffened. “I don’t think that will be possible.”
“Why not?”
“I have orders to stop you by any means necessary, Mr. Jin.”
“I see.”
“I don’t know what you came here for, but turn back while you still can. How many Hunters do you think are in this building? In Ares Guild House?”
“With this many in the lobby, a thousand altogether would be easy.”
“I guarantee that if you don’t leave now, everyone in this building will be after you within five minutes.”
I answered calmly.
“And I guarantee that if you don’t put down your weapons and run right now, within five minutes, every last one of you will be physically incapable of functioning normally.”
“So get out of my sight. I don’t want to cripple people who had nothing to do with this.”
Whoooooosh!
A sudden wind swept through the lobby.

The Security Team Leader clenched his teeth beneath the powerful wave of qi pouring from my body. The polite tone he had struggled to maintain was gone, blown away by pressure beyond anything he had imagined.
“Why... Why go this far?”
“Because I’m a Hunter.”
“What?”
“Go Jun, that bastard, is a monster. Hunters don’t need a reason to kill monsters.”
Go Jun was hardly going to broadcast what he had done. Most of the people here probably had no idea what I meant.
But they would have realized one thing for certain.
Standing in my way would end badly for them.
The Security Team Leader looked at me with a complicated expression and muttered, “Fuck. What rotten luck.”
“I like your honesty. So, what’s your answer?”
The question wasn’t for him alone.
A conflicted light appeared in the eyes of the Security Team Leader and the roughly two hundred people surrounding me from every direction.
Their hands trembled around their weapons.
Then a voice boomed from the large speakers installed throughout the skyscraper.
— Code Red. Code Red. Target: all Ares Guild members. Objective...
— Jin Taekyung.
The air around us trembled.
The conflict vanished from hundreds of wide-open eyes, and countless streaks of light burst from their hands, becoming a gigantic flash that flooded every direction.
Kuwaaaaaaah!
Red, blue, and white.
I swung the dazzlingly white blade of my spear toward the enormous flash.
Whoooooosh!

chapters.title: Chapter 589
paragraphs: Countless rays of light gathered and gathered until they became a massive pillar.
Attack spells and debuffs descended from overhead. Spears, arrows, and other weapons hurled with all their might rained down around me.
But...
It was already too late to retreat. For me and for them.
Step.
I advanced toward the multicolored flashes.
As I stepped forward, I slashed White Flame diagonally downward. Scorching heat erupted from its spearhead and set everything around me ablaze.
Sssshhhhh!
Space warped. The searing blue-white hellfire forcibly dispelled every spell and devoured the weapons hurtling toward me at tremendous speed, still infused with mana.
Whoooosh!
Heat billowed upward, and the air shimmered. Beyond the haze, I could see hundreds of pairs of shocked eyes.
Realizing that every attack had come to nothing, the Security Team Leader drew his bowstring again. He fired ten arrows with Multi Shot and shouted, “Formation!”
Screeeeech!
While the arrows flew toward me, he moved like the wind in the opposite direction, retreating behind the tanks.
His quick judgment and precise attack were impressive, as befitted an A-rank Hunter of Ares Guild, but...
This time, you picked the wrong opponent.
I muttered the thought inwardly and thrust out my fist. The single punch driven along my smoothly rotating shoulder and arm smashed through the empty air.
Whoom! Bang!
A short, powerful straight punch.
Compressed air burst outward, whipping up a small typhoon around me. The ten arrows streaking toward me like rays of light struck it and veered off course.
Swish-swish-swish! Boom!
As the deflected arrows slammed into the lobby, I launched myself ahead of them. I crossed the dozen or so meters between us and appeared before the Security Team Leader.
“You should’ve shot more gently. Then I would’ve made it hurt less.”
I was far too close for him to draw his bowstring again.
Instead of answering, the Security Team Leader swung the bow in his hand. With a faint metallic click, a blade sprang from the tip of the bow and flew toward my chest.
Sssshhh!
He had probably mastered that move through thousands, perhaps tens of thousands, of repetitions.
But speed was relative. To my eyes, his attack was so slow and feeble that it made me want to yawn.
Slow enough to catch with one hand.
Clack.
The blade stopped half a handspan from me and trembled.
In a moment too brief to call an instant, I saw unmistakable shock flash across the Security Team Leader’s eyes. I tightened my grip on the middle of his bow.
Crack!
Strength beyond human limits shattered the defensive spell on the weapon, then snapped the bow made from hard monster bone.
Before the archer could cry out over the loss of his cherished weapon, my palm pressed against his chest.
Boom!
The Inner-Family Heavy Hand—striking the outside to damage the inside.
With a small explosive sound, the Security Team Leader shot backward like a cannonball.
He slammed into the lobby wall and spat blood. Screams and shouts erupted from every direction, and countless attacks poured toward me.
Swish-swish-swish! Boom-boom-boom!
Front, back, left, right. Thirty-six directions.
Watching the rays of light shoot toward me from every side, I let out a hollow laugh.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi rose from my dantian, became a fire dragon, and entered my spear.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, First Form: Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.
Fwoosh! Whoooosh!
I turned smoothly and swung the spear. Flames surged upward in a whirl, blocking and burning everything in their path.
I stepped forward without hesitation. The marble beneath my foot crumbled like sand.
Sssshhh!
A fierce wind brushed past my ears. Someone’s desperate shout mingled with it.
“Stop him—!”
Boom!
The roar swallowed the rest of the shout. Dozens of tanks who had frozen in place to block my path were flung away, their screams filling the gap.
“Guh!”
“Graaaah!”
Bodies as hard as steel. Combat experience gained over hundreds of raids. None of it helped them now.
Overwhelming strength was enough to crush anything in its way.
Yet the Hunters in the lobby, who had turned against me after wavering, kept coming.
Their weapons caught the light of a half-severed chandelier and flashed as they closed in from every direction.
Pap-pap-pap!
Cheek, neck, armpit, waist, calf...
I saw and felt it all.
It wasn’t only my body that had surpassed human limits.
Before my brain could pass along what my sharpened senses told it, I was already moving.
Crack!
I caught a swordsman’s arm beneath my armpit and broke it.
Thud!
I drove my elbow into another Hunter’s solar plexus and knocked him down.
Tap—swish-swish-swish!
I snatched an arrow flying toward my throat and flung it back the way it had come.
As I turned toward the enemies closing in from all sides, short screams pierced my ears.
“Gah!”
“Ugh!”
It wasn’t happening in just one spot. Screams rang out across the lobby.
Every time I dodged a weapon, threw a punch or a kick, or swung the shaft of my spear, someone screamed and collapsed or flew away like a cannonball.
“Don’t hesitate! Fight!”
Boom! Whooooom!
“Hit him all at once!”
Swish-swish-swish!
Two hundred against one.
No—a raid launched against a single human being. But I wasn’t the one being driven back. They were.
Magic? Weapons?
Nothing could touch me. I plunged deep into their formation and tore through it, wrecking it from within—without killing them.
I struck enough fear into them to keep them from charging at me again before today’s battle was over.
Crack-crack-crack!
“Graaaah!”
Boom!
Before one person’s scream had even ended, three people fell. By the time three screams rang out, five had collapsed.
They were sheep, and I was a great tiger.
With one difference: I had the patience to hold back from slaughtering them.
I’m not a monster. I’m not a monster.
I had to repeat it endlessly in my mind to calm the rage swelling inside me to the point of bursting.
Those who crossed to the other side of the river never returned. Jopil hadn’t. Neither had the forces of Dark Heaven, or Go Jun, who had stepped into the realm of monsters for the sake of his goal.
But I was a Hunter. A martial artist of Murim.
I suddenly remembered something a certain person had once told me—a person who had gone from being the greatest assassin of all time to the greatest physician under heaven.
The weak kill, but the truly strong can save lives instead. It means they can prevent innocent deaths, no matter the circumstances.
If I had been less powerful than I was now—if I had been both weak and evil—they would all have died.
But I was human, not a monster. And I had the strength to save them.
“Everyone... move aside.”
Boom!
The palm force I thrust out swept away dozens of people and sent them flying.
Maybe it was the battle that had gone on for hours without a break. Maybe it was the aftermath of One Annihilation. I was exhausted beyond measure.
Yet everything seemed slow and clear. Their movements. Their expressions. I caught every detail.
I could see the mages’ staffs shining between the fragments of shattered Tower Shields.
Vrrrrrrm!
The Magic Gems embedded in the heads of the staffs vibrated faintly and gave off a dazzling glow.
But before their spells could take shape, I was already among the twenty or so mages.
“Ma—Magic Shi—!”
Too late.
Swish—thump!
A mage trying to cast a defensive spell went rigid and fell.
He wasn’t the only one. Ten fingers sent out ten streams of Finger Qi. The instant they brushed the mages’ acupoints, the mages crumpled like a collapsing wall.
But this was Ares Guild headquarters, a place said to recruit only the best. High-ranking Hunters—whom ordinary Hunters rarely even encountered—were as plentiful as grains of sand here.
“Binding!”
Shrrrriiiip!
Between the broken marble, vines burst from the wall where an unknown oil painting had once hung and wrapped around my ankles like whips.
Crack!
A magical rope appeared out of thin air and bound my wrists with tremendous force.
Was he the Team Leader in charge of the mages? An A-rank mage I had once seen on television fixed me with a look full of killing intent.
“Kill him.”
At that moment—
Swish!
The air above my head rippled. A pale shadow, faint as mist, dropped toward the crown of my head.
Realizing that the sound cutting through the air came from a short sword, I let out a hollow laugh inwardly.
Look at these bastards.
I realized two things.
First, Code Red meant it didn’t matter whether the target lived or died. Second, I had no reason to go easy on the ones who were actually trying to kill me.
In that case...
I welcomed it.
Boom!
The instant a short flame erupted, the assassin was flung away with his limbs twisted, unable even to scream amid the explosive roar.
The A-rank mage stared wide-eyed as I burned through every rope and vine, turning the assassin’s short sword over in my hand.
“What are you doing? Why aren’t you using Magic?”
“I-Ice Blo—!”
Crash! Thunk!
The short sword streaked forward like a ray of light, shattered the Magic Gem in his staff, and buried itself deep in his abdomen. The backflow of mana must have made the pain unbearable.
I struck the chest of the mage, who was screaming loudly enough to shake the lobby.
Boom!
The Inner-Family Heavy Hand was fatal to anyone, but it possessed even greater destructive power against those who directly handled mana, such as mages and healers.
Even if this one survived, he was in no shape to call himself a mage again. His eyes rolled back, and he collapsed.
I stared calmly at the mage, unconscious with an irrecoverable injury, and suddenly opened my mouth.
“Anyone else want to retire while we’re at it?”
“If not, go to sleep.”
Swish-swish-swish! Thump!
Another volley of Finger Qi flew out. The remaining mages dropped without a fight, and silence fell over the lobby.
The clock straight ahead showed that only three minutes had passed since the battle began. Of the roughly two hundred Hunters, fewer than one in ten were still on their feet.
Wheeeeeeeeeeng!
Beneath the unending wail of the alarm, the scene was horrific.
Tanks were embedded in the walls. Damage dealers gasped in pain. Mages lay stiff, staring at the ceiling.
And there I stood, looking down at them all.
My voice came out through parted lips, hoarse and cracked.
“Don’t stand in my way again. There won’t be a second time.”
Those still standing and those on the floor alike stared at me with trembling eyes.
They must have understood by now. They weren’t alive because they had been lucky.
Step.
With the alarm blaring over the silent crowd, I walked slowly to the center of the lobby.
Then I channeled three jiazi of internal energy, kicked off the floor, and shot upward.
Screeeeech!
The lobby ceiling rushed toward me with the fierce wind. At the same time, blue-white flames flickered over my clenched fist.
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist burst forth, burning through the air.
Kuwaaaaaang!

chapters.title: Chapter 590
paragraphs: Everything began and ended in an instant.
Fwoosh.
The overwhelming heat of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist lived up to its name, surging upward in blue-white flames.
Kuwaaaaaang!
The tremendous roar that erupted the next moment swallowed every other sound.
Layer after layer of powerful defensive Magic gave way. Even ceilings made of exceptionally durable magical materials collapsed and melted under the extreme heat.
Boom! Boom! KABOOM!
One, three, five. Ten.
Each time a ceiling vanished, another appeared to block my path.
But I surged upward as a pillar of fire, smashing, piercing, and melting everything that stood in my way.
Boom. Crack.
How high had I climbed? How many ceilings had I broken through?
When I finally came to a stop, beyond the wavering flames...
“Fire!”
There were people waiting for me—no, enemies who had finished making every possible preparation.
Screeeeech!
As if they had been waiting for this moment alone, the enemies fired arrows, Magic, and everything else at once.
And at the moment countless rays of light shot toward me, I muttered a command in my mind that no one could hear.
Inventory. Store.
Swish.
The cool spear shaft vanished from my grip. I drew the lingering flames into both hands and thrust out my palms.
Flame Divine Palm.
Fwoosh. Whoooooosh!
Flame Divine Palm at eight-tenths mastery. A fire dragon burst from both palms and writhed through the air.
Terrible heat swept through the wide corridor stretching out on either side. Magic, arrows, and even people were caught in it.
“Graaaaaaaaaah!”
“Healer! Healeeer!”
When the flames died down, screams and a foul stench remained. The smell of cooking flesh hung over the corridor, and cries of pain rose from every direction.
If I had used my full strength, more than half of them would have burned to death without a scream.
“H-How could this...?”
I turned toward the voice.
At the end of the corridor, a dozen or so healers stood with their mouths open, staring at the scene before them.
“What are you doing? Get your asses over here and save your comrades.”
At my flat remark, a middle-aged woman who looked like a Team Leader bit her lip.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, why on earth are you...?”
“Because there’s something I absolutely have to do. And because you people got in my way.”
“I don’t know what your circumstances are, but still... This is too much, isn’t it?”
Her eyes were full of fear and anger. Looking at her, I felt like the worst bastard in the world. Maybe that was why a hollow laugh escaped me.
The Ares Guild emblems sewn onto their clothes irritated me. So did the nerve of them.
That was why I stopped instead of walking away.
“Too far? Fuck, you’re the ones who went too far.”
“W-What?”
“I don’t think people who came swarming over to kill me at the words Code Red get to say that.”
“I said all I needed was to meet one person. I even tried to avoid a fight with people who had nothing to do with this. But you attacked first, and you’re the ones who went down.”
I understood that they had no direct connection to Kim Hwajong’s death. How could the hands and feet know what the head had planned?
But receiving an order didn’t erase what they had done. They had assembled to kill a person because someone told them to.
“Why are you doing this? I don’t know what your circumstances are, but...”
My quiet voice carried over the low groans and echoed through the blackened corridor.

“Don’t spout bullshit. You should’ve thought about it before asking. Why did that bastard Jin Taekyung suddenly start acting like this? Why did a guy everyone praised for saving people and killing monsters come to our Guild and cause a scene, demanding that we bring out Go Jun? And why was an order given to kill him?”
These days, people called me a hero.
To give them the conclusion first: I wasn’t. I didn’t have some noble spirit of self-sacrifice. I cared about money, and I’d rather live for my own people than for strangers I’d never met.
But... I thought I’d lived without shame.
Since gaining power far beyond anything I deserved, I believed I’d used it for other people whenever I could.
I had always questioned myself—what kind of person I was, whether the choices I made were right.
“So why? Why? Why?”
I kept throwing out those empty questions. The vacant faces in my view disgusted and repulsed me.
“When you’re told to kill someone, why do you come here without even questioning the order?”
No one answered. I knew the answer anyway.
Because they were nothing more than fingernails—not even Go Jun’s hands and feet. Because they were dogs living off the food Go Jun and Ares Guild gave them.
Do the job, and they could gain more wealth and status. That was why they had stood in my way, just as they always had.
“Do you even have any idea what that bastard Go Jun has done? What if the Monster Waves in Busan and Pyeongchang were artificially caused by him?”
The moment I finished speaking, shouts erupted from every direction.
“Bullshit!”
“That’s impossible!”
Right. I’d expected that. It was why I’d come all the way here.
I looked at their disbelieving faces and let out a laugh.
It was fascinating. They remained silent about why a man called a hero had invaded Ares Guild, yet when it came to other matters, they immediately denied everything.
“What did your bosses promise you for taking me down? A fast track to the top of the Guild? Enough money to keep your families fed for generations?”
“And please, spare me the bullshit about needing money to raise your kids or support your widowed mother. None of you are going hungry.”
Everyone here had made it. Whether they’d wanted to or not, they’d Awakened one day and shown enough talent to join Ares Guild.
I didn’t begrudge them the wealth or status that came with it. I’d once dreamed of having those things myself.
What disgusted me was that they’d chosen to do wrong to get even more, then found ways to justify it.
When each person stayed silent, the whole group learned to do the same. That was how they had become the defenders of Ares, an impregnable fortress.
“So.”
I took a deep breath. Exhaustion, anger, disgust—everything churned together in my chest.
“Stop spouting this fucking nonsense and lie down. Suck down your potions and get healed while you think about it. Today is my second birthday. Think of it that way.”
The corridor fell quiet. Even the groans I’d been hearing all around me stopped.
Those still standing and those lying on the ground alike either closed their eyes or firmly shut their mouths.
I ignored their trembling gazes and started walking. I didn’t forget a final goodbye.
“Morons.”
Whether my words had gotten through to them or they still thought like hunting dogs, I didn’t care. I had only one target.
And to reach the fucker who still hadn’t shown himself, I had plenty more obstacles to break through.
Step.
My foot came down on neatly trimmed grass.
The world was still in the middle of a bitterly cold winter, but after passing through the corridor, the garden spread out at its center was a lush spring.
I had no idea what floor I was on. Hundreds of flowers bloomed around me, and a smaller number of enemies waited among them.
“Quite a turnout, you fuckers.”
Swish!
My greeting was answered by an arrow packed with mana.
It was aimed straight at my eye. The archer was a nasty bastard, and with that much mana in the arrow, he was plainly trying to kill me.
In that case, returning the favor was only fair. At least, that was how I did things.
Clack. Swish!
I caught the arrow and hurled it back in the same motion.
The arrowhead flashed as it returned to its owner twice as fast and twice as powerfully as when it had first been fired.
Kang!
A white sword blade shuddered with a sharp metallic ring.
A middle-aged man in his fifties stared at me with deeply sunken eyes. He had deflected the arrow with an enormous greatsword.
His seasoned bearing and aura reminded me of a Murim martial artist nearing the far end of Peak.
“You’re as impatient as I heard, junior.”
“It’s nice to meet you, Senior.”
With all the courtesy of a junior, I cracked my knuckles.
Crack.
The joints, stiff with dried blood, made a sound like bones shifting out of place.
“If you step aside now, I’ll pass through quietly. Except for the bastard who fired that arrow.”
Slap!
The archer’s head snapped to one side.
The middle-aged man slapped the archer on his right across the face with lightning speed, then looked at me.
“He’s young and foolish. I ask you to show him mercy.”
“That wasn’t a mistake. I’ll have to break his wrist.”
“He should be grateful to get off with that. What matters is that he survives.”
What was with this guy?
He was different from the Ares Guild members I’d faced so far. As I watched him, the middle-aged man went on calmly.
“I appreciate your offer, but I’m afraid I have to refuse. I may not look it, but I’m a Guild executive. I have to hang on to your trouser leg, if nothing else.”
“That won’t end well for you.”
“What can I do? I’m a hunting dog too, in the end. I can guess how this will turn out, but I’d appreciate it if you went easy on me.”
What was it about his attitude?
I silently studied the middle-aged man. Then I suddenly arrived at a conclusion and opened my mouth.
“Song Cheonwoo. No—you’re with Director Song’s faction.”
His eyes widened. I’d guessed right.
Which meant I had no reason to fight them.
Song Cheonwoo had led his own faction within Ares Guild and openly opposed Go Jun. The middle-aged man in front of me must have shared his convictions.
“You... knew?”
“I heard it from someone close to him. We don’t need to fight. Step aside.”
The middle-aged man let out a hollow laugh.
“The enemy of my enemy is my ally?”
“At least right now, I don’t want to waste my strength or my time.”
Step.
As I started forward again, he raised his greatsword at an angle.
He was ready to attack. His troubled voice reached me.
“Stop. I don’t want to do this either, but I have no choice.”
I answered without stopping.
“If you don’t want to, why are you here? Because you’re a hunting dog who can’t do anything but obey orders?”
“If you’re afraid of Go Jun, say you’re afraid. Don’t dress it up as having no choice.”
It wasn’t only the middle-aged man. Everyone looking at me had trembling eyes.
I continued forward. The more than a hundred people ahead of me backed away.
The middle-aged man’s composure began to crack.

“The tide has already turned. I heard Director Song returned to the United Kingdom this morning. What do you think that means? I had to find a way to survive. Even if it meant acting like a hunting dog.”
Song Cheonwoo had gone to the United Kingdom this morning? Obviously a lie.
Certain that Go Jun had put forward a stand-in, I let out a quiet snort of laughter.
“What if that hunting dog’s master dies today?”
Every eye widened.
I reached into empty air and summoned White Flame from my Inventory. Its blade swept down diagonally.
Swish!
A single line cut through the air.
Everyone caught their breath. But there was no spray of blood, no death.
The Force that shot from the white spearhead had cut something other than a person.
Slice. Crash!
At the center of the garden stood an ornate fountain. The enormous stone statue planted atop it broke apart and collapsed.
The remains of a statue modeled after a man who was already dead crushed the flowers beneath it.
Its head, severed from the body, rolled and rolled until it reached my feet.
The statue was so lifelike I had no trouble recognizing its face.
Lee Jungryong.
That was right.
Today, the magnificent palace built by an ambitious warlord who had wanted everything would fall.
Along with the Disciple who had become a monster.
I tossed a few words at the stunned crowd.
“You have two choices. Put down your weapons and clear a path, or cover my back.”

sentences.text: Everything began and ended in an instant.
Fwoosh.
The overwhelming heat of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist lived up to its name, surging upward in blue-white flames.
Kuwaaaaaang!
The tremendous roar that erupted the next moment swallowed every other sound.
Layer after layer of powerful defensive Magic gave way.
Even ceilings made of exceptionally durable magical materials collapsed and melted under the extreme heat.
Boom!
Boom!
KABOOM!
One, three, five.
Ten.
Each time a ceiling vanished, another appeared to block my path.
But I surged upward as a pillar of fire, smashing, piercing, and melting everything that stood in my way.
Boom.
Crack.
How high had I climbed?
How many ceilings had I broken through?
When I finally came to a stop, beyond the wavering flames...
“Fire!”
There were people waiting for me—no, enemies who had finished making every possible preparation.
Screeeeech!
As if they had been waiting for this moment alone, the enemies fired arrows, Magic, and everything else at once.
And at the moment countless rays of light shot toward me, I muttered a command in my mind that no one could hear.
Inventory.
Store.
Swish.
The cool spear shaft vanished from my grip.
I drew the lingering flames into both hands and thrust out my palms.
Flame Divine Palm.
Fwoosh.
Whoooooosh!
Flame Divine Palm at eight-tenths mastery.
A fire dragon burst from both palms and writhed through the air.
Terrible heat swept through the wide corridor stretching out on either side.
Magic, arrows, and even people were caught in it.
“Graaaaaaaaaah!”
“Healer!
Healeeer!”
When the flames died down, screams and a foul stench remained.
The smell of cooking flesh hung over the corridor, and cries of pain rose from every direction.
If I had used my full strength, more than half of them would have burned to death without a scream.
“H-How could this...?”
I turned toward the voice.
At the end of the corridor, a dozen or so healers stood with their mouths open, staring at the scene before them.
“What are you doing?
Get your asses over here and save your comrades.”
At my flat remark, a middle-aged woman who looked like a Team Leader bit her lip.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung, why on earth are you...?”
“Because there’s something I absolutely have to do.
And because you people got in my way.”
“I don’t know what your circumstances are, but still...
This is too much, isn’t it?”
Her eyes were full of fear and anger.
Looking at her, I felt like the worst bastard in the world.
Maybe that was why a hollow laugh escaped me.
The Ares Guild emblems sewn onto their clothes irritated me.
So did the nerve of them.
That was why I stopped instead of walking away.
“Too far?
Fuck, you’re the ones who went too far.”
“W-What?”
“I don’t think people who came swarming over to kill me at the words Code Red get to say that.”
“I said all I needed was to meet one person.
I even tried to avoid a fight with people who had nothing to do with this.
But you attacked first, and you’re the ones who went down.”
I understood that they had no direct connection to Kim Hwajong’s death.
How could the hands and feet know what the head had planned?
But receiving an order didn’t erase what they had done.
They had assembled to kill a person because someone told them to.
“Why are you doing this?
I don’t know what your circumstances are, but...”
My quiet voice carried over the low groans and echoed through the blackened corridor.
“Don’t spout bullshit.
You should’ve thought about it before asking.
Why did that bastard Jin Taekyung suddenly start acting like this?
Why did a guy everyone praised for saving people and killing monsters come to our Guild and cause a scene, demanding that we bring out Go Jun?
And why was an order given to kill him?”
These days, people called me a hero.
To give them the conclusion first: I wasn’t.
I didn’t have some noble spirit of self-sacrifice.
I cared about money, and I’d rather live for my own people than for strangers I’d never met.
But...
I thought I’d lived without shame.
Since gaining power far beyond anything I deserved, I believed I’d used it for other people whenever I could.
I had always questioned myself—what kind of person I was, whether the choices I made were right.
“So why?
Why?
Why?”
I kept throwing out those empty questions.
The vacant faces in my view disgusted and repulsed me.
“When you’re told to kill someone, why do you come here without even questioning the order?”
No one answered.
I knew the answer anyway.
Because they were nothing more than fingernails—not even Go Jun’s hands and feet.
Because they were dogs living off the food Go Jun and Ares Guild gave them.
Do the job, and they could gain more wealth and status.
That was why they had stood in my way, just as they always had.
“Do you even have any idea what that bastard Go Jun has done?
What if the Monster Waves in Busan and Pyeongchang were artificially caused by him?”
The moment I finished speaking, shouts erupted from every direction.
“Bullshit!”
“That’s impossible!”
Right.
I’d expected that.
It was why I’d come all the way here.
I looked at their disbelieving faces and let out a laugh.
It was fascinating.
They remained silent about why a man called a hero had invaded Ares Guild, yet when it came to other matters, they immediately denied everything.
“What did your bosses promise you for taking me down?
A fast track to the top of the Guild?
Enough money to keep your families fed for generations?”
“And please, spare me the bullshit about needing money to raise your kids or support your widowed mother.
None of you are going hungry.”
Everyone here had made it.
Whether they’d wanted to or not, they’d Awakened one day and shown enough talent to join Ares Guild.
I didn’t begrudge them the wealth or status that came with it.
I’d once dreamed of having those things myself.
What disgusted me was that they’d chosen to do wrong to get even more, then found ways to justify it.
When each person stayed silent, the whole group learned to do the same.
That was how they had become the defenders of Ares, an impregnable fortress.
“So.”
I took a deep breath.
Exhaustion, anger, disgust—everything churned together in my chest.
“Stop spouting this fucking nonsense and lie down.
Suck down your potions and get healed while you think about it.
Today is my second birthday.
Think of it that way.”
The corridor fell quiet.
Even the groans I’d been hearing all around me stopped.
Those still standing and those lying on the ground alike either closed their eyes or firmly shut their mouths.
I ignored their trembling gazes and started walking.
I didn’t forget a final goodbye.
“Morons.”
Whether my words had gotten through to them or they still thought like hunting dogs, I didn’t care.
I had only one target.
And to reach the fucker who still hadn’t shown himself, I had plenty more obstacles to break through.
Step.
My foot came down on neatly trimmed grass.
The world was still in the middle of a bitterly cold winter, but after passing through the corridor, the garden spread out at its center was a lush spring.
I had no idea what floor I was on.
Hundreds of flowers bloomed around me, and a smaller number of enemies waited among them.
“Quite a turnout, you fuckers.”
Swish!
My greeting was answered by an arrow packed with mana.
It was aimed straight at my eye.
The archer was a nasty bastard, and with that much mana in the arrow, he was plainly trying to kill me.
In that case, returning the favor was only fair.
At least, that was how I did things.
Clack.
Swish!
I caught the arrow and hurled it back in the same motion.
The arrowhead flashed as it returned to its owner twice as fast and twice as powerfully as when it had first been fired.
Kang!
A white sword blade shuddered with a sharp metallic ring.
A middle-aged man in his fifties stared at me with deeply sunken eyes.
He had deflected the arrow with an enormous greatsword.
His seasoned bearing and aura reminded me of a Murim martial artist nearing the far end of Peak.
“You’re as impatient as I heard, junior.”
“It’s nice to meet you, Senior.”
With all the courtesy of a junior, I cracked my knuckles.
Crack.
The joints, stiff with dried blood, made a sound like bones shifting out of place.
“If you step aside now, I’ll pass through quietly.
Except for the bastard who fired that arrow.”
Slap!
The archer’s head snapped to one side.
The middle-aged man slapped the archer on his right across the face with lightning speed, then looked at me.
“He’s young and foolish.
I ask you to show him mercy.”
“That wasn’t a mistake.
I’ll have to break his wrist.”
“He should be grateful to get off with that.
What matters is that he survives.”
What was with this guy?
He was different from the Ares Guild members I’d faced so far.
As I watched him, the middle-aged man went on calmly.
“I appreciate your offer, but I’m afraid I have to refuse.
I may not look it, but I’m a Guild executive.
I have to hang on to your trouser leg, if nothing else.”
“That won’t end well for you.”
“What can I do?
I’m a hunting dog too, in the end.
I can guess how this will turn out, but I’d appreciate it if you went easy on me.”
