What was it about his attitude?
I silently studied the middle-aged man.
Then I suddenly arrived at a conclusion and opened my mouth.
“Song Cheonwoo.
No—you’re with Director Song’s faction.”
His eyes widened.
I’d guessed right.
Which meant I had no reason to fight them.
Song Cheonwoo had led his own faction within Ares Guild and openly opposed Go Jun.
The middle-aged man in front of me must have shared his convictions.
“You... knew?”
“I heard it from someone close to him.
We don’t need to fight.
Step aside.”
The middle-aged man let out a hollow laugh.
“The enemy of my enemy is my ally?”
“At least right now, I don’t want to waste my strength or my time.”
Step.
As I started forward again, he raised his greatsword at an angle.
He was ready to attack.
His troubled voice reached me.
“Stop.
I don’t want to do this either, but I have no choice.”
I answered without stopping.
“If you don’t want to, why are you here?
Because you’re a hunting dog who can’t do anything but obey orders?”
“If you’re afraid of Go Jun, say you’re afraid.
Don’t dress it up as having no choice.”
It wasn’t only the middle-aged man.
Everyone looking at me had trembling eyes.
I continued forward.
The more than a hundred people ahead of me backed away.
The middle-aged man’s composure began to crack.
“The tide has already turned.
I heard Director Song returned to the United Kingdom this morning.
What do you think that means?
I had to find a way to survive.
Even if it meant acting like a hunting dog.”
Song Cheonwoo had gone to the United Kingdom this morning?
Obviously a lie.
Certain that Go Jun had put forward a stand-in, I let out a quiet snort of laughter.
“What if that hunting dog’s master dies today?”
Every eye widened.
I reached into empty air and summoned White Flame from my Inventory.
Its blade swept down diagonally.
Swish!
A single line cut through the air.
Everyone caught their breath.
But there was no spray of blood, no death.
The Force that shot from the white spearhead had cut something other than a person.
Slice.
Crash!
At the center of the garden stood an ornate fountain.
The enormous stone statue planted atop it broke apart and collapsed.
The remains of a statue modeled after a man who was already dead crushed the flowers beneath it.
Its head, severed from the body, rolled and rolled until it reached my feet.
The statue was so lifelike I had no trouble recognizing its face.
Lee Jungryong.
That was right.
Today, the magnificent palace built by an ambitious warlord who had wanted everything would fall.
Along with the Disciple who had become a monster.
I tossed a few words at the stunned crowd.
“You have two choices.
Put down your weapons and clear a path, or cover my back.”

chapters.title: Chapter 591
paragraphs: Beep. Beep. Beep.
The ringing went on for a long time before abruptly cutting off.
Instead of the voice he had been waiting for, a familiar yet still strangely unfamiliar woman’s voice came through the phone.
“Your call cannot be connected. After the beep, you will be directed to voicemail...”
Normally, he would have hung up. No, he would never have called in the first place.
But the middle-aged man had a vague sense that the words he was about to record might be the last he ever left his family.
Beeeeeeep.
The tone sounded, but he couldn’t bring himself to speak.
What could he say to his wife, who was carrying their second child, and their child, who had only just turned four?
And just as the middle-aged man—Go Se-won—was finally about to speak after much thought...
Rumble...
A faint vibration shook the entire building. At the same time, the voice of a security-team member waiting outside seeped through the crack in the door.
“Team Leader, I think you need to come out.”
“Team Leader?”
“Wait. I’m coming.”
Go Se-won ended the call.
Maybe it’s a sign. Someone telling me to stay alive and see my family again.
And if it isn’t...
Then I suppose I don’t even deserve to leave them my last words.
Go Se-won muttered bitterly to himself before opening the door. A security-team member with a hard, expressionless, familiar face was waiting for him.
“I’m sorry. It’s just that outside—”
“I know. Let’s go.”
Go Se-won cut him off calmly and crossed the unlit corridor.
Ahead lay a vast circular hall befitting the top floor, with roughly a hundred fully armed elite Guild members inside.
And filling the hall was a holographic image.
BOOM!
A flash burst across it with a deafening explosion.
Fwoooooosh!
Rays of light surged from two opposing formations and shot toward each other.
“Graaaaaah!”
“Tanks! Reform the line!”
Screams and shouts came from every direction. Hundreds of Hunters clashed in a scene so vivid it might have been unfolding right before him.
Only minutes ago, they had belonged to the same Guild. Now they fought as enemies.
That’s...
Go Se-won watched the fierce battle in the hologram, his gaze darkening.
He recognized the faces fighting at the front: Guild executives from Song Cheonwoo’s faction.
Anti-Ares... So it’s come to this.
A body without a head was bound to fall.
But not this time. Song Cheonwoo, its head, had been removed, only for a stronger one to grow in his place. That was how a body sentenced to death had risen again.
In the hologram, a young man walked forward drenched in human and monster blood. He had become their new rallying point.
“A monster...”
Someone watching muttered the word like a groan.
At that moment, blue-white hellfire blazed around the young man—Jin Taekyung.
Fwoosh! KABOOOOOM!
A streak of flame tore through the space, scorching everything around it.
Huge Tower Shields shattered. Dozens of tanks who had held firm as an iron wall were sent flying at once, and the balance that had held until then collapsed.
“Graaaaaah!”
“Now! Attack!”
Amid spraying blood and falling bodies, the flame that had incapacitated an entire raid team in one blow kept shooting forward.
Screeeeeech!
It was an inextinguishable flame, an unstoppable meteor.
Ceilings said to withstand bombardment collapsed like dominoes, and the forces waiting on each floor fell like bundles of straw.
Whenever the hologram wavered, unable to keep pace with the flame, Jin Taekyung was already on another floor, bringing down new enemies.
“St-Stop him...!”
KABOOOOOM!
Nothing could stand against that overwhelming power. Jin Taekyung had become a streak of flame, shooting onward without pause.
As the troops stationed floor by floor crumbled, the executives in Song Cheonwoo’s faction—still wavering, still unable to decide—finally turned their weapons on their former allies.
“W-we’re on the eighty-fifth floor! Managing Director Kim Jong-pil and Team Thirteen have betrayed us. Gah!”
“Headquarters, respond! There’s a revolt on the ninety-seventh floor...!”
Fwoosh! Boom!
A strong current became a wave. A rolling snowball grew larger.
That was what was happening now. The fire that had been racing in one direction had spread on all sides.
And Go Se-won knew Jin Taekyung’s flame would not go out until his anger subsided—until it swallowed one man whole.
“The target has broken through the hundredth floor!”
“Fighting has broken out on twelve floors at once! Hostile elements have joined the target and are engaging our forces!”
“The target is moving alone! He’s on the 103rd floor! No—the 104th!”
Urgent reports flew from every direction. The executives who had seemed so relaxed when first summoned to the top floor now looked anxious.
“H-hey, Team Leader Go. May I ask you something?”
Go Se-won answered without looking away from the hologram.
“Go ahead, Executive Director Choi.”
“I’ve been wondering for a while...”
The half-gray-haired man swallowed. Then he voiced the question on everyone’s mind.
“Where... where on earth is the Vice Guild Master?”
Go Se-won glanced around. Among the hundred or so people in the hall, the one man who should have been fighting ahead of them all was nowhere to be seen.
Yet despite the bleak situation, Go Se-won felt lighter.
Yes. This should be enough.
When told to bite, he bit. When told to bark, he barked.
He had been one of the countless war orphans left by the Great Cataclysm. He had risen to his present position by living as a faithful hunting dog.
The irony was that knowing it made him sick with himself.
With this, I’ve repaid everything I owed you. Whether I live or die, it has nothing to do with you anymore.
Go Se-won muttered those words in his heart toward the person who still refused to appear, then firmly drew his sword.
Shing.
His calm voice cut through the sharp sound.
“The Vice Guild Master... He won’t be coming.”
“W-what did you say?”
“So fight if you want to live. You’ve eaten far too much from his hand to spit it back out now.”
Everyone here was a hunting dog. They had taken the food their master gave them and lived well on it. They had no choice left.
I’m no different.
A humorless laugh escaped Go Se-won. The executives stared at him.
Then a cry rang through the enormous hall.
“The 119th floor! The target has broken through the 119th floor!”
No one had trouble understanding what that meant. They all knew the building they came to work in every day had 120 floors.
He’s coming.
There was no avoiding the fight.
Clad in full armor, a sword in one hand and a spear in the other, Go Se-won spoke with a heavy heart.
“Formation. Prepare for battle.”
His quiet command reached the hundred Hunters around him.
Rumble! KABOOM!
With a deafening roar accompanied by a tremendous vibration, one of the world’s most famous skyscrapers shook.
An uninvited guest had set foot on the top floor of an impregnable fortress no one had ever been able—or dared—to challenge.
Step.
A lone figure appeared through the rising dust.
Every hair on Go Se-won’s body seemed to stand on end. He hurled his spear with all his strength.
Whoosh! Screeeeeech!
Slice!
The spear hurtling toward me split apart, along with the cloud of dust.
Through the clear path White Flame had cut, I saw a middle-aged man who looked strangely familiar.
Where have I seen him?
The answer came almost at once.
At Lee Jungryong’s national funeral, a new Head of Security had stood beside Go Jun like a shadow. This was him.
The name I had heard in passing back then was probably...
“Go Se-won.”
His eyes trembled faintly when I said it.
Maybe he was surprised I knew his name. Maybe it was how easily I’d dealt with his spear.
Either way, I’d finally found someone who might give me a proper answer. I asked the question I’d repeated dozens of times since entering the lobby.
“Go Jun. Where is he?”
Before I’d finished speaking, a flash shot from Go Se-won’s hand.
Whoosh! KABOOM!
A throwing spear missed me by a hair and buried itself in the floor, leaving a small crater.
It was a signal.
Fwish-fwish-fwish!
Go Se-won wasn’t the only one waiting on the top floor. Roughly a hundred Ares Guild members filled the hall, every one of them worthy of being called a high-ranking Hunter. They attacked together.
Fwoosh!
A vast surge of energy shook the hall, filling it with blue, red, and brilliant light.
Their attacks were stronger and their barrage denser than anything I’d faced on the way up. I stepped forward alone.
Step.
My foot struck the floor, charged with internal energy, and flames rose to heat the air.
Flamefire Path.
Fwoosh! Screeeeeech!
One step was enough. I erased more than ten meters of distance and struck at the air with my palm.
Arrows melted before the blue-white hellfire. Every spell flying toward me came apart.
BOOM!
Water, earth, wind, flame.
The intense heat of Scorching Yang Qi ignored even elemental affinities. As attack spells made from all four elements burst outward, the tanks at the front swiftly raised their Tower Shields.
KABOOM!
Despite the considerable impact, the Tower Shields didn’t waver an inch. They blocked the aftermath of the Magic without suffering the slightest damage, then tilted diagonally.
At the same moment, twenty figures sprang up, using the wall of steel as a foothold.
Pat-pat-pat!
I understood at once. Everyone gathered here was among Ares Guild’s elite. But the ones coming at me now were in another class.
Killing intent.
Their movements were spare and swift. Their calm, impassive eyes had the look of practiced killers.
More than twenty weapons stabbed and slashed at the speed of light, flashing brightly.
Screeeeeech!
As they came at me from every angle, I couldn’t hold back a short laugh.
“What a load of bullshit. You fucking morons.”
In the slowed world, I saw shock spread across their blank faces.
But it was too late to turn back. For them and for me.
Slice!
Blue-white Force extended from White Flame’s spearhead. The incoming weapons lost their strength, and five bodies split in two.
Having turned five bodies into ten with one strike, I drove my fist into empty air.
BOOM!
Compressed air wasn’t the only thing that burst.
A stealthily approaching assassin toppled over, headless. By then, the chain sickle in his hand was already moving at my will.
Whoosh! Thud!
Wielded by Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, it buried itself in another man’s neck.
His once-calm eyes flew wide. As he began to fall, I planted my palm against his chest.
BOOM!
The force of my Flame Divine Palm wasn’t meant to finish him off. He was already dead.
It struck the enemy behind him, who had been about to use his comrade’s body as a shield while thrusting his spear.
“Graaaaaah!”
Blood burst from the man’s seven apertures.
Before the man whose heart meridians had been severed throughout his body could even lower his head, I was already moving toward another enemy.
Crack!
My fist crushed a head.
Fwish! Thud-thud!
Finger Qi shot through another enemy’s neck and chest. He dropped his weapon and pressed a hand to the blood gushing from his throat. It wasn’t enough.
“Ghk. Guh...”
The light faded rapidly from his eyes. I watched the last of them collapse, my gaze cold.
You brought this on yourselves.
On another day, I might have let them live. But not today. Not now.
As when the Black Hunters had attacked Uncle Kkeokjeong, I had no intention of stopping. I couldn’t stop.
I have to show them here. Make sure this never happens again.
I had been a Hunter long before I became a martial artist.

I had also been a modern man born in the twenty-first century, someone who had lived in a civilized society where reason and the law existed. That was why I hadn’t been able to eliminate Go Jun in Sichuan.
Unlike Lee Jungryong, whom I had been able to eliminate amid chaos and destruction, Go Jun had been protected by a fence built from the two-syllable Korean term for the rule of law.
But now none of that mattered.
My choice had allowed Go Jun to live. He had crossed a river he could never cross back. And I—no, all of us—had lost Kim Hwajong.
I would never again see the half-gray-haired old butler who had always spoken to me with a polite, gentle smile.
That was why I had come here. Why I had torn down the fence called the rule of law and made myself an outlaw.
Splash.
My blood-soaked footsteps sounded unnaturally loud.
A suffocating silence had settled over the vast hall. Everyone stood frozen by the slaughter they had witnessed.
But the face I wanted wasn’t among them. Neither was the one man who could tell me where to find him.
Go Se-won.
I turned my head to look for Go Jun’s right hand.
A faint, stealthy sound cut through the air.
Whoosh!
I turned around and slammed my hands together as though in prayer.
KABOOM!
The sharp sword blade caught between them stopped just above my forehead.
Its owner, Go Se-won, spoke calmly.
“Looking for me?”
“Yeah.”
I pressed my palms together harder. The Sword Energy—or rather, Aura—formed from powerful mana yielded to my blue-white Force.
Unable to withstand my immense internal energy, the sword glowed red and began to melt.
Drip, drip. Hiss!
As the molten steel struck the floor, I thrust out a hand blazing with heat.
BOOM!
One palm strike was enough. Layer upon layer of defensive Magic shattered, and Go Se-won’s armor broke apart.
But the blow that shook him to the core didn’t bring him down. He swallowed the blood rising in his throat and reached for my shoulder with his gauntlet.
He tried to, anyway.
Tap-tap-tap! BOOM!
A flowing grappling technique followed seamlessly. Another burst of heat drove Go Se-won back, and he thrust out his hand.
Fwish!
A blade sprang from between the plates of his gauntlet and grazed my chin. I felt a sting, caught his wrist, and twisted.
Crack! KRAK!
My grip crushed the gauntlet. Flesh tore, exposing white bone.
The pain must have been worse than he’d imagined, but Go Se-won didn’t scream. Pale-faced, he asked flatly,
“Is that it?”
“No. Not yet.”
I caught his other arm.
KRAK!
He sucked in a breath.
This time the pain broke through his composure. Blood ran between his lips, and his voice shook.
“Take it easy... and finish it.”
“That’s the plan. After I hear where that bastard Go Jun is.”
“What if the confidentiality clause in my employment contract says I can’t?”
I gripped his collarbone.
“Then it definitely won’t end with just taking it easy.”
Go Se-won gave a weak laugh.
“You searched everywhere and still couldn’t find him. Of course you couldn’t.”
Unfortunately, he was right. I’d fought my way through an endless pack of hunting dogs and wrecked the inside of the building, but Go Jun had never appeared.
If there was one thing I had gained from all the information I had collected so far, it was the identity of the secret area where he was staying.
“Area A. I think you know where it is.”
Cough.
Go Se-won spat blood.
“I picked a bad day. I was planning to hand in my resignation soon.”
“Enough talking. Tell me.”
“That’s easy. But I have a condition.”
“T-Team Leader Go. You’re not going to tell that crazy bastard—!”
There was always someone who couldn’t read the room. The nameless executive who stepped forward soon went quiet, though. Few people could go on talking after taking Finger Qi to the throat.
“A condition?” I asked.
“Yes.”
What he said next caught even me off guard.
“...You want me to kill you?”
Go Se-won gave a small nod. Even as pain wracked his body, his eyes remained calm, reflecting my face.
“It’s too late to go back to how things were. Do it cleanly. Right here. That’s all.”
“I think you understand.”
Breathing heavily, Go Se-won raised a trembling finger and pointed somewhere.
When I finally learned where Area A was, I stopped short.
Empty air?
It was hard to make sense of at first, but the world called things like this Magic. Besides, I’d experienced things far stranger and more dangerous than Magic.
Where?
I stared into the empty air. After a moment, an unfamiliar sensation stirred in my exhausted body.
What’s this?
I couldn’t see it. But I could feel another space there, surrounded by an immense, carefully concealed energy.
It was hidden so perfectly that it could only be detected by someone who recognized its existence.
Go Se-won had kept his end of the bargain. His lips, turning blue, began to move.
“Now kill—”
Bzzzz.
A vibration cut him off.
A smartphone slipped from the trouser pocket of the suit exposed beneath his broken armor and rolled across the floor.
Tap. Bzzzz.
A family photo lit up its cracked screen beneath the caller’s name: Wife.
A young child and his wife smiled brightly. Beside them stood Go Se-won, his expression stiff.
For a moment, neither of us spoke. I looked from the photo on the cracked screen to the cracks showing in his expression.
I remembered his request to be killed. The calm way he’d said it was too late to go back.
“Let me ask you something.”
“Why is today your last day at work?”
Go Se-won hesitated, then answered with a sigh.
“Turns out the job doesn’t suit me. Especially... my boss is a fucking asshole.”
“Yeah. Got it.”
Did Go Se-won know that answer had decided his fate?
I quietly drew up my internal energy.
Not toward my fist.
Toward my legs.
“You—”
KABOOM!
The rest of his words vanished beneath the roar.

I was already soaring into the empty air high above. Fierce wind rushed past me. I felt the strange buoyancy of being seized by invisible hands, and the unknown space that refused entry to anyone without permission.
But I was an outlaw. I didn’t need permission.
There.
Everything had a flow.
I took a deep breath and closed my eyes. Blue-white Force burst from the spearhead in my hand and tore through the empty air.
Swoooooosh!

sentences.text: Beep.
Beep.
Beep.
The ringing went on for a long time before abruptly cutting off.
Instead of the voice he had been waiting for, a familiar yet still strangely unfamiliar woman’s voice came through the phone.
“Your call cannot be connected.
After the beep, you will be directed to voicemail...”
Normally, he would have hung up.
No, he would never have called in the first place.
But the middle-aged man had a vague sense that the words he was about to record might be the last he ever left his family.
Beeeeeeep.
The tone sounded, but he couldn’t bring himself to speak.
What could he say to his wife, who was carrying their second child, and their child, who had only just turned four?
And just as the middle-aged man—Go Se-won—was finally about to speak after much thought...
Rumble...
A faint vibration shook the entire building.
At the same time, the voice of a security-team member waiting outside seeped through the crack in the door.
“Team Leader, I think you need to come out.”
“Team Leader?”
“Wait.
I’m coming.”
Go Se-won ended the call.
Maybe it’s a sign.
Someone telling me to stay alive and see my family again.
And if it isn’t...
Then I suppose I don’t even deserve to leave them my last words.
Go Se-won muttered bitterly to himself before opening the door.
A security-team member with a hard, expressionless, familiar face was waiting for him.
“I’m sorry.
It’s just that outside—”
“I know.
Let’s go.”
Go Se-won cut him off calmly and crossed the unlit corridor.
Ahead lay a vast circular hall befitting the top floor, with roughly a hundred fully armed elite Guild members inside.
And filling the hall was a holographic image.
BOOM!
A flash burst across it with a deafening explosion.
Fwoooooosh!
Rays of light surged from two opposing formations and shot toward each other.
“Graaaaaah!”
“Tanks!
Reform the line!”
Screams and shouts came from every direction.
Hundreds of Hunters clashed in a scene so vivid it might have been unfolding right before him.
Only minutes ago, they had belonged to the same Guild.
Now they fought as enemies.
That’s...
Go Se-won watched the fierce battle in the hologram, his gaze darkening.
He recognized the faces fighting at the front: Guild executives from Song Cheonwoo’s faction.
Anti-Ares...
So it’s come to this.
A body without a head was bound to fall.
But not this time.
Song Cheonwoo, its head, had been removed, only for a stronger one to grow in his place.
That was how a body sentenced to death had risen again.
In the hologram, a young man walked forward drenched in human and monster blood.
He had become their new rallying point.
“A monster...”
Someone watching muttered the word like a groan.
At that moment, blue-white hellfire blazed around the young man—Jin Taekyung.
Fwoosh!
KABOOOOOM!
A streak of flame tore through the space, scorching everything around it.
Huge Tower Shields shattered.
Dozens of tanks who had held firm as an iron wall were sent flying at once, and the balance that had held until then collapsed.
“Graaaaaah!”
“Now!
Attack!”
Amid spraying blood and falling bodies, the flame that had incapacitated an entire raid team in one blow kept shooting forward.
Screeeeeech!
It was an inextinguishable flame, an unstoppable meteor.
Ceilings said to withstand bombardment collapsed like dominoes, and the forces waiting on each floor fell like bundles of straw.
Whenever the hologram wavered, unable to keep pace with the flame, Jin Taekyung was already on another floor, bringing down new enemies.
“St-Stop him...!”
KABOOOOOM!
Nothing could stand against that overwhelming power.
Jin Taekyung had become a streak of flame, shooting onward without pause.
As the troops stationed floor by floor crumbled, the executives in Song Cheonwoo’s faction—still wavering, still unable to decide—finally turned their weapons on their former allies.
“W-we’re on the eighty-fifth floor!
Managing Director Kim Jong-pil and Team Thirteen have betrayed us.
Gah!”
“Headquarters, respond!
There’s a revolt on the ninety-seventh floor...!”
Fwoosh!
Boom!
A strong current became a wave.
A rolling snowball grew larger.
That was what was happening now.
The fire that had been racing in one direction had spread on all sides.
And Go Se-won knew Jin Taekyung’s flame would not go out until his anger subsided—until it swallowed one man whole.
“The target has broken through the hundredth floor!”
“Fighting has broken out on twelve floors at once!
Hostile elements have joined the target and are engaging our forces!”
“The target is moving alone!
He’s on the 103rd floor!
No—the 104th!”
Urgent reports flew from every direction.
The executives who had seemed so relaxed when first summoned to the top floor now looked anxious.
“H-hey, Team Leader Go.
May I ask you something?”
Go Se-won answered without looking away from the hologram.
“Go ahead, Executive Director Choi.”
“I’ve been wondering for a while...”
The half-gray-haired man swallowed.
Then he voiced the question on everyone’s mind.
“Where... where on earth is the Vice Guild Master?”
Go Se-won glanced around.
Among the hundred or so people in the hall, the one man who should have been fighting ahead of them all was nowhere to be seen.
Yet despite the bleak situation, Go Se-won felt lighter.
Yes.
This should be enough.
When told to bite, he bit.
When told to bark, he barked.
He had been one of the countless war orphans left by the Great Cataclysm.
He had risen to his present position by living as a faithful hunting dog.
The irony was that knowing it made him sick with himself.
With this, I’ve repaid everything I owed you.
Whether I live or die, it has nothing to do with you anymore.
Go Se-won muttered those words in his heart toward the person who still refused to appear, then firmly drew his sword.
Shing.
His calm voice cut through the sharp sound.
“The Vice Guild Master...
He won’t be coming.”
“W-what did you say?”
“So fight if you want to live.
You’ve eaten far too much from his hand to spit it back out now.”
Everyone here was a hunting dog.
They had taken the food their master gave them and lived well on it.
They had no choice left.
I’m no different.
A humorless laugh escaped Go Se-won.
The executives stared at him.
Then a cry rang through the enormous hall.
“The 119th floor!
The target has broken through the 119th floor!”
No one had trouble understanding what that meant.
They all knew the building they came to work in every day had 120 floors.
He’s coming.
There was no avoiding the fight.
Clad in full armor, a sword in one hand and a spear in the other, Go Se-won spoke with a heavy heart.
“Formation.
Prepare for battle.”
His quiet command reached the hundred Hunters around him.
Rumble!
KABOOM!
With a deafening roar accompanied by a tremendous vibration, one of the world’s most famous skyscrapers shook.
An uninvited guest had set foot on the top floor of an impregnable fortress no one had ever been able—or dared—to challenge.
Step.
A lone figure appeared through the rising dust.
Every hair on Go Se-won’s body seemed to stand on end.
He hurled his spear with all his strength.
Whoosh!
Screeeeeech!
Slice!
The spear hurtling toward me split apart, along with the cloud of dust.
Through the clear path White Flame had cut, I saw a middle-aged man who looked strangely familiar.
Where have I seen him?
The answer came almost at once.
At Lee Jungryong’s national funeral, a new Head of Security had stood beside Go Jun like a shadow.
This was him.
The name I had heard in passing back then was probably...
“Go Se-won.”
His eyes trembled faintly when I said it.
Maybe he was surprised I knew his name.
Maybe it was how easily I’d dealt with his spear.
Either way, I’d finally found someone who might give me a proper answer.
I asked the question I’d repeated dozens of times since entering the lobby.
“Go Jun.
Where is he?”
Before I’d finished speaking, a flash shot from Go Se-won’s hand.
Whoosh!
KABOOM!
A throwing spear missed me by a hair and buried itself in the floor, leaving a small crater.
It was a signal.
Fwish-fwish-fwish!
Go Se-won wasn’t the only one waiting on the top floor.
Roughly a hundred Ares Guild members filled the hall, every one of them worthy of being called a high-ranking Hunter.
They attacked together.
Fwoosh!
A vast surge of energy shook the hall, filling it with blue, red, and brilliant light.
Their attacks were stronger and their barrage denser than anything I’d faced on the way up.
I stepped forward alone.
Step.
My foot struck the floor, charged with internal energy, and flames rose to heat the air.
Flamefire Path.
Fwoosh!
Screeeeeech!
One step was enough.
I erased more than ten meters of distance and struck at the air with my palm.
Arrows melted before the blue-white hellfire.
Every spell flying toward me came apart.
BOOM!
Water, earth, wind, flame.
The intense heat of Scorching Yang Qi ignored even elemental affinities.
As attack spells made from all four elements burst outward, the tanks at the front swiftly raised their Tower Shields.
KABOOM!
Despite the considerable impact, the Tower Shields didn’t waver an inch.
They blocked the aftermath of the Magic without suffering the slightest damage, then tilted diagonally.
At the same moment, twenty figures sprang up, using the wall of steel as a foothold.
Pat-pat-pat!
I understood at once.
Everyone gathered here was among Ares Guild’s elite.
But the ones coming at me now were in another class.
Killing intent.
Their movements were spare and swift.
Their calm, impassive eyes had the look of practiced killers.
More than twenty weapons stabbed and slashed at the speed of light, flashing brightly.
Screeeeeech!
As they came at me from every angle, I couldn’t hold back a short laugh.
“What a load of bullshit.
You fucking morons.”
In the slowed world, I saw shock spread across their blank faces.
But it was too late to turn back.
For them and for me.
Slice!
Blue-white Force extended from White Flame’s spearhead.
The incoming weapons lost their strength, and five bodies split in two.
Having turned five bodies into ten with one strike, I drove my fist into empty air.
BOOM!
Compressed air wasn’t the only thing that burst.
A stealthily approaching assassin toppled over, headless.
By then, the chain sickle in his hand was already moving at my will.
Whoosh!
Thud!
Wielded by Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, it buried itself in another man’s neck.
His once-calm eyes flew wide.
As he began to fall, I planted my palm against his chest.
BOOM!
The force of my Flame Divine Palm wasn’t meant to finish him off.
He was already dead.
It struck the enemy behind him, who had been about to use his comrade’s body as a shield while thrusting his spear.
“Graaaaaah!”
Blood burst from the man’s seven apertures.
Before the man whose heart meridians had been severed throughout his body could even lower his head, I was already moving toward another enemy.
Crack!
My fist crushed a head.
Fwish!
Thud-thud!
Finger Qi shot through another enemy’s neck and chest.
He dropped his weapon and pressed a hand to the blood gushing from his throat.
It wasn’t enough.
“Ghk.
Guh...”
The light faded rapidly from his eyes.
I watched the last of them collapse, my gaze cold.
You brought this on yourselves.
On another day, I might have let them live.
But not today.
Not now.
As when the Black Hunters had attacked Uncle Kkeokjeong, I had no intention of stopping.
I couldn’t stop.
I have to show them here.
Make sure this never happens again.
I had been a Hunter long before I became a martial artist.
I had also been a modern man born in the twenty-first century, someone who had lived in a civilized society where reason and the law existed.
That was why I hadn’t been able to eliminate Go Jun in Sichuan.
Unlike Lee Jungryong, whom I had been able to eliminate amid chaos and destruction, Go Jun had been protected by a fence built from the two-syllable Korean term for the rule of law.
But now none of that mattered.
My choice had allowed Go Jun to live.
He had crossed a river he could never cross back.
And I—no, all of us—had lost Kim Hwajong.
I would never again see the half-gray-haired old butler who had always spoken to me with a polite, gentle smile.
That was why I had come here.
Why I had torn down the fence called the rule of law and made myself an outlaw.
Splash.
My blood-soaked footsteps sounded unnaturally loud.
A suffocating silence had settled over the vast hall.
Everyone stood frozen by the slaughter they had witnessed.
But the face I wanted wasn’t among them.
Neither was the one man who could tell me where to find him.
Go Se-won.
I turned my head to look for Go Jun’s right hand.
A faint, stealthy sound cut through the air.
Whoosh!
I turned around and slammed my hands together as though in prayer.
KABOOM!
The sharp sword blade caught between them stopped just above my forehead.
Its owner, Go Se-won, spoke calmly.
“Looking for me?”
“Yeah.”
I pressed my palms together harder.
The Sword Energy—or rather, Aura—formed from powerful mana yielded to my blue-white Force.
Unable to withstand my immense internal energy, the sword glowed red and began to melt.
Drip, drip.
Hiss!
As the molten steel struck the floor, I thrust out a hand blazing with heat.
BOOM!
One palm strike was enough.
Layer upon layer of defensive Magic shattered, and Go Se-won’s armor broke apart.
But the blow that shook him to the core didn’t bring him down.
He swallowed the blood rising in his throat and reached for my shoulder with his gauntlet.
He tried to, anyway.
Tap-tap-tap!
BOOM!
A flowing grappling technique followed seamlessly.
Another burst of heat drove Go Se-won back, and he thrust out his hand.
Fwish!
A blade sprang from between the plates of his gauntlet and grazed my chin.
I felt a sting, caught his wrist, and twisted.
Crack!
KRAK!
My grip crushed the gauntlet.
Flesh tore, exposing white bone.
The pain must have been worse than he’d imagined, but Go Se-won didn’t scream.
Pale-faced, he asked flatly,
“Is that it?”
“No.
Not yet.”
I caught his other arm.
KRAK!
He sucked in a breath.
This time the pain broke through his composure.
Blood ran between his lips, and his voice shook.
“Take it easy... and finish it.”
“That’s the plan.
After I hear where that bastard Go Jun is.”
“What if the confidentiality clause in my employment contract says I can’t?”
I gripped his collarbone.
“Then it definitely won’t end with just taking it easy.”
Go Se-won gave a weak laugh.
“You searched everywhere and still couldn’t find him.
Of course you couldn’t.”
Unfortunately, he was right.
I’d fought my way through an endless pack of hunting dogs and wrecked the inside of the building, but Go Jun had never appeared.
If there was one thing I had gained from all the information I had collected so far, it was the identity of the secret area where he was staying.
“Area A.
I think you know where it is.”
Cough.
Go Se-won spat blood.
“I picked a bad day.
I was planning to hand in my resignation soon.”
“Enough talking.
Tell me.”
“That’s easy.
But I have a condition.”
“T-Team Leader Go.
You’re not going to tell that crazy bastard—!”
There was always someone who couldn’t read the room.
The nameless executive who stepped forward soon went quiet, though.
Few people could go on talking after taking Finger Qi to the throat.
“A condition?” I asked.
“Yes.”
What he said next caught even me off guard.
“...You want me to kill you?”
Go Se-won gave a small nod.
Even as pain wracked his body, his eyes remained calm, reflecting my face.
“It’s too late to go back to how things were.
Do it cleanly.
Right here.
That’s all.”
“I think you understand.”
Breathing heavily, Go Se-won raised a trembling finger and pointed somewhere.
When I finally learned where Area A was, I stopped short.
Empty air?
It was hard to make sense of at first, but the world called things like this Magic.
Besides, I’d experienced things far stranger and more dangerous than Magic.
Where?
I stared into the empty air.
After a moment, an unfamiliar sensation stirred in my exhausted body.
What’s this?
I couldn’t see it.
But I could feel another space there, surrounded by an immense, carefully concealed energy.
It was hidden so perfectly that it could only be detected by someone who recognized its existence.
Go Se-won had kept his end of the bargain.
His lips, turning blue, began to move.
“Now kill—”
Bzzzz.
A vibration cut him off.
A smartphone slipped from the trouser pocket of the suit exposed beneath his broken armor and rolled across the floor.
Tap.
Bzzzz.
A family photo lit up its cracked screen beneath the caller’s name: Wife.
A young child and his wife smiled brightly.
Beside them stood Go Se-won, his expression stiff.
For a moment, neither of us spoke.
I looked from the photo on the cracked screen to the cracks showing in his expression.
I remembered his request to be killed.
The calm way he’d said it was too late to go back.
“Let me ask you something.”
“Why is today your last day at work?”
Go Se-won hesitated, then answered with a sigh.
“Turns out the job doesn’t suit me.
Especially... my boss is a fucking asshole.”
“Yeah.
Got it.”
Did Go Se-won know that answer had decided his fate?
I quietly drew up my internal energy.
Not toward my fist.
Toward my legs.
“You—”
KABOOM!
The rest of his words vanished beneath the roar.
I was already soaring into the empty air high above.
Fierce wind rushed past me.
I felt the strange buoyancy of being seized by invisible hands, and the unknown space that refused entry to anyone without permission.
But I was an outlaw.
I didn’t need permission.
There.
Everything had a flow.
I took a deep breath and closed my eyes.
Blue-white Force burst from the spearhead in my hand and tore through the empty air.
Swoooooosh!

chapters.title: Chapter 592
paragraphs: Whoooosh.
Red mist rose with his exhaled breath.
It was a long, slow breath—so long and slow that one might mistake him for not breathing at all. It was also a secret technique he had learned from his Master long ago.
“I’ve been watching you all this time.”
“M-Me?”
Nearly thirty years had passed, but Go Jun had never forgotten that day. It was the day he first found a dream.
He had lost his parents, been abandoned by his relatives, and drifted from one orphanage to another.
“The other children you live with are talented, too. But you’re different. You’re very special.”
The Great Cataclysm had left behind more than death and peace. It had created an enormous number of war orphans, and Go Jun was one of them.
Just one of countless war orphans. If he had remained ordinary, he would have been raised like a chicken confined to a poultry farm, then turned loose on society.
But meeting his Master, Lee Jungryong, had made him someone special.
That was the greatest reason he had stayed alone in Area A after everyone else had disappeared, waiting for the person who would soon come crashing in.
He could not flee his Master’s enemy from the place where his Master had once lived.
“...Jin Taekyung.”
Go Jun’s voice was chilling. His tightly shut eyes slowly opened, and he drew the red glow back into them. Then he instinctively reached for his neck.
Clink.
His fingers touched cold metal.

He did not even know who had originally owned this cheap necklace. Yet it had become the keepsake his Master had left him, and his most precious possession, for one reason alone: it was the only thing that had kept its shape when everything else in that place turned to ash.
Are you watching, Master?
Go Jun clenched his fist. Red qi shimmered like heat haze over the skin stretched taut across his prominent veins.
Only two months ago, Jin Taekyung had trampled him mercilessly. But things were different now.
Hatred greater than his fear, and the power he had newly acquired, had allowed Go Jun to overcome it.
I’ll kill him. Today. With my own hands.
Was it his imagination? Or a coincidence?
At that very moment, the black jewel set into the necklace gave off a strange light.
Rumble!
A tremendous vibration shook the space.
This was a place where anyone who had not been granted permission could not even become aware of its existence. Now, at last, it had allowed someone to intrude.
Countless spells and barriers that had never once been broken since their creation were collapsing even now.
“He’s here.”
Go Jun muttered quietly, released his cross-legged position, and slowly rose to his feet. Top-grade magic armor surged up around his body, wrapping around him according to his will.
Clatter-clatter-clatter!
The transformation began and ended in an instant.
By the time Go Jun stood firmly on both feet in blackened full-body armor, blue-white flames were flickering like will-o’-the-wisps at the end of the unlit corridor.
No. It was the glow in someone’s eyes.
“Jin Taekyung...!”
He spat the three syllables with hatred. The man whose name he had called answered willingly.
“Yeah. So you were here.”
Unlike the burning glow in his eyes, his voice was cold.
But Go Jun could clearly feel it—the ember hidden inside that voice. The fuse that had refused to burn while waiting for this one moment.
And then—
“Thanks.”
Fwoosh.
At last, the flame caught. A voice boiling like lava heated the dark corridor.
“For staying here all this time.”
An overwhelming energy pressed down on the space.
Rrrrmmble!
There would be no more waiting.
As the world shook, two figures became streaks of light and shot across the corridor toward each other.
The instant the blue and red streaks met—
Whoom, KABOOM!
A blinding flash and a deafening roar that seemed to split the sky erupted, coloring the entire area.
The most important thing when facing an enemy was composure. When reason grew clouded, the mind became unsettled. When the mind became unsettled, the hands and feet lost their coordination.
Maintaining composure was the surest way to win.
That rule held true in both the modern world and Murim, and I had always followed it.
But...
“Jin Taekyung.”
The moment I heard the hatred in his voice and saw that fucking face clearly beyond the dark corridor, I realized something.
Composure was no shield against anger reason could not contain.
Once that fire caught, there was no controlling it.
“Thanks.”
My eyes grew hot. I had fought my way through a 120-story skyscraper and around a thousand enemies without wavering once, but now my heart churned.
I thought of the silver-haired old butler collapsed against a snow-covered rock and continued.
“...For staying here all this time.”
I meant every word. I was sincerely grateful to Go Jun.
Because he had stayed instead of running, I could end his life with my own hands.
Rrrrmmble!
My dantian was half empty after all the internal energy I had spent, but what remained was enough. A massive wave spread out from me and shook Area A.
For this moment, I could forget the fatigue of the endless battles and the growing weight of my limbs.
I’ll kill him.
With that one thought, I stepped forward.
Flamefire Path.
Flames rose from the tips of my feet as I kicked off the ground and surged forward. They drove back the darkness that had conquered the corridor and illuminated the way.
At the far end, a figure was streaking across the corridor as a beam of light.
Go Jun.
I could see the red glow of his eyes between his clenched teeth and the helmet pulled low over his face.
The instant light flashed from the waist of the man charging toward me without hesitation, I raised White Flame’s shaft.
Whoom, KABOOM!
Two enormous energies of different colors tangled amid the roar.
The collision sent a tremendous force back through my weapon. A wave of energy slashed in every direction like a blade.
Beyond our locked weapons, I saw his red eyes. Then his voice reached me.
“You’re not much, are you? Don’t you think?”
My eyes widened despite myself.
His feet should have been knocked backward. Instead, they were planted firmly in the ground.
And that was not the only thing I had failed to anticipate.
Crunch. Crrrunch.

An unbelievable pressure traveled up White Flame’s shaft. An enormous power, large enough that it would not have been strange for it to explode at any moment, continued to flow out and wrap around the sword blade.
Slowly, but without stopping, it continued to grow in size and crushed White Flame’s shaft.
What is this?
I had never faced Force this immense—or rather, an Aura Blade of this magnitude.
At the sight of me frozen there, Go Jun’s eyes filled with delight.
“You should’ve put that stupid head of yours to work and wondered why I stayed.”
Before I could finish, the Aura Blade surrounding his sword swelled outward as if it had exploded.
Craaaack, KABOOM!
A roar left my ears ringing. A powerful shock swept through my body, and a red flash filled my vision as I flew backward.
Before I could fully feel the wind rushing past my ears, my back struck a solid marble wall.
KRAK!
The layers of defensive Magic surrounding it scattered, and the whole wall caved in.
I was embedded in the exact center of the wall, leaving behind a crater large enough for three or four people to stand inside. I blinked.
My vision trembled from the impact to my head. Through it, I saw Go Jun charging at me with his teeth bared.
“I’ll kill you.”
Whoooooosh!
He moved faster than he spoke. His sword cut diagonally down through the air, sending out a burst of red light.
Then, in the next instant, a crescent-shaped Aura Blade that had crossed dozens of meters came rushing right up to my face.
Slice! KRAAAAAASH!
I escaped by a hair.
My aching body moved on instinct, carrying me clear of the attack. Looking at the space the Aura Blade had shredded, I thought:
What if I’d tried to block that head-on?
The answer was easy enough.
I was more exhausted than I had realized.

Suppressing two Monster Waves had made me bear the full aftermath of One Annihilation. Then, from the moment I entered Ares Guild, I had fought while holding back enough to avoid killing most of my opponents.
Facing an attack like that head-on in my current condition would not have ended well.
“Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung.”
Go Jun hummed my name like a tune, then grinned.
“You should see your face. You’re no hero. You’re just a rat. You’ll die crying and begging for your life.”
I watched him approach, his voice almost cheerful. Then a thought struck me.
“Did you take something?”
“What?”
“No, wait. In this case, should I call it a Magic Gem instead of drugs?”
At that moment, the smile on Go Jun’s lips faded.
I no longer needed an answer. His face had given me one.
“Hah.”
I let out a small, hollow laugh.
The rage that had paralyzed my mind and body for a moment began to fade, and only then was I finally able to see the cold reality in front of me.
“Of course. That’s how you did it.”
“Seeing someone in a new light” and “improving by leaps and bounds” were just four-character idioms. At least when it came to martial arts.
Martial strength had to be honed through training and real combat.
Even with the System, I could not have grown stronger at that rate. Go Jun certainly could not have done it.
No one became this strong in only two months.
There had only ever been one answer.
“You juiced up. You really did. You fucking idiot.”
I couldn’t hold back my laughter.
It wasn’t amusement. It was disgust. Go Jun had chosen to give up being human and become a monster, and the sheer stupidity of it kept making me laugh.

“Fuck, I’ve never seen an idiot like you. You couldn’t beat me any normal way, so you started sucking down Magic Gems? If you were going to do that, why not go to Magic Johnson? I bet that guy would’ve taken real good care of you with his magic wand.”
I had hit a nerve. Go Jun’s face went rigid, and his already-red eyes darkened further.
“Shut your fucking—”
“Just shut up and listen, you son of a bitch.”
Thud. Thud.
Rubble and chunks of marble fell away as I got up.
I cracked my stiff neck from side to side and stared at him.

“What? You set off a few Monster Waves with an S-grade Magic Gem and pissed yourself over how well it worked? Watched people die because you barely lifted a finger and thought you were a god? No, sir, you fucking moron. You’re just a monster. At best, you’re some idiot side character with a Named Monster for a constellation.”
“Shut up!”
“Fuck off. Want me to give it a title, too? Go Jun Swallows an S-Grade Magic Gem.”
“Jin Taekyuuung—!”
Fwoooooosh!
A gale rose with a tremendous wave of energy and swept through the area.
But I calmly answered as I watched that unprecedented power swell until it looked ready to burst.
“What, you fucking idiot?”
I had never been afraid. Now that I knew what he had become, I had no reason to hesitate.
He was a monster who had crossed the line, and he had to die by my hand today.
For the old butler who had fallen into a darkness from which he would never return. For the people and Hunters who had died in the Monster Waves.
And... for me, furious at this goddamned reality.
“You have to die.”
I bit out the words with all my heart. Go Jun’s blood-red figure blurred.
Whoooooosh! KABOOM!
The red Aura Blade stopped above my head.
The tremendous pressure transmitted through White Flame’s spearhead made my wrists throb, and my ankles sank deep into the ground.
But I did not give way. At least the power I wielded had been built through countless hours of training and insight, with the good fortune of the System added on top.
“Get lost, you drugged-up bastard.”
Rrrrmmble!
I grinned as I looked into Go Jun’s wide-open eyes, then thrust my fist forward with all my strength.
Wham!

sentences.text: Whoooosh.
Red mist rose with his exhaled breath.
It was a long, slow breath—so long and slow that one might mistake him for not breathing at all.
It was also a secret technique he had learned from his Master long ago.
“I’ve been watching you all this time.”
“M-Me?”
Nearly thirty years had passed, but Go Jun had never forgotten that day.
It was the day he first found a dream.
He had lost his parents, been abandoned by his relatives, and drifted from one orphanage to another.
“The other children you live with are talented, too.
But you’re different.
You’re very special.”
The Great Cataclysm had left behind more than death and peace.
It had created an enormous number of war orphans, and Go Jun was one of them.
Just one of countless war orphans.
If he had remained ordinary, he would have been raised like a chicken confined to a poultry farm, then turned loose on society.
But meeting his Master, Lee Jungryong, had made him someone special.
That was the greatest reason he had stayed alone in Area A after everyone else had disappeared, waiting for the person who would soon come crashing in.
He could not flee his Master’s enemy from the place where his Master had once lived.
“...Jin Taekyung.”
Go Jun’s voice was chilling.
His tightly shut eyes slowly opened, and he drew the red glow back into them.
Then he instinctively reached for his neck.
Clink.
His fingers touched cold metal.
He did not even know who had originally owned this cheap necklace.

Yet it had become the keepsake his Master had left him, and his most precious possession, for one reason alone: it was the only thing that had kept its shape when everything else in that place turned to ash.
Are you watching, Master?
Go Jun clenched his fist.
Red qi shimmered like heat haze over the skin stretched taut across his prominent veins.
Only two months ago, Jin Taekyung had trampled him mercilessly.
But things were different now.
Hatred greater than his fear, and the power he had newly acquired, had allowed Go Jun to overcome it.
I’ll kill him.
Today.
With my own hands.
Was it his imagination?
Or a coincidence?
At that very moment, the black jewel set into the necklace gave off a strange light.
Rumble!
A tremendous vibration shook the space.
This was a place where anyone who had not been granted permission could not even become aware of its existence.
Now, at last, it had allowed someone to intrude.
Countless spells and barriers that had never once been broken since their creation were collapsing even now.
“He’s here.”
Go Jun muttered quietly, released his cross-legged position, and slowly rose to his feet.
Top-grade magic armor surged up around his body, wrapping around him according to his will.
Clatter-clatter-clatter!
The transformation began and ended in an instant.
By the time Go Jun stood firmly on both feet in blackened full-body armor, blue-white flames were flickering like will-o’-the-wisps at the end of the unlit corridor.
No.
It was the glow in someone’s eyes.
“Jin Taekyung...!”
He spat the three syllables with hatred.
The man whose name he had called answered willingly.
“Yeah.
So you were here.”
Unlike the burning glow in his eyes, his voice was cold.
But Go Jun could clearly feel it—the ember hidden inside that voice.
The fuse that had refused to burn while waiting for this one moment.
And then—
“Thanks.”
Fwoosh.
At last, the flame caught.
A voice boiling like lava heated the dark corridor.
“For staying here all this time.”
An overwhelming energy pressed down on the space.
Rrrrmmble!
There would be no more waiting.
As the world shook, two figures became streaks of light and shot across the corridor toward each other.
The instant the blue and red streaks met—
Whoom, KABOOM!
A blinding flash and a deafening roar that seemed to split the sky erupted, coloring the entire area.
The most important thing when facing an enemy was composure.
When reason grew clouded, the mind became unsettled.
When the mind became unsettled, the hands and feet lost their coordination.
Maintaining composure was the surest way to win.
That rule held true in both the modern world and Murim, and I had always followed it.
But...
“Jin Taekyung.”
The moment I heard the hatred in his voice and saw that fucking face clearly beyond the dark corridor, I realized something.
Composure was no shield against anger reason could not contain.
Once that fire caught, there was no controlling it.
“Thanks.”
My eyes grew hot.
I had fought my way through a 120-story skyscraper and around a thousand enemies without wavering once, but now my heart churned.
I thought of the silver-haired old butler collapsed against a snow-covered rock and continued.
“...For staying here all this time.”
I meant every word.
I was sincerely grateful to Go Jun.
Because he had stayed instead of running, I could end his life with my own hands.
Rrrrmmble!
My dantian was half empty after all the internal energy I had spent, but what remained was enough.
A massive wave spread out from me and shook Area A.
For this moment, I could forget the fatigue of the endless battles and the growing weight of my limbs.
I’ll kill him.
With that one thought, I stepped forward.
Flamefire Path.
Flames rose from the tips of my feet as I kicked off the ground and surged forward.
They drove back the darkness that had conquered the corridor and illuminated the way.
At the far end, a figure was streaking across the corridor as a beam of light.
Go Jun.
I could see the red glow of his eyes between his clenched teeth and the helmet pulled low over his face.
The instant light flashed from the waist of the man charging toward me without hesitation, I raised White Flame’s shaft.
Whoom, KABOOM!
Two enormous energies of different colors tangled amid the roar.
The collision sent a tremendous force back through my weapon.
A wave of energy slashed in every direction like a blade.
Beyond our locked weapons, I saw his red eyes.
Then his voice reached me.
“You’re not much, are you?
Don’t you think?”
My eyes widened despite myself.
His feet should have been knocked backward.
Instead, they were planted firmly in the ground.
And that was not the only thing I had failed to anticipate.
Crunch.
Crrrunch.
An unbelievable pressure traveled up White Flame’s shaft.
An enormous power, large enough that it would not have been strange for it to explode at any moment, continued to flow out and wrap around the sword blade.
Slowly, but without stopping, it continued to grow in size and crushed White Flame’s shaft.
What is this?
I had never faced Force this immense—or rather, an Aura Blade of this magnitude.
At the sight of me frozen there, Go Jun’s eyes filled with delight.
“You should’ve put that stupid head of yours to work and wondered why I stayed.”
Before I could finish, the Aura Blade surrounding his sword swelled outward as if it had exploded.
Craaaack, KABOOM!
A roar left my ears ringing.
A powerful shock swept through my body, and a red flash filled my vision as I flew backward.
Before I could fully feel the wind rushing past my ears, my back struck a solid marble wall.
KRAK!
The layers of defensive Magic surrounding it scattered, and the whole wall caved in.
I was embedded in the exact center of the wall, leaving behind a crater large enough for three or four people to stand inside.
I blinked.
My vision trembled from the impact to my head.
Through it, I saw Go Jun charging at me with his teeth bared.
“I’ll kill you.”
Whoooooosh!
He moved faster than he spoke.
His sword cut diagonally down through the air, sending out a burst of red light.
Then, in the next instant, a crescent-shaped Aura Blade that had crossed dozens of meters came rushing right up to my face.
Slice!
KRAAAAAASH!
I escaped by a hair.
My aching body moved on instinct, carrying me clear of the attack.
Looking at the space the Aura Blade had shredded, I thought:
What if I’d tried to block that head-on?
The answer was easy enough.
I was more exhausted than I had realized.
Suppressing two Monster Waves had made me bear the full aftermath of One Annihilation.
Then, from the moment I entered Ares Guild, I had fought while holding back enough to avoid killing most of my opponents.
Facing an attack like that head-on in my current condition would not have ended well.
“Jin Taekyung.
Jin Taekyung.
Jin Taekyung.”
Go Jun hummed my name like a tune, then grinned.
“You should see your face.
You’re no hero.
You’re just a rat.
You’ll die crying and begging for your life.”
I watched him approach, his voice almost cheerful.
Then a thought struck me.
“Did you take something?”
“What?”
“No, wait.
In this case, should I call it a Magic Gem instead of drugs?”
At that moment, the smile on Go Jun’s lips faded.
I no longer needed an answer.
His face had given me one.
“Hah.”
I let out a small, hollow laugh.
The rage that had paralyzed my mind and body for a moment began to fade, and only then was I finally able to see the cold reality in front of me.
“Of course.
That’s how you did it.”
“Seeing someone in a new light” and “improving by leaps and bounds” were just four-character idioms.
At least when it came to martial arts.
Martial strength had to be honed through training and real combat.
Even with the System, I could not have grown stronger at that rate.
Go Jun certainly could not have done it.
No one became this strong in only two months.
There had only ever been one answer.
“You juiced up.
You really did.
You fucking idiot.”
I couldn’t hold back my laughter.
It wasn’t amusement.
It was disgust.
Go Jun had chosen to give up being human and become a monster, and the sheer stupidity of it kept making me laugh.
“Fuck, I’ve never seen an idiot like you.
You couldn’t beat me any normal way, so you started sucking down Magic Gems?
If you were going to do that, why not go to Magic Johnson?
I bet that guy would’ve taken real good care of you with his magic wand.”
I had hit a nerve.
Go Jun’s face went rigid, and his already-red eyes darkened further.
“Shut your fucking—”
“Just shut up and listen, you son of a bitch.”
Thud.
Thud.
Rubble and chunks of marble fell away as I got up.
I cracked my stiff neck from side to side and stared at him.
“What?
You set off a few Monster Waves with an S-grade Magic Gem and pissed yourself over how well it worked?
Watched people die because you barely lifted a finger and thought you were a god?
No, sir, you fucking moron.
You’re just a monster.
At best, you’re some idiot side character with a Named Monster for a constellation.”
“Shut up!”
“Fuck off.
Want me to give it a title, too?
Go Jun Swallows an S-Grade Magic Gem.”
“Jin Taekyuuung—!”
Fwoooooosh!
A gale rose with a tremendous wave of energy and swept through the area.
But I calmly answered as I watched that unprecedented power swell until it looked ready to burst.
“What, you fucking idiot?”
I had never been afraid.
Now that I knew what he had become, I had no reason to hesitate.
He was a monster who had crossed the line, and he had to die by my hand today.
For the old butler who had fallen into a darkness from which he would never return.
For the people and Hunters who had died in the Monster Waves.
And... for me, furious at this goddamned reality.
“You have to die.”
I bit out the words with all my heart.
Go Jun’s blood-red figure blurred.
Whoooooosh!
KABOOM!
The red Aura Blade stopped above my head.
The tremendous pressure transmitted through White Flame’s spearhead made my wrists throb, and my ankles sank deep into the ground.
But I did not give way.
At least the power I wielded had been built through countless hours of training and insight, with the good fortune of the System added on top.
“Get lost, you drugged-up bastard.”
Rrrrmmble!
I grinned as I looked into Go Jun’s wide-open eyes, then thrust my fist forward with all my strength.
Wham!

chapters.title: Chapter 593
paragraphs: Wham!
My fist slammed into Go Jun’s chest with a dull thud.
The layers of defensive Magic shattered at once, and part of his sturdy full-body armor caved inward. He gritted his teeth and roared.
“Jin Taekyung!”
That punch would have left most high-level Hunters or Peak masters with severe Internal Injury, unable to fight.
But Go Jun was different. Perhaps it was the Magic Gem’s influence, but even my Inner-Family Heavy Hand had failed to do much damage.
An S-rank Hunter. And more.

Whatever else had happened, he was already a recognized S-rank Hunter. He had learned an internal cultivation technique—what the modern world called a mana cultivation technique—and absorbed the energy of an S-grade Magic Gem from a Named Monster. His strength was immense.
“Die!”
Whoooooom! KABOOM!
The energy had gone beyond red. Now the color of blood, it burst outward like an explosion.
White Flame’s shaft trembled under the mountain of pressure bearing down from the enormous Aura Blade.
I haven’t been pushed this hard in a long time.
Right now, even three jiazi of internal energy and physical abilities beyond human limits felt inadequate.
Maybe it was the fatigue I’d built up over the course of the day. Or maybe Go Jun had absorbed that much magical power.
One thing was certain: this idiot had gained far more strength than I’d expected.
Rrrrrumble. Crack!
The tremendous pressure drove me and the ground beneath me downward. By the time I was buried up to my ankles, Go Jun was baring his teeth in a grin.
“Starting to get it? Hmm? Finally feel like you’re fucked?”
He gave a low laugh.
He was enjoying this. He thought he was finally going to avenge his Master.
“Ever since the day my Master died, I’ve killed you every night. Over and over. I’ve lived for a moment like this.”
I watched for an opening as I answered.
“No wonder I felt like I’d been born again every morning. I thought I was just waking up refreshed from dreaming about Jungryong dying every night.”
Fwoosh!
The instant his blood-red energy wavered, I yanked my foot free and kicked upward.
Boom!
My toes, swinging like a beam of light, were blocked by his shin with a thunderous crash. Go Jun, who had been about to pour out his anger, let out a hollow laugh.
“It’s too late to struggle. Now that it’s come to this, killing the rest of them will be easy.”
“What?”
I blinked, not quite understanding him. Then his quiet voice reached my ear.

“You and that goddamned Peace Guild. Your parents and that bitch of a little sister waiting at home... Ah. Your father’s already dead, isn’t he? Doesn’t matter. If he were still alive, he’d be following his son to the grave soon enough.”
“Did you like having the world call you a hero? Think you’d all live happily ever after? It’s bullshit. Kim Hwajong, that old man, was only the beginning.”
His sticky, unpleasant breath touched my face. He cackled.

“This time it’s you, then Choi Minwoo. After that, I don’t care who it is. I’ll kill everyone with even the slightest connection to you, one by one. Sweeping them all away with a Monster Wave sounds good, too. What do you think?”
I stared at him, blinking as he went on.
What the fuck is this bastard saying?
It was strange. The thing in front of me looked human, but all that came out of its mouth was the sound of a dog barking.
Here stood a monster in a human shell.
He’s going to kill them? All my people?
I felt sick.
Go Jun could make good on those words. I hated that he could. And when I pictured the people I couldn’t live without lying dead, my mind went blank.
Mother. Hayeon. Team Leader Choi. Uncle Kkeokjeong, Song Song, Jinho hyung...
Their faces flashed before my eyes, one after another. So did the graying old butler who had died on the snow-covered mountain.
He’s going to kill them all, and he wants to know what I think?
My answer came out calm.
“Fine. I understand.”
“What?”
“Go ahead. Try it.”
The smile on Go Jun’s face faded. I drew on every bit of strength I had.
Grrrrrkk.
The spear, slowly sinking under the pressure, stopped. So did my bending knees.
For that moment, I forgot my fatigue. My muscles still ached as though they might tear from the lingering aftermath of One Annihilation, but I forgot the pain, too.
The anger layered over my fatigue and pain covered and paralyzed everything else.
Internal energy boiled like lava through my Eight Extraordinary Meridians and hundreds of acupoints.
When I spoke, my voice burned.
“You shouldn’t have said that.”
“You shouldn’t have talked about my people that way. At the very least, you shouldn’t have.”
I’d suspected it. Go Jun was capable of doing exactly what he’d threatened.
But suspecting it myself and hearing it directly from his mouth were entirely different matters.
“Don’t you think, you inhuman piece of shit?”
Go Jun was a monster. Whether he’d always been one or I’d made him into one no longer mattered.
He had to die for my people to live. And they had to live for me to live.
Grrrrrrkk!
I hauled my foot out of the ground and straightened my knee.
Putting my back and arms into it, I drove the spear shaft up against the Aura Blade’s pressure.
Slowly. Little by little. Without stopping.
“How are you...?”
As Go Jun’s eyes widened, I whispered a command in my mind.
Inventory open. Store White Flame.
Pop.
It happened in an instant.
The spear and the blue-white flames holding back the enormous Aura Blade vanished. With nothing opposing it, the blood-red energy plunged straight down.
Whoooooom! Slice!
It cleaved through the space where I’d stood. But I was already gone.
Dozens of hairs, severed by the sword pressure, scattered past my shoulder. My fist was already deep inside Go Jun’s guard, wreathed in blue-white hellfire.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
The world slowed. Space warped in the ultra-high temperature heat. It looked almost like the expression Go Jun was making now.
“No—”
Too late.
I answered without a sound and threw my punch.
Fwoosh! KABOOM!
The impact drowned out the rest of his cry. My fist burned through the air and struck his solar plexus, sending him flying like a cannonball.
I launched myself after him.
Whoooooosh!
Wind rushed past my ears.
In less than an instant, I covered more than ten meters and overtook him. As he hurtled toward me, I clasped my hands together and brought them down like a hammer.
CRASH! KRAKAKAK!
The blow struck his abdomen. Already battered, the upper half of his armor melted under the Scorching Yang Qi.
Go Jun hit the ground on his back and smashed through it. Blood erupted from his mouth.
Pshhh!
I moved to drive my fist into him while he was down, but the blood he spat drenched me.
My vision turned red. I faltered for a fraction of a second, and my senses screamed a warning.
Danger!
He hadn’t spat blood by accident. It was part of his attack.
I kicked off the ground the instant I realized it. Red energy shot toward me as I retreated.
Shhk! Slice!
Heat seared my side.
I’d moved as fast as I could, but the Aura surging from the sword Go Jun had never let go of was too large to evade completely.
Drip. Drip-drip.
I pressed a hand to my bleeding side and wiped the blood from my eyes.
Go Jun was already on his feet and charging, his helmet discarded.
His furious shout rang through the devastated corridor.
“You fucking bastard!”
Whoooooosh!
Blood-red Aura burst from the tip of his sword and tore through the air.
I narrowly avoided it with a series of backward steps, then flung both arms out.
With the Magic only I could use.
Inventory open. Summon.
Shhk-shhk-shhk!
A moment ago, my hands had been empty. Now dagger handles met my palms, and the blades flew from my grasp.
Streaks of light shot toward Go Jun. He hurriedly turned his sword sideways, holding the blade across his front.
Clang-clang-clang-clang!
Four daggers bounced off it and lodged in the walls and ceiling. I drew up my internal energy and sent it into my legs. Flames rose from the foot I set forward.
Flamefire Path.
Fwoosh! Whoooooosh!
I became a streak of flame racing toward Go Jun. Seeing me charge without my spear, he roared.
“I’ll kill you!”
His eyes were blood-red now, their glow bright in the darkness.
Then an energy unlike anything he’d unleashed before burst from his body and swept in every direction.
WHOOOOOOOOOM!
It was a raging storm, a fog with no way out. Far from tiring, he was giving off an even stronger wave of energy.
I kept going, shooting through that murky, violent fog of magical power.
Go Jun charged through it toward me.
Zzzzzzzzz!
His Aura Blade, an absurd two meters long, came cleaving through the air.
Each time I twisted aside to avoid it, the sword pressure carving up the space around me tore my skin and drew blood.
That was fine. As long as I didn’t fall.
As long as I could bring him down, make him pay for Kim Hwajong’s death, and protect everyone still alive from another threat.
Slice!
A burning pain swept across my chest.
My clothes and armor had long since been torn away in the fight. A thin line appeared on my bare skin, then reddened.
Fwoosh!
Blood spurted from my chest. The cut was shallow, but the immense energy forcing its way through it made my vision swim.
I steadied myself and kicked off the ground.
Boom!
I shot forward, leaving the crash behind me. At the end of my path stood a monster who had chosen to stop being human.
“Jin Taekyuuung!”
Go Jun charged with his sword held upright. The Aura Blade around it had turned a murky, dark red.
The closer I got, the more clearly I felt that sticky, unpleasant energy.
That isn’t mana anymore.
The world had another name for energy so corrupted and ominous, the opposite of pure mana.
Magical power.
The moment the words came to mind, I knew I had to use everything I had.
Go Jun and me. Me and Go Jun.
We were close enough to kill each other now.
I could see the fury in his eyes and smell the stench on his hot breath.
And then...
We extended our arms almost at the same time.
Shhk!
The world slowed to a crawl. The wind split, and space vanished between us.
Faint delight spread across Go Jun’s face as he thrust his sword toward my chest.
I’ve won.
That was what his eyes seemed to say.
I was empty-handed. His sword was wrapped in murky magical power, with strength and reach on its side. Of course he thought he’d won.
He was wrong.
Inventory open. Summon.
Thought was faster than light, and the System answered without hesitation.
White Flame appeared in my hand as though it had been there all along.
Blue-white hellfire coated its transparent spearhead.
Fwoosh!
The searing heat burned through the air.
The spear had started after Go Jun’s sword, yet it slipped past the murky Aura Blade and reached its target first.
Squelch!
Flesh parted with a sickening sound, followed by the smell of it burning.
Go Jun’s eyes bulged. There was no delight left in them.
He stared down at the spear piercing his chest, shock and pain filling his eyes, and forced out a few words.
“What... is this?”
I answered calmly.
“Striking Second, Hitting First. You got your strength from a Magic Gem. You wouldn’t understand it even if you died and came back.”
Every fight, every movement, had a flow.
Know your opponent’s movement, predict it, and you could reach your target first even if you started later.
Training and experience had taught me the principle of Striking Second, Hitting First. Go Jun had pursued nothing but greater power.
That was what decided this fight.
“Idiot. You should’ve used that rock of a head at least once to think about why your dead Master never recommended Magic Gems to you in the first place.”
At the anger and disgust in my voice, Go Jun’s eyes trembled as if he’d accepted his fate.
Then the sword that had fallen short of me shot upward like lightning.
Shing!
It happened in an instant. Murky energy—much smaller than before—gathered at its tip and thrust toward my heart.
A fraction of an instant earlier, I’d spoken another command in my mind.
Inventory open. Summon.
KRAK!
The concentrated energy, with all its destructive force and cutting power, struck an obstacle.
Go Jun’s eyes widened again. Reflected in them was armor with a faint red glow.
Fire Dragon Armor.
“What, what is this...?”
“What do you think, idiot? Life insurance.”
I’d kept Fire Dragon Armor hidden all the way to the top floor, even after taking that shallow cut across my chest, for a moment just like this.
And I’d been right.
“You... What the hell are you...?”
I looked into his frightened eyes.
The eyes of a human—no, a monster—driven to the edge.
Then I drove the spear deeper into Go Jun’s chest.
KRAK!
