“You shouldn’t have talked about my people that way.
At the very least, you shouldn’t have.”
I’d suspected it.
Go Jun was capable of doing exactly what he’d threatened.
But suspecting it myself and hearing it directly from his mouth were entirely different matters.
“Don’t you think, you inhuman piece of shit?”
Go Jun was a monster.
Whether he’d always been one or I’d made him into one no longer mattered.
He had to die for my people to live.
And they had to live for me to live.
Grrrrrrkk!
I hauled my foot out of the ground and straightened my knee.
Putting my back and arms into it, I drove the spear shaft up against the Aura Blade’s pressure.
Slowly.
Little by little.
Without stopping.
“How are you...?”
As Go Jun’s eyes widened, I whispered a command in my mind.
Inventory open.
Store White Flame.
Pop.
It happened in an instant.
The spear and the blue-white flames holding back the enormous Aura Blade vanished.
With nothing opposing it, the blood-red energy plunged straight down.
Whoooooom!
Slice!
It cleaved through the space where I’d stood.
But I was already gone.
Dozens of hairs, severed by the sword pressure, scattered past my shoulder.
My fist was already deep inside Go Jun’s guard, wreathed in blue-white hellfire.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
The world slowed.
Space warped in the ultra-high temperature heat.
It looked almost like the expression Go Jun was making now.
“No—”
Too late.
I answered without a sound and threw my punch.
Fwoosh!
KABOOM!
The impact drowned out the rest of his cry.
My fist burned through the air and struck his solar plexus, sending him flying like a cannonball.
I launched myself after him.
Whoooooosh!
Wind rushed past my ears.
In less than an instant, I covered more than ten meters and overtook him.
As he hurtled toward me, I clasped my hands together and brought them down like a hammer.
CRASH!
KRAKAKAK!
The blow struck his abdomen.
Already battered, the upper half of his armor melted under the Scorching Yang Qi.
Go Jun hit the ground on his back and smashed through it.
Blood erupted from his mouth.
Pshhh!
I moved to drive my fist into him while he was down, but the blood he spat drenched me.
My vision turned red.
I faltered for a fraction of a second, and my senses screamed a warning.
Danger!
He hadn’t spat blood by accident.
It was part of his attack.
I kicked off the ground the instant I realized it.
Red energy shot toward me as I retreated.
Shhk!
Slice!
Heat seared my side.
I’d moved as fast as I could, but the Aura surging from the sword Go Jun had never let go of was too large to evade completely.
Drip.
Drip-drip.
I pressed a hand to my bleeding side and wiped the blood from my eyes.
Go Jun was already on his feet and charging, his helmet discarded.
His furious shout rang through the devastated corridor.
“You fucking bastard!”
Whoooooosh!
Blood-red Aura burst from the tip of his sword and tore through the air.
I narrowly avoided it with a series of backward steps, then flung both arms out.
With the Magic only I could use.
Inventory open.
Summon.
Shhk-shhk-shhk!
A moment ago, my hands had been empty.
Now dagger handles met my palms, and the blades flew from my grasp.
Streaks of light shot toward Go Jun.
He hurriedly turned his sword sideways, holding the blade across his front.
Clang-clang-clang-clang!
Four daggers bounced off it and lodged in the walls and ceiling.
I drew up my internal energy and sent it into my legs.
Flames rose from the foot I set forward.
Flamefire Path.
Fwoosh!
Whoooooosh!
I became a streak of flame racing toward Go Jun.
Seeing me charge without my spear, he roared.
“I’ll kill you!”
His eyes were blood-red now, their glow bright in the darkness.
Then an energy unlike anything he’d unleashed before burst from his body and swept in every direction.
WHOOOOOOOOOM!
It was a raging storm, a fog with no way out.
Far from tiring, he was giving off an even stronger wave of energy.
I kept going, shooting through that murky, violent fog of magical power.
Go Jun charged through it toward me.
Zzzzzzzzz!
His Aura Blade, an absurd two meters long, came cleaving through the air.
Each time I twisted aside to avoid it, the sword pressure carving up the space around me tore my skin and drew blood.
That was fine.
As long as I didn’t fall.
As long as I could bring him down, make him pay for Kim Hwajong’s death, and protect everyone still alive from another threat.
Slice!
A burning pain swept across my chest.
My clothes and armor had long since been torn away in the fight.
A thin line appeared on my bare skin, then reddened.
Fwoosh!
Blood spurted from my chest.
The cut was shallow, but the immense energy forcing its way through it made my vision swim.
I steadied myself and kicked off the ground.
Boom!
I shot forward, leaving the crash behind me.
At the end of my path stood a monster who had chosen to stop being human.
“Jin Taekyuuung!”
Go Jun charged with his sword held upright.
The Aura Blade around it had turned a murky, dark red.
The closer I got, the more clearly I felt that sticky, unpleasant energy.
That isn’t mana anymore.
The world had another name for energy so corrupted and ominous, the opposite of pure mana.
Magical power.
The moment the words came to mind, I knew I had to use everything I had.
Go Jun and me.
Me and Go Jun.
We were close enough to kill each other now.
I could see the fury in his eyes and smell the stench on his hot breath.
And then...
We extended our arms almost at the same time.
Shhk!
The world slowed to a crawl.
The wind split, and space vanished between us.
Faint delight spread across Go Jun’s face as he thrust his sword toward my chest.
I’ve won.
That was what his eyes seemed to say.
I was empty-handed.
His sword was wrapped in murky magical power, with strength and reach on its side.
Of course he thought he’d won.
He was wrong.
Inventory open.
Summon.
Thought was faster than light, and the System answered without hesitation.
White Flame appeared in my hand as though it had been there all along.
Blue-white hellfire coated its transparent spearhead.
Fwoosh!
The searing heat burned through the air.
The spear had started after Go Jun’s sword, yet it slipped past the murky Aura Blade and reached its target first.
Squelch!
Flesh parted with a sickening sound, followed by the smell of it burning.
Go Jun’s eyes bulged.
There was no delight left in them.
He stared down at the spear piercing his chest, shock and pain filling his eyes, and forced out a few words.
“What... is this?”
I answered calmly.
“Striking Second, Hitting First.
You got your strength from a Magic Gem.
You wouldn’t understand it even if you died and came back.”
Every fight, every movement, had a flow.
Know your opponent’s movement, predict it, and you could reach your target first even if you started later.
Training and experience had taught me the principle of Striking Second, Hitting First.
Go Jun had pursued nothing but greater power.
That was what decided this fight.
“Idiot.
You should’ve used that rock of a head at least once to think about why your dead Master never recommended Magic Gems to you in the first place.”
At the anger and disgust in my voice, Go Jun’s eyes trembled as if he’d accepted his fate.
Then the sword that had fallen short of me shot upward like lightning.
Shing!
It happened in an instant.
Murky energy—much smaller than before—gathered at its tip and thrust toward my heart.
A fraction of an instant earlier, I’d spoken another command in my mind.
Inventory open.
Summon.
KRAK!
The concentrated energy, with all its destructive force and cutting power, struck an obstacle.
Go Jun’s eyes widened again.
Reflected in them was armor with a faint red glow.
Fire Dragon Armor.
“What, what is this...?”
“What do you think, idiot?
Life insurance.”
I’d kept Fire Dragon Armor hidden all the way to the top floor, even after taking that shallow cut across my chest, for a moment just like this.
And I’d been right.
“You...
What the hell are you...?”
I looked into his frightened eyes.
The eyes of a human—no, a monster—driven to the edge.
Then I drove the spear deeper into Go Jun’s chest.
KRAK!

chapters.title: Chapter 594
paragraphs: Crack!
The grisly sound came with a sensation I had felt hundreds—thousands—of times before, traveling up through my fingertips.
Flesh splitting. Bone breaking.
Somewhere along the way, I had grown used to it. Sometimes that left a bitter taste in my mouth. Being used to it meant I had taken that many lives with my own hands.
But not this time. As I looked down at the dying man, I felt no bitterness at all.
A final groan escaped with a deflating sound. At the same time, the solidly built man dropped to his knees.
Thud.
The blood-red glow in his eyes, once chilling to look at, slowly faded. His whole body trembled before the death closing in on him.
No. Perhaps it wasn’t death itself that Go Jun feared. Perhaps it was me, the one who had dealt it to him.
“J-Jin Taekyung.”
His voice was fading, and so was the light in his eyes. I felt no pity.
He wasn’t human like me. He was a monster.

The Peace Guild had lost Kim Hwajong today. Thousands of people whose names I would never know had lost family and friends they loved. For the madness Go Jun had caused, this death almost seemed too easy.
“Cough. I-I can’t die like this...”
I looked down coldly at him as he knelt there, convulsing in pain.
“Die. Oxygen is wasted on a piece of shit like you.”
I had no intention of listening to a long-winded final speech, or giving him the chance to make one. I wrenched White Flame from his chest.
Fwoosh!
The moment the transparent spearhead came free, the blood that had not yet evaporated sprayed out like a fountain.
Go Jun stared blankly up at me, a fist-sized hole in his chest. Then his body slowly tipped over.
Splash.
That was the end. His face fell into a pool of his own blood, and he stopped moving, eyes still wide open.
As I looked at the monster’s corpse, with no breath or trace of life left in it, a thought came to me.
It’s over.
Lee Jungryong’s loyal Disciple of several decades—the man who had effectively ruled Ares Guild, one of the foremost Guilds in the world—had died by my hand.
He had deliberately caused two Monster Waves, leaving thousands dead or injured and costing Kim Hwajong and some twenty Peace Guild members their lives. He had paid for it with his own.
So this really is the end...
Then why did I feel so hollow? I had taken my revenge, yet it felt as though the hole was in my chest, not Go Jun’s.
It was probably because I knew that the people who had left my side would never return.
Are you still cold? Is it still dark?
I turned away, asking questions that could never reach them.
Fatigue and drowsiness weighed on me more heavily than I could have imagined. I fought them off and slowly crossed the dark corridor, wrecked by our battle.
Step.
With every step, faces and memories rose before my eyes and obscured my vision.

I saw Gwangan Bridge collapsing. I heard people screaming in terror. A family photograph dangling from a car’s rearview mirror brought back a promise I had made long ago, pinkies linked with someone I missed more than words could say.
“When Hayeon gets a little older, and you, Taekyung, start middle school, let’s come see the sea again. All right?”
“Really?”
“Of course. Come on, pinky promise.”
But today, the place from the promise I had kept deep in my heart had collapsed.
Innocent people had died, and monsters had spread like a plague. I had done everything I could, but I hadn’t saved more of them.
Step.
My thoughts were as unsteady as my feet. Through the confusion, a warm voice echoed in my mind.
“It wasn’t your fault.”
“You did your best.”
The graying old butler who had comforted me even as he died had gone somewhere he could never return from.

I had no way of knowing whether it was night or day where he had arrived. Whether it was cold or warm. I could only hope that his world was a little brighter. That he, who had shivered in the cold, was somewhere warmer.
And... that he had believed my lie to the very end—the lie that the person he had wanted to see one last time had come.
Step.
There is no process without a result. Someone had to pay the price. I believed it was only natural to be punished for doing wrong.
That was why I had come here. I had thrown open the gates of a palace no one had dared approach and brought down an impregnable fortress.
I had fought, and fought, and fought again. And after finally killing the monster wearing a human face, I suddenly felt hollow inside and found myself wondering:
What am I supposed to do now?
I had thought that killing Go Jun, the cause of it all, would ease my anger, even a little. I had thought I might laugh out loud with relief.
But that wasn’t what happened.
With one gesture, I could make a massive pit and fill it again. But I couldn’t fill the empty place in my heart.
It had been the same three years ago. It was the same now.
Damn it.
My mouth tasted bitter. In the end, the wounds were left for those of us still here to bear.
I almost regretted giving Go Jun such a painless death.
Step.
I stopped.
At some point, an inexplicable sense that something was wrong had taken hold of me. A chill crept up my spine.
What is this feeling?
Was it the exhaustion? Or everything weighing on my mind? My thoughts were as murky as fog.
I stood there for a moment. Then I realized what was wrong.
Go Jun should be dead. So why...
Why hadn’t the System window announcing the kill appeared?
I had driven a spearhead into the center of his chest and burned his organs. I had watched his face fall into the pool of blood and felt him stop breathing.
“Don’t tell me.”
I muttered the words and turned around. An unusually deep darkness had settled over the ruined corridor.
The System was absolute, and it was immediate.
I knew that better than anyone. I simply had not noticed anything strange because I had been overwhelmed by exhaustion and deep thoughts in the moment of victory.
So when I found the pool of blood empty, I was not especially surprised.
He’s alive. Go Jun is alive.
That much was certain. What I wanted to know was how.

There had been only two of us in Area A: Go Jun and me. He had been dead. His heart had stopped, and he had stopped breathing. Even a half-body bath in top-grade potion could not have brought him back.
Then how?
I followed the traces he had left behind.
Area A was a maze, fitting for a secret zone open to only a handful of people. But the trail of blood led in one direction, and it was easy enough to follow.
I moved quickly, taking in what I saw.
No one helped him. He didn’t have time to cover his tracks, either.
The marks told me he had been desperate. I could almost see him crawling alone, pressed flat against the floor, struggling to keep going.
And then...
He got to his feet. Right here.
Two clear footprints stood out in the blood. Countless handprints marked the wall beside them.
What had happened to him? Why had he been writhing in pain?
Before long, I found the answer.
That’s...
Blood.
Not the bright red of human blood. Drops of monster blood tinged blue.
There was no mistaking what that meant. I stared at the monster blood on my hand, then shot forward.
Whoosh!
The wind rushed past me, carrying a strong scent of blood and a foul stench. Even through my exhaustion, I could sense someone drawing closer.
Then I entered another corridor and saw him with my own eyes.
He looked nothing like he had the last time I saw him.
“Go Jun.”
My quiet voice echoed down the corridor. Go Jun—or rather, the monster—turned as he staggered along.
“Krrk. Kurruk.”
Whatever he was trying to say came out as a metallic rasp. Compared with the rest of him, that was nothing.

He stood four meters tall. His arms and legs were grotesquely swollen, as if they might burst. His body looked like creatures of different species had been thrown together, each part bearing its own shape and features.
Only his face had kept anything like its original form: a human face half-covered in scales, with blood-red eyes shining between them.
“Jin... Taekyung. Karruk.”
Fear and hatred mingled in his eyes as he looked at me. I took in the sight of him from head to toe and spoke with disgust.
“Did you want to live that badly? Even if it meant becoming a monster?”
“Shut... up. This... this wasn’t what I wanted either—”
Crack! KRAK!
It happened in an instant.
Before he could finish, his right arm suddenly bent as if an invisible hand had twisted it. Blue blood burst from the break.
“GRAAAAH!”
As he screamed, his grotesque body began changing rapidly.
Shlk. Crackle!
The thick skin covered in hide and scales like a monster’s began to heal, while his crushed joints fitted themselves back together like puzzle pieces.
“Hah. Hah.”
Go Jun panted, still in pain. Watching him, I began to understand how he had made it this far.
“Troll. Right?”
His eyelids trembled at the question. I had my answer.
Trolls had extraordinary regenerative abilities. The Named Monster that had originally owned the S-grade Magic Gem Go Jun had absorbed must have been an immensely powerful Troll.
And...
The S-grade Magic Gem he absorbed wasn’t the only one, was it?
One look at him was enough to tell me. His swollen body and incredible regeneration were Troll traits, but the scales and hide covering half of him had come from another monster.
Mutation. That’s what he’s become.
Unlike mana, magical power was dark and turbid. It corrupted humans. After absorbing two S-grade Magic Gems packed with it, of course the forces inside him would clash.
“Kurruk. I could have been stronger. Stronger than this. But you. You...”
I cut him off.
“Not stronger. You would’ve become an even more horrifying monster. Look at yourself.”
“You’re worse than a monster. You’re no Hunter, no human—just a monster. That’s what you are.”
Step.
I moved toward him. Go Jun stared at me, eyes wide, and shouted as though he were screaming.
“Don’t come closer! Krrk! Stay away!”
“That’s a problem. There’s a monster right in front of me.”
“T-This can’t be!”
His blood-red eyes filled with fear.
He must have known it, too. His body was showing signs of falling apart while he stood still. There was no way he could fight me in that condition.
Tap-tap-tap!
When Go Jun turned and ran, I wasn’t surprised. I reversed my grip on White Flame’s shaft and hurled it.
SHWAAAAK! BOOM!
A streak of flame-wreathed light burst through his legs and buried itself in the ground. He screamed and thrashed, both legs gone, while flesh and bone rapidly grew from the severed ends.
I wasn’t going to stand there and watch.
“Go on. Regenerate. Keep doing it as long as you can.”
Thud!
Drawing up the internal energy I had left, I rushed him. I planted my foot on his back, grabbed both of his thick arms, and pulled.
Crack. KRAKAKAK!
Go Jun lost both arms after his legs, and his scream rang through the corridor.
I didn’t blink. I kept moving.
Slice! Stab!

I pulled the spear from the ground and slashed and stabbed his body in several places. I seared the sections trying to regenerate with the Flame Divine Palm, then gripped them tightly and tore them apart.
Under ordinary circumstances, I would never have done anything so brutal. Now I did not hesitate.
KRAKAKAK!
Regeneration. Destruction. Again and again.
Go Jun was the first to give out under the endless pain.
“GRAAAAH! S-Stop!”
His voice was hoarse, and his eyes were not as red as before. His regeneration had been slowing for some time. Now it had stopped altogether.
“Now... kill me...”
“I was going to.”
This time, I would make sure he could never come back.
I looked into his eyes.
“Whether you’re going to heaven or hell, go on ahead and wait for me. When I get there, I’ll kill you to my heart’s content.”
Those were the last words Go Jun heard in this world.
It ends now.
I did not wait for an answer. Without a moment’s hesitation, I brought the transparent spearhead down.
Slice! Thud!
His head came free with a sharp cutting sound and rolled across the floor.
That was the end of the monster who had become neither a hero like Cheon Taemin nor an ambitious warlord like his Master, Lee Jungryong.
Ding.
The familiar chime rang in my ears. I picked up Go Jun’s head from the pool of blood and crossed the space where I alone remained, my steps slow and unsteady.
I was tired.

The Named Monster that had originally owned the S-grade Magic Gem Go Jun had absorbed must have been an immensely powerful Troll.
And...
The S-grade Magic Gem he absorbed wasn’t the only one, was it?
One look at him was enough to tell me.
His swollen body and incredible regeneration were Troll traits, but the scales and hide covering half of him had come from another monster.
Mutation.
That’s what he’s become.
Unlike mana, magical power was dark and turbid.
It corrupted humans.
After absorbing two S-grade Magic Gems packed with it, of course the forces inside him would clash.
“Kurruk.
I could have been stronger.
Stronger than this.
But you.
You...”
I cut him off.
“Not stronger.
You would’ve become an even more horrifying monster.
Look at yourself.”
“You’re worse than a monster.
You’re no Hunter, no human—just a monster.
That’s what you are.”
Step.
I moved toward him.
Go Jun stared at me, eyes wide, and shouted as though he were screaming.
“Don’t come closer!
Krrk!
Stay away!”
“That’s a problem.
There’s a monster right in front of me.”
“T-This can’t be!”
His blood-red eyes filled with fear.
He must have known it, too.
His body was showing signs of falling apart while he stood still.
There was no way he could fight me in that condition.
Tap-tap-tap!
When Go Jun turned and ran, I wasn’t surprised.
I reversed my grip on White Flame’s shaft and hurled it.
SHWAAAAK!
BOOM!
A streak of flame-wreathed light burst through his legs and buried itself in the ground.
He screamed and thrashed, both legs gone, while flesh and bone rapidly grew from the severed ends.
I wasn’t going to stand there and watch.
“Go on.
Regenerate.
Keep doing it as long as you can.”
Thud!
Drawing up the internal energy I had left, I rushed him.
I planted my foot on his back, grabbed both of his thick arms, and pulled.
Crack.
KRAKAKAK!
Go Jun lost both arms after his legs, and his scream rang through the corridor.
I didn’t blink.
I kept moving.
Slice!
Stab!
I pulled the spear from the ground and slashed and stabbed his body in several places.
I seared the sections trying to regenerate with the Flame Divine Palm, then gripped them tightly and tore them apart.
Under ordinary circumstances, I would never have done anything so brutal.
Now I did not hesitate.
KRAKAKAK!
Regeneration.
Destruction.
Again and again.
Go Jun was the first to give out under the endless pain.
“GRAAAAH!
S-Stop!”
His voice was hoarse, and his eyes were not as red as before.
His regeneration had been slowing for some time.
Now it had stopped altogether.
“Now... kill me...”
“I was going to.”
This time, I would make sure he could never come back.
I looked into his eyes.
“Whether you’re going to heaven or hell, go on ahead and wait for me.
When I get there, I’ll kill you to my heart’s content.”
Those were the last words Go Jun heard in this world.
It ends now.
I did not wait for an answer.
Without a moment’s hesitation, I brought the transparent spearhead down.
Slice!
Thud!
His head came free with a sharp cutting sound and rolled across the floor.
That was the end of the monster who had become neither a hero like Cheon Taemin nor an ambitious warlord like his Master, Lee Jungryong.
Ding.
The familiar chime rang in my ears.
I picked up Go Jun’s head from the pool of blood and crossed the space where I alone remained, my steps slow and unsteady.
I was tired.

chapters.title: Chapter 595
paragraphs: Unlike the way in, the journey back was long and hard.
Exhaustion made my body feel like waterlogged cotton, and my eyelids kept falling shut.
I want to collapse right here.
But I couldn’t. I still had somewhere to go. First, though, I had to drive off the hyenas who had caught the scent of trouble and gathered in front of me.
Quite a crowd.
I staggered out of Area A and looked around through half-closed eyes.
I was back in the spacious hall on the top floor. Around two hundred Ares Guild members waited there, their faces tense.
Then I spotted a familiar face at the front and sighed.
“Maybe I should’ve just killed you.”
The middle-aged man at the front, Head of Security Go Se-won, answered in a calm voice after hearing my mutter.
“Yes. That wouldn’t have been a bad choice either.”
He looked fully recovered. He must have received treatment while I was gone. Gazing at the sword in his hand, he went on.

“It must have been thirty years ago when I first picked up a sword. I was trained even before I awakened. And on the day I awakened as an A-rank Hunter, the former Vice Guild Master gave me this sword as a gift. The other members of the security team probably received theirs the same way.”
That didn’t surprise me. Team Leader Choi had told me Lee Jungryong took in war orphans after the Great Cataclysm and trained them as his personal guards according to their mana affinity.
The man in front of me was one of them.
“So, are you going to avenge that grudge now?”
“...That grudge.”
Go Se-won murmured the words, then asked, “Before that, tell me one thing. Why did you spare me?”
I thought for a moment.
“I figured you should at least get to answer the phone.”
“What?”

“You should at least have told your family you were working late. Or that you weren’t coming home. My father couldn’t do either. I thought he’d come home when the time came, but... he never did. Now I can barely remember his voice.”
Maybe I was tired. I’d said more than I needed to. I clicked my tongue, and Go Se-won studied me for a moment before asking, “What about the Vice Guild Master?”
Instead of answering, I shrugged. It had been a fight that could only end with one of us dead. But I was the only one who had appeared.
“He’s dead, then,” Go Se-won muttered.
“Go up and check. It’s quite a sight.”
The Ares Guild members surrounding us stirred at once. Several executives who were plainly loyalists urged Go Se-won on through clenched teeth.
“Team Leader Go, what are you waiting for?”
“Eliminate him immediately!”

“I’ve already told you. Kill Jin Taekyung, and we won’t hold you responsible for revealing Area A’s location. The Guild will reward you handsomely, too. You could even put yourself forward for the next Vice Guild Master.”
Anger and temptation mingled in their voices.
As Go Se-won stood silently among them, I rubbed my stiff, tired eyes and spoke.
“I’m exhausted. If you’re done asking questions, let’s get this over with. I’ve got somewhere to be.”
His sharp gaze traveled over me.
“Even someone like you seems to be having a hard time in your current condition.”
“That’s my problem, not yours.”
“...Fair enough.”
Go Se-won replied quietly. Then, just as his fingers toyed with the hilt of his sword—
Whoosh! Slice!
Blood sprayed. One of the executives fell, eyes wide at the unexpected strike. It was the man who had just offered Go Se-won the Vice Guild Master position.
“You crazy—!”
“What the hell are you doing?”
“T-Team Leader Go!”
As the executives shouted, Go Se-won turned the area into chaos in a single instant and spoke in an even voice.
“Subdue them all. The fight is over.”

The executives here had plenty to lose. The other Guild members didn’t. They had no direct ties to Go Jun and no reason to take a needless risk—especially against a monster who had wrecked Ares Guild headquarters single-handedly.
Clatter-clatter-clang!
Weapons were leveled from every direction the moment Go Se-won spoke. Realizing they had no chance, the loyalist executives lowered their own with a groan.
Go Se-won turned to me. “That was quick enough, wasn’t it?”
I was about to say something, but then I nodded.
“Looks like sparing you paid off.”
“Thirty years,” he said. “That’s how long I’ve lived as a hunting dog. I’ve done enough.”
“A late change of heart?”
“I don’t know. I’m not that good a man. But it doesn’t matter anymore. It’s been more than I could bear for a while now.”
Apparently, I wasn’t the only one who was tired. Go Se-won surveyed the chaos with weary eyes, then stepped aside.
“Go. No one will stop you.”
I didn’t refuse and began walking. Just as I was about to pass by Go Se-won, a quiet murmur reached my ears.
“...Thank you for the call.”
That was enough. I gave him a small nod and walked past him and the two hundred or so Ares Guild members.
Step. Step.
I dragged my exhausted body onward, walking and walking. I had to meet someone before sunset.
I don’t remember how I reached my destination. Only fragments remain.
The troops surrounding the devastated Ares Guild headquarters. Combat drones filling the sky.
President Baek Hanseong’s rigid face as he arrived under heavy guard, despite his aides’ attempts to stop him.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, what in the world...?”
He couldn’t finish. I offered to surrender peacefully on one condition, and after giving it some thought, President Baek agreed to my request.
That was why I was here.
“Hey, you!”
“T-Taekyung!”
Familiar faces approached through my blurred vision. I wanted to smile and wave, but my body wouldn’t cooperate.
My legs buckled. Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong hurried to catch me.
“Sorry. My legs gave out.”
“How can you say that right now...?”
Song Song pressed her lips together before she could finish. She rubbed at her reddened eyes.
“What about my family?” I asked. “They’re not here, are they?”
“Are you insane?”

“I sent Guild members to bring them somewhere safe,” she continued, her voice hoarse. “Luckily, your mother was in the middle of cooking and didn’t know anything. Hayeon, who’s with her... is pretending she doesn’t know.”
Relief washed over me. I couldn’t imagine how badly the news about me would have shaken my mother.
Hayeon was there, though. She’d handle it. She had always been more thoughtful than I was.
“And Team Leader Choi is safe,” Song Song added. “He still hasn’t regained consciousness.”
“Thanks. For looking after him.”
Song Song was looking at me with a complicated expression when Im Kkeokjeong’s shoulders began to shake.
“I’m sorry, Taekyung. I’m so sorry...”
What did he have to be sorry for? Why was he so sad?
I wanted to answer his sobs, but my throat closed up. I knew exactly how he felt. The helplessness and guilt of being unable to do a thing—there were no words for it.
Song Song had turned away, too. Tears slipped down her cheeks.
Damn it.
I clenched my teeth and tried to ignore the heat in my eyes. Then I managed to force out a question.
“What about him... Butler Kim?”
“He’s been waiting. All this time.”
The answer came from neither Im Kkeokjeong nor Song Song. I turned my head and saw a blond foreigner standing in front of a door.
“So you’ve come, wicked human.”
The Skeleton King’s voice sounded far away. I had seen the sign before I saw his face.
Morgue
My heart sank. As I stood frozen, the Skeleton King opened the door.
And through the gap in the open door... I saw the body of a person covered in a pure white sheet.
“It is impolite to keep the dead waiting, human.”
“Do you intend to send him off like this?”
At those words, I left Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong behind and forced my unmoving feet forward.
The door closed quietly behind me. In the chill of the morgue, it was only him and me. Just the two of us.
Swish.
With trembling hands, I drew back the white sheet.
Kim Hwajong had died with a faint smile on his face.
He looked as though he were having a pleasant dream. But I knew that dream would never end.
He would never again greet me in a pressed suit, smiling gently. He would never again get up early and offer me coffee.
Today, he had said goodbye to us. Now we had to let him go.
Drip. Drop.
Something hot rolled down both my cheeks. They were the first tears I had shed today, and tears I must never shed again.
I swear.
It felt like being taken back three years. Regret came with a vow.
I’m sorry. I won’t let anyone else go the way you did.
So please...
“Rest in peace.”
With those quiet, heartfelt words, I took Go Jun’s head out of my Inventory and set it on the floor.
So the monster who had died with his eyes wide open might understand what he had done. So Kim Hwajong might rest a little easier.
It was the promise I had made to myself while holding the old butler’s hand as it slowly grew cold on the snow-covered mountain.
Fwoosh.
As if in answer, Kim Hwajong’s face flushed red. Violet sunset light streamed through the morgue window.
I gazed at its beauty through blurred eyes and felt the strength leave my body.
Ah.
I had reached my limit, body and heart alike.
I leaned my back against the wall and sank down as if collapsing. Accepting the sleep pressing down on me with a weight greater than Taishan, I thought:
Today was a long day.
Click.
The firmly shut door opened with a faint sound.

A slender beauty, a middle-aged man who looked like a bandit, and a blond foreigner who might have stepped out of a magazine saw the severed head first and startled. Then they saw the peaceful face of the dead man and felt sorrow. Last, they saw the young man asleep where he had collapsed, and fell silent.
Jin Taekyung.
Indescribable emotions filled the three pairs of eyes gazing at him.
What more could they say?
Today, he had fought desperately against disaster and threats. He had made himself an outlaw and exacted the price for an innocent death.
There was only one thing they could do for him now.
Sleep well. Don’t worry about what comes next.
The fire would spread in every direction. No one knew where it would die down.
Even if the whole world condemned him for what had happened today—even if the authorities branded him a criminal—they would stand beside Jin Taekyung.
They would protect him, no matter what.
Just as you did for us.
Warm sunset light spread through the morgue.
One person’s long day had ended, but the day of the other three had not. No—in fact, they were about to become even busier.

chapters.title: Chapter 596
paragraphs: Just because the sun had set and the second hand had passed midnight didn’t mean the day was over.
As long as people were awake and there was an interesting story to follow, their day went on.
That was how it happened on a bitterly cold, windy afternoon in mid-January.
[Breaking News] S-Rank Hunter Jin Taekyung Launches Solo Assault on Ares Guild Headquarters
The breaking news threw Korea into an uproar. No—the entire world was shaken.
Almost as soon as it broke, posts and comments flooded websites everywhere.

└ Hey, what is this? └ What is? └ I got a sudden alert and checked it out, and... holy shit, Lord Fuck supposedly stormed Ares Guild headquarters alone? └ ??? └ ??? └ Quit talking bullshit, lol. I was watching the news just now, and they were looking for Lord Fuck because he disappeared from Pyeongchang. So why is he suddenly storming Ares Guild headquarters— └ Fuck, it’s real. What the hell is this?

└ ?? What is this, The Truman Show? You’re not doing this to fool newbies like me, are you? └ If it were The Truman Show, at least the ratings would be good. Why would we bother fooling you? It’s real. Turn on WBS—they’ve got an exclusive report. The Capital Defense Command has been dispatched and everything’s going crazy; └ Why would the fire department be involved? └ Not the fire department. The Capital Defense Command;

└ I get that Lord Sibu-leol went to Ares Guild headquarters, but isn’t saying he “stormed the place” a bit much? Maybe he went to have tea with Go Jun. └ Probably not. There were more than a thousand witnesses, and apparently Jin Taekyung punched the Ares headquarters building right in the solar plexus before going inside. Even if he went for tea, I bet every teacup in there got smashed. └ Got proof? If more than a thousand people saw it, someone must’ve taken a video. Post a link. └ The thousand witnesses part is real, but apparently nobody took a video or even a picture. They said they only came to their senses after Lord Fuck went inside. Before that, they just watched like they were possessed. └ ?? Lol. That many people and not one piece of evidence? Sounds like a false report. └ Yeah. Why would Lord Fuck go there after disappearing for a while? Even if he did go, the rest sounds like rumors. Feels like the media’s using rumors as kindling.
Immediately after the media began broadcasting the breaking news on a massive scale, most people refused to believe the shocking report.
A hero who had put down two monster waves in succession and then vanished had supposedly stormed Ares Guild, of all places, alone. It made no sense.

But within minutes, Jongno was designated a temporary disaster zone. Hunters and troops from the Capital Defense Command began evacuating civilians and establishing a defensive line, and the mood changed completely.

└ I think this might actually be real. └ Damn, what the hell is going on? └ Why all of a sudden... └ I’m living in the United States. They’re broadcasting breaking news here, too. Every major news program, including CNN and FOX, is monitoring the situation. └ Seems like it’s the same all over the world, not just the United States. Korea and the foreign media are both going crazy;
Everyone who heard the news, at home and abroad, felt the atmosphere grow heavy.
President Baek Hanseong delivered an emergency letter concerning the current situation to the media, while experts in every field busied themselves analyzing the situation and its causes.
But before a complete answer could be found, the person at the center and beginning of everything revealed himself.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
President Baek Hanseong stepped forward despite his aides’ attempts to stop him. At his call, the young man raised his head. Cameras carried both their faces across Korea and around the world.
Jin Taekyung. It was him.
Red and blue blood—human and monster—covered him from head to toe. He looked exhausted, and his eyes held a sadness no one could name.
His voice came out bleakly through dry, cracked lips.
“I... only did what I had to do.”
That was all the people staring at the screen, having forgotten even how to breathe, were allowed to see.
The live broadcast was cut off immediately at the Blue House’s request. For some reason, reporters from around the world who had been at the scene said nothing more.
At the end of that day, one enormous question remained.
Jin Taekyung and Ares Guild. Ares Guild and Jin Taekyung.
An unprecedented clash between one man and an organization.

No one could say for certain what had happened inside. But the effects of a battle lasting roughly an hour had swept through Jongno, and Jin Taekyung had walked out on his own two feet to stand before them all.
Two names with enormous influence in Korea and across the world had collided for reasons unknown. The individual had won.
That was shocking enough when the organization in question was Ares Guild. But what everyone wanted to know most was why.
Why had a man in his twenties, newly established as both a powerful Hunter and a young hero, gone to Ares Guild alone?
That night, a major news outlet broke the guidelines agreed upon in advance and set fire to the powder keg.
[Exclusive Report] Hunter Go Jun (Current Ares Vice Guild Master) and 25 Others Confirmed Dead; Total Casualties Around 500
[Chief Editorial Writer Lee Kanghee—Jin Taekyung: The Hero’s Hidden Side. The Devil’s Face.]
It was a bombshell.
Two monster waves unlike anything seen since the Great Cataclysm had struck in succession. Before the shock of them could fade, this new explosion shook everything again.
The whole of Korea boiled like a furnace beneath a bed of charcoal, and the heat spread throughout the world.
Midnight passed. The hours before dawn wore on. Still, the uproar showed no sign of subsiding.
The barrage, once begun, seemed as if it would never end.
Some condemned Jin Taekyung as a devil. Others submitted formal petitions demanding that he be executed.
But not everyone pointed a finger at him. In fact, most people still held a mixture of belief and doubt.
The belief that Jin Taekyung, who had accomplished so much, couldn’t possibly have done such a thing.
The suspicion that media reports without an official announcement were nothing more than nonsense.
Those unbelievable hours passed, and morning came.
[Close Aide of the Late Hunter Go Jun, a Mr. Go, Turns Himself In]
[Official Blue House Press Conference at 10:00 a.m. Draws Worldwide Attention]
Then came a downpour that dampened the fierce flames of condemnation.
And through the rain that fell without pause for two full days—from the media and from the sky—one person finally woke.
Drip. Drip-drip-drip.
At the sudden sound of rain, I blinked blankly.
As my vision cleared, the first thing I saw was an ornate, magnificent painting.
I knew that ceiling. I knew the painting. I’d heard about it so many times that it would have been strange not to recognize it.
Michelangelo’s The Creation (The Genesis).
Only then did I realize I was lying in Team Leader Choi’s mansion.
I turned my head. Raindrops tapped against the window that took up an entire wall.
No way.
A single thought flashed through my empty mind, and my heart began pounding violently.
What if—against all odds—it had all been a nightmare? What if nothing had happened yet, and I had only just left Henan and logged out?
The absurd hope burst like a bubble a moment later.
“You’re awake. I’d just come to check on you. I’m glad.”
A smooth, low voice. Younger than Butler Kim’s, and impossible to read.
How had I failed to notice him until now?
I clenched my teeth when I saw the face of the unwelcome guest who had broken through my deep thoughts and approached me.
President Baek Hanseong.
It was him.
And if the President was here instead of at the Blue House, then everything that had happened was real.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung?”
What more was there to say? I felt hollow.
Instead of answering, I sank back into the bed from where I’d half risen.
He pulled a chair close and spoke with concern.
“You still seem unwell. The doctor will be here soon, so please wait just a moment...”
I didn’t need a doctor or a Healer. Perhaps because I had gotten such deep rest, my body had completely recovered. My physical condition was not what mattered right now.
“How long... how long has it been?”
“Hmm.”
President Baek Hanseong paused at the sound of my hoarse voice, then held out the newspaper in his hand.
“This morning’s paper. It’ll be quicker if you see for yourself.”
I took it and checked the date first.
Two days had passed since the day I remembered. An enormous photograph of my face covered the front page, accompanied by a bold headline.
The Truth of That Day, Sullied by Countless Misunderstandings. The Hero Who Has Not Awakened.
I could tell from the headline alone. It told me how much the media had talked about me and about what had happened that day over the past two days.
But I felt neither irritation nor anger. Only a heavy, numbing sadness.
So it was true. It really was true.
Butler Kim—Kim Hwajong—was dead.
Weighed down by that reality, I stared blankly out the window. President Baek Hanseong spoke carefully.

“One news outlet acted rashly and broke the agreed guidelines, so public opinion was against you at first... Fortunately, the misunderstandings about this incident have been cleared up. Go Se-won stepped forward at just the right time. Thanks to him, matters were resolved sooner than we expected.”
“Go Se-won?”
I turned from the window at the unexpected name. President Baek Hanseong met my eyes and nodded.
“Yes, the same Go Se-won you know. The closest aide who served as Head of Security for the Vice Guild Master—no, for the late Go Jun.”
“He turned himself in first. The executives from Go Jun’s faction who resisted until the end had already been subdued by him. His testimony was very conclusive as well.”
When I’d spared him, I hadn’t expected this kind of help.
I looked at the newspaper again. My face wasn’t the only one on the front page.

Halfway down was a photograph of Go Se-won before a crowd of cameras and microphones, wearing his usual calm expression. Beside it was his testimony that Go Jun had caused the two monster waves two days earlier.
“It was decisive testimony. And furthermore...”
President Baek Hanseong frowned before continuing.
“It also corroborated the evidence concerning Go Jun’s body, which had been discovered earlier.”
Go Jun had died as a hideous blend of human and monster. His corpse alone was clear physical evidence.
President Baek Hanseong shuddered, as though he had seen the scene with his own eyes, and continued.
“Go Se-won played a very important role. Thanks to him, Hunter Jin Taekyung was able to clear himself of most of the charges.”
I nodded, feeling nothing.
Charges. Judgment under the law. Words everyone feared, but right now they meant little to me.
“I see.”
“Yes. He’s being held in a special detention center for now... but he’s asked to see you as soon as possible. He says he has a debt to repay.”
A debt to repay.
I repeated the words to myself and shook my head.
I had no objection to seeing Go Se-won, but something more important was on my mind.
Butler Kim. And Team Leader Choi.
Had the old butler’s funeral begun? Had Team Leader Choi regained consciousness?
That was what I wanted to know most.
I was just about to part my dry lips when the door flew open without a knock.
A blond foreigner ignored President Baek Hanseong entirely and spoke with a grave expression.
“That human. No—he’s awake.”

sentences.text: Just because the sun had set and the second hand had passed midnight didn’t mean the day was over.
As long as people were awake and there was an interesting story to follow, their day went on.
That was how it happened on a bitterly cold, windy afternoon in mid-January.

└ Hey, what is this? └ What is? └ I got a sudden alert and checked it out, and... holy shit, Lord Fuck supposedly stormed Ares Guild headquarters alone? └ ??? └ ??? └ Quit talking bullshit, lol.
I was watching the news just now, and they were looking for Lord Fuck because he disappeared from Pyeongchang.
So why is he suddenly storming Ares Guild headquarters— └ Fuck, it’s real.
What the hell is this?
What is this, The Truman Show?
You’re not doing this to fool newbies like me, are you? └ If it were The Truman Show, at least the ratings would be good.
Why would we bother fooling you?
It’s real.
Turn on WBS—they’ve got an exclusive report.
The Capital Defense Command has been dispatched and everything’s going crazy; └ Why would the fire department be involved? └ Not the fire department.
The Capital Defense Command;
└ I get that Lord Sibu-leol went to Ares Guild headquarters, but isn’t saying he “stormed the place” a bit much?
Maybe he went to have tea with Go Jun. └ Probably not.
There were more than a thousand witnesses, and apparently Jin Taekyung punched the Ares headquarters building right in the solar plexus before going inside.
Even if he went for tea, I bet every teacup in there got smashed. └ Got proof?
If more than a thousand people saw it, someone must’ve taken a video.
Post a link. └ The thousand witnesses part is real, but apparently nobody took a video or even a picture.
They said they only came to their senses after Lord Fuck went inside.
Before that, they just watched like they were possessed. └ ??
Lol.
That many people and not one piece of evidence?
Sounds like a false report. └ Yeah.
Why would Lord Fuck go there after disappearing for a while?
Even if he did go, the rest sounds like rumors.
Feels like the media’s using rumors as kindling.
Immediately after the media began broadcasting the breaking news on a massive scale, most people refused to believe the shocking report.
A hero who had put down two monster waves in succession and then vanished had supposedly stormed Ares Guild, of all places, alone.
It made no sense.

Hunters and troops from the Capital Defense Command began evacuating civilians and establishing a defensive line, and the mood changed completely.
└ I think this might actually be real. └ Damn, what the hell is going on? └ Why all of a sudden... └ I’m living in the United States.
They’re broadcasting breaking news here, too.
Every major news program, including CNN and FOX, is monitoring the situation. └ Seems like it’s the same all over the world, not just the United States.
Korea and the foreign media are both going crazy;
Everyone who heard the news, at home and abroad, felt the atmosphere grow heavy.
President Baek Hanseong delivered an emergency letter concerning the current situation to the media, while experts in every field busied themselves analyzing the situation and its causes.
But before a complete answer could be found, the person at the center and beginning of everything revealed himself.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
President Baek Hanseong stepped forward despite his aides’ attempts to stop him.
At his call, the young man raised his head.
Cameras carried both their faces across Korea and around the world.
Jin Taekyung.
It was him.
Red and blue blood—human and monster—covered him from head to toe.
He looked exhausted, and his eyes held a sadness no one could name.
His voice came out bleakly through dry, cracked lips.
“I... only did what I had to do.”
That was all the people staring at the screen, having forgotten even how to breathe, were allowed to see.
The live broadcast was cut off immediately at the Blue House’s request.
For some reason, reporters from around the world who had been at the scene said nothing more.
At the end of that day, one enormous question remained.
Jin Taekyung and Ares Guild.
Ares Guild and Jin Taekyung.
An unprecedented clash between one man and an organization.

chapters.title: Chapter 597
paragraphs: The path I had walked until now had been strewn with countless deaths and screams.
But I could say with certainty that I had never felt grief as quiet and suffocating as this.
Tap. Tap-tap.
Beyond the silence, wind and rain battered the window.
We had said everything we needed to say long ago, yet silence still filled the room where only the two of us remained.
Team Leader Choi had been staring out the window with his head turned away. At last, he spoke.
“I think I was seven when Butler Kim came to me.”
His memories of those early years had grown hazy. More than twenty years had passed since then.
The child who had suddenly lost his parents had grown into a young man, and frost had settled in the butler’s hair.
“I can barely remember my parents’ voices anymore, but every memory I have with him is vivid.”
When his parents died and even his only maternal grandfather disappeared, Butler Kim had always been there beside him.
“One day, I realized how much he had devoted to me. More than I could ever measure. But...”
His voice trailed off, and he turned toward me.
Perhaps it was because he had spent so long looking out at the rain, but his eyes were drenched when they met mine.
“Now I can’t give anything back. Not ever.”
Tap. Tap-tap.
I had never seen him like this.
A tear rolled down his cheek as he spoke in a heavy, subdued voice. It fell onto the snow-white blanket.
No. That was the wind and rain striking the window. For now, I chose to believe it was.
“Mr. Jin.”
I nodded instead of answering.
Team Leader Choi had spent more time with Butler Kim than anyone. The grief I’d felt earlier was nothing beside what he must be feeling now.
He’d lost family.
To Team Leader Choi, Kim Hwajong hadn’t been a butler. He had been family—the one person who stayed beside a child left alone, the only person that child could lean on.
He could blame me for failing to save him. He could grab me by the collar and curse me out.
Right now, that would be fine. Better to let it all spill out than keep forcing it down. I didn’t want Team Leader Choi drowning in everything he was holding back.
Then his next words caught me off guard.
“Thank you.”
“For watching over his final moments. For doing what I couldn’t... I sincerely thank you.”
I couldn’t speak. I wanted to answer, but something rising inside me had locked my throat shut.
I stared at Team Leader Choi in silence for a long time before finally forcing out my voice.
“Team Leader Choi.”
Before I could say more, he shook his head slightly.
“I’m all right. Really.”
It was an obvious lie. I knew it was, and I had no choice but to let him tell it.
I pressed my lips together. Team Leader Choi gave me a faint smile.
“I’m embarrassed you had to see me like this. Would you mind giving me some time alone?”
What could I say to him now? I had neither the words nor the right.
Team Leader Choi needed time. Time to accept the death of someone who had been as close as blood. Time to find the courage to face his body.
“Get some rest, then. There are people standing by, so call if you need anything.”
I tried to sound cheerful as I got up and headed for the door. But when I put my hand on the doorknob, I thought of one last thing I wanted to tell him.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“It’s all right to lose your balance sometimes. You can cry out loud. No one will hear you. Except for him.”
“I’ll be going now.”
My back was already turned, so I couldn’t see his expression or know how my words had struck him.
I was glad I couldn’t.
Click.
As I stepped out and pulled the door shut, I heard a faint sob through the narrowing gap.
It was the quietest, saddest sob I had ever heard. The sound of a man who had never wavered, no matter what happened, finally breaking down.
“Taekyung, how’s Team Leader Choi—”
I wasn’t the only one who could hear him.
Im Kkeokjeong had started to ask with a worried look on his face, but he fell silent. So did the other two waiting with him in the hall.
“Ah, I’m tired. I need some coffee.”

Song Song stretched and walked away quickly. The Skeleton King caught my eye, scratched his chin, and said, “This body could use some coffee too. I haven’t been sleeping lately. I feel like I might collapse...”
“Huh? Oh. Yeah, me too.”
Im Kkeokjeong was one thing, but an undead monster claiming he was sleepy and needed coffee? I let out a quiet laugh at the ridiculous excuse and patted the Skeleton King’s shoulder.
“Make me a cup too.”
“You wretched human. Have you no hands? No feet?”
“I have a spear.”
The Skeleton King fell silent for a moment at my answer, then narrowed his eyes.
“...Black?”
“Mix.”
“You don’t even know what good coffee tastes like. I’ll make it for you this once. Just this once.”
By the time Im Kkeokjeong had left the hallway after the Skeleton King, who continued grumbling curses under his breath, the sound of dress shoes echoed from the distance.
Step. Step.
Three men in black suits came into view.
Their steady breathing and measured steps told me they were well-trained Peak masters—or rather, A-rank Hunters.
But the fact that they had entered this mansion at all meant they were no ordinary Hunters. They belonged to an organization very different from a Guild.
“Pleased to meet you, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
Instead of answering, I looked at them. More precisely, at their tie pins.
Each black-and-gold badge bore a rose of Sharon and tiny engraved letters.
President’s Security Service
It was clear whose orders they were following.
I gave a small nod. “President Baek Hanseong is looking for me?”

“No, sir,” the officer in front replied in a stiff, military tone. “His Excellency left thirty minutes ago. He asked for your understanding. Affairs of state required him to leave without saying goodbye.”
He must have gone while I was in Team Leader Choi’s room. I understood his situation well enough. I had no complaints.
“There’s nothing to apologize for. I’m sure I’ve made him ten times busier than usual.”
“...Twenty times?”
“Ahem.”
“Cough.”
They couldn’t bring themselves to say it, but the repeated throat-clearing told me he was busy as hell.
I hadn’t checked what was happening outside yet. Still, the events of two days ago must have turned not just Korea but the whole world upside down.
No wonder.

Several monster waves in a single day were unprecedented. Learning that they had been deliberately caused—and that Ares Guild’s Vice Guild Master was behind it all—would hit harder than a nuclear bomb.
Even I, who knew little about the situation, couldn’t easily guess how large and far-reaching the aftermath of this incident would be.
“So did you stay just to give me that message?”
“Not exactly.”
“Then...”
As my voice trailed off, all three bowed politely.

“By order of His Excellency the President, we have been assigned to provide temporary security for Hunter Jin Taekyung and your family. Although we have been described as a surveillance detail on the surface, we ask that you put yourself at ease.”
“A surveillance detail?”

“This will only continue until the current situation has settled down. It has only been two days, after all, and under the current circumstances, Hunter Jin Taekyung remains a suspect who has been booked without detention.”
Booked without detention. Like surveillance detail, it didn’t have a pleasant ring to it.
I’d heard the phrase since I was a kid. Whenever a high-ranking politician or chaebol chairman got into trouble, it seemed to turn up on the news.
At least I haven’t been detained.
Being booked without detention meant that the suspect or defendant’s physical freedom was guaranteed, while the case itself had been formally registered with the judicial authorities.
“What are the charges?”
“There are extenuating circumstances for the other matters, but... for now, the main issue is the injuries you inflicted.”
The officer who seemed to be in charge added, looking at me with a mixture of respect and fear, “As you know, more than five hundred people sustained injuries, major or minor, at your hands.”
“Oh.”

“Of course, you needn’t worry too much. Given public opinion at home and abroad, as well as the circumstances of the incident, there’s a strong possibility your actions will be recognized as self-defense.”
I had expected some kind of punishment, but my situation was far better than I’d thought.
Once the truth came out, people in Korea and overseas had begun to accept that my actions were justified. Meanwhile, the late Go Jun had become a fucking bastard in the eyes of the entire world.
That was the gist of it.
I thought I might be going straight to prison.

Right before I went to Ares Guild Headquarters, I’d said I was leaving Peace Guild in case my actions brought trouble down on them. Things had turned out so well that the decision almost seemed pointless.
Of course, I couldn’t really call any of this good. It had begun with Kim Hwajong’s death.
And...
Things probably settled down this fast because someone gave them solid testimony.
I thought back to my conversation with President Baek Hanseong an hour or so earlier, and to the photograph of a middle-aged man who had looked composed before a crowd of cameras and microphones.
Go Se-won.
The President had told me Go Se-won was being held in a special detention center and wanted to see me. He said he had a debt to repay.
A debt to repay. What could he mean?
We’d met only briefly, but Go Se-won didn’t strike me as someone who would ask for a meeting just to exchange pleasantries.
Even if I was wrong, I needed to talk to him at least once. He had given up everything to reveal the truth.
The countless crimes Go Se-won must have committed while rising to become Head of Security could never be washed away, but it was also an undeniable fact that I owed him a debt.
While I stood there thinking, the Skeleton King came swaggering down the hall.
“I brought your coffee. Drink it.”
I looked at the steaming cup of instant coffee mix. Then I made up my mind.
“Don’t want it.”
“...You shitty hu—bastard.”
Leaving him growling behind me, I turned to the officers.
“Let’s go. Show me the way.”
“Pardon?”
“Go Se-won. He’s being held in a special detention center, right?”
The officers looked bewildered for a moment, then nodded.

“I’m embarrassed you had to see me like this.
Would you mind giving me some time alone?”
What could I say to him now?
I had neither the words nor the right.
Team Leader Choi needed time.
Time to accept the death of someone who had been as close as blood.
Time to find the courage to face his body.
“Get some rest, then.
There are people standing by, so call if you need anything.”
I tried to sound cheerful as I got up and headed for the door.
But when I put my hand on the doorknob, I thought of one last thing I wanted to tell him.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“It’s all right to lose your balance sometimes.
You can cry out loud.
No one will hear you.
Except for him.”
“I’ll be going now.”
My back was already turned, so I couldn’t see his expression or know how my words had struck him.
I was glad I couldn’t.
Click.
As I stepped out and pulled the door shut, I heard a faint sob through the narrowing gap.
It was the quietest, saddest sob I had ever heard.
The sound of a man who had never wavered, no matter what happened, finally breaking down.
“Taekyung, how’s Team Leader Choi—”
I wasn’t the only one who could hear him.
Im Kkeokjeong had started to ask with a worried look on his face, but he fell silent.
So did the other two waiting with him in the hall.
“Ah, I’m tired.
I need some coffee.”
Song Song stretched and walked away quickly.
The Skeleton King caught my eye, scratched his chin, and said, “This body could use some coffee too.
I haven’t been sleeping lately.
I feel like I might collapse...”
“Huh?
Oh.
Yeah, me too.”
Im Kkeokjeong was one thing, but an undead monster claiming he was sleepy and needed coffee?
I let out a quiet laugh at the ridiculous excuse and patted the Skeleton King’s shoulder.
“Make me a cup too.”
“You wretched human.
Have you no hands?
No feet?”
“I have a spear.”
The Skeleton King fell silent for a moment at my answer, then narrowed his eyes.
“...Black?”
“Mix.”
“You don’t even know what good coffee tastes like.
I’ll make it for you this once.
Just this once.”
By the time Im Kkeokjeong had left the hallway after the Skeleton King, who continued grumbling curses under his breath, the sound of dress shoes echoed from the distance.
Step.
Step.
Three men in black suits came into view.
Their steady breathing and measured steps told me they were well-trained Peak masters—or rather, A-rank Hunters.
But the fact that they had entered this mansion at all meant they were no ordinary Hunters.
They belonged to an organization very different from a Guild.
“Pleased to meet you, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
Instead of answering, I looked at them.
More precisely, at their tie pins.
Each black-and-gold badge bore a rose of Sharon and tiny engraved letters.
President’s Security Service
It was clear whose orders they were following.
I gave a small nod.
“President Baek Hanseong is looking for me?”
“No, sir,” the officer in front replied in a stiff, military tone.
“His Excellency left thirty minutes ago.
He asked for your understanding.
Affairs of state required him to leave without saying goodbye.”
He must have gone while I was in Team Leader Choi’s room.
I understood his situation well enough.
I had no complaints.
“There’s nothing to apologize for.
I’m sure I’ve made him ten times busier than usual.”
“...Twenty times?”
“Ahem.”
“Cough.”
They couldn’t bring themselves to say it, but the repeated throat-clearing told me he was busy as hell.
I hadn’t checked what was happening outside yet.
Still, the events of two days ago must have turned not just Korea but the whole world upside down.
No wonder.
Several monster waves in a single day were unprecedented.
Learning that they had been deliberately caused—and that Ares Guild’s Vice Guild Master was behind it all—would hit harder than a nuclear bomb.
Even I, who knew little about the situation, couldn’t easily guess how large and far-reaching the aftermath of this incident would be.
“So did you stay just to give me that message?”
“Not exactly.”
“Then...”
As my voice trailed off, all three bowed politely.
“By order of His Excellency the President, we have been assigned to provide temporary security for Hunter Jin Taekyung and your family.
Although we have been described as a surveillance detail on the surface, we ask that you put yourself at ease.”
“A surveillance detail?”
“This will only continue until the current situation has settled down.
It has only been two days, after all, and under the current circumstances, Hunter Jin Taekyung remains a suspect who has been booked without detention.”
Booked without detention.
Like surveillance detail, it didn’t have a pleasant ring to it.
I’d heard the phrase since I was a kid.
Whenever a high-ranking politician or chaebol chairman got into trouble, it seemed to turn up on the news.
At least I haven’t been detained.
Being booked without detention meant that the suspect or defendant’s physical freedom was guaranteed, while the case itself had been formally registered with the judicial authorities.
“What are the charges?”
“There are extenuating circumstances for the other matters, but... for now, the main issue is the injuries you inflicted.”
The officer who seemed to be in charge added, looking at me with a mixture of respect and fear, “As you know, more than five hundred people sustained injuries, major or minor, at your hands.”
“Oh.”
“Of course, you needn’t worry too much.
Given public opinion at home and abroad, as well as the circumstances of the incident, there’s a strong possibility your actions will be recognized as self-defense.”
I had expected some kind of punishment, but my situation was far better than I’d thought.
Once the truth came out, people in Korea and overseas had begun to accept that my actions were justified.
Meanwhile, the late Go Jun had become a fucking bastard in the eyes of the entire world.
That was the gist of it.
I thought I might be going straight to prison.
Right before I went to Ares Guild Headquarters, I’d said I was leaving Peace Guild in case my actions brought trouble down on them.
Things had turned out so well that the decision almost seemed pointless.
Of course, I couldn’t really call any of this good.
It had begun with Kim Hwajong’s death.
And...
Things probably settled down this fast because someone gave them solid testimony.
I thought back to my conversation with President Baek Hanseong an hour or so earlier, and to the photograph of a middle-aged man who had looked composed before a crowd of cameras and microphones.
Go Se-won.
The President had told me Go Se-won was being held in a special detention center and wanted to see me.
He said he had a debt to repay.
A debt to repay.
What could he mean?
We’d met only briefly, but Go Se-won didn’t strike me as someone who would ask for a meeting just to exchange pleasantries.
Even if I was wrong, I needed to talk to him at least once.
He had given up everything to reveal the truth.
The countless crimes Go Se-won must have committed while rising to become Head of Security could never be washed away, but it was also an undeniable fact that I owed him a debt.
While I stood there thinking, the Skeleton King came swaggering down the hall.
“I brought your coffee.
Drink it.”
I looked at the steaming cup of instant coffee mix.
Then I made up my mind.
“Don’t want it.”
“...You shitty hu—bastard.”
Leaving him growling behind me, I turned to the officers.
“Let’s go.
Show me the way.”
“Pardon?”
“Go Se-won.
He’s being held in a special detention center, right?”
The officers looked bewildered for a moment, then nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 598
paragraphs: There is always a reason behind things described as special.
The special detention center where Go Se-won was being held was no exception.
“Stop. We need to verify your identities.”
The soldier’s voice was stiff, his sharp eyes visible behind dark sunglasses. He wore a bulletproof vest and carried an automatic rifle.
The Blue House security officer in the driver’s seat held out a thin card.
“The warden should have received a call already.”
“I’m sorry, but everyone goes through the same procedure here.”

The soldier didn’t budge. Only after checking us with a magic detector to make sure no one was disguised did he raise the barrier. A little later, I got my first glimpse of the detention center I’d heard so much about.
Around a hundred soldiers stood guard, armed to the teeth. Hunters disguised as soldiers were hidden among them.
As if that weren’t enough, heavy weapons were positioned throughout the facility, along with concealed magic traps.
Most people wouldn’t be able to walk out of here in one piece.
This place held people who hadn’t yet received a verdict. Even so, security was far tighter than at a prison reserved for serious criminals.
One look at the warden waiting outside the main building told me why.
“Ho-ho. I’ve been waiting for you.”
He had the warm, genial face of an old man from a fried-chicken restaurant. The energy he gave off was anything but warm.
A former A-rank Hunter with an impressive record, the warden greeted me with a friendly attitude.

“When I first heard the news about you, I felt so relieved. This isn’t something I should say as the warden, but... honestly, every time I see the bastards in here, I feel like smashing their heads in with a mace. Isn’t that why I’ve gone bald from holding myself back?”
“...Oh. I see.”
His confession caught me so off guard that I could only give an awkward reply. Then I looked at his gleaming head and muttered, “You must have held back a lot.”
“What else could I do? Though when I really can’t stand it, I do give one of them a beating now and then. Only the worst ones, of course.”
“Pardon?”
“Give them a cup of potion and plenty of healing, and they’re good as new. What are they going to do? There’s no evidence. None.”
“Criminal bastards need a beating. Especially the ones in here.”
The Blue House security officers wore expressions that seemed to ask whether they should report this to the President, and I began to worry about whether one particular person was still alive.
“Is Go Se-won still alive?”
“Ah, that fellow.”
The warden laughed heartily.

“Of course. He’s perfectly fine. On his first day, I thought he might cause a major incident, but... he does as he’s told, and from what I hear from the prosecutors’ office, he’s been giving his statement without any trouble. I had the visitation room cleared out for you. Follow me.”
The security officers and I followed him inside.

The corridors were dark and cold. Alloy doors stood in rows like cages where iron bars would normally have been. Small hologram projectors outside each door showed every movement and expression of the people inside.
I’d heard about this place, but I’d never seen it for myself.
What made the special detention center special was that everyone held here was Awakened.

If an Awakened person committed a crime, they were brought here immediately, regardless of the charge. They might not have been convicted yet, but that didn’t spare them the tight security or constant surveillance.
They’re Awakened, after all.
Even an F-grade Awakened could easily subdue two or three grown men.
If they were higher-ranked and had obtained a Hunter license through formal training, that went without saying.

“They’re awaiting verdicts, sure, but most of them are obviously guilty. You never know what they might try. We get two or three escape attempts every year without fail. Once they’re convicted and transferred to a special prison, they won’t have another chance. That place is hell.”
As he explained while crossing the corridor, the warden pointed toward three or four metal doors that looked particularly thick and sturdy.
“We’re watching the bastards who came in this time particularly closely. They’ve got nothing left to lose, and they’ve been pretty rough.”

I checked the holograms to see who he meant. They were the Ares Guild executives I’d briefly glimpsed on the top floor. Go Se-won and the other Ares Guild members must have subdued them and sent them here.
They lay wrapped in mana suppressors from head to toe like mummies. I studied them, then made a heartfelt request.
“Please beat the shit out of them—good and proper.”
“I was planning to. I’ve already greased up the mace I used back in my active days.”
“You really do have everything planned, Warden.”
The warden smiled, pleased by my compliment, then asked, “Ah, but what’s going to happen to you, Hunter Jin Taekyung? I hope things work out for you, but the law is a complicated thing.”
“Who knows? I still have no idea.”
“It would be nice if you came here. I’d take good care of you.”
“...Oh. Right.”
Why was I suddenly picturing a mace glistening with grease?
While that unpleasant image occupied my mind, the long, twisting corridor came to an end at a large door.

Once we had finished every procedure at the security checkpoint, the warden explained, “You’ll meet with him alone, Mr. Jin Taekyung. By special request from above, there won’t be a guard in the room or a time limit. But everything inside will be recorded on audio and video, so please bear that in mind.”
Given Go Se-won’s situation, that much was only natural. I nodded, and the door opened.
Click.
Cold air met me as it swung inward. The room looked like one of the prosecutors’ interrogation rooms I’d seen in movies, and a familiar face was waiting inside.
“You came. Sooner than I expected.”
Go Se-won.
He looked noticeably more haggard than he had two days ago. Once the door closed, he pointed to a chair.
“Don’t just stand there. Sit down. My neck hurts from looking up at you.”
Clank.
Heavy metal rattled whenever he moved. He noticed me looking at the chains linking his neck, arms, and legs, and shrugged.
“Mana suppressor. It’s uncomfortable, but all things considered, they’re treating me well.”
I pulled out a chair and sat.
“I suppose so. On the way here, I saw your friends looking about ready to move into a pyramid.”
“Who? Executive Director Park? Managing Director Lee? Or...”
“Probably both. I couldn’t tell you which was which.”
“Fair enough. Neither of them is my friend anyway.”
Even now, he was as calm as ever. I watched him for a moment, then asked, “Should I thank you?”
The question came out of nowhere, but Go Se-won knew what I meant. He gave a quiet laugh.
“I’d been thinking about doing it for a long time. I just needed a reason.”
“Any regrets?”
“Not a single one.”
His face was haggard, but his eyes were clearer than ever. Maybe that was why I’d spared him.
When everyone else in Ares Guild had looked at me with anger and fear, he’d kept that clear, steady gaze. Even when death was right in front of him.
“You must have lost a lot over this.”
“I lost as much as I gained. I’ve only gone back to the way I was then—a war orphan who had nothing. More importantly, I protected my precious family. I should be satisfied with that.”
Everyone gets a chance to change. For Go Se-won, his family had probably been the reason. Maybe that last phone call, arriving when death was almost upon him, had led him to this choice.
“I saw the photo on your phone. Your son’s cute. Looks like a tough kid, too. He’s already got a solid build. He’d be perfect as a tank when he grows up.”
“She’s my daughter.”
They do say the eldest daughter takes after her father.
When I fell silent after accidentally assigning someone’s daughter to the tank class, Go Se-won let out a small sigh.
“I called you because I thought you might be able to help me, but you make me lose the desire to ask.”
“Well, never mind. In any case, the fact that you came to see me means you’ve already heard about it, right?”
Relieved that he’d changed the subject, I nodded.
“What did they tell you?”
“That you had a debt to repay me. I didn’t hear anything more specific.”
“Then you heard right. Passing it along through someone else didn’t sit right with me, so I kept quiet.”
Didn’t sit right with him?
Go Se-won was cooperating with every investigation and interrogation. He was laying out even his own wrongdoings without holding anything back, almost like a confession.
Yet there was something he hadn’t told them.
I knew there was more to it.
Just as I sensed that something serious was coming, he began fiddling with his earlobe.
It wasn’t a signal we’d agreed on, but I had no trouble understanding it.
Fwoosh.
Internal energy rose from my dantian and surrounded the visitation room. Sound was cut off in an instant.
Go Se-won noticed despite the mana suppressor. He pretended to rub the corner of his mouth and whispered, “Area A isn’t the only secret area hidden in the Guild headquarters.”
“What?”
“Search Area A carefully. There’s another secret area inside it.”
Another hidden space.
I blinked at him, then hurriedly asked, “Where? What’s the exact location?”
But contrary to my expectations, the answer that came back was low and brief.
“I don’t know.”
“What?”

“If I knew, I’d tell you. But only Vice Guild Master Lee Jungryong and Go Jun could enter. I don’t know where it is or how to get in. I only learned it existed shortly after I became Head of Security.”
Go Se-won had once been counted among Go Jun’s closest aides. Even he knew only that the second secret area existed, and nothing more.
“Then maybe...”
“Of course, I don’t know what’s inside or what they do there. That’s all I know.”
He cut me off sharply, then continued.
“The government investigation team must be searching Area A from top to bottom by now, but they probably haven’t noticed it yet.”
“Why?”
“If they had, they would have asked me about it before anything else.”
“So, Jin Taekyung. Find it. I don’t know what secrets it holds, but...”
I was about to ask another question when the heavy door opened with a metallic clang. The warden and the Blue House security officers looked at us suspiciously.
“We couldn’t hear anything. Is there a problem?”
Go Se-won answered calmly.
“The visit is over.”

chapters.title: Chapter 599
paragraphs: All the way back to the estate after my visit, I sensed a subtle change in the air.
Their glances and movements looked natural enough, no doubt thanks to rigorous training. But they couldn’t escape my senses.
They definitely suspect something.
The A-rank Hunters of the President’s Security Service.
They’d said they were there to provide temporary protection for my family and me, but I wasn’t naive enough to take their word for it.
If they notice even the slightest thing out of place, they’ll report it straight up the chain.
They weren’t Peace Guild members or ordinary Hunters. They were government employees whose direct superior was one person: the President.
President Baek Hanseong might already have received a report about today’s visit—my private meeting with Go Se-won, and the minute or two when no one had been able to hear what we said.
What should I do?
I sank into thought as I stared at the specially treated window that prevented anyone from seeing inside the vehicle.
Go Se-won had told me there was another secret area. Now I had to decide when to reveal that information, and to whom.
I didn’t have to think for long.
I can’t do anything right now anyway.
Only two days had passed since that day. The world was still in turmoil, and people had yet to recover from their grief and shock.
Even Team Leader Choi, who needed to know more than anyone, was no exception.
So I had to keep my mouth shut at least until Kim Hwajong’s funeral was over.
It wasn’t only for Team Leader Choi’s sake. I needed time to sort things out myself.
“Phew.”
At my quiet sigh, the security officer in the driver’s seat glanced at me in the rearview mirror.
“Is something bothering you?”
“No. It’s nothing.”
I sank deeper into the seat as I lied.
The truth was, I was uncomfortable. Everything around me made me uncomfortable.
Silently repeating the truth I hadn’t voiced, I looked out at the world beyond the window.
The scenery slipped past, and time passed just as quickly.
January 19.
A week had passed since the day that came to be known as the January 19 Incident, and the world was still in an uproar.
